title: Not worth it. Get a Bialetti stove top instead.
text:
It is solid steel and fits ok (hard at first but then one can learn how to load it without jamming it into the machine - Pixie)
The not so good news is that I have not found a way to get a strong enough coffee, comparable to the nespresso cups. I am not talking about the cream, which is less and not as dense, I am talking about the flavor. I tested different quantities of coffee (espresso ground) and the best was well below acceptable. The other issue is that no matter the amount of coffee in the capsule, a significant amount of water was lost in the process and went down in the tray. We all know that the capsules are smaller than the original disposable nespresso to fit them in the machine without damaging the loading mechanism, but I was not expecting the waste of water and such a poor flavor.

Washing was ok. Loading them a bit of a pain (especially early in the morning, right out of bed, if I forgot to get them ready the night before)

I have no experience with other brands of reusable capsules, but I suspect they all have similar challenges based on my research prior to buying these. I bought them because the price was ok enough to give it a try but they ended up in my kitchen drawer after a week of use.

I wish someone could come out with a better product. Frankly, for the price, I get a much better result with my old and lifelong trusted Bialetti stove top Coffees maker. Not much cream, but a good and reliable espresso.

title: Keeps food off the sides of counters and stove
text:
Sometimes I cook like the Cookie Monster, with food flying everywhere. I swear, the harder I try NOT to make a mess, the worse it is! Periodically, I’ll have to pull out the stove, and wipe spills off the cabinets and oven. So when I saw this, I thought it was a great idea.

This is pretty foolproof to install. You just lay it across the gap between the range and your countertop with the divider in the space. The 25 inch cover was about an inch longer than the width of our stovetop, so I trimmed it at an angle to transition between the counter and the range.

This works great. Now all the food and spills are staying on the stovetop and counters where it can easily be wiped off. I don’t have to pull out the appliance to wipe it down. I think it has also reduced the amount of food I have to vacuum off the floor around the stove.

Almost $12 for two 2.25 x 25 inch silicone strips seems a bit high, but I’m not going to fuss. This product is going to save me a fair amount of labor!

title: Avoid the Self Clean Option
text:
We bought our Capital Culinarian in June of 2011. One giant negative, the ovens. On the plus side, the unit is built solidly using excellent stainless steel. It's built like a tank. It took 4 men to move it into the house. The burners are excellent at 23.5k, but as you'd expect the simmer isn't that good. What we do is to stack one grate on top of another thus elevating the pan away from the heat. Problem solved. The grates are solid, heavy and of excellent quality, and clean up nicely in the dishwasher.
We have the 48" with 2 ovens, 6 burners and the grill. The grill is underpowered. I preheat for 30 to 45 minutes and still it can be challenging to get proper grill marks. I've talked with Capital and they told me they don't have a higher output burner and that I cannot drill more holes to get more flame. I'm stuck with what I have.
The ovens are the weak link. the large oven convection works well, but if the oven had a digital read out baking would be much better. One disappointment is the markings on the face of the stove, i.e., next to the oven dial selector, lights labeled "Bake, Broil, Clean, Door Lock". They and all the other labels are just decals! After 6 years of use and cleaning, they are wearing away.... Sadly some are unreadable.
The small oven is useful only as a warming oven really, as baking in it requires constant attention - turning the trays to avoid burning at the rear.
And DONT GET THE SELF CLEAN model! Oh the horrors I've had with that! I'm on the 4th repair. I just want to remove the self cleaning function and make it a manual clean. Most everything about this range is excellent except for the self clean! A word to the wary, don't get it!

title: Not really a convertible
text:
Pro: super easy to install. Comes with a diagram of the hood, with the exact dimensions. Great for drilling holes on wall for installation. Suction power falls in the expectation range for the price.

Cons: NOT good for ductless. This product is being marketed as a convertible hood. However it is really designed as a vented hood. It has a top vent that sticks out about 3/4 inch above. This is where your exhaust would come out if you go with ductless. Assuming you have a cabinet that’s above the hood, would you drill a 6” hole on the bottom of your cabinet and let the exhaust exit into your cabinet? If not, you’ll need leave a gap of at least 2.5 inches between the top of the hood and the bottom of the cabinet. Don’t forget there are two dampers inside the top vent that would flap open when the hood is turned on. Envision what esthetic value that’ll add to your kitchen. Besides, the greasy/warm exhaust would blow right on your hair/face when you cook. Well, they do sell charcoal filter separately for about $20-30 (cheap cheap stuff, completely a rip-off) that you can attach to the suction intake vent. Supposedly these two filters would trap the oily component in the exhaust. Plan to buy a new pair every other month. So, the choice is yours, should you ever go ductless.

title: Skip this one and go to HD
text:
Such an overpriced product that I thought I would just so this with 4 inch vent pipe... And success! Don't waste your money on this. Just pull the old vent pipe out of the rear and measure and cut to length with a hacksaw for the new output hole. Cut the wide end and flare the edges with a pair of pliers. Use te pliers to remove the tacked on braket too. Test fit over the blower output. It should wiggle in about 1 inch max. Add a 90 from Home Depot which fits over the original pipe easily. The 90 has 4 parts so put it in straight then rotate inside the machine to get the angle. I vented out the bottom so that's all I needed! It can push up so you can slide the dryer into place then pull the 90 down a little from underneath ( assuming basement access). I don't see a need for tape as the 90 fits over the pipe by 2-3 inches and it's all solid smooth pipe. If you need side venting just add a straight length of pipe off the 90 and out of the machine.

Hope this helps someone out there wondering if it would work!

title: Buy these

title: Loved....for the first year and a half
text:
I loved this washing machine. I was so excited to get it and actually looked forward to washing clothes. It was rated very highly on Consumer Reports, so of course it had to be good, right? I loved all the settings and it got many stains out. It had so many pros to it....until a year and a half later. (warranty is only good for a year...coincidence?)

The noise it makes while spinning started a little loud at first. A year and a half later, it sounds like a jet engine. I feel like the noise gets louder by the load and just this past cycle, it started squeaking as well (like something is rubbing together). I finally couldn't take it anymore, so I called a repairman to come out. Apparently there are very few repairmen who actually work on front loaders. (and I thought front load washers were supposed to be the best thing since sliced bread!) We have a repairman coming tonight to tell us what is wrong. I will update later on his assessment.

title: Low quality
text:
Way lower quality compared to other brands. The inlet hose is a joke, the water does not go through it and the opening is so small it doesn’t go over any faucet so including a tightening mechanism is pointless. Stuck filling containers with water to fill this as shower head is not removable to fill with that.

The drain hose is WAY TOO SHORT and does not even fit over a tub ledge if you wanted to set this on the floor. Had to stand it on a box inside the tub so that the hose would have somewhere to go and drain.

The “normal” wash cycle level is too harsh and needs to be set to soft.

The power cord is short and there are no hooks to wrap it around like other brands. It’s also 3 prong so if your outlet is 2 prong you’ll need an adapter. Drain hose came crushed as well.

If you get passed these issues, it washes ok and spins pretty dry.

title: Ingenious system!  But with some caveats
text:
[[VIDEOID:20f684a84473fabec26a3a585e6f17f8]] So for $20 ther are 100 pods. That's .05$ a pod. Great! But.. the pods themselves are not reusable or recyclable. Once the ring is snapped on, it's not coming back off. So it makes no difference whether there are more foils or not. My thinking is that they could charge a lesser amount for refill packs of the cups AND foils but without the contraption that puts them together.
I am not using these to save money, but for my husband to continue to use his regular Folgers coffee (he is old school and does not like change) and I can have my espresso, etc.
They are however, EXCELLENT for their intended use. The Folgers comes out with a beautiful crema and smooth taste just like the Vertuo pods. The machine recognizes them just fine.
All in all, although I do wish they were recyclable as well, I will re-up when the time comes.

title: Nifty but cheap
text:
I am a homebrewer and I own one of these I purchased from HomeDepot. They're really great if you're a small-batch brewer (I was bring 3gal batches at the time which means two 1.2gal mini-kegs were perfect for my useable beer once separated from the trub), or if you have a source for regularly purchasing Heineken-style minikegs of ready made beer (by the way, Hofbrauhaus ships their Oktoberfestbier internationally in said minikegs...you're welcome ;)). I absolutely loved my minikegerator...while it lasted.
While the system is easy to use, keeps your beer carbonated and fresh for days (I've had a keg last two weeks which is about the slowest I'll go through that amount of beer), not too hard to clean and really quite stylish, its critical parts are all cheap plastic.
Mine lasted just over a year of constant use and reuse before the diptube broke on removing it from a keg. Unfortunately I do not have a back up plan and have had to suspend my home brewing while I build up a supply of bottles or purchase a real kegging system.
tl;dr:
Great gimmicky gift for your beer loving friends and family for short-term use, not a long-term solution to small space kegerating.

I suppose the idea is to get people to keep buying because things don't last, on purpose. The best solution for me has been these drip pans. When I gave up on being able to make the original drip pans decent, I put in a set of these pans and threw the originals away. Then I bought another set to have on hand in the event that I need to replace those, which I am projecting will happen. Wouldn't it be nice to be proven wrong? In the meantime, the new pans are very nice looking although not as substantial as I remember drip pans being in the past. title: One of Those Items You Didn't Know You Needed!
text: Let's get something straight right at the outset. This handy little product is 4"x2", not 10"x10"x10" as stated in the listing. However, 4"x2" is the perfect size for the job it does, which is to prop your front-loading washing machine door open far enough for the inner basket to air out between washes, cutting down on mold growth and bad smells. I always left my washer door open anyway, but it didn't stay open far enough to make much of a difference. Four inches is just enough to let more air in but keep my cats out, who each sniffed it once then have totally ignored it. The prop is magnetic on both ends and will hold tight to any metal part of your washer. Mine has a metal body but a plastic inner door. The prop manufacturer has solved that problem by including three metal disks with adhesive backing that can be attached to your door for the prop magnet to stick to. Nice clear instructions are included, although usage is pretty self-explanatory. Made of sturdy plastic and not bendable at all. Very practical and should last a long time.

I keep buying them because when using room temperature water the resulting ice is similar to ice common to ice dispensers at fast food fountains or gas stations costing $3,500-$4,000. I'm an ice chewer, half a container of liquid with ice filling the rest and go through 3 liters of water daily making ice.

The internal ice making mechanisms of just about all the ice makers here on Amazon are the same. The external plastic housings surrounding them differ as do external button locations and other options and drain plugs, if any. More than likely whichever one you pick will last as long as another. Its great to have such a varied choice at reasonable prices. This brand, so far, seems to be a good one.

title: Important things to know, save you time and worry.
text:
Important things to know:
1. Most people find the new wire harness to be too short and end up using the old one. It was at least for me, and would have saved me some hassle if I’d of used the old one to begin with. Not sure why they supply this harness when it’s so short.
2. The universal funnel insert has pre cut slots for how your ice maker was set up. I wasn’t a fan, it was hard to cut out, even with it precut. Be careful, it’s not very sturdy.
3. If you can reuse your old bottom bracket, use it. My old one was metal, the new one is plastic and off by a quarter of an inch making it unusable.
4. It can take up to 24 hours for your first batch of ice. Mine took 3 hours. Not sure why this is, but you’ll have to wait.
5. Put the top to screws in to the freezer wall slightly and the ice maker can be slid on to them, and then tighten. I did it this way but saw in other reviews people say they didn’t think of it.

The ice maker is making ice, was a lower cost replacement for my older fridge, and over all I’m happy. Wish I knew some of those things I went over before I started, could have made my 30 minute install, 10 minutes or less.
The wire harness is useless, the company could save themselves money by not even including it, but if they are going to, it needs to be longer. They should also maybe provide separate universal fill cups, instead of making you cut the one they provide.
Overall I’m satisfied and hopefully this review helps someone else.

title: A few things to know
text:
Completely saves space and now my clothes are never musty or need re-washing bc forgot to dry (which I was horrible at).

It would be better on a pedestal as you have to gravity drain about 2 cups of water out the bottom each time. Bc I don’t have pedestal I use a larger to go food container so it is shallow enough to actually drain but big enough to get up with the water and dump it without spilling.

Also instead of grabbing dry lint from a trap you take a wet paper towel (it takes me 2) to wipe wet lint from the rubber around the door. By the time the water has drained I have finished wiping so no big deal.

Total wash and dry takes me about 3 hours and 15 minutes for a medium-large load. But because you can set it to wash and then dry, I don’t notice the time because at work or asleep. It will say crazy stuff on the time left when it first gets going like 7 or 8 hours but it resets that lower and lower as it does its job.

If you like to sort your stuff and have more smaller loads then this isn’t going to be so great for you but, if like me just mixing everything and doing a load a week, its perfect.

Oh, also the dryer only has regular or turbo so not many options. Again fine for me bc I really don’t care enough to ever change the settings but if you like setting options to specialize your stuff not a great choice.

Def better than stackable as have so much extra space now. Even if I had room for conventional side by side washer and dryer I would still want this. If I ever had some imaginary large family that required washing more than two load a clothes a day (put one in before bed and one in before work would totally be practical), I would still rather have two of these than regular ones!

Wiping the lint out is easy and if I had imaginary kids, it would absolutely be one of their chores. Its easy and takes only a few minutes but without a pedestal you are squatting to do so making it much better for littler people.

title: Works as well as expected...not as good as full-size dishwasher, but good enough
text:
It cleans stuff pretty well. Reading other reviews, I think this is a generic countertop dishwasher with the brand name slapped on, similar to lots of others, but I got this specific one so I'll review it. Just get it; it'll be fine. I paid around $200+shipping.

I used to have an awesome expensive full-size General Electric dishwasher before I moved to a smaller place. That one was way better and had more settings, a digital timer readout, etc. But it's not fair to compare the two. This one washes dishes just as well; it's just smaller and way cheaper.

Size: I can't load big pots or pans like my previous under-countertop dishwasher, so I wash them by hand. But everything else fits. It's impractical to load it as shown in the user manual. Bowls will not stand up that way due to physics. So I lay them flat or angled, and it's good enough, but they take a lot of space. Since it can only take a small load, I run it once or twice a day, whereas my big dishwasher could be filled up every 2-3 days. If you have a big family, you might have to leave dishes in the sink for the next morning. Which is honestly manageable and within expectations for something of this size.

Cleanliness: It washes well. The default cycle is great. The different wash cycles don't really make sense to me, and the user manual doesn't clarify them, so I use the default one. No thinking needed. If I accidentally put in too much washing liquid and it smells weird, I just run the rinse cycle.
The corners don't wash well. Don't put anything there. Wasted space.

Noise: It's pretty loud, which is expected. Not much louder or quieter than other dishwashers I've used.

Installation: This part sucked, and it's the reason this is 4 star instead of 5. It didn't fit my weird-shaped modern faucet so I either had to change my faucet or connect it directly to the water line. I expect that some people have fancy or non-standard faucets, so they have to connect directly to the water line. Well I tried to hook it to the water line, but it turns out that the factory PVC pipe fittings won't work with standard couplings that I had laying around. I'm sure the provided fittings are standard sizes, but they were manufactured weirdly so they didn't couple well. They looked kind of cheap. So I bought a replacement water supply and it works great; no leaks. I wish I didn't have to spend the extra $20 of couplings and pipes to get it working. The drain pipe was fine; no problems. Thankfully I have experience in plumbing. If you don't know plumbing and have a non-standard faucet, this could be a real headache.

Other thoughts: Sometimes the wash cycle stalls. I just turn it off and turn it on. Not a big deal. What do you expect for this price? And I wish the tray was more...designed. It has big gaps where dishes could fall through. It seems so easy to just add a few extra bars. And some bars are too small to slide in a dish. Like why? Just get rid of it. To the designer: have you ever loaded dishes before? I'm just nitpicking though; it works well overall and you can figure out how to use it.

text:
Egg cartons do not belong in the fridge for long periods of time, but this does.

I've owned a few egg containers in the past and they all suffered from the same annoying problem.

The eggs became difficult to take out after refrigeration. The area where it sat conformed exactly too its prolate spheroid shape. Combination of those two factors made the egg too slippery for grasping with fingers.

I don't have that problem at all with this KATEI STORY plastic egg holder.

The individual round egg trough where each egg sits isn't recessed into the actual container. You can take the entire tray out and clean it if you want. Very clever design allowing you to easily remove an individual egg, no matter the size without damaging it.

The other features I really like about this egg container:

*Securely holds two dozen eggs.
*Has an individual 120°flip top for the front and rear of the egg container. You don't need to take the whole thing out of the fridge to access them.
*Lid is large enough to stack other food containers on top.
*Has open side handles allowing fresh cold air to flow inside the storage area.
*Box is transparent so you can see at a glance how many eggs remain.

The only downside is the BPA-free Food-grade PET and PP this Stackable Egg tray is constructed of is very thin. Doubt it would survive an accidental drop. The lid sits loosely on top, so I wouldn't task my kids to handle it neither.

Makes my fridge look a whole lot neater though!

Give your store-bought eggs the Mother Hen treatment with this KATEI STORY 24 count egg container.

title: 1st Remove existing connector, install new last, unit is held in with 3 screws with ¼" hex heads!
text:
Feb 2022 Update - all still good, no change in the 5 stars, but 2 things.

In the last ~week, the thing started spitting out ice without stopping. In investigating it looks like the metal bar that is supposed to sense the ice level had been slid out on the side closest to the door (the side you can't easily see). Used a mirror to put that back in. The easy test as to whether this is potentially a problem is to push the metal leveler-arm "up" and it should click to the off position. If it doesn't then use a mirror to see if maybe you have the same problem.

FYI, for the refrigerator KBFS25ECMS00 the original ice maker was W10469286.

I also found online a pretty reliable sounding source that suggested if you have problems with an ice maker after ~ 5yrs then it's probably the cheapest approach to just replace it!

End Feb 2022 Update

This worked well in my Kitchenaid kbfs25ecms00. Not a difficult repair, but nor was it as easy as it appears. Learned a few things I thought I'd share.

There were a few videos that were helpful in getting the shelves out as well as removing the icemaker. We did not remove the shelves, as it always seemed like it was more work than necessary (though one video seemed to suggest it was easy). On my model, to get the top shelf out you needed to remove a few extra screws, pop up some clips, carefully disassemble . .. . etc., so decided to just try without. It was doable, but definitely harder with the top shelf in. If I were doing it again, I'd probably pull the top shelf. Replacement might be possible without removing the lower shelf at all, but the door was open for a bit so be cautious.

I lucked into this, but strongly suggest unclipping the connector first, and (re)connecting it back up last. Otherwise, there could be a bit of a leak of water. Almost as soon I'd connected the new one up the water ran to fill it, so I was quite happy it was already fully installed! Also realized that while jostling the broken unit I could've closed the broken connection and water would've flowed then as well.

To remove the old unit there are 3 screws that have ¼" hex heads, so a nut driver of that size works well. The bottom and back screws are readily accessible, but the top-forward one (closest to the opening) was hard to see and therefore hard to get to. It was a bit of hunt and peck. On install, we left the top two screws loosely in place, and that made it a bit easier. Turns out if you leave them a bit loosely installed then you can slide the icemaker down onto them before tightening. But, make sure the water hose is pointed to the right place on the unit (which was also easy to do).

I got this unit anticipating the icemaker was the problem, but was not positive that that was the case. I only knew that we weren't getting ice cubes, and a bad icemaker seemed a common cause. Thought it easier to have this as a replacement unit and return it if not needed rather than to empty the freezer and disassemble the shelves twice. Before installing the new icemaker I did open the old one to see if it was likely the problem (vice a valve or other part). As with other folks, when opened the unit I found the heating element (that releases the cubes from the tray) terminal was corroded through. This turned out to be a great move this time, and I'd probably risk it again.

As mentioned above, the icemaker filled with water immediately upon hooking up the connector, and then dropped the first set of ice ~ 1 to 2 hrs later. Been slowly filling the tray ever since.

title: Using a Paper Filter
text:
I'm not a huge fan of Keurig's multistream pod. It's definitely durable and does the job, but it's
pricey and has more parts and steps to deal with than the non-Keurig pods that fit and worked
beautifully in my previous keurig. Having said that, I love my new multistream Keurig so I'm
dealing with the reusable pod inconveniences.

One issue I didn't want to compromise on was using paper filters. Yes, I know filters aren't required, but 1) I don't like sediment in my coffee and 2) filters capture coffee oils (Studies have shown coffee oils can raise cholesterol).

I initially tried putting the paper filter into the keurig mesh filter which didn't work that well. I then
tried setting the paper filter in the black pod adapter and used the mesh filter to push it down.
Success! The filter is now in place and the pod is ready to fill. Take a look at the filter after you've made a cup and you'll see what didn't go into your cup.

title: Beautiful but NOISY, vibrates and is hard to clean
text: This cook top is elegantly designed and nice to look at. It heats up quickly and evenly and we're happy overall with the cooking quality. We are, however, very disappointed with how NOISY the vent fan is and how it VIBRATES so much that our pans constantly migrate off the center of the elements. We have to continually watch them to make sure they are centered and getting even heat. The vent is not that effective at removing fumes and steam even on the highest speed. We switched from a natural gas cook top because it was hard to clean but the glass ceramic is worse. Every little thing sticks and you literally have to scrape fine food particles off with a razor blade in addition to using a special cleanser specifically for this type of surface. I have to buff the surface repeatedly (with a LOT of elbow grease) each time I clean it. It's not a simple wipe it and you're done. We would not recommend this cook top. It's too bad showrooms don't really let consumers see this and other appliances like dishwashers, washing machines, blenders, etc. in action before you buy them.

Before buying these, I read a review that suggested the flannel is so tightly woven that this person had to poke holes in them with corn holders to help the flow. (Cornholes?)

My experience is the opposite. In fact I started grinding coffee (seed grinder) extra fine to try and slow down the flow. Not a bad cup, and I can live with a little weaker brew, but a little more steep would be preferred. I have a french press if I need stronger or larger pot, but I don’t usually want the hassle of using it for just a cup, and kind of like the ceremony of a pour over.

Considering a ceramic filter holder to possibly help. Any better suggestions for a reusable filter to make a quick (but full-flavored) cup of coffee would be appreciated.

I thought the stainless filter would be it; maybe a better version of that? Maybe I should just stop drinking coffee? 🤨

So 4 stars, as these can be used to filter juices and other things as well.

You don't get the hot air unless you turn the dial past 120 minutes and two hours is a long time to run a dryer. I've been turning the dial to 160 to get the hot air. I check the load in about 40 minutes when it will be decreasing to warm air. The clothes are usually dry in that time but hot so I let it run with the warm air for about 10 minutes and remove them. Total time is about 40-50 minutes per load which is good but I cant set it and go like i used to with my old dryer. title: Everything you need for a complete overhaul!
text:
Long POSITIVE review:

This includes literally everything you need to replace all your most common wear and tear parts in the front loading dryer. Not only does it include the wheels, but they’re actually already mounted on brand new hardware, with fasteners and all! Literally remove the old wheel/post by loosening the nut, and replace it all in one step! The hardest ones to replace are located at the back of the machine. If you have the room, which I did not, simply remove the 12 or so fastener screws to separate the back panel and allow easier access to the hexhead holding the post in place, so you can loosen the nut on the front. You can still get a wrench in the access holes without removing the rear panel, but there was a lot of swearing, and cut my thumb on the sharp aluminum by the lower wheel next to the exhaust pipe. And pay attention to the belt routing before you remove the old belt or you’ll be trying to finagle the routing blindly with one hand while trying to maintain pressure on the tensioner all while guessing which way the belt goes lmao

All in all, very well made kit, easy to install, and in 30 days in with no issues!

PS be sure, while the dryer is apart, CLEAN EVERYTHING YOU CAN! I literally vacuumed over a pound of lint and dirt from every nook and cranny!

title: Coffee Filter
text:
I purchased this filter hoping that I would not need to buy more paper filters. It is not that paper filters are all that expensive, but more that they have a habit of falling over every now and then when brewing and then you wind up with a pot full of grounds!

The filter itself works ok, but as noted by others, there is a definate "sludge" in the bottom of the pot no matter what grind you use. The only difference is the amount of "sludge" in the pot. The finer the grind, the more material in the pot!

So, I now use this filter with a paper filter in it. Happily, if a paper filter should fold over during brewing, it prevents the grounds from getting into the pot of coffee. On the negative side, it still means that I am buying paper filters.

From the environmental point of view, paper filters are not an issue for me since I composte them into the earth with the grounds. Seems to work well.

The filter does keep grounds out of the pot and that saves using extra filters to refilter the already brewed coffee plus it saves the agrivation of doing that.

Over all, the filter works for what I need. It just is not enough by itself unless you like extra thick coffee.

title: They need to provide better documentation if they want to beat their rivals.
text:
The X800 is a great hood (looks almost the same as the Fotile) but the install was painful. They do not provide template or directions what so ever. The booklet can be throw away the second you open it. Call me a perfectionist but I need to leave no gap between my hood and my cabinet (which is an extreme tight fit if your pipe do not go straight up).

NOTE IF YOUR VENT DO NOT GO STRAIGHT UP THE HOOD EXHAUST WILL SOUND WEIRD BECAUSE IT IS SO POWERFUL. I GET ABOUT 65 db ON THE LOWEST SETTING.

They did not provide any template or measurements on where to drill the holes in the cabinet if you want to install it like a under the cabinet microwave/hood. I had to find someone to literally hold this thing for 15 minutes (it is about 40 lbs as we secured it on the wall but it was tipping down). The install ends up perfect where it is 32 inches from the stove with zero gap between the hood and my cabinet.

Of course they want you to pay hundreds of dollar and get one of their people to do a sloppy job (they will leave a big gap mounting the hood using the middle mounting holes) and tell you that's the best way to do it or you should have bought the 30 dollar stainless steel plate cover (which you can get a flashing for 5 dollars at home depot). Overall they will rip you off unless you know what you are doing.

Also, the plastic that was protecting the stainless steel was a pain to take off.

Overall the hood is great but the installation documentation and the plastic film made this product 2 stars.

title: Not worth the hassles it came with
text:
This is an updated review:
We purchased a Cosmo 30 inch range (Model #: EPGR304) and had a very poor customer experience dealing directly with the appliance manufacturer. The oven range light did not function from the beginning, the burners were set too high and our food kept burning. When we called and spoke to Cosmo so they could help us repair these issues, the representative on the phone could not walk us through the next steps and asked us to take and upload videos of our issues, and answer a number of questions for their review. Two days after completing this process, I got an email confirmation that they would send someone from their contracted service center. Surprisingly, however, they followed up with an additional request asking for more video and then denied our service request altogether indicating that our issues did not meet their criteria for sending a service technician.

At this point, my husband and I arranged for a product return. Dealing with Cosmo directly felt like a serious waste of time and I am grateful the experience is behind us. Based on our experience, I would not recommend this product to family or friends.

Original Review:
The Cosmos 30" inch slide-in range arrived and was installed yesterday. It is beautiful to look at and I'm looking forward to cooking and baking with it. While the stove fit the width and height that we needed very well, the electrical cord that came with the stove is not a flat plug in as viewed in the user manual on pg 29 (did they choose a flat plug in for the 48 inch model only?). So now, we are left with a 1/2 to 1 inch gap (see picture number 2) of unused space at the back of the stove which requires it to push out beyond our cabinets. Also, the LED oven light(s) did not function after install so we will likely be on the phone with customer support to discuss that...

title: Keurig Mini Single Serve HACK
text:
So I received this as a gift. The product description says it is compatible with the Keurig Mini Single Serve Cup, but when I inserted this in my Keurig Mini it bent the insert needle. The needle DOES NOT PERFECTLY align with the hole on this k-cup. I noticed that there was less ease to pushing my handle down and that should have made me question using this reusable k-cup. I pushed it down with some force and then heard a bit of a crack noise. I let my Keurig brew, and it did brew me a cup of coffee. However, when I went to remove this cup, I noticed the top insert needle of the Keurig bent. What a bummer on my new Keurig!!!

I did some investigation and research on this, and it appears that either the hole is too small or the K-cup is slightly too high, sits too high or is too large. I did a couple of different techniques to see if I could still use this product. Most of them ended up with coffee grinds and water everywhere.

Here's the GOOD NEWS: if you unscrew the purple plastic piece from the metal piece and keep it off, it fits perfectly in the pod, you can push the handle down with ease AND it brews well. Check out the picture to so you can see what I mean.

My Keurig Mini still is able to punch a hole in normal K-cups, though the hole is not perfect, it does the job and did not completely break that part. So, I am able to use my Keurig as normal. Overall, I am giving this 2 stars because it says it is compatible with the Keurig Mini when it's not, it bent my Keurig entry needle, and I had to figure out a hack for it to work. It is cheap enough, but for all you KEURIG MINI USERS BE WARNED!

title: Does this Filter Add Dangerous Chemicals to Coffee?
text:
I have two coffee presses and I did a side-by-side comparison, one with this filter and one without. The coffee press with this filter imparted a chemical flavor in my coffee which was not present in the coffee press without the filter. I thought that, over time, the chemical flavor would subside but after using this filter daily for a week I did the same comparison and the chemical flavor did not go away with this filter.

What chemicals were used to make this "polyester" filter and are these chemicals dangerous? I was so confused as to what was causing the chemical taste so I removed the filter and bit into it in several places. The areas of the filter that don't touch the bottom metal plate (and filter coffee) had zero flavor but I was surprised to find out that the areas that touch the metal plate (not filtering the coffee) had the same strong chemical flavor that was in my coffee. There must be some type of chemical reaction that's triggered when the polyester material is wet and is pressed against metal. It seemed quite dangerous to me so I removed this filter and threw it in the trash.

I am also wondering if there is an organic filter similar to this but made without bleach or chemicals that will not change the flavor of my coffee. I would love to give this filter a higher rating because it is designed and works as intended but I can not due to this issue.

title: Works well, small issues, but worth owning.
text:
I use this several times a day. We use a room humidifier, we're curious about the high and low settings, this allows us to actually visualize the Relative Humidity. During the summer, I use it outdoors to determine humidity. Inside as well, when the Air Conditioner is on.

I use grease on the pivot point, just a little, to reduce friction and wear.

The Scale used for calculating Relative Humidity doesn't go to 100%, that occurs when properly used, the Wet Bulb is wet, Dry Bulb is dry, and it's spun for the recommended time, and both Temperatures are the same. But frankly, when both temperatures are the same, you don't need the scale anyway. I also use an Android App that I write the values into and it gives the Relative Humidity. There's also online sites where you can write in the temperatures and get the relative humidity.

The cap that holds the wick could be better designed, I don't open it to fill, just wet the wick on the bulb and where it goes in the cap. The scales could use correcting to be more accurate on high humidity, and when spinning, an index finger pushing up on the base of the Thermometer Pivot Block makes the spinning much more steady.

You can buy highly calibrated Thermometers for this unit, very expensive, but the two that come with it work fine. The thermometers are not referenced to the Psychrometer, they are individually indexed with the Temperature, and you use the built in scale with the temperatures as noted from the reading.

It's not a toy, it works well, and I use it often. Winter here, humidifier in bed room on, low, and after a few hours, it's 60% Relative Humidity here, which, in the winter, makes it comfortable. But I love being able to measure the humidity.

I don't think we paid this much, though I'm sure we purchased through Amazon.

title: Reasonably priced, sharp looking, LOW SOUND under counter fridge.  LASTED 5+ years.
text:
Fridge arrived well packaged with foam around entire unit inside cardboard box. Box was skidded and banded so it wouldn't move and had a cardboard cone on top that said no stacking and prevented further stacking during shipment.

Fridge is being used in our finished basement where we have cabinets and countertop sunk back into wall. Fridge sits neatly between 2 cabinets and underneath the countertop. I have less than the 1/5" recommended space on both sides available for venting so I put a grille in the back wall to allow the fridge to draw cooling air from the unfinished storage space on the backside of the wall. It is imperative to allow enough space around the unit for venting purposes or you will burn out the compressor prematurely.

Assembly was easy. Just had to tighten some screws to get the handle on. Had to adjust the leveling legs to get it to fit flush within undercounter cabinet space. This was quick and easy. I just had to initially loosen with some pliers and then turn by hand. Rubber boots on legs helped avoid any scratching on my laminate flooring as I slid into place. This is designed for can storage so it does not lend itself as nicely to beer and water bottles. The shelving can be changed to different levels so I moved one of the shelves to allow a layer of standing bottles to go in while still having plenty of can storage.

After allowing to sit for a day (compressor oil needs to settle), I turned it on. I set to lowest setting of 38F to see if and how quickly it would reach set point. Cooled to set point, down from ambient temperature, within 1 hour . Fluctuates regularly by +/- 1 or 2 degrees. Stocked with 12 cans and bottles and it quickly came down to setpoint in under 20 minutes. I imagine that if you packed with room temperature cans it might take an hour or so to come down to temperature.

The inside light is a fluorescent blue, similar to the controller lights, and is very stylish. Light is either on all the time or off all the time. It does not come on when you open the door. I will likely only turn it on when entertaining since it is kind of cool looking. The stainless steel door, handle and front return grille along with the glass door are very stylish.

The settings can quickly and easily be toggled between F and C.

The major reasons for picking this fridge when doing my research were;
- Correct size for my under counter installation
- Fully viewable glass door
- Large 148 can storage volume
- Front air intake to accommodate under counter installation
- SOUND, SOUND, SOUND

The reviews on this item mostly stated that the noise was low. Since this was going into an area where we would be listening to music, entertaining, or most importantly watching tv/movies on our projector screen, I did not want an obtrusive noise cycling on and off. Although not completely quiet, and how could it be since there is a compressor that needs to run, it is very quiet. I am very happy with how little noise is coming off of this thing. I might have heard it cycle on once during my 4 or 5 hours of watching football and I have no doubt it cycled more than that while I was down there. With nothing else on in the room I can hear a low hum.

It is not the cheapest fridge ($649) in the marketplace but it met all of my criteria and was well worth the investment. The only remaining question is the durability. Has only been running for 1 week so we'll see how it holds up over time.

UPDATE 12/15/14: Over 1 year in and still working great.

UPDATE 3/10/17: Over 3 years in and still working great. Apparently I got the only good one ever made based on all the other reviews or I'm the only one that installed it correctly.

UPDATE 4/30/19: It finally died this past weekend. I got over 5 years out of it. A refrigerator should last longer so I've reduced the stars from 5 down to 3 due to mediocre longevity.

title: Re-ordered (identical) item doesn't fit inspite of correct specs.
text:
Update January 2015

We've been ordering this filter every 6 months for our RF267AWEP Samsung refrigerator since 2011. We just re-order this original Smasung filter for DA29-00003G (they kept updating it from 3b and on, and we kept re-buying the latest one). We generally stick with the OEM when available to ensure we get the most out of our product per its design, and drinking safe and tasty water is important enough to not risk for a save of a few bucks. This is why we were very annoyed when this routine re-order resulted in a filter that did not fit. Worst yet - we carefully read all labels on the filter and the box, and they stated the exact model we need (and that was consistent with the old filter).
Searching the reviews we saw we were not the only ones, and when we called Amazon, the representative said there is a mismatch between the product title in the order page and the actual product shipped (???). His suggestion was to buy a substitute made by the same manufacturer that was even cheaper (Samsung Aqua-Pure DA29-00003G Plus Compatible Water Filter - Refrigerator). Reluctantly we agreed. The filter indeed fit, but it does not have the same NSF certifications of the original.
Very disappointing for such a common and popular item.
Not sure who is more at fault - Samsung or Amazon for not fixing this issue properly.

Original review 2013

Fits perfectly, easy to install and replace, and the price on Amazon is reasonable. We get great tasting water year round from our fridge - use two of these in a year - a bargain compared to buying water bottles, not to mention the decreased environmental foot print.

The design issue is with the unit shape and location of lights in that they are not shielded out of direct line of vision to the bulb. Light on the stove top is good but if the bonehead designer thinks that staring at a halogen bulb is stylish, they need more schooling in reality. The glare is very obnoxious even at my height of 5'10" so I can only imagine how upset a shorter person would be with it. I'll build my own glare shields from stainless steel to remedy this oversight on the part of their designers but very few people have the capability of doing this modification.

The build quality issue was with installation of the rivets in the back holding the leaf springs that retain the filters. title: Useful, but don't throw out your washing machine!
text:
My wife and I moved into a smaller apartment from a house (in which we had a washing machine), and thought this would be a perfect way for us to do laundry, save money (over the laundromat) and do a bit more for the environment.

It's not exactly as good as we expected and, as others have mentioned, it is very much an oversized salad spinner.

Pros:
--Easy to store in a small apartment
--Great arm workout
--Doesn't use much detergent or water
--Simple to use

Cons:
--Flecks of plastic often shred due to friction and get into the pod. Adding some oil helps, but it's not a permanent fix.
--"Ten Garments" is a lie. You might be able to get five pairs of adult socks in there with some room to spare, but good luck doing more than one pair of pants.
--Speaking of garments, you aren't getting much bigger than a pair of pants; I'm 6'2" with a 39 waist, and my pants barely fit. Most bigger things, like sheets or big towels, most likely won't work here.
--When spinning to drain, it goes off balance quit easily. I had two silk sari in one load and it kept falling off.
--Even with pre-soaking, soaking, and multiple washes, some stains won't come out of here.
--The mechanism to turn it pops off track far too often for my taste. I often have to lock everything back into place multiple times during a load of laundry.
--As you aren't getting the same agitation as a machine, you'll be soaking for a while, re-doing some clothing, or going over the clothing with a lint roller as some physical things will NOT come off (cat hair, general hair, the white plastic from the pod).

It's a useful device if you want an alternative of dealing with the laundromat and have the time to spare to do laundry, but it's not a final solution. I would still consider buying it again considering my situation, but it's FAR from the best way of doing things.

text:
I've had a couple of coffee presses but last week the glass broke in one of them because I was trying to pull the glass from the plastic holder and it shattered. I still have another coffee press but sometimes the grounds still get around the filter and end up in my cup. So I really wanted something different to use and when I saw this I knew I had to try it. I've now used this dripper to make several cups of coffee over the past couple of days and there have been no grounds in my coffee at all.

It's really easy to use, you jut have to be careful when pouring the hot liquid that you pour it slowly and use something where the water pours out smoothly otherwise you could burn yourself. I really like that I didn't have to use a paper filter with this and that unlike a french press, there aren't a lot of different parts to clean after using it.

Disclosure: I was given this product at a discount in exchange for an honest review.

UPDATE: So after using this coffee filter for a couple of months, it started clogging up to the point where the water won't even pour through it anymore. I cleaned it really good each time I used it. I cleaned it with vinegar and water and even tried baking soda and water. Nothing cleared it from being clogged once it was clogged. It only lasted about 2 months for me so therefore I am changing my star rating from a 5 to a 2. I've since thrown this away and pulled my coffee press back out of the closet.

title: A good fix for an old dryer
text:
This kit proved to be just what I needed to fix a dryer that was making a ridiculous amount of noise, for a fraction of the price of OEM replacement parts. The quality of the drum rollers seemed comparable to the ones I replaced. The replacement belt was, at least to visual inspection, a higher quality belt than the original OEM belt that I replaced. The idler pulley was slightly more narrow than the original, which from repair videos could be the result of a change in the design of the part -- there is a washer that is included with the kit that makes up for the difference in width.

I had some trouble with two of the tri-rings snapping during installation without the application of any more force than necessary to get them onto the shaft, which seemed to be a manufacturing issue. The OEM tri-rings were extremely tough,

If you have a dryer that is compatible with this kit, be aware that the model of your dryer may affect how easy (or difficult) it is to complete this repair. I have an early model of the dryer, for which the installation was more cumbersome than that shown in many of the videos for this family of dryers.

A side note about the dryer, as opposed to the kit: I have long known that the dryer model that I have has a poorly designed lint filter, but when I pulled apart the dryer to perform this repair I found the situation inside the dryer -- lint accumulation -- to be a lot worse than I had anticipated. If you complete this repair, I suggest taking the necessary time to get as much lint and dust as you can out of the interior of the dryer and to make sure that the vent is clear inside the dryer, from front to back, before reassembling. Lint is highly flammable, and a ten- to fifteen-year-old dryer had had a lot of time for lint build-up.

title: Too thick
text:
This dishwasher hose is difficult to bend in tight places such as under the sink. It's easy to kink because it's too thick and heavy for use as a simple discharge hose. But this is what has always been used, and things haven't changed in a hundred years.

Long ago virtually all discharge hoses were this type. Those used for washing machines have mostly been replaced with corrugated ones which are easier to bend. But dishwasher hoses need to fit snugly at both ends, so this is what we get. You might think with modern technology we could have thinner, more flexible ones. Instead we're stuck with this type, which is really designed for applications where high temperature and pressure are present, such as automotive radiators. Someone needs to start making flexible tubing with a 7/8" inside diameter. Surprisingly, no such thing exists!

I wonder whether I could use standard 3/4" transparent tubing, and push it over the ends tightly. After all, we're talking about a difference of only 1/8 of an inch. Maybe using a hair dryer to soften the end a bit. I'll have to give that a shot, because this hose sücks!

text:
These Napco built heaters are not all they may seem to be, Yesterday i had one fail a and nearly cause a fire, the screw which holds the porcelain insulator at the wire connectors worked loose and grounded with the lower high limit thermostat PART NO (3977767) this in turn caused the screw to weld to the thermostat causing a ground which eventually melted the top high limit thermostat PART N0 (279769) and the wiring.Whilst ground faults are common in worn out elements i have never seen a brand new element nearly start a fire, the element should be re-designed with the screw being replaced by a rivet.

I am a fully experienced technician with many years of experience, i wanted to share this information with other technicians to help avoid this potential danger in these elements.

We were really excited to upgrade our old dishwasher, and we looked around online quite a bit and then went to an appliance store and got the full schpiel about the Bosch. We probably didn't ask enough questions or look at enough reviews. I think it is hard to know what you will find a deal-breaker until you have it. We were told how great it was, how squeaky clean it gets everything without any rinsing, how wonderful it was to not have a heating element, and that the food trap was wonderful for any large pieces of food but that really 99% of all food would be disintegrated, and the only thing you might find is a piece of steak or something.

We had upgraded our kitchen in our last home and felt like we cheaped out a little on the dishwasher when we chose a GE Profile model. It actually did a very nice job, didn't have to rinse too much unless you had peanut butter on a spoon. It was relatively quiet, and had a heated dry cycle and therefore a heating element which I know is not most desirable but it got the dishes clean and dry and didn't take too long. It had a very nice rack layout and silverware tray. We moved to a new home that had an ancient dishwasher and we thought we would go big and get someone great.

This dishwasher is really disappointing. It doesn't get the dishes very clean, it SMELLS horrible after every wash, it doesn't have a heating element so it uses some kind of condensing dry which leaves the dishes wet forever, and the cycle is TWO hours! Yes it has a quick wash, but if they aren't coming out clean with the full wash why on earth would I use it. Yes, it is quiet. And yes we won't have any melted plastic due to no heating element. But I would trade this overpriced shiny imposter for my GE Profile in a minute. We are planning to return it.

title: Nice for cooking ... but with annoying electronics
text:
Positives: Everything in terms of cooking (i.e. baking, burner controls, etc.) works well. The stove looks pretty good. Have not tried the temp probe yet or the griddle. Oven heats quickly (but gives no feedback as to how fast it is heating).

Features requiring mastery: Every burner is a different size and has a different BTU rating ranging from simmer to monster. In my first week of use, apart from boiling water, everything was cooked a bit wrong -- too low, long, and dried out or too hot and a bit overcooked. "Medium" on one burner is not the same as any other burner. I think I will like this feature eventually but it requires getting some experience with the stove as well as care about the burner you pick. The griddle looks like it will be great but likely will also have a learning curve - and the same applies to the wok ring.

Minor Negatives: the display is too small to read unless you are right at the oven (e.g. the clock); as noted the glass panel collects fingerprints; the range feet do not adjust very much so the oven sticks up well over an inch above the counter top; fan is loud and it does not go off until it decides the oven is cool enough; warming drawer (which I mainly use for storage of pots and pans) is too shallow to hold much; the special 'simmer' burner is still too hot for delicate sauces but much better than my previous stove. My old stove showed the temperature as it was heating up so I could estimate when it would get to the correct temp. The Samsung simply says 'Preheating' until it finally gets to the temperature you set. It beeps when it gets to the temp but the beep can not be heard unless you are very close to the stove. The timer beep has the same low volume issue.

Bigger negative: Samsung support is pretty bad (see below) and the manual only describes the top level functions (e.g. bake, broil, convection bake, etc.) and does not completely describe how to set everything such as timed cooking, using the meat temp probe, or the great mystery of setting the three 'favorites.'

Worst negative: I bake a lot and proofing dough is an essential feature - and one of the reasons I bought this stove. Alas, you can not use the conventional controls for proofing - the minimum temperature is 175 degrees. You can only use the 'Healthy Choice #6' option which is a convection bake at 100 degrees. You can not set a start delay time nor can you set a stop time. This means it can not be used with frozen dough overnight nor can the oven proof for say, 2 hours and then bake for 1 hour. The 'Bread Proof' has to be turned off manually and then you have to set the baking options. My theory is the heating for proofing is electric rather than gas and all of the electronics only control the gas - but it is only a theory.

Samsung phone support took my name, phone number, issue, put me on hold to 'research the issue' (about proofing), disconnected me, and never called back. Samsung Chat support told me I could set the baking temp at 100 degrees. This would have solved my problem but it is not true - the minimum temp the stove allows is 175 degrees.

title: Has a lot of positives, but also a few negatives
text:
PROS:
-Outstanding build quality. Feels like it's worthy of the asking price.
-Looks very nice! Has a "professional" style handle which matches well with things like pro-style range, fridge, dishwasher, etc.
-Sliding shelves make it easy to get to things towards the back of the shelf.
-Gets down to 34 degrees quickly, and holds that temperature well.
-Has a nice slide-out wooden wine rack on the bottom which holds up to 10 bottles depending on the bottle width.

CONS:
-Shelves are NOT adjustable for height! This means if your items don't happen to fit on the pre-determined shelf heights then you're going to be restricted on what you can put on each shelf. There is a taller shelf on the bottom for water bottles or anything taller than a soda can, there is a second shelf which is exactly the height of a soda can, and the shelf on top on allows for things to be laid down.
-While the shelves do slide out, they are not full extension and only pull out about half way.
-The shelves are wire and the gaps between wires are fairly large, so if you have something that is either narrow (Izze, White Claw, etc) or doesn't have a flat bottom (pretty much any bottle) it's extremely hard to keep it standing upright. Things are constantly tipping over which drives me nuts.
-The LED light is very weak, it only illuminates the top shelf. It also doesn't turn on when the door opens, you need to manually turn it on. This means if you open the door in the dark you need to feel around for the button and hope you don't hit the temperature adjustment button.....which leads me to the next negative.
-There is only ONE button for temperature control, and it only goes up. So if you accidentally touch that button and raise the temp, you need to hit it 20-30 more times to go all the way to 64 degrees before it starts back over at 34 degrees. It's extremely irritating because it gets bumped all the time when feeling around for the light button in the dark. Why wouldn't they just put an up/down button like literally EVERY other mini fridge I've seen? So dumb.
-While it does get down to 34 degrees, the temperature varies widely by shelf. I placed a thermometer on each of different shelves while the fridge is full of beverages, and the temps ranged from 32-50 degrees depending on the shelf.
-It's fairly loud. The specs say 42dB, but I've tried other 42dB fridges and this one seems louder than most.

It's a shame that it has so many "big ticket" cons because like I said the build quality is outstanding, it keeps things super cold, and looks really nice. The non-adjustable wire shelves are the things that made me return it. I could have lived with everything else, but I can't live with my kids constantly tipping everything over and having to spend time every time I go to the fridge to stand things upright again.

title: Nicely shipped, attractive, odd shelves and a little lite on the cooling.
text:
This fridge came shipped in an outer carton with styrofoam lining with a retail box inside - unit arrived in perfect condition.

I like the looks of the unit - I bought this in opposition to a 'normal' mini fridge so it could hold more cans and bottles without a small freezer and useless door shelves taking up space that could otherwise been used to hold cans and bottles.

The wires on the shelves are a little far apart and have a tendency to make the cans or bottles tip or lean. This could lead to the contents spilling out or breaking. The shelf should have had a lip as to 'catch' roll-away bottles and can to prevent them from rolling onto the floor. Another review had some custom plexiglass cut and seems like a good solution - I will follow their lead - how ever I do not have that ability nor do I want to spend the money. I think I will use custom cut beer case cardboard to line the shelves. We'll see how that holds up to the humid summers.

Lastly - the other review seem to be wildly different on the actual cooling temperature.. I placed a fridge thermometer in the front center shelf and get reading that vary from 40° - 45° this is with the unit to the maximum cooling level. The unit is well ventilated at ½ capacity and out of direct sunlight - early March in Minnesota with an average house temperature of 65° and low humidity (dry winter air). What concerns me is when it starts to get hot outside and the temp in the house rises will this lil fridge keep up and still be able to keep the contents cool at below 45° (although I would prefer 35° - 38°). I am afraid it will not keep it at 45°.... Only time will tell.

A little experimentation will lead you to find the right stacking/loading that fits your needs. I keep bottles on the bottom most shelf laid horizontally cap towards the door - if you take from the top of the pile the bottles do not crash around too much. I have not has this unit too long as to find the correct loading solution for my needs yet.

I'll try to keep this updated as I continue to use this.

title: Hyped up salad spinner that makes disasters
text: Where shall I begin? It's made well. Sturdy enough. You can fit two shirts in it. Simple to use (on paper not in practice). Let me explain. I added the correct amount of water and soap. Added my two garments. Started spinning. Great, it's working... Then I noticed the harder I spun the higher the water level. OK, I drain some. Begin to spin again and the same issue occurs. At this point water has gone up and leaked out of the lid. Now the counter is wet. I continue to spin. The whole apparatus is now moving all over the counter. So I unsuction it, wipe the counter down and the suction cups and proceed to drain and refill with fresh water in order to rinse the clothes. Well, this is where the same issue occurs. I'm now soaked as is most of my RV kitchen. Dump the water and proceed to move on to the spin dry portion of this nightmare. I have the drain open I start spinning fast. Water is draining out. Wonderful. As I continue to spin  the suction  cups start migrating all over th countertop again as somehow water got out  and made the  counter wet. I hung onto the thing for dear life while spinning it to ring out the clothes. The entire RV is shaking now (the neighbors must have had ideas of other activities going on) approximately a cup of water is rung out of the clothes and I proceed to hang up two shopping wet shirts in the shower which took two days to dry. Lesson? Unless you want to pretend your stirring a giant bowl you can barely grip full of earthquakes and octopus to create a saturated half washed clothes cake, only to create a second load of laundry in the form of every towel you own to sop up the mess...do not buy this thing. Just don't do it. Trust me.

title: Consider yourself WARNED: CUSTOMER SERVICE WILL BURN YOU
text:
So we ordered the flex wash washer and dryer, and after set up tried to run our first cycle of the washing machine. The machine lost all power shortly after starting up. Now queue the samsung customer service nightmare.
Day 1: called samsung customer service (on a wednesday) and was told we couldn't get a technician out to look at the machine until next tuesday.
Over the next two weeks, i have had to wait for 5 service appointments, arranging schedules to be available, I have spent at least 15 hours telling the same story to Samsung customer service, and have gotten nowhere.
Two weeks later: after 5 service calls from technicians with no solution, during which time Samsung refused to assist us with a replacement or refund, we still have a non-functioning machine. Samsung customer support insists that they require some form 7000 from the service technician. However, Samsung won't facilitate this project so i am essentially attempting to act as a general contractor between Samsung and its own service technicians. While the technician acknowledges the machine is a total lemon, Samsung technical support refuses to accept this conclusion and is advising continued service calls.
So ESSENTIALLY, SAMSUNG REFUSES TO ACKNOWLEDGE AFTER FIVE VISITS THAT THEIR MACHINE IS BROKEN AND AGREE TO REPLACE, but instead prefers to hold on to my money while it tries to salvage its broken product.

SO, if you are willing to gamble never getting what you pay for, then this machine is perfect for you, otherwise, I strongly advise you do not purchase any Samsung products.

title: The product was listed as in stock when ordered but never arrived
text:
I wrote and corresponded twice with the seller to make sure the item indeed was in stock and would be shipped on time prior to Thanksgiving (since it is a probe that I wanted to use with my oven for a turkey especially.) I was met with responses that said that the probe would even arrive early. Then after sending an e-mail thanking them in advance for sending it and stating that it was just ordered (this all was the same day), I received an e-mail the following day stating it was not in stock and a refund would be issued. I was charged for it when I ordered it (as is protocol so I was told by Amazon too.)
Then I received an e-mail stating it was shipped hours later...so I corresponded once more with the seller and was told, "I accidentally hit the "ship" button instead of the refund, but the item has been refunded and should show up soon on my account. I did call Amazon too, but this was the vendor. Oddly Amazon sends me e-mail, constantly asking me to review the item I never did receive, so I am writing this. I did get the refund as promised, but I really was disappointed that it was listed on stock for a week and still was just after I received the e-mail that said it was not in stock...until I wrote again. They then updated the Amazon ad. I guess it has to do with the vendor, not the product. I did locate one after a couple of months and it is a remake of a GE part, not the original. The probe is shorter but not much, and it's otherwise identical. I believe the company makes GE parts that GE no longer makes...so most likely they all get them from the same GE supplier...even GE does, where I eventually got the part...after being told it was no longer manufactured but would be in the future...They kept my phone number and called me when they located one...in time for Christmas.

title: Pump works, rest of the assembly not so much....
text:
I was told this was an exact replacement for my Whirlpool Duet drain pump assembly. It does appear very similar but a few issues exist. Ultimately, I removed the new pump and installed it on my old drain assembly and in the end I have a functional unit.

Cons
1. the feet that slide into the bottom slots to anchor the assembly in place do not match up with the existing slots (the feet are clearly wider apart than the original part). This is a problem because it will shake when the pump is running and make noise or even worse, loosen the hose connections over time.
2. The plastic catch drain section (the half opposite the motor assembly) had a pin-hole leak. It was driving me insane and I have no idea why it was like that. I don't know if it was defective or if it is a poorly designed vent of some kind. Regardless, after securing the in/out hoses to the assembly, there was a small trickling leak coming from the middle of the plastic assembly itself, not from the hoses or their connections.

Pros
1. Great price. This assembly with the motor is $130 locally.
2. The pump itself is fine and has been working properly since installation.

title: Stay away!
text:
Have model NXRPRO3651 for little over 2 years. Excellent initially become pain in the neck : within this 2 years 2 igniters failed (one replaced under the warranty, 3 top burners (I have dual burners model with ultra low simmer) warped and have flames coming from under the burner, inner burners have unstable flames (too much air flow cause flames to shut down or flatter and igniters to try to ignite the flames ) that will work at low set only. From research I found out that burners getting warped and this cause for the problem. One of the greatest become warped too, so pot placed in it unstable and may be a safety concern due to possible water splash on the burners. title: Generates ice fairly slowly, and the ice melts quickly because the ice compartment isn't insulated or cooled.  Needs insulation.
text: This little ice maker does a decent job of making ice, but it's not insulated in such a way that the ice compartment stays cold.  I bought this new and set it up in my kitchen with an average room temperature.  I let it run, and by the time the basket had finished filling with ice, the first dozen ice cubes had already melted back into the water repository.  On a warm day in a trailer, which is what I actually bought it for, your ice would melt before the second batch of ice dropped.  I wanted to use this to keep the ice in my cooler fresh when out camping for extended camping trips, running it off generator or solar panel power.  But it's just not designed for that.  If you pulled the ice out immediately after each batch dropped and put it into your cooler, it might work okay.  They should have insulated the ice compartment from the internal mechanics which generate a lot of heat, and they should have insulated the compartment and door from the outside, creating a cooler compartment for the ice.  It generates ice at a moderate speed, but you can't just leave it for an hour in a warm environment and come back to a compartment full of ice.  And of course, I didn't return it fast enough because I was on a long road trip, so I'm stuck with it.

title: It worked great - for a while
text:
We installed the Fiber Optic unit in our vacation home in May of 2012. October of 2013 - walking into the house after not being there for a month - the garbage disposal is running by itself. After ensuring the fiber cable had not pulled loose and was still tight into the button, I just unplugged the unit. After plugging it back in later, it seemed OK, but then 12 hours later it just kicked on by itself again while we were watching TV. After talking to Waste King, they recommended trying to replace the switch - which I did for $32. It was OK after replacing the switch for almost a day when it just turned itself on again. They now recommend replacing my base unit, not under warranty any longer, of course, for another $90. If I was sure this one would be any better, I would do it in a heartbeat before I burn up my garbage disposal. Wish I would have installed the Air Switch instead - half the price and the last two houses I have had used them with zero problems. Now to install one, I need to drill a larger hole in the granite, which is not an easy job for your typical homeowner. I don't just happen to have a 1 3/8" diamond hole saw sitting in my toolbox.

Great idea on the switch - love the look and the concept - loved the switch while it worked right, but this seems to be a common problem, based on some of the other reviews on here after a year or two of owning. Twice the cost to buy initially and even more if you have to replace the Base Unit every couple of years.

title: Overpriced, Flimsy Polycarbonate Dome, Temperature Max of 333 degrees.
text:
We've been using it for 18 weeks now (8/1/11), ~ once/day. All parts are washed in a DW, maybe once a week. Cooks slower than advertised. Cooks anything from frozen (vegetables, chicken, steaks, ribs) with superb results. Five stars absolutely. Why did I rate it two stars? It's flimsy, but not inexpensive. The dome is already cracked from the base flange upwards several inches, but still under warranty, so I'll replace it. But why did it crack? It's handled with great (really) care, like a good digital camera, but it still cracked... and the dome now looks mottled and dirty even coming out of the DW. I understand why the competing Superwave is made from glass... The Superwave (which I returned) is just too big, and the NuWave Mini is just too cheap IMHO.

Soooo, we'll replace the dome and continue using it. However, if you really look at it with a dispassionate eye, you'll probably agree that it's really just an inverted electric hotplate with a fan and a digital touch pad. I suspect that the manufacturing cost is around five bucks... maybe. It's just not worth its presently advertised price - to me even a $29.95 price point would be a bit high for the quality of this Mini model. There's just not that much to it. I also suspect that these Mini models are used much more frequently than the larger NuWave models. They're incredibly convenient. If that's true, the Mini needs to be more robust, unless a product cycle of 8-12 months is the goal.

ADDENDUM - 12-7-13 - The second dome also disintegrated. A new one will cost $23.93 with shipping.

text:
All three replacement filters from FiltersFast exhibit issues. Poor water flow and squeal from inside the fridge. Replaced new filter with old one and all is fine. New filters are different on the insert - old ones had one large hole with multiple tiny holes around it. New ones have one large hole and two slotted holes on each side. All three new ones are lousy. Takes 45-60 seconds to fill a standard 8oz glass. Not acceptable. Called GE directly who said no change has been made to product line. Bought two more in town, one from Sears, another from HH Gregg. Both have the same design as the new ones from FiltersFast and are also lousy.

I have resorted to using the filter plug in order to have decent water flow. The filter design has obviously changed and either GE is not admitting to it or their representatives are ignorant to the change.

I hate my fridge now and currently using a Brita pitcher filter on the counter top. Neither Filtersfast, Sears or HH Gregg will accept a return. I'm now a proud owner of six new filters, over $200 in cost, that won't work worth a flip. Oh, and those of you who want to repeat what GE told me over the phone - yes, both the old filter with the tiny holes and the bypass plug work fine. There is NO clog in the water line. It's the lousy new filters that GE is pushing to all the vendors.

title: It's not about the pod, it's about the plastic
text: Here's the thing. The problem with recycling k-cups is that the plastic itself is rarely recyclable. Unless the plastic is stamped with the triangular recycling symbol with a number in the center, it is a composite of different plastics that is very difficult to recycle and is not acceptable at most recycling centers. The maker of this device seems to think the cups are #7 class of recyclables, but that is not the case. Keurig has begun to introduce a line of recyclable plastic pods, but most are still unsuitable. So if you want to make seed starters or craft projects with the cups, this gadget would be fine. Otherwise, look for pods with the recycling mark on them. One source is intelligentblends.com. The pods are #5 plastic and the foil lids have a tab to simplify removal.

title: Wish I Didn't buy this annoying POS
text:
My old admiral washer finally gave it up after 10 years. It was a simple basic model where you select load size, temp and style of washing and pretty much that's it. These new appliances are so ridiculous with all of their useless ineffective overpriced features that most people will never even have a use for. This model is no exception even though I was trying to find something with large capacity but not too many bells and whistles.
I have had this for less than 4 months and already I notice it doesn't work properly. After setting up a small to medium load of clothes I walk away thinking it is doing its thing only to find out when I come back an hour later that it is still on load size sensing mode (a stupid feature that would be ok if it actually worked) and the clothes are sitting in a puddle but not even close to being covered. I go old school and walk back and forth a 4 or 5 times with souppot loads of water to help get the level up to where it should be and then lo and behold it decides to help me a little tiny bit more after closing the lid for the last time. Then it goes about washing.
So let's see, how many features? 4 soil levels, 5 temp 12 wash styles, most of which u will never use, 4 rinse choices and a presoak.
Lipstick on a sick pig.
All of these new appliances, washers fridges,stoves, etc, with all these computerized features are often just total crap that fail prematurely costing the consumer grief and wanted money
