title: TERRIBLE PRODUCT; TERRIBLE COMPANY; AVOID / AVOID / AVOID
text:
This is absolutely one of the worst consumer products ever made and the company that makes this product has no regard for their customers at all.

We purchased this oven as a birthday gift for me back in September of 2011. Within less than 1 year, the back control panel started to warp and within a few weeks of it beginning to warp, about half of the buttons quit working. Fortunately we were still within the one year warranty period, but it still was like pulling teeth to get Frigidaire/Electrolux to come our and fix their garbage designed appliance. So finally, they came out and replaced the entire board and key pad........

.........and then about 10 months later THE EXACT SAME THING HAPPENED AGAIN! Only this time, the range was more than one year old. Frigidaire/Elextrolux didn't care. They were, in fact, quite rude on the phone.

......so for the last few years, we have been able to turn the oven on and keep limping along, but to turn the oven off, we have to go to the garage and turn the oven off at the breaker. This is incredibly unsafe. It blows my mind that such a product would even be allowed to exist on the market. Government has failed us too. We have reported the issue to the CPSC and nothing but crickets......I guess someone will have to die or get seriously injured for Frigidaire / Elextrolux or the federal government to care. What a sad, sad world it is that we live in.

I don't know how in the world the executive leadership, shareholders or anyone associated with this company sleeps at night knowing darn good and well that they make dangerous products that could seriously injure or kill someone. My husband is an Engineer and he says without a doubt that the product has a design flaw related to the build up of heat in front of the control panel and the quality of the laminates and adhesives used to make the control panel cannot withstand the temperatures. Its very telling that Frigidaire has now discontinued making the larger display panels........because they know they have a serious design flaw with their product.

Now, just 3 days ago, we cant even get the oven to turn on....it is completely broken and the cost to replace the damaged part is $200.....I feel so used and betrayed by this company. We cannot afford to go and by another, but we cant afford to go and by a $200 part that we know will fail in less than one year.

Does anybody who works for Frigidaire / Elextrolux have a conscious? Does any one at that company care about the mental anguish and suffering that they inflict upon other human beings? This was supposed to be a happy birthday gift for me and it has turned into a nightmare.

Thanks a lot Frigidaire / Elextrolux. I will never never never by a product made by your company as long as I live and I will always tell my friends or anyone else looking for appliances of how bad an experience I had.. not just with the product itself, but with the company that sells it.

title: Great little machine, & tips for new users
text:
Don't expect it to perform, overall, like a full size washer, because it isn't. But it does wash clothes and bedding well (the agitation function works very well), and gets them clean. Just make sure you don't overload it, and fill it with enough water per load, so it can do its job.

Too bad the container for spinning the water out of your laundry is smaller than the container for washing, which means you have to leave some of your sopping wet laundry in the washer side, while you spin what can fit into the side that spins off the water. Then do the same for your remaining (wet) laundry,

The water intake hose that's included probably won't fit your faucets. As with many others, it didn't fit mine either, so I have to fill it by hand, using a bucket or pots full of water.

If you have a hand-held shower attachment and a bathtub, that will probably work well, but I don't.

It will smell like plastic when you first get it, as others have commented. I put a combo of water and white vinegar in the first wash, and that helped, as well as letting it air out for the first 24 hours.

If you're washing towels, clothes, or, anything that is likely to have a lot of lint in it, for the first time, I advise you first use a full size washer so the lint can drain out well. The washing tub isn't big enough, and doesn't allow for enough water, for this to happen.

These are the things I'd have liked to have known before making the purchase, but I have to say that even so, it really is a great little washing machine, and I'm quite happy with it.

title: Falsely advertised
text: The picture on the web shows a design with corners adjusted closely (~2 inches). This suggests from which point the base may be adjusted to accommodate a portable appliance/washer, such as a Panda. In fact, when mounted with all four corners of the base in place, the space in-between the bars (which are soft and cheap) are longer with approximately 6 inches (or more) between each corner -- limiting how far the unit can be adjusted in. Consequently -- the unit can only be adjusted to accommodate the washer's width. The rest sticks out and the appliance easily slides through and tips and the washer is unstable. The description and illustrations are inaccurate. Alterations of the unit (which seem necessary to accommodate the Panda portable washers I have) should not be necessary and could result in safety issues and further problems with the design. title: good product, dreadful customer service
text:
This is rewrite of my original review. I originally rated the spin dryer 1-star because I couldn't get it to spin, and the company's customer service is absolutely dreadful.

In googling the company, I happened upon their Better Business Bureau (BBB) page. BBB gives the company a rating of "F" (Fail) due to multiple complaints, mostly about poor customer service. I, too, have experienced their terrible customer service, but - ironically - I also found the solution to my spin dryer problem in a company response to a complaint on the BBB page.

There is a metal bar screwed into the bottom of the spin dryer. It's not documented anywhere (not in the manual, or on the product page on their Web site), but it's a motor lock, and you have to unscrew and remove it or the spin dryer won't work. I'm just glad I didn't try it too many times with the motor lock on - that likely would have damaged it.

This is a company with good products, and just about the worst customer service and product documentation I've ever experienced (especially from a company with good products). They are very hard to get hold of. They do not always answer their phone during their stated business hours, and they do not answer email. When you are able to reach them by phone, the person answering speaks such poor English it's almost impossible to communicate. It's a 3-person company: the owner (who the woman answering phones never lets you speak to - "he's too busy"), the warehouse manager (who sent me incorrect tracking numbers for both items I ordered), and the woman answering the phone, who has a very heavy Asian accent, and does not speak or understand fluent English.

Their bad customer service wouldn't be such a liability if their documentation weren't so dangerously insufficient. I can't fathom how they could print a manual for this spin dryer without the instruction to remove the motor lock on the bottom. I saw the metal bar on the bottom, but I had no idea what it was, or that I should remove it. Their Wonder Wash machine (very cleverly designed) also has insufficient documentation. The assembly instructions are incomplete. I was able to figure it out, but some people can't (see the reviews for that product).

All that said, the spin dryer does work very well, and I'm glad I have it. But it was a stressful few hours until I figured out why it wouldn't spin (with no help from the company). Some people on the BBB site say the company honors their warranties, some say they don't. I'm glad I didn't have to test that.

title: Good, but...
text:
Ekobrew (brown) Review:

Pros:
I like it. It's definitely better than the one that Keurig makes which removes the entire housing just so you can brew your own coffee. This makes it that much faster for easy fill, drop, and brew.
Easy clean up, no nipple at the bottom to try and dig coffee grinds out of.

Cons:
This will not fit any of the commercial Keurig brewers. (B30, B130, B150, & B155)
I searched around and could not find anyone that found a suitable mod to make this work.
The issue is the bottom needle for the commercial brewers being 1/8th too far from the edge to make this fit.

I purchased the ekobrew in hopes that I could use it for when I'm at work, but unfortunately for me, my company just purchased the B150. Instead I plan on getting the Solofill cup because at least that (despite the tough cleanup of the bottom nipple) can be modded with a simple gasket/o-ring to fit in the commercial brewers.

Ekobrew (Stainless) Review:
UPDATE Nov 11, 2013: I had to update my review on this product because for some reason, the Stainless version is considered the same as the plastic one so I could not submit a separate review.
I had to purchase a new one because my original (brown) Ekobrew had seen some very good use and wear & tear.

Pros:
Same as the plastic version.
Additionally, this appears to be more durable (obviously it's steel) and the hinge is metal as well. So there's no chance of the cap eventually breaking off.
Also, the steel will help prevent the mis-seating of the cup int he Keurig and the potential of puncturing the cup from the needle.

Cons:
Same as the plastic version.
Additionally, I think it could use more perforation. Even after filling the cup properly and making sure the seal is tight, you will still see over spill when brewing your coffee. I tried this with fine & course ground beans as well as filling it half way to see if it still spilled. No matter what, it spilled over. Not a complete issue since the spill over trickled into my mug and the only clean up was wiping down the Keurig, but still an issue.

I started to clean out old V-Cups and refill them with our favorite coffee. Done right you get a good cup and not a lot of sediment, but it's certainly not convenient and it does little to avoid the waste problem. This is a problem that could easily be solved by someone making paper filters for the V1 or some competing plastic housing. If you open a V-Cup it's well designed and has a paper filter for the brewing portion and one at the top to prevent grounds from blowing up into the water jet. Come on Kuerig! title: Very disappointed with these filters
text:
I purchased these for a new Cuisinart coffee maker and decided that I could save myself some money by buying these off-brand replacement filters. How much different could they be? I mean, it's activated charcoal and a filter with the same shape as the Cuisinart brand. But I was wrong.

Before replacing the filter, you're supposed to soak the activated charcoal filter in water for a few minutes. For whatever reason, the filter simply wouldn't saturate and floated on the surface of the water. I tried to hold it under water with a weight, but it never seemed to soak up the water as the original filters do. Then you're supposed to rinse them under running water to flush out the charcoal before using for the first time.

The filter snaps into a plastic rod and fit perfectly, but again, it wouldn't saturate with water, so every morning when I pour in the water to make a pot of coffee, the filter and the rod float up to the top. I have to push it back down and quickly close the lid of the coffee maker to keep it in place.

I thought that maybe I simply had a bad one, but the other two I've tried are doing exactly the same thing. I'm not sure why this is, but I would avoid purchasing this brand and either go with the original or look for another brand. I assume it actually works as it's supposed to, but honestly, who knows?

I always appreciate thoughtful, honest reviews and I hope you find my review helpful and insightful.

title: overpriced
text:
This is a polyphosphate cartridge. Practically, it cannot "filter" the scale-causing minerals from the water, as there is far too much volume of minerals to hold in the tiny cartridge. Instead, the cartridge releases a small amount of polyphosphates into the water. Those chemicals inhibit the formation of the scale -- in simple terms, they keep the minerals suspended in the water and inhibit them from forming the white deposits. Of course, the minerals have to go somewhere, and they can't stay suspended indefinitely as they won't evaporate as steam. Some of the mineral material inevitably forms scale, while the rest is flushed out of the humidifier tank in the flush cycle (which is frequently problematic on the troublesome TrueSteam humidifiers). So the polyphosphates released by this cartridge help to inhibit scale by keeping the minerals suspended until they get flushed.

Now that you understand how it works, you can go get a standard 1/4" quick-connect, in-line polyphosphate scale-inhibiting filter that's twice the size for half the price. Either way, you can only expect it to last about 6 months. The polyphosphates used in these filters are "food grade" and considered acceptable for whole-house use, including drinking water (although there's no benefit for drinking). Polyphosphates are sometimes used in lieu of water softeners.

title: Got despite the reviews and am pleased I did, works great for dishes
text:
This and all the similar gadgets have some pretty bad reviews but I was desperate and don't want to spend $400 on a counter top dishwasher right now. So I took a chance, not expecting much and this turned out to be a good decision.

I filled the container I have with a bunch of small but very dirty food cups. These things take forever to scrub by hand and still come out feeling not fully clean so I've just been letting all dishes pile up. This is a great time saver. It somehow does work to do the heavy scrubbing for you.

You need to rinse them after, obviously the water doesn't get magically clean that they wash in. Some need a light wipe down as well, especially if it's a item that got nestled in another. But this is tons better than the intense scrubbing I would have had to do.

My second load was a bunch of plastic containers and lids. It worked well but they tended to nestle together a bit more than the cups. Washing none fitting together items obviously will work better. Like your dinner dishes.

I also threw a dirty metal dog bowl in. It got it clean of food but did not remove the calcification from past hardwater use, which I didn't expect it to but seems worth mentioning.

Bonus it also deodorizes the plastics even ones I could not get smell out of by soaking and scrubbing before.

The only down side I have is the suction cups just aren't strong enough. The vibrations make it slowly move to the top and I need to rush over to push it back down to stop water splashing. I will try to find a solution, maybe a giant clamp.

It is also noisy but it's not terrible.

I have not used for clothes since I do not need it for that. I was also very liberal with the dish soap and used only hot water. This still did way more than soaking without the washer in it ever has.

So recap is if you only need to lightly wash dishes then this may not be for you since you still need to rinse and sometimes lightly wipe the dishes. However if you need to really scrub and deep clean things then this is great and saves time. Does the major work, removes odor and did also get rid of any greasy feeling.

Tips. Be liberal with the soap so it really suds up and use hot water. Don't go to big with the container. You may need to find a better way to keep the washer in place on the side.

I DID try holding one of the cut pieces under a flame to see what would happen. It didn't catch fire, but it definitely was burning, and if it is Teflon coated, you don't want that under the flame for very long. I'm sure that the brief second when the burner ignites and there is a bit of a billowing of flame that may touch the edges is fine. But if it slips and gets too close, you could be releasing some nasty stuff into the air. So it is also probably best to err on the side of caution and cut the center hole bigger than you want. Better to have a small ring of spatter that you may have to clean up than to have these burn.

title: Pancaked in under 6 months
text:
Buy the hockey pucks instead. We installed two sets of these under our nice front load set and at first they did very well at eliminating some serious vibration. But recently vibrations gradually returned to almost as bad as before. I inspected the pads and it was obvious they had pancaked. When we removed them and replaced them with the highest quality hockey puck feet we could find, I found that these feet had smushed their structure so only ~1/4in of rubber was left and had formed tears. The rubber is permanently damaged. This same damage was found with the dryer pads too, which is about the same weight as a cheap washing machine. I don't recommend this product for a washing machine, but other antivibration applications like speakers would probably work very well.

For anyone curious, we replaced these pads with the big hockey picks that have the honeycomb pattern in the foot cavity and on the bottom that are advertising no foul smell. I can confirm those have no smell like the other hockey pucks. They work very well and are solid rubber so I expect them to hold up very well.

title: Great features, easy to adjust and personalize, dissappointing accuracy and minor problems with power adaptor.
text:
This weather station has great features, it may require some adjustments to calibrate the factory settings. It took me several days to calibrate the temperature display (need to keep in mind the specifications state a + or - 2% tolerance), I would have preferred a closer tolerance. It is not difficult to calibrate but the unit needs time to stabilize, I would make an adjustment and 8 hours later it was off again. Make the adjustments in small increments or decrements and it will be easier.
The color changes on the display are very useful since they provide an indication from far away even if the display is not readable, with a quick glance the color indicates the temperature range outdoors. However, I am disappointed with the communication range from the remote unit, in Florida most homes use CBS construction and it seems the signal is not strong enough, my outdoors sensor could not be placed any farther than about 30 feet to work properly.
The quality on the console is very good and have not had any problems with is in almost 30 days of use, however the power adaptor for the AC worked quietly for only 4 days, after that it developed a 60HZ hum which has increased over time and becomes very annoying. The unit will work without the AC power with the batteries but if you use the backlight it will run the batteries down quickly. I have contacted the manufacturer and requested a replacement for the adaptor, I will have a follow up to report how this went.

text:

title: Terrific beverage fridge
text:
This fit into an existing space I just perfectly. It's 14.9" wide which was great in my case since I had about 15.25" of space. It fit with enough clearance all around. Fit better than the shorter fridge I replaced actually.

It is quiet too! Much quieter than my old beverage fridge and also quieter than the wine fridge I have. I was very impressed by how quiet it is.

It has shelves that you can position in a few spots that slide out, with a stopper. Along with the shelves having a lip in the front. This was really nice as you can put soda cans in without worrying about them rolling out and you can pull the drawer out to reach things.

I ended up zip tying some wood blocks to the back of the shelves so that cans wouldn't get pushed all the way back, blocking the fans or the exhaust. If you put cans in with the opening of the cans facing outward, you can't fit 4 anyway. So this helps keep the space clear in the back and it's not otherwise used. Maybe if you put cans the other way, you could fit more, but I'd rather ensure good air flow.

The shelves aren't designed to help here. So you will need to be careful not to block the exhaust or the fans.

Really happy with the fridge on day two here. Only thing that would make me unhappy I think now is if the thing got noisy later or died too soon. Not going to be able to know that for a while.

text:
I have a mixed review here. As far as fit, function and appearance it is top notch and really dressed up our aging RV kitchen. Based on this, my rating would be 5 stars.
With that said, there is a signifcant safety issue. The stainless sheet metal it's made with is very thin, possibly even 24 or 26 gauge, which means that any unfinished edge is quite literally equal to being a razor blade. The seams between the top and the sides have a very slight mismatch leaving that edge to project and so as I reached into the cupboard yesterday I effortlessly sliced off the top 1/16" or so of my knuckle as I brushed against it. (There was a lot of blood)
I plan to bring home an angle grinder and a flap disc designed for stainless steel to try and smooth these edges a little; and I hope that I don't damage the finish too much in the process.
So, for this reason I give it 3 stars as most buyers will not have access to such resources.

title: NOT COMPATIBLE with Hamilton Beach FlexBrew
text:
One of the images in the description clearly shows a Hamilton Beach FlexBrew unit as being a compatible pod brewer. It's actually not!

The problem is that the needle, which normally pokes through a foil membrane on a normal plastic pod and delivers the hot water to the coffee in the pod, is physically stopped by the little blue plastic shield, which in turn prevents the coffee maker's lid from closing... which of course means the coffee maker is not going to make coffee. The only foreseeable way to remedy this would be to break off the blue plastic shield, but I'm not going to modify something like that, when I could just return it and try to get something that does work.

Adding to this, the gaskets for the lids definitely do not look like they would last long. They're only there to keep the lid in place, and not to create any kind of seal. However, the gasket material is some cheap gummy plastic, akin to the little adhesive boogers found in junk mail, except without the sticking power. Other reviews have pointed out problems with the lids not consistently staying in place, and now I can see why up close.

title: It works, but coffee is mediocre and machine vibrates heavily and creates very lound noise
text:
The good news is, this capsule is recognized by Nespresso Vertuo (first generation) machine and one can make coffee with it. The quality of coffee is a little better than from a mocha pod, but much worse than when one uses original Nespresso capsules. In most cases, it is much more watery. I experimented with different settings of the grinder, it seems that one does not need the finest (espresso) grind, something between espresso and medium works better, but still, taste is not the same and crema consistency and texture is worse (crema is less dense and more bubbly).
The bad news is that this capsule is very difficult to fill to keep it evenly balanced. If you spin unbalanced capsule, it vibrates and the whole machine vibrates like my old washing machine. From maybe 40-50 cups of coffee which I made using this capsule so far, only 2-3 were brewed without excessive vibrations of the machine. - still noisier than with original capsules, but at least, not violently to think that the coffee machine may explode. Most of the time, when the capsule spins in the machine, it vibrates heavily, creates very loud noise like an airplane, and one has to hold the cup in place because it tries to "walk" from vibrations like old generation washing machines.
I opened a not-brewed original capsule of Nespresso and found that coffee in the capsule was pretty loose. Hence, tamper included in the kit is not needed for Nespresso! Actually, vibration gets a little less, although does not disappear, if one just taps the capsule against the table to let coffee redistribute itself in the capsule. Also, coffee quality is better without tampering. If this is the case, why the tamper is included, why do we pay for what makes Nespresso coffee worse (note, nespresso uses a different principle than espresso machines, it does not push hot water through coffee at high pressure, it uses the forces generated when capsule spins to get water through, so one can speculate that water might not be pushed through too densely packed coffee grinds), and why there are no instructions how to use it to get at least a decent quality coffee?
I guess, I got my money worth after making like 50 cups of coffee with it, and it did not break down my machine as of yet (although the force of vibrations makes me think it is possible that it would eventually break from vibrations), but after multiple tries I ended up buying Nespresso original capsules again because coffee from this capsule, honestly, sucks.

This little washer has been a life safer for a friend who lives on a fixed income and has developed continence issues. The complex coin laundry costs $3.25 a load to wash and dry. Just remember to keep the doors open otherwise the washer will start to have a mildew smell. He uses this washer 99% of the time instead of using the commercial coin washer in his building. I recommended using a scent booster such as Gain so his clothes always have a nice scent to them.

title: This product works fine, but after having used them they defeat the ...
text:
This product works fine, but refilling the pods and disposing of the spent grounds defeats the purpose of having a pod coffee maker.
Use a quality coffee to refill the pods, Use an espresso grind. Lavazza espresso is the best relatively inexpensive coffee. Sorry Starbucks, but your coffee doesn't cut it. I wish it did, but it just doesn't.

You will want a flat bottomed spoon to fill the pods with coffee. You will want to compress it lightly, but do not fill the pod all the way to the top of the pod. Some space is needed when you spin it up. If overfilled the machine will make awful sounds and the coffee will come out horrid.
Center the cap over the pad and using just your fingers lightly cramp on the cap then use your fingernail to press the camp into where the outer rim and the flat surface encircling the coffee and then use your fingers to fold the cap around the outer edges.\It's simple once you get used to it.

Use the same pod over and over. It makes it easy once you get one stripped of the old cover.
I suggest that you still buy official Nespresso pods from time to time as well, but the equivalent cost of around $70/lb I won't blame anybody for using these refill capsules exclusively.

title: Easy enough to replace
text:
Our Affinity front load washer kept flashing the error code "dr" and beeping 4 times. It did this over and over as long as the power was plugged in. Other online forums say you should replace the door lock mechanism which I did. But when I plugged it back in, the problem came back.

THE TRICK that worked is: you have to break rule number one for working with electrical things and leave the power plugged in! Then open the door and peel back the rubber seal/boot. (You may need to remove a spring loaded metal ring that's hidden inside the groove of the seal.)
Then reach inside to the right. Find the door lock mechanism. Unplug the bottom connector. (The one to the wax motor.) You will hear a clunk sound. The dr code will change to something like "18h" and the darn beeping will STOP. Wait a few seconds. Plug it back in. You'll hear another sound.

If you have long skinny arms, you might be able to do this by sliding off the top of the washer and reaching in.

This won't fix all problems of course, but it's a cheap and easy thing to try before replacing parts.

title: It's Quick and Easy but the Ice just isn't Icey enough.
text:
Pros:
Makes ice in 6 minutes
Produces up to 26 pounds of ice per day
Self-cleaning
Two ice cube sizes
Compact and portable

Cons:
LOUD
Ice is not very frozen and melts quickly
Water reservoir is small
No water filter

Overall, the Silonn Ice Maker Countertop is a good option for those who need a small, portable ice maker. It makes ice quickly and easily, and the self-cleaning feature is a nice bonus. However, the ice is not very frozen and melts quickly, which may be a dealbreaker for some users.

I would give the Silonn Ice Maker Countertop 3.5 out of 5 stars. It is a good product, but there are some minor flaws that prevent it from being a top-rated choice.

Here are some additional details about the product:

The ice maker is small and compact, measuring 12.3 x 8.7 x 12.5 inches. It weighs 12.3 pounds, so it is easy to move and store.
The water reservoir holds 2 liters of water. This is enough to make about 120 ice cubes.
The ice maker has a self-cleaning function that runs automatically every 24 hours. This helps to prevent the build-up of bacteria and mold.
The ice maker can produce two different sizes of ice cubes: small and large.

Overall, the Silonn Ice Maker Countertop is a good option for those who need a small, portable ice maker. It makes ice quickly and easily, and the self-cleaning feature is a nice bonus. However, the ice is not very frozen and melts quickly, which may be a dealbreaker for some users.

title: JUNK.....COMPANY AND PRODUCT
text:
[[VIDEOID:cfbc67f64aa9aad96ac8f496d55fec20]] UPDATE: 6/02/2014

i HAVE FILED A COMPLAINT AGAINST THE MAKER OF THIS PRODUCT. I WAS SENT 3 LEMONS.... 2 MOTOR ISSUES, 1 WITH A BROKEN BOTTOM. THE OHIO ATTORNEY GENERAL SHOULD BE GETTING TO THEM ABOUT A REFUND, EXCHANGE, DIFFERENT MODEL WITH A DISCOUNT, ETC. "SEPGO UNITED" HAS A GRADE "F" FOR THE WEBSITE. I ADVISE YOU DO YOUR RESEARCH BEFORE PURCHASING. I AM A TOTALLY UNSATISFIED CUSTOMER. 3 LEMONS MADE NO BELIEVER OF ME, IN THIS PRODUCT. ITS JUNK, PLAIN AND SIMPLE!!!!! THE VIDEO SHOWS THE WASHER AGITATING IN ONLY 1 DIRECTION. IT IS TO GO BOTH CLOCKWISE AND COUNTER-CLOCKWISE. NOTE THAT IT DOES NOT. THE WASHER IS ONLY 3 MONTHS OLD, AND IS MY 3RD FROM SEPGO UNITED. THE COMPANY IS NOT WILLING TO WORK WITH ME ON GETTING A REPLACEMENT. THEY CLAIM I ONLY HAD 6 MONTH TO GET A REPLACEMENT.HOWEVER, PRIOR COMMUNICATION SHOW 1 YEAR. HOWEVER, THE REPLACEMENTS WERE ALSO FAULTY, WITHIN THE YEAR OF EXCHANGE OR SHIPPING.

Now that I have had this appliance for a few months, I want to review it. I'll give the positives and the negatives as separate parts, so you can see each one easier. I'll do everything I know and have experienced with this machine, even beyond the mechanics of the machine. This way, you will be more informed. I am not involved with the company that makes this product, and purchased this product, not knowing who the company is, or it's history.

Positives:

- Small/compact, fits in a closet for storage
- Strong spin agitation in the washer
- High RPM Spin "dryer"
- Easy to understand when operating for the first time.
- Hooks up to any (or shall I say most USA faucets, kitchen or bath)
- Saves you money, by not having to go to a laundry room or laundromat.

Negatives:

- Noisy agitator motor, will cause other floors below you to hear you washing and spinning, with a loud hum going through the floor.
- You must put pants in a STURDY QUALITY laundry bag. If you don't, your pants will knot together.
There is no such thing as "gentle." I have towels that now are shreds. It is not easy on fabrics, no matter how empty or full it is.
- Lint trap cover may not stay in place, assisting in the ripping of clothing. You have to bend the tab lock outward to keep the tight lock.
- Water level is rather low. Fixed this with duct tape, which came off due to the lack of "gentle" in this machine. It came off within 4 washes. I had to then epoxy the hole in the front of the water holding tank, to get the maximum amount of water in and be useable.
- Only washes 2 Pairs of jeans and a t-shirt. Or washes 3 pairs of shorts and a t-shirt.
- Flimsy inlet hose, which is not found elsewhere easily. In fact, mine is a trifle short, for what I really need. If it were 6 inches longer...
- Cannot find the spin disk anywhere else, which goes over your clothes, so they don't jam up in the centrifuge and the top.
- Drain motor is weak and very slow.
- Is a manual machine. you must wash, spin, then rinse, spin... and repeat the rinse and spins as many times as you need. This means if you are allergic to the detergent, wear gloves to switch from water side to spin side. You have to manually fill the machine to your desired level too.
- Unit is only plastic. Therefore, you must use care when transporting and in other situations, with things above it. If heavy objects fall on it, your washer is doomed.
- When water overflows, it will flow into the spinner side. If you spin your clothes, make sure to do it empty, after fully draining the machine, to insure you will not damage the spin motor, and guarantee that you removed the water.
- Spinning centrifuge/basket is about half the size of the water/washtub.
- Safety stopping is only on the spin side. Washtub/water side still works, if door is opened. You must make sure children are not to go near the machine with water in it.

There are more negatives to this machine, than positives. This review was to show you what they do not say in the Youtube demos or Ebay listings... or any other sites. Too bad that I am the first to say these all in one place.

I have this unit, so I know the ins and outs of how it works... or does not.

text: Substituted this bulb assembly to replace an impossible to find bulb used in my Dacor Microwave.  I was able to affix (screw, washer & nut) this flanged assembly into the plastic duct area (had to first remove outer microwave cabinet skin and carefully remove the plastic duct not touching any electronics that can still hold a charge even when unplugged - capacitor leads!) where the old proprietary bulb was located.  This bulb uses same spade lug connections and works as good or better than the old bulb.  So it was plug and play once I attached the base inside the duct area.  Note:  This assembly is NOT a screw in bulb and base; it is a one piece assembly and when it burns out the holder/bulb assembly will need to be removed as one piece and replaced with same.  I went this route because this "assembly with bulb" was cheaper than just a screw in base mount without bulb.  My OEM bulb lasted 10 years and if this bulb lasts that long I will probably be due for a new microwave anyway, or whatever the latest technology brings, as my Dacor will be 20 years old by then.

title: Original GE MWF filter compared to many others
text: After 4 hours of researching brands to replace the MWF GE water filter for my refrigerator I found that none of the brands had the same standard as the OEM brand of GE.  Many had at the most  - an  nsf 42 standard which reduce specific aesthetic or non-health-related contaminants (such as chlorine, taste and odor, and particulates). .. but none had an NSF standard of 53 which  reduce specific health-related contaminants such hazardous contaminants may be microbiological (including filterable cysts), chemical (including disinfection byproducts, pesticides, herbicides, and insecticides), or particulate in nature.  Most didn't list an NSF standard at all they just claim a filtration system that will make your water taste better.  The GE brand has gone up in price a lot which ticks me off and is ridiculous, so that is why I was hoping to find a knock off brand that was the same but cheaper.  In the end I found a site cheaper than the GE site by around $18 and they were the original GE filters.  A lot of time researching which I feel wasted a good portion of my Saturday, but now I know and I guess I learned some things.. and I can at least leave my review for others who may be wondering the same thing.  I ended up getting mine at freshwater.com as of this date Aug 16, 2014 - they were the cheapest I could find online.  I hope some other companies who can make these water filters will do it at the same standard and not charge as much as GE. .. if they do they will make a lot of money on volume selling because i'm sure people would buy them.

title: Fixed the Ice Build-Up issue in the Freezer
text:
The reason for 4-stars and not 5 is the fact that the mounting bracket is not an exact fit. This fixed the ice build-up issue in my freezer. Here are the steps for trouble-shooting.

1. Check the defrost timer. Mine has a small post that I can access and turn with a screw driver. Also, my unit is rate 10-hours on and 30-minutes off. Turn the timer clockwise until the fans turn off and wait about 10 minutes, if you can hear water sizzling on the heating coil, then you may have bad gaskets/seals on the doors.

2. If you did not hear the water sizzle on the heating element in the freezer as the ice melted, then disconnect the fridge, defrost, remove the back panel so you can access the heating element. Remove the heating element. Use a volt-meter and measure the resistance of the heating element. It should be in the 10-ohms to sub 1-ohm range. If the heating element resistance is high (open circuit), then your heating element is bad. If the heating element is good, go to the next step.

3. Remove the defrost thermostat and connect the two wires together (this will mimic a closed thermostat circuit). Plug the unit in. (Caution!!! The electronic contol and wiring is at 120VAC). Observe the heating element, if it is glowing, replace your thermostat and you should be good to go.

title: Pretty outside hides lousy insides
text:
What a great looking unit -- too bad the sleek stainless steel outside hides a lousy inside!

My wife and I have been looking a more updated unit to replace our 15 year old electric range oven. We thought we found a unit that was both functional, sleek and useful. For the two months that the unit worked, it was actually a great range oven. We found ourselves using the upper oven (although smaller of the two) more than 95% of the time. It heated up quickly and baked evenly. The stove top is also designed thoughtfully and the control unit, while not as advanced as some other units, was very functional and surprisingly intuitive to use.

The unit broke down after just two months of use (bought on Sep 10, 2010 and broke on Nov 4, 2010). The unit shut down completely and when it re-powered, the "door locked" indicator was on. While the stove top was still functional, neither of the ovens were. The GE technician looked at the unit for about three minutes, ordered a bunch of parts and left. The follow up appointment was rescheduled by dispatch, without notification. GE Customer Service was useless (but at least they all spoke English). Now we're stuck without an oven for Thanksgiving holidays with family coming to town. Will call the store we bought the unit from and see if we can return it. Searching around there are more reports of control board circuit boards being "fried" by the oven, so this is not an isolated incident. Do not buy this unit until the problem is resolved.

title: Has a nice look but is NOT a 36" hood!!
text:
I looked high and low for a review of this range hood before ordering it online. Unfortunately I was unable to locate one. We liked the lines and simple front in the photos and being made in China it fit our budget a little better than the higher end brand names. What I did not notice when I bought it was that the width dimension is NOT 36" which is a real problem when you are mounting it under a 36" cabinet. The width is 3/4" narrower than the cabinet and with flanking cabinets it leaves 3/8" gaps on either side. Not only is the appearance not as nice but it leaves a nice grease collection pocket between the hood and adjacent cabinets.
I contacted the distributor in California and they said it was "industry standard" practice to undersize it for "variance in opening for the hood". Well if it is industry practice then someone forgot to tell the rest of the industry because I could not find another 36" undermount hood that didn't have a 36" dimension!
As for the function of the unit, it does what it is supposed to (so far) but if you are looking for a clean look to your kitchen, look elsewhere. Also, if the width is not an issue for you, check your local building codes before you install it. Most do not allow you to use the flex duct provided with the unit (most codes require rigid steel duct).

text: I am an ice-aholic. I NEED ice. It's a large purchase for me. This isn't money I had just laying around. But, I was convinced that this would last. I bought this machine in March of 2020. Within 3 months, it quit working. Customer service was helpful since it was still under warranty and they sent me a refurbished machine in June. Not what I was hoping for considering I'd just plunked down close to $600 for a new one. But, it was better than nothing. When the machine works it's AMAZING. I can literally snack on ice as if its popcorn. But, this machine is so inconsistent. Sometimes I would get full bin of ice pretty quickly, sometimes hardly any. And, the machine would get HOT. So, I pointed a little fan at the ice machine and it would cool it down and really pump out the ice. I cleaned it as recommended and always hold my breath that it will just keep working. The other day I came home to a flashing orange light and zero ice in the bin. I was devastated. I tried cleaning it. Again. Nothing. It flashes like it's making ice, the water is full, but literally nothing. I unplugged it, and tried again in a few hours. Nothing. Again. Cleaned it. Again. Nothing. I'm not much into a hot coffee first thing in the morning, I'd like a LARGE cup of ice with a little iced tea. Now when I get up, I'm looking at an empty ice maker. I finally drained it and took it to the garbage. I feel "lucky" that mine lasted a year and half. After reading MANY reviews online, sounds like a lot of people don't even make it passed 6 months with this thing. I'll be ordering another nugget machine as soon as I can save the cash for one. I will NOT be buying the GE Opal. Such a huge disappointment. For almost $600, I was really hoping for more than a little over a year with it.

title: Really cost-effective; seem to be well-made
text: My LG washing machine (from 2007 or 2008) began making unhappy noises that were getting worse.  A little research indicated that it was almost certainly one or more of the drum rollers.  (One of the front ones, it turned out, clearly had a bearing that was failing pretty badly).  I decided to give this kit a try because it was much cheaper than buying the OEM replacements from a specialty appliance site, as this kit includes all four rollers as well as the belt, idler pulley, and spring.  I replaced all four rollers and the belt, but didn't touch the idler pulley or spring.  The rollers seem to be very well-made and were identical to the OEM parts.  The only oddity is that you need two (2) washers and a nut for each roller, and this kit only includes one, so you'll need to use one of the original ones.  I ended up re-using all of the original washers and nut, simply because they seemed larger and maybe a tiny bit thicker than the ones that came with this kit.  That's the only reason I only gave 4 stars for the rating.  The repair was pretty easy (most of my time was spent removing dust and lint), and the reassembled washer is now as quiet as the day we first bought it.  I can't vouch for the longevity, (again, the rollers seem well-made and solidly constructed) but I'm very happy with this kit so far.

text:
Right so I've had this machine for quite a while. First let me say, yes it does make ice, in three different sizes. That's the good bit. Now come the not so good bits.

1) The instruction manual seems as if it was written first in another language and then pasted into Google Translate and voila! Non, c'est ne pas bien! The manual gives the most vague and generalised instructions, not just for operation, but for care and maintenance as well.

2) In spite of my best efforts (i.e. setting the time, not setting the time, setting the timed on/off feature, not setting the timed on/off feature, etc.), the thing beeps at really inconvenient times, say in the middle of the night.

3) The clock is in 24-hour display only with no option to change to a 12-hour a.m. / p.m. display.

4) CLEANING - This is why I rated it two stars. I've been wiping out the ice maker receptacle as per the instructions (as useful as they are - not!) regularly. Taking the whole thing (it is heavy for my standard) over to the sink to flush and drain out the back, etc...well recently, and for the first time, (was wearing my reading glasses) I saw the inside to the back, behind the evaporator, and to my absolute horror there was black mold everywhere. I tried a variety of brushes, different sizes and shapes to get to the area, no joy. I had to get my tool kit out, find the bit small enough for the screws and take the bloody top off! Even after all that, it took three more times to get it all out. There were more screws holding things down in places but I was dubious of going full throttle with dismantling of the machine.

I absolutely DO NOT recommend this machine. There have got to be much simpler models, much, much easier to clean, with a much better instruction manual. (For the record, I'm a Technical Writer and writing manuals for the end user is my work for 15 years now.)

text:
This isn't compatible with some machines, out of the box. Keurig has been increasing the size of the top needle, or possibly moving it slightly off-center on some models. When using a K-Cup, that never matters of course. When using a reusable K-Cup like this one, the machine's lid might not close without ruining the machine ... or without wearing down either the needle or the reusable K-Cup's lid opening.

They're all copying each other's designs, because of course they are. Who's gonna be brave, and the first to just make the top opening a radical 1 mm wider?

The "smoosh down" method of securing the lid isn't the best, however I'm aware they're all like that. If using a disposable filter, push it down into the cup, otherwise the lid will not stay shut. title: Arrived without a cap (Amazon Prime/Fulfilled by Amazon)
text: **The product works as described.**  The low review is due to Amazon Prime.  I received my first order in time, but without a cap.  This product is an environmental toxin, and as such, should *never* have been shipped without a cap (only the metal/plastic safety shield was intact}.  For reference, my cat had previously been exposed to a bacteriostat such as this, and has spent a night at an emergency vet due to life-threatening chemical burns. Upon receipt of the product I contacted Amazon and was offered the option of a return for reimbursement, or a replacement at cost.  So for anyone considering purchase, the product works as described and I have zero complaints... seriously, if you have a humidifier that you wish to remain mold-free, it's great!  But if you're purchasing through Amazon Prime or "fulfilled by Amazon", perhaps you may do better going through a different seller.  My report of a Hazmat violation raised no red flags for them, and they're expecting me to send Bacteriostat through the mail without a cap.  Really, really not okay -- says both myself, and my cat who's racked up nearly a grand in vet bills.  Bacteriostat means it kills microscopic life forms, as well as being a pretty harsh chemical.  Do yourself a favour and order from someone who has some sense.

title: This is NOT compatible with WF3CB or ALTRAWF
text:
This replacement (non-oem) filter is NOT compatible with WF3CB or "the longer" ULTRAWF by Frigidaire. The middle latch is different ( See attached photos) and WILL NOT lock into the filter housing. This manufacture states in installation instructions to press hard to install. Every oem we've ever used didn't require force to lock the filter in. I went with my better judgment, and didn't attempt to force it. Even our normal alternative replacement didn't require force.

I now have read multiple reviews of others damaging the filter or filter housing and needing expensive $$$ repairs!

We normally buy the SCW3CTO by Smart Choice as an oem alternative. It is (certified by Frigidaire) as a compatible replacement filter for about $3 more than this one. That filter actually works. However, unfortunatly that filter was out of stock at the time of this purchase. NEVER again will I buy this brand filter!

My advice, save yourself the headaches, possible damage, and time. Either buy the Frigidaire oem WF3CB or ALTRAWF filter or the Smart Choice SCW3CTO.

title: Fascinating material.  Not sure about long-term net benefit for cofee-brewing, but maybe tea.
text:
The material is amazing. It has the feeling of a sheer, stiff fabric, with threads so fine they are nearly invisible. But it is of course woven steel. The manufacturing process must be quite advanced and beyond coffee I suppose there are many home and industrial uses for steel cloth.

As a coffee filter, it does work. I've been using perhaps an overly-fine grind, so it tends to clog. I will try a coarser grind. It imparts only a slight metallic taste, not a problem for me. But it has these drawbacks

- With repeated use, coffee oils and coffee dust will clog the mesh
- This means it must be cleaned with soap & hot water regularly, and cleaned with hot water after each use.
- The need to wash this way, negates most of the "environmentally friendly" aspects-- disposable paper may be more earth-friendly than an energy-intense manufactured steel product that requires hot-water maintenance.
- Dumping the grinds is also a little awkward-- I can get most of them out by banging against side of can but again a significant amount must go down the drain, a potential risk to sewer/septic systems.

So as a convenience-- never run out of paper filters-- this does a fine job. But for economy or environment, I think it is a net loss.

I'd still recommend to have one. It may have other uses beyond coffee.

In fact it may be far better suited to lose-leaf tea, and I will try it.

title: Well caffinated in PA
text:
I can't say enough great stuff about this product.

At my frugal and non-coffee-drinking husband's urging, I purchased a Keurig to eliminate my 2 large cup per day DD addiction. My discovery -- the cost for pods was almost as much and didn't taste nearly as good. I tried DD pods. Tasty -- but no savings beyond gas since the cups they brew are small. It took three pods to brew the equivalent of one large DD cup. Next move was to fill the reusable filter that came with my Keurig with DD coffee. That turned out to be a major pain in the a** to clean and even worse -- it allowed "sludge" into my coffee. I didn't bother trying any other mesh filters since I figured they would come with the same issues.

I parked my Keurig and went back to the DD drive through. Some time later I stumbled across these little gems. This product is FANTASTIC because it is simple to use yet completely effective. No sludge in my coffee and clean up is easy as popping off a platic lid, dumping the filter and re-loading with a new one. (Heads up - you'll also need to purchase the cup that these fit into). These filters beat the crap out of any mesh filter that needs to be cleaned out with a toothbrush after each use. My arbovitae are loving them too since they compost like any other paper filter. I'm in coffee heaven and bouncing with joy (equal parts satisfaction and caffine!)

title: Broke after 7 months (and wasn't great to begin with)
text:
This icemaker was mediocre while it worked, and didn't take too long to break.

When we first bought the icemaker, the biggest issue I immediately found is that it's very challenging to clean. There's no easy way to access most of the internals that need cleaning the most, and I ended up buying a variety cleaning brush set just to work on it. Worse, even with filtered or distilled water, the system still gets gunky very vast, and mold will start to grow in the hard-to-reach corners of the system quickly.

When it did run, I discovered several issues that made the system frustrating to use. First, it's noisy, draws a lot of electricity (equivalent to a mini-fridge three times its size), there's almost no insulation in the ice tray so ice melts very fast, runs out of water very vast, and worst of all, constantly clumps, resulting in nowhere near full baskets of ice; the system needs an agitator or something to knock down freshly frozen cubes or they pile up and stop with less than a quarter bucket.

The biggest issue however, is that it broke irreparably after only half a year of use. The left-side spindle for the freeze bucket and paddle (a critical component) fractured and twisted, meaning that it can't fully cycle, and the machine errors out and flashes all lights. Resetting the device just causes it to immediately jam after homing again. As an engineer, I don't see an effective food-safe way to resolve this.

I'm going to attempt to make a manufacturer warranty claim as I'm outside the return period but I don't have high hopes. Avoid this product and the thousands of clones that look like it; they're all the same product with different badges.

EDIT: Manufacturer came through; they did honor the warranty and replace the device with a slightly larger and newer model, but I did have to jump through some hoops to get it, and it was a challenge to even figure out who to contact. The person I worked with via e-mail almost had an air of "ugh, this isn't worth my time", and we had to wait ~1 month for them to send a replacement. So still not recommended, but at least I wasn't completely SoL on this one.

title: IMPORTANT MODIFICATION REQUIRED
text: This part is cheap and arrives quickly. It would be very easy to install if not for its major flaw. I have returned and replaced this part 4 times over the past year before figuring out what was going on. The heat from the coil warps its thin frame causing it to fall from its location and short out and fry itself. When installing this you need to drill some holes on the side of the coil frame opposite of its electrical connector. 2 screws through the heat tube into the heating coils frame should keep the frame from falling and possibly help it from warping in the first place. Reinforcing the frame would be an extremely easy and cheap thing for the manufacturer to do but I doubt that will happen. If you are unwilling to do this I recommend sourcing a part elsewhere. Using the lower temp switch or running your dryer on cooler setting may also keep this from happening.

title: Not 1800 Watts and does not boil water all that fast
text: I did not evaluate every feature as the main selling point of induction cooking is that it's supposed to boil water much faster than conventional electric and gas burners.  When the unit arrived I was pleased that it was compatible with my existing cookware all of which strongly attract magnets on their bottom plates, as specified in the manual.  Next, I measured out exactly 3 quarts of cold tap water at about 80 degrees here in Florida into a 5 quart pot used for cooking pasta.  The diameter of the pot matched the outer circle on the unit -- a perfect fit.  When powered up and set to the maximum power output there was only the faint noise of the cooling fan without any other noises, such as squealing noted by some other reviewers.  The lack of noises other than from the fan indicated to me that my cookware was not a problem. The unit is supposed to give an error when incompatible cookware is used and this never occurred in my case further confirming my cookware is compatible.  When I measured the amount of time to a rolling boil with the pot covered and the unit set at the max power setting of 10 the result was very disappointing.  It took all of 12 minutes and 30 seconds just 30 seconds faster than my conventional electrical resistance 240 volt Jenn-Air cartridge unit (back burner) made around 1989, which took 13 minutes to reach a rolling boil. Both tests used exactly the same pot and the same amount of tap water at the same starting temperature. So much for induction units boiling water so much faster than conventional burners, at least those rated only 1800 watts and less.  Next, I connected an electrical power meter to the unit while it attempted to boil water cold water.  The measured power into the unit never exceeded 1650 watts and this was on a circuit rated at 20 amps, far in excess of the 15 amp circuit required.  My conclusion is that the 1800 watt rating is misleading.  Note also that if it did indeed draw 1800 watts that's 15 amps at 120 volts (15 times 120 = 1800 watts), which would be enough to trip some 15 amp circuit breakers.  Therefore, I suspect that my measured input power of 1650 watts maximum is by design to avoid tripping common 15 amp circuit breakers.  If that were to happen there would be far more customer complaints and returns.  But since this unit only draws 1650 watts at 120 volts AC input it should be rated at 1650 watts and not 1800 watts.  If it were rated at 1650 watts I doubt I would have considered the purchase.  Secondly, there are always losses in any device so if the unit pulls only 1650 watts from the wall outlet then the heat delivered to the water must be even less than this figure.  I've decided to return this unit to Amazon and perhaps buy a higher power unit requiring a 240 volt circuit.  A much higher power induction unit is required to boil water faster than my old Jenn-Air electrical cartridge.  Lesson: Don't believe the hype about induction units boiling water super duper much faster than anything else.

title: Wouldn't make this purchase again
text: This worked well for about 3 months, then stopped working (the pump quit). The seller agreed to accept it back even though it was after the warranty period of 30 days, but I would have had to pay return shipping. I'm not sure how much that would have been. I decided to just throw it out. It was also much more tedious to use than I had anticipated. You have to stay with the machine as it fills (several minutes), then set the timer for it to wash/agitate. Once it's done washing, you need to stay with it while it drains. Then to rinse, you have to stay with it to fill it a second time. Then set the timer for it to rinse/agitate. Once it's done rinsing, you have to watch it again while it drains a second time. There is a timer, but if you leave the drain pump going for too long, the pump will burn out (I think that's what happened to mine). Once the clothes have been washed and rinsed, you transfer them to the other side for the spin cycle. The spin cycle does a very good job of getting most of the water out. Then you run the pump again to drain the water from the machine. At this point, the clothes are wrung dry, but you still need to either hang them to dry the rest of the way, or put them in a regular dryer. It was just way too much work. If you want a portable washing machine, I suggest investing in a fully automatic one.

text:
Basic advice: don't buy this overpriced & under-performing range!
We bought our expensive GE "Cafe Series" gas range when we finally started renovating our home after Hurricane Katrina, and like so many others who have reviewed this range, we are disappointed for multiple reasons:
The "stainless steel" knobs are cheap plastic and now a 2nd knob (GE part #222D1387) has cracked and become useless for turning the gas burners ON or OFF, or for adjusting the flame height.
Also, the center griddle burner is terrible -- it takes forever to heat up the griddle and never heats evenly, we have never been able to use it for its intended purpose!
Likewise, the convection oven seems to take longer to cook everything.
And it really is DUMB to have the two large burners in the front, assuming you are a serious cook, thereby making it a challenge just to get to any smaller pots once you have two large pots on the front burners.
Very, very disappointed overall.
The range looks good, for sure -- but looks aren't everything especially once you start actually using your range for what it's intended, namely cooking!

title: Good ice, but a loud machine
text:
I wanted to use this ice machine and get familiar with it for a little while before reviewing. The ice itself is really “the good ice” and is so great to have available since we all like super cold drinks in my house. We didn’t know how to use the machine at first, so we kept it on at all times. We kept wondering why it was randomly turning on and producing ice after it’d stop and the “Add Water” light was on, or the “Ice Full” light was on. So, we left it thinking it’d just stay full. The water is underneath the ice box, so the ice would melt and the machine would restart again. It doesn’t keep the ice cold for very long, maybe 30 minutes to an hour, so this isn’t the kind of machine the hold it for long. You need to get the ice right away when it is done. It doesn’t take long once you turn it on, I usually can fill up my cup after about 10 minutes or so. I do think that the placement of the handle is odd looking… but it’s readily available for you up there, lol.

Final thoughts, it works, it’s really “the good ice,” but it’s loud and restarts itself once the ice melts, so if that bothers you, then turn it off when you won’t be using it. ::)

title: Free at Last from the Throes of HE Machines - Clean Clothes and No More Stink
text:
This basic machine is sold by the big box retailers also with only a change of a couple of letters so they have some sense of exclusivity. For all practical purposes they are the same. GE offers one of the largest 3.9 cu ft conventional washers now available. The offer an HE model, an EnergyStar model with agitator, and they offer the nonEnergyStar conventional machine which actually has some more desirable features than the more expensive brethren.

This machine has been the beginning of a new and better life at our house.

We installed a new LOW efficiency clothes washer with as big a tub as we could find and all mechanical dials -no electronics - complete with manual temperature controls and with no electronic override on hot cycles which often tempers even HOT cycles to only 110 deg F washes. Our still-youthful, very large deluxe main brand HE washer has been relegated to basement storage -after draining all the stagnant water out of it which HE machines cling to in between washes..

You may read that this model is noisy - it is not. It is quieter than our old HE, which also played a symphony depending upon the stage of the cycle - very irritating. So unless you have your washing machine installed in the den right next to the TV, you may not even know it's working.

Does it fill the tub? Oh my - on LARGE load setting it fills to within a couple of inches of the top of tub-very satisfying.

Is hot water really HOT?-yep, just like it comes out of the heater. Likewise, warm is warm, cold is cold. How about that?

We had already decided we wanted a very large machine, so a 3.9 cu ft was the one for us. Over the last six months our family has bought three GE 3.9 cu ft machines. One was an EnergyStar rated for a rental property. No complaints from the tenant on that one. My son-in-law spoke highly of this nonEnergyStar model. He had replaced a deluxe HE machine which smelled and needed sanitizer regularly, whose pump broke down three times, and which yielded dry, unwashed clothes sometimes on the BIG wash cycle. The dirty little secret (not so secret anymore) about HE machines is that most of that large stainless steel drum goes basically unused on the wash cycle, therefore the big numbers for size are misleading....and they hold onto significant amounts of old rinse water in name of efficiency which sits and festers waiting for your next load of unmentionables Remember that the next time you wash clothes contaminated with lawn and garden chemicals, oil and gasoline or other work related substances.

So, I was leaning toward the GE 3.9 EnergyStar Model. Then, I met a lady at Lowe's who was trading hers back in after a few weeks. To Lowe's credit they were allowing her to do so. She said that the agitator only turns very little, that it would not fill very much with water and the water never reached a high temperature on HOT cycles.

Some research told me that she was right on two out of three counts. A GE spokesman wrote online in a reply to similar complaints that the EnergyStar machine tempers hot water to a maximum of 110 deg. F. One can culture bacteria at 110! GE also says that some of the same models may have a problem with the manual override not allowing it to fully fill the tub-hers must have had that problem. The third complaint about the agitator; I took a chance on that. It does turn slowly and quietly but it thoroughly agitates the clothes, if there is enough water.

Worried about durability? - Buy the extended warranty. The price is already very competitive at most places. No machine is going to last like the old 40 year-old Maytag your grandmother used..or is still using.

I now enjoy the pleasures of fresh smelling towels and sheets, and jeans that actually get clean....and the wife not complaining because the cycle is lasting too long, and about large loads coming out with dry unwashed spots, and having to use Afresh every couple of days to keep the machine from smelling like an open sewer. Sometimes progress is stepping back a bit and finding something that works.

title: Horrible Machine and customer relations service
text:
A NIGHTMARE with GE!! Stackable Model # GUD27ESSJWW
The "one star" was given because a value for overall rating was mandatory. If I had a choice, the overall rating would be -5 stars.
DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE EVEN IF GE PAID YOU!! The 1st new unit was installed on 12/17/16 and had increasing problems. First problem: washer spin cycle was so loud it sounded like the rotors of a helicopter on full throttle. Second problem: machine stops mid-cycle during the spin cycle. Third problem: spin cycle would not stop and kept going for another 20 minutes and had to be stopped manually. Called GE about the problems. Was told that we would receive a call from their service person to schedule service. Never received a call back from anyone. When service was finally scheduled, it was at least a week later and after multiple requests by the dealer. Serviceman diagnosed it as a transmission problem. Since it was a new machine, we requested GE exchange the broken machine for a new one. Request was denied. Reason? They said the machine was under warranty. But who in their right mind would want to keep a new machine that comes broken?!! Spoke to Terry at GE Customer Relations Dept. who said there is no way we could proof that the machine came off the delivery truck broken. What is she insinuating...that we broke the machine on purpose because we want to sit on the phone waiting for over half an hour to speak with someone? After weeks, the dealer was finally able to exchange the broken machine for a new one. The second new machine came today and was installed. Guess what! It is still broken. This time it is the dryer. During the dry cycle, when the drum is rotating, a rhythmic loud noise comes out of the side of the machine, like a hammer banging. We will be contacting GE AGAIN! What happened to quality control? GE should compensate us for time spent waiting on the phone to speak to a GE rep, time away from work waiting for their service person, and frustration and angst from this entire experience.

The stainless mesh on the replacement definitely seems sturdier than the original.

Upon installation the replacement didn't quite drop into place like the original - see the photo - there were gaps on either end. It only took a little bit of pressure to push it into place and maybe over time and exposure to heat it will fit better? Meantime though there is a gap where lint can get sucked through so make sure if you're using this that it fits tightly. title: Fits and works but....
text:
It is clearly a quality product. That fit perfectly into the space and onto the motor shaft. It provided a much needed repair to the clothes dryer so that laundry could resume.

However the fit and apparently quality was marred by how it was shipped.

The blower fan itself is a solid "plastic" fan, as shown in the pictures, mounted onto a metal shaft. For shipping the blower fan was wrapped in a single layer of thin bubble wrap and put back into a box that oversized enough that the fan was just bouncing around inside. Also the box material was a little on the thin and flimsy side.

As a result when I opened it and checked the fan blade out it showed the bright white signs of stress on several the individual fan blades where they attach to the solid base plate. When I looked at it very carefully I couldn't see any obvious signs of cracking but for something spinning at a high rate of speed this was not confidence inspiring.

I needed the blade as I needed to get the dryer back into working order. So I installed it. After several loads being put thru the dryer all is still well. I guess only time will tell if it is going to work long term.

In summary: If the box had been a bit more durable and the fan protected with more packing I think it would have arrived in perfect condition. I went back and forth between 3 stars and 4 stars as I wrote this review and finally settled on the 3 because of the unknown nature of the observable damage and fact that it would be so simple to the prevent the problem in the first place. I just hope and pray that the blade will hope up for a long time to come.

title: Major Fail!
text: I bought this for my Kenmore 200 Series washer. I was thrilled about the savings and the delivery time. I was however unable to use lid switch because it was defective. The locking mechanism did not not open all the way which prevented the lid strike from being inserted so that the washer would start. It looks open so I didn't realize that the switch was the proplem. I originally thought maybe I needed a smaller strike because this was a replacement part. I found a local appliance part place with the intent of buying a new strike but when the new strike didn't fit into this part, they grabbed a new OEM lid switch off of their shelves. The strike it into it which confirmed that this part that I purchased off of Amazon was the problem. I ended up buying the new OEM part for $103 plus tax. It was the right decision and what I should have done in the first place. When I compared the OEM part to this replacement part, I found the OEM to be sturdier plastic, better movement and overall way better quality. I don't want to have to ever replace this part again (especially during supply chain issues and shortages) and buying the more expensive, better quality part was the right choice for me.  Just a note to save someone from a bunch of confusion. None of the videos I found online addressed this part and it was very confusing how to remove the old part. You have to push the right side the switch from the top where the picture of the lock is. Push it to the left. Once you do this, the right  side of the part will drop down so that you can pull the whole part out. Just do that in reverse to install the new one. Push the left side of the white up and slide all the over to the left so that you can push the whole white piece through the whole so that it is on the top ouside. Now slide it to the right to lock it into place. Done!

Bulky items like towels and jackets and even heavy jeans should always be done alone but I throw small garments in to make the time more efficient. Ok so about 10min into the wash I flip on the fresh water and let it overfill and it will help get the soapy water out, if not you have to drain and re fill for a rinse cycle but that takes time. I find that 10 min wash and 5-8 min with the fresh water on does the trick. Now drying I only put a few pieces of clothing in and run for 30sec to 1 min l. I found that anytime over 1 min is wasted. I can do all that laundry in 45 min. It’s not automatic so an egg timer or use your phone to maximize time. Now for full dry I dry indoors in a vented room and fan blowing on the clothing. T shirts dry in 3-4 hours but jeans and towels take all night.

Hey everybody. It's the dude here with another dudely review.

I've had this item for years. I took it from my brother or a friend who never used it. In fact, I might have bought it for my parents who never used it. Anyways. The fact is, I've had it for years and it runs like a champ.

Tea-ball infusers don't give the tea enough room for the leaves to unfurl, and often get a little messy. They require that you have a small plate nearby to place the ball on after removing from the tea. (and thus, one more piece of dishware to wash)

This thing solves both problems, and more closely imitates the environment the tea deserves, which is in a proper teapot.

I've brewed multiple teas from Mariage Freres, Tea Ginza in Tokyo, and with the finest Assam you can find in Istanbul.

For the hard-core, single-cup, tea-punk drinker, this is it.

title: Take More Coffee To Brew One Cup Of Strong Coffee!
text:
I was disappointed with how this filter works. I brought so that I could use our regular brand of coffee, Folger's French Roast. After trying different combination out, the cup of coffee still doesn't compare to brewing a whole pot using my cuisinart coffee maker. I ended up using way more coffee in the filter to get anything close to what my old stand by produced.

The ratios that I tried were:
1) coffee filled to the max line of the filter, plus strong brew setting, plus 14 oz (produced a very water down cup of coffee)
2) coffee filled to the max line of the filter, plus strong brew setting, plus 12 oz water (produced an okay cup of coffee, but lacked the regular robust taste)
3) coffee filled to just below where the lip of the cap for the filter sits and way above the max line, strong brew setting, plus 12 oz water (produced a stronger cup, similar to what the cuisinart coffee marker would produce, however it did have a bite to the coffee which we don't normally have when brewing with the cuisinart.)

Since I ended up using about 3+tablespoons for the 3rd cup, it kind of defeats the purpose of having the filter since it uses way more coffee than you would use if you were to prepare a pot of coffee. I don't think this is a filter I will use again. I may try the ones where you put a paper filter in it to see if I get a normal cup from just 2 tablespoons. Comments posted for other plastic and metal filters that come with paper disposable filters are saying that the paper filters slow down the coffee coming through and it makes for a better cup of coffee. If I go that route, I will post an review as to whether it works better than this product. On a flip side, I did see some comments posted here, that were saying they get coffee grounds in their cups of coffee. I, personally, haven't experienced that. I find no coffee grounds in my cup of joe at all.

I did get my keurig so that my husband and I could have hot and fresh coffee for the weekday mornings. Guess I'll continue to make whole pots of coffee on the weekends using the cuisinart since it's more cost effective.

text: We have had this washer for approximately 2 months.  So far it is working fine.  We fill water into our washer by hand using a pitcher.  We do not connect the hose to a faucet.  We keep our washer on a sturdy wooden cart.  We drain the water into a five gallon bucket and then empty the bucket.  The washer moves a lot when on spin cycle. title: Do not purchase GE appliances
text:
We did not purchase our GE range from Amazon but from Home Depot. But we want to share our experience with GE as a company and how they stand behind their products.

Less than 4 weeks after purchasing the range it has become inoperable. We used the oven to prepare a meal last night, turned it off and sit down to enjoy the meal with dinner guests. The oven had been turned off for approximately 2 hours when we began to smell fumes coming from the oven. Open the oven to find smoke coming from the vents in the bottom of the oven. Even though it had been turned off for 2 hours the back of the oven was hot. We unplugged the stove it continued to produce fumes and smoke. We turned off the gas and the next morning called GE to arrange for service. This is the week of Christmas so we were told the soonest they could come to do the repair would be the Monday after the holiday. Which means we have no means to cook with for the next 5 days. We live in a very rural area in the mountains. So we ask for different options perhaps a replacement of the stove, we were told the only option was to have service come look at it. I'm sure if it's fixable it will require ordering parts and returning to install parts which means even longer before we have a working oven. It also means for the next 5 days and over the Christmas holiday we are without a stove to cook on.

I'm old enough to remember when companies like GE sold appliances that were reliable and they stood behind them if they weren't. This is the second new gas range we've purchased in less than 2 years of building our new home. The first one was a Samsung. We highly recommend you do not purchase a Samsung! That stove turned out not to be fixable and they would not stand behind seeing that the year warranty had expired. So we had to sell it on Craigslist for next to nothing.

Don't know what the answer is to buying a dependable appliance these days.
