title: Simplicity trumps tech
text:
My husband is a bit obsessed with coffee. At last count, we have at least 10 methods in our kitchen (including some expensive, trendy, and far-flung contraptions: a Chemix (former favorite), standard grind-and-perc machine, two french presses, yama silverton, yama cold brew, turkish pot, aeropress espresso maker, rok expresso maker, saeco espresso maker, and now this pour over.) My point in noting this is that I've tasted a lot of different coffees made a lot of different ways, and cleaned up after a lot of different processes.

I'd loved using the Chemix for its flavor, but keeping multiple cups warm through the morning was a pain. And as we know, there's no good way to reheat coffee. I also hated the number of filters we were going through. This pourover is now my favorite. I can make a cup at a time, the flavor is wonderful (oils come through to the cup since they don't get trapped in a paper filter), the dual mesh filter does a wonderful job of keeping grounds out of the cup, and cleanup is simple. I smack the filter against the inside of my trash can to knock the grounds out, and the welds appear to take the stress. Design is a good combination of strong and functional; haven't yet had an issue with any spillage, and have made ~2 dozen cups.

Have read others' concerns about the stability of the base, and I just don't see it. If you're only making a cup at a time--which this is meant to do, sitting over the top of a single mug--you should have no issues. For reference, I'm pouring 330g (8 oz) of water over 20g of med-ground coffee into an 8 oz mug, which leaves about 1/2" left at the top. Cup diameter is ~3.5".

title: Both were advertised as excellent machines. While I fully realized they were not ...
text: I am writing this review after trying so hard to resolve the issue I was having with my LG washer and dryer. I purchased the matching LG 2250 washer and dryer at the end of 2013. Both were advertised as excellent machines. While I fully realized they were not the top of the line LG machines I was hopeful that they would be longlasting and do a comparable job as the 12 year old whirlpool machines I was replacing. The machines looked beautiful and I chose to purchase the pedastal companions which were outrageously expensive in my opinion. Regardless, I did this because I found the machines too low for comfortable use and it certainly completed the "look". What I found was that the washer was mediocre at best. It never fully cleaned the clothes regardless of settings. In addition, I found the "tub" of the 2250 series incredibly small. Although said to be efficient I ended up doing several loads rather than one large load because the machine couldn't handle the extra clothing. When I tried to do too much laundry at one time the results were horrible. I used high efficiency detergent with the hope that might have resolved some of the issues. It did not. Regardless of the quality of laundry, the most annoying and disgusting aspect of these front loading machines was the awful smell that came from the machines. I called LG numerous times and they told me about cleaning the tub with a special cycle, leaving the door open, cleaning the rubber gasket, etc. I did all of these things over and over. What it came down to is that a front loading machine pools water and the gasket gets mold build up on it. This is unlike top loading machines. Did I mention the dryer would hardly dry anything unless I ran it for more than an hour regardless of the amount of clothes. I checked and rechecked to make sure I had a clear outlet to the roof. They just stunk!  I pleaded with LG for a better solution. I got nowhere and I felt they really didn't stand by their product. Only later did I find that numerous complaints about this "small" issue had surfaced. Rather than fight with them any longer I sold the machines (yes I informed the buyers of their problems------some people just want front loaders.....) and purchased the top loader HE machines from Samsung which are spectacular. Unfortunately, I will never again purchase an LG product

title: Avoid GE Fridges That Require This Filter
text:
My wife wanted to buy a top end GE, and we did. Unfortunately, the top end GEs now require a water filter with an RFID chip. Why should you care? Because you can't just buy any replacement filter, you have to buy the $50 RFID replacement. If you don't buy the RFID replacement, your refrigerator will be flashing you mean red lights every single day, saying your filter is expired. What's funny is that the non-RFID filter will fit your refrigerator, but it won't turn off the warning.

In essence, they are making you buy a $50 filter every 6 months to shut your fridge up. If you don't, it will flash at you constantly. Not a good way to treat customers.

title: Loved it at first, now disappointed
text:
I purchased this in September of 2022. Loved it at first. It was easy to use, and a nice little luxury since we never had an ice maker before. In November, I went to do the regular cleaning and noticed black stuff in the ice basket. It was not mold; it was something very greasy and would not wash off easily even with soap and water. I thoroughly cleaned the unit; the black stuff didn't reappear, but a puddle of water showed up under the unit, sometimes a lot, sometimes a little, but when the puddle dried it left behind a lot of white crystalline stuff. Since we used only reverse osmosis water in it, that shouldn't have been happening because the water doesn't contain a lot of minerals. I called the support line to see if they could help me diagnose the leak thinking maybe something just pulled loose when I was cleaning it. They first offered to just replace the unit stating it had a one year warranty, but sorry, they claimed to have none in stock with no idea when it would be back in stock. That's a red flag. Then they offered to send me one through Amazon, but claimed it was out of stock on Amazon. (It is not at this time). They then offered me a full refund, which I am currently waiting for. The support person was very nice, and I have no complaints about the support call, but I am disappointed. I am left with a $400 piece of refuse which I will have to find a place to recycle, probably for a fee. I thought this was a reputable brand, but I think like so many other things, it is just factory made in China and branded with the Mueller name. You can find other mystery name brands that look identical. Maybe I just got a lemon. If I purchase another one and have no problems with it, I will update this review. My one recommendation if you do buy this unit would be to spend the extra $11.52 and buy the extra 5 year warranty. It was really nice while it lasted, but it only lasted 2 months.

Update: 3/30/23
The replacement for our original ice maker purchase has been working well now for 3 months. It has a louder hum than the first one so I stuck a magnet on the side and that quieted the vibration. The original defective unit got a new home with a handy guy who repaired it with a new o ring and some new screws.

title: Love It!!
text:
I love THE LAUNDRY ALTERNATIVE WONDERWASH. I am disabled and live in a not so great neighborhood a mile or so from the laundrymat and it becomes a pain to have to load up laundry,find quarters, shlep everything in and out of the laundry mat and come home with not- so- clean laundry. I put this little beauty in my tub, put in a few pieces of clothing or 2-3 bath towels along with a tablespoon of laundry detergent and within minutes I have clean laundry! I use this in conjunction with the BREATHING MOBILE WASHER , and it works great! This is my routine

1. Add laundry to the WONDERWASH with laundry detergent and wash for 3 minutes.
2. Remove laundry and place in a five gallon bucket and rinse and agitate with the BREATHING MOBILE WASHER 1-2 minutes
3. Place back in the WONDERWASH with fabric softener and again agitate for 2-3 minutes
4. Drain, wring and hang dry
5. 6-8 minutes CLEAN LAUNDRY!!!

I plan on buying a spin dryer in the future to make my routine easier as it is hard on this old ladies hands to wring laundry but hey at the rate I'm saving $$ I'll be able to do so very soon!!

title: Mixed Feeling
text:
After a year or two of the random beeps where our dishwasher would randomly think the door opened, it finally completely died. Couldn't turn it on or anything. Since then, over the last few months, I've replaced this board three times, as all of them do the same thing with the phantom open door. I have a Wyze switch hooked up to it so when a load finishes, it cuts the power until I need it again. Not ideal, but cheaper than buying a whole other dishwasher.

Maybe I'll try for a 4th that just works? It seems highly unlikely it's actually the door sensor. I've taken it out and apart and verified all connections on the PCB and pins and it checks out. It's just two simple switches. The behavior changes with the boards too. I think there's a design issue with the boards themselves.

title: Recycle Hack
text:
Well, anyone who owns a Samsung French Door Refrig with a POS Ice Room Ice Maker knows that even after applying all the fixes, they'll still be hair-dryer defrosting it, every ~3 months; I've got it down to ~15 minutes now. So instead of buying a new refrigerator-with-ice-maker-in-the-freezer-drawer (at C0stc0), I decided to limp it along another year and buy another filter. There's just the two of us in the household and I've calculated we dispense <300gal through the filter annually PLUS we have a clean water supply, so I ignore the 6 month reminder and replace it every December.
The filter is a simple plastic 1/4" thick, two piece plastic cartridge with 3 rubber o-rings, housing the carbon-filter insert. It's not difficult to disassemble the filter for recycling/disposal:
1) remove the o-rings with an awl or precision mini bladed screwdriver. shake out the water.
2) clamp the filter in a vise or brace appropriately
3) (hack)saw 1/4" deep around the diameter at the cartridge seam, about 1/3 up from the bottom.
4) discard the carbon-filter insert and recycle the two plastic cartridge pieces.
Maybe call your recycler and confirm they recycle Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) (7).
Remember to run 3 gallons of water through your new filter. Maybe water the plants, fill a toilet tank, or clean the sinks and use it for rinse water.

title: Not too bad....yet.
text: To start...I bought this fridge from Best Buy.  I plugged it in this morning and it has been running continuously because other reviews (Best Buy website) said to put the temperature setting lower than the recommended setting because it is finicky.  So far the freezer has stayed below zero degrees but the fridge is difficult to maintain around 34-36 without readjusting the temperature setting.  I'm sure I'll get it right in a few days time.  As for the plastic parts breaking that other customers have complained about...well, it's plastic.  The doors are meant to hold gallon jugs, not skinny bottle of whatever will fall through the crack between the shelf and rail.  Also, this fridge has a wicked seal so you have to be careful opening it because I can only imagine that you will break the plastic handle that it comes with.  Oh, did I mention that it was only a little over $500 dollars for an 18 quick foot fridge?  You get what you pay for and I purchased this for a garage fridge because it states it is "garage ready".  Now to get to the noise part.  People on other websites have compared the sound of the fridge to a gas powered generator.  I'm not going to lie, when I plugged it in I thought a plane was about to take off.  I'm not an engineer, but upon opening the freezer door and pressing against the plastic hosing on the back wall (where the evaporator fan is located), I immediately realized that the noise was coming from the fan rubbing up against the plastic housing.  To remedy this, I simply pushed on the rear wall (made of aluminum) back a little bit because the fan is attached to the back wall.  This pushed the fan back far enough to where it wasn't rubbing against the plastic piece in the middle and it immediately became quieter.  I could not be happier now that it doesn't sound like a jet engine in my garage...simply an engineering defect on Fridgiaire's part.  I'll post back here in a few months to let you know how wel it is holding up in a garage environment (Oklahoma summers) to see if it is truly "garage ready".  Until then...do not shy away from this fridge because the price point is rights for the quality.  So until then, I am only giving it 3 stars because of the finicky temperature control.

This was never a problem on my previous units that used a simple metal bar and sensor to detect whether ice is full and they generally lasted until the compressor went out in around 3 years.  Unfortunately, most of the icemakers are made by one Chinese company and other companies just stick their brand on the units.  This unit also holds a very small amount of ice, which wasn't enough to even make an iced coffee.

I don't expect them to last while under that kind of stress, so I guess I got what I paid for. The area that is supposed to lay flat on the outside of the fridge door has a big gap on one end as well because of the bend in the handle, so it doesn't lay flat on the door.

I don't understand how a manufacturer could put the research and development in to making a replica of a refrigerator door handle and have such poor quality control that it doesn't work the way it's supposed to. If the handles were straight they would have worked perfect, so they measured everything right and got the finish pretty spot-on. Go figure.

They can be tested with an ohmmeter by measuring the resistance between J16 pins 1 and 2 from the control panel. The resistance should be between 2000 and 3500 ohms. When new it tested within spec. Within one month the resistance is infinite meaning an electrical connection must have broken inside.

title: DO NOT BUY THIS OVEN
text: I purchased and had this oven installed in September of 2020. I used it for several months with good success and reasonable satisfaction.In January 2021 the oven turned itself off and refused to turn back on. I had my electrician check that it was receiving power and then called EMPAVA customer support. They instantly diagnosed the problem as one or more faulty thermostats [there are 2] and offered to send me two replacement thermostats. The problem is that this is a wall-mounted oven and the thermostats are located under a backplate on the back of the oven. To change the thermostats will require having an electrician uninstall it: disconnect the hard-wired oven from the 240V circuit, remove it and replace the thermostats, reconnect and reinstall it. This represents a considerable expense to correct a problem that I am certain the company was aware of when they shipped the oven. They wre just too ready with the solution. They will send you the replacement thermostats at no cost, but the cost of replacing them in the oven is all yours. This is a dumb design for wall mounted oven and even worse if the thermostats can be expected to fail the first time your broil. DO NOT BUY IT. AT TJHIS POINT I WOULD NOT BUY ANY EMPAVA PRODUCT.

title: External water hookup is great, but other issues. (Lowered review from 4 stars to 2 stars)
text:
The style of the ice maker/water dispenser is really nice. It looks good and fits under our upper cabinet perfectly. My unit did not come with instructions on how to hook up the external water line, but having owned my own maintenance business for over 20 years, I eventually sorted out how to make it work (Less mechanically inclined people might want to consider this before buying). Now that it is hooked up, it works great! The only complaint about the machine so far is that the ice tends to clump together in the storage bin and has to be broken apart before it will dispense. Although this is a pain, we still find it better than scooping the ice like we had to do with our old counter-top ice maker.

This review is being revised as a few more issues have been realized. 1) Dispensing the ice is very slow - you have to put the glass under the dispenser and hold it up against the button for a good 30 seconds to get all the ice from the machine. 2) Port where ice comes out can get plugged with clumping ice - it eventually melts and comes out and often ends up on the floor (NOT GOOD!). 3) The beeping for when ice starts being made and again when the ice is full is annoying - as far as I could figure out, there is no way to shut off the beeping.
The only thing that is a huge plus is the water line hookup. Unfortunately, the negative aspects of this ice maker have caused us to buy one that has to be filled manually, and return this unit.

title: Could be better
text:
Did quite a bit of research on these type of ice makers prior to buying this one, and thought this was my best option other than the 4k industrial nugget ice maker.
Pros:
Once you set it up it is easy to run. Add water when the low water light comes on, push dispenser for ice.
Ice is exactly what I wanted. Just like getting ice at Sonic.
Cons:
The amount of ice it says it produces on Amazon does not match directions in the box and is less than what it actually produces. It is much less.
You HAVE to use purified water. Tap water as well as filtered water wont work. It constantly puts itself in clean mode and you never get ice.
It is not as user friendly as it could be. You can't open it to see if there is ice. It gets dusty inside even though covered, and is difficult to clean. Adding water could be easier.
It is a little noisy while it is making ice.
Conclusion:
It does produce the ice I like, but not nearly enough. It is very heat sensitive. I had to move it 3 times before I found a spot it would actually produce ice. I seem to have found the right spot and I now get several glasses of nugget ice per day.

title: Horrible Range
text:
I purchased a new home in August 2019 and there was a new Bertazzoni 36" range included. The first time I attempted to preheat the oven, it lit and a few minutes later I came back to find it no longer preheating and the strong smell of gas in the kitchen.

I waited for the gas odor to clear and re-lit the oven. I let it preheat for 30 minutes and it never got to 350. Called for service a they told me the setting on the oven is only a guide and do not go by that. It is typically 50-75 degrees off.

Long story short, the repair people have been to my home several times over the past 3 years and replaced several parts. The range still turns off 90% of the time on preheat and still does not get to temperature.

I have tried to work with the Factory Builder Sales in Houston (the dealer) to get the range replaced, since October 2019 and they will not work with me. I have also reached out to Bertazzoni Customer Support, requesting a replacement range, and they will not work with me. They offered to pay for parts, all of which have already been replaced once, and they labor is on me.

title: Great decision to purchase
text: I was on the fence about purchasing a portable washing machine for a long time, but after moving into an apartment without an in-unit W/D it has already saved us so much time and money. Figuring out the set up for the faucet hook up took a bit of work, but once we figured that out and got a dolly to roll it around on, it’s very easy to use. You have to be careful about the drainage tube (we had 1-2 spills at first), but just make sure that it’s secured with something that ensures it won’t fall out of whatever basin you have it flowing into. Highly recommend if your other alternatives are a laundromat or hand washing. It doesn’t take up very much space at all but it holds a surprising amount in each load; we’ve done king sheets (fitted sheet and flat sheet in separate loads) and a Queen duvet cover with no issues. The spin cycle on this machine also does a great job of getting most of the water out, so we’ve easily been able to hang dry everything. It’s easily paid for itself already in the money we saved by not paying $5 for every wash and dry at a laundromat.

title: Lasted only a couple weeks
text: After 13 years of faithful operation our LG dryer stopped drying.  Found an on-line service manual and watched a few YouTube videos on how to disassemble the dryer and test the various components.  The thermal fuse was bad.  Since the original lasted 13 years I decided to spend a few more $ and buy the LG replacement part.  Received the thermal fuse promptly and got it installed and returned to service in probably 20 minutes or so.  The dryer worked fine for about 2 weeks before it stopped drying again.  Disassembled the dryer again and tested all the components again, it was the thermal fuse again!!  Original lasted 13 years, replacement lasted 13 days!!  Called Amazon on Friday and had a replacement the following Monday.  It is up and running again, but I have to wonder how long it will last this time.  Kudos to Amazon for the prompt replacement and VERY easy return process through the UPS Store!!

title: Not perfect but pretty good
text:
I bought this as an alternative to spending $2,600 on a washer dryer from my RV dealer. The RV here js a 2020 Montana High Country 373RD in case that helps anyone. There are some great things about this Washer Dryer combo and some not so great things.

Pros: 110 Volt
A dryer vent is not required
Wash and Dry capability
Can turn it on and forget it
Does a good job of cleaning clothes if not overloaded
Look is appealing to the eyes
Very fast spin cycle
Many modes to choose from
Compact
Saves space

Cons: WILL SHAKE VIOLENTLY IF NOT LEVEL
WILL SHAKE VIOLENTLY IF NOT LEVEL (Yes I said that twice)
Buttons feel kinda cheesy
Pretty small tub
Very heavy
If condensing to dry will heat up RV or room
Can drip moisture if condensing albeit very little
Easily overloaded

All in all this is a very good compact Washer and Dryer combo. Eliminates the need for both a separate Washer and Dryer. The spin cycle shake is not apparent if the unit IS LEVEL. If your RV and thus the Wash Dry combo is not very level you WILL KNOW IT. I experienced this first hand when I first set up my RV. First time I used it it shook like crazy in a 41.5 ft RV with 6 electric Jacks all with 8 inch round bases. This RV weighs 13,000 lbs completely empty! If you put a level on the Combo, and it is just right, you will feel a slight shake but not bad. But remember it has to be level AND it cannot be over loaded. If you want to wash a comforter, forget it. It isn't big enough for that. I wash maybe 2 pairs of jeans and maybe 3-4 T shirts. That's the maximum. If you do more than that expect a whole lot of shake and your clothes not getting dry. All these smaller RV type washer and dryer combos cannot handle a whole lot at once. This thing will do its job but if you let laundry go a couple weeks, expect to spend an entire day washing laundry for 2 people max.

This machine is not lightweight. It weighs more than my 5 cubic ft Washer or Dryer at home. Theres a whole lot in a compact dual purpose machine. Condenser allows you to dry with no vent but expect the room to get pretty warm. It does a fine job if not overloaded.

Overall I would buy it again for sure to use in an RV as I did not have to remove the upper shelve in the closet where it sits. It takes up one washer or dryer space and does the job of 2 seperate units, but you cannot expect it to act like a full size washer and dryer. If you have it level and do not overload it and I know I have stressed this point but it is important, it will do a very good job. If those things are not done, you won't like it at all as it will shake and if overloaded your clothes will not fully dry and may not properly wash.

The face looks slick and sophisticated but the controls "feel" kinda cheap. This does not effect it's performance though. On a quick wash the washer takes 20 minutes and the dryer takes 1 hour. You can turn it on and go boating if you want and if properly set you will have clothes ready to fold when you get back, albeit not a lot of clothes. I have the 2019 model in gold.

title: 3-months later, epic fail
text:
I purchased this fridge from Lowes on May 1. By early August the ice maker was dripping. I called Whirlpool and they sent out a service person. HOWEVER...before the repair guy arrived I realized that the entire unit was warming up. The dripping was caused from the ice melting (and pouring out the dispenser, down the front of the fridge). The freezer contents were thawing and the milk and meat in the fridge section were spoiling. Helpful Whirlpool customer service suggested I "reset" the computer by unplugging and replugging in the unit. Surprise! The compressor had been off, which I didn't realize. The unit began cooling down again and I hoped it was ok. But when the service guy arrived the next day he read the temperature and said my fridge was 47 (I had it set at 33) and the freezer was 44 degrees (set at -1). According to him, the sealed system was flawed. They were going to need to replace the evaporator, compressor and all the freon. It would take a few days to order parts and be a long process to replace the entire refrigeration function of my 3-month-old fridge.
The AMAZING part: Lowes is REPLACING my unit (hurray!) within a day, the price has gone down so I'll get some $$ back. Hopefully it will not go into repairing the stupid thing in another few months. But I'm really proud of Lowes. Fingers crossed that I don't have a big piece of garbage in my kitchen.

title: I love this stove--when it works.......
text:
I purchased this GE profile induction stove early in 2016 From Sears appliances. It worked great for the first 18 months or so. Induction cooking is great--heat controlled, easy to clean, fast--I don't think I could go back to gas (using the smoke detector for a cooking timer) or regular electric (waiting for the unit to finally heat up, then cleaning all the unit pans from the boil-overs and grease splatters that inevitably happen). BUT, after the first 18 months, this stove has been on about a 3-day work week--it cannot be depended upon to work on any given day or time. It intermittently shuts itself off and refuses to work, then a day or two later will magically agree to come to work for no apparent reason whatsoever. Just try to invite friends to dinner and the stove will go on vacation. Christmas dinner was an adventure.

The circuit breaker for the stove has become my best friend. Sometimes, I can turn off the breaker for a minute or two, and the stove will work. Sometimes I get error code FA92. Thank goodness I purchased an extended warranty, because the repair folks have replaced the big "motherboard" that makes the whole thing work twice, replaced the fan once, and the components for the big stove top unit is coming in a couple weeks. There was another repair for the panel under the touch panel. I'm sure the cost of these repairs (under my extended warranty) cost more than the stove in the first place, so if you buy one of these, be sure to get the warranty!

So in a nutshell, I really like induction cooking. Its clean, safe, and controllable. The downside is that it is a giant computer and if one thing shuts down, the whole stove is dead (except sometimes the oven will work---sometimes) Repair people can only replace components, not really track down problems other than looking up the error code and hope they guessed right.

I am hoping that my stove is just a lemon, and that other stoves, even of the same model, work flawlessly for years, because my next stove (and I don't think this one will ever get fixed) will also be an induction stove.

title: Comparison of Klein 2 quart and 1 quart filters
text:
3 Stars for the 2 quart filter -- 5 stars for the 1 quart model.

I ordered and received the 2 quart filter, but there was a problem with sharp edges along the outside seam. Klein promptly responded and sent a new filter, but sent the 1 quart model, which as it turns out, I like much better.

CONSTRUCTION: The 2 quart filter is tapered at the bottom. The ridged grain of the mesh caused sharp protrusions along the outside seam. I believe this is because those ridges join at an angle on the outside seam. The photo of the product shows those ridges running horizontally but the ridges on mine were vertical. You may not have this problem if your filter arrives with the horizontal grain. The quart filter has flawlessly smooth seams, has the same capacity as the 2 quart filter, and I have the option of using it in either 2-quart or 1-quart mason jars.

Both filters are rigid and sturdy, so no worries about damage when tapping it gently to remove the grounds. There’s no leaking (even upside down) when I use the silicone seal together with the County Line flip top lid: https://smile.amazon.com/County-Line-Kitchen-Leak-Proof-Innovative/dp/B0776YQTLS/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1526670220&sr=8-1&keywords=county+line+kitchen+wide+mouth+flip+cap

CLARITY OF THE BREW: The filters prevent seepage of grounds into the brew and allow for easy removal, but there’s more sediment than I like. (I’m not sure whether my grounds aren’t uniformly coarse enough, or whether the filter isn’t fine enough.) After removing the filter and grounds from the jar, I strain the brew using a pour-over filter holder and paper cone filters and get a sediment-free brew. Some reviewers complain about no instructions, but I noted that they are now clearly printed on the box.

Tip: a plastic canning funnel (about $1.50 at Wally World) fits the opening of the coffee filter and makes it fast and easy to add dry coffee grounds and water.

title: Need to be able to clean this thoroughly.
text:
This seems to be a very well made machine, especially for the price. It REALLY cranks out the ice, but it does make noise until it is full and shuts itself off. The noise is not unbearable, but you WILL hear it unless it is in another room. Does not take up much counter space, (about the size of a Kuerig), and looks nice. Will definitely blend with ss appliances. Makes ice very quickly. Really only complaint is the noise.

Update: I had to send the machine back because you really cannot clean it properly of mold. Many people have said that using a vinegar solution and running this thru the machine will do it, then wiping with a clean towel, any remaining black spots.. However, what I have found is that mold grows INSIDE the unit mechanism(s), and you cannot see this readily, and the vinegar does not clean/kill this. I had thoroughly cleaned the unit and then noticed a black fluid draining from the upper left inside of the compartment. This concerned me greatly, so Amazon, which is always great, took it back, no questions asked. The manufacturer needs to come up with some solution to properly clean this, it could be a serious health hazard to a young, old or sick person. You are literally drinking mold.

title: Looks better with it in place!
text:
We have a GE refrigerator we like (except for the RFID-chipped Water Filter) a lot, and it has a Water/Ice Cude Dispenser in the door which is convenient. Here in Phoenix AZ, we have some of the highest mineral particulates in our city water, and when it splashes and dries, it definitely leaves a mark.
Every month or so, I take a shallow pan, place the drip tray upside down in it and pour enough vinegar to cover the bottom and let it set for about 30 mins. After that, any mineral residue left wipes right off, and we're good for a while. I was looking for something else entirely when I saw these Lopnur Absorbent Drip Catchers, and I was intrigued enough to try them out.
If you look at the photos I posted, you'll see that the pad is smaller than my tray. The size is clearly mentioned on the product page, but the shape seemed right... I think now I'd try the Semi-Circular ones instead. I wiped down the dispenser with vinegar/water and rinsed it clean, and I do notice that the pad does cut down on splashes. I've used it for about a week now, and while it's not the right shape, it seems to actually work!
If this works for a couple months, then I'll probably re-buy these in a different shape so it better fits the curved back edge. They are cheap enough, and I can repurpose the ones I have into coaster mats. Either way, I hope this cuts down on the splatter and cleanup!

title: Whirlpool with v coils-  worked for me
text: I have a whirlpool with the v coils at the bottom. I used a brush similar to this (all wire instead of wood handle) and was successful in getting coils clean. The trick is to bend wire part at right angle to clean coils in sections using access holes provided in coils. Clean the inside and outside of the v,  following access holes to center v.  I had 3 v sections to clean-  front and center v,  I did from front and back v I did from back. I put a rubber hose on a shop vac to get into tight spots. I lifted the fridge front 4” up using a dolly to lift until 4x4 blocks were slipped in-  this made accessing the center v section easier. The brush doesn’t have to go through the small vertical ties on the v- brushing the inside and outside of the v will leave the larger refrigerant coils clean. Take your time to avoid breaking anything. I unplugged elec for safety after turning down temp control to make sure fan/compressor not running.

title: Couldn't get it installed
text:
Looking at my order history, I have ordered this filter 9 previous times, for my dad. It's always been able to be installed in their 9+ year old Samsung fridge without issue. However, this time...this time was different. I saw some of the reviews talking about the filter not installing, but I ordered it anyway when a lightning deal or something came up for it. I've kind of gone back and forth on OEM and 3rd party depending on current pricing over the years, never having an issue with either. I had it delivered to my dad directly, and sure enough I got a text the next day that it's the wrong filter and wouldn't install.

I went over to take a look, and gave it a try. Reading some of the other reviews here, some people were able to get it installed by pushing up a little harder or other tricks. I kind of tried that, but since it wasn't my fridge, I did not want to use too much force and end up breaking something, after all it is just plastic it twists into. So back it went. I purchased a 3rd party filter, and it installed just fine...the bad reviews are real people! Unfortunately I cannot say for sure what fridges are impacted, I am assuming it's older ones more based on the age of my parent's one.

title: Defective upon Arrival
text:
Purchased for a Xmas gift for the family. Followed directions for first time use and then for ice. Got a blinking blue light stating "needs more water" and realized that no water from the reservoir had been pulled up into the freezing tray. Went on line to get troubleshooting info (but the manufacturer's website has issues like "Why is there air coming out of the left side?" and "How can I turn off the nightlight?" as the troubleshooting questions). That didn't help.
Here's the problem (I think)...there are two drain lines from the back. One is from the reservoir and the other is from the freezing tray. Only the reservoir line drains so it means that no water is making it to the freezing tray. The water level of the reservoir doesn't decrease. So either the pump or the selenoid that energizes the valve to open the valve to the freezing trays is defective.
That's a lot of money to have a machine arrive with a faulty pump....Where was QA in the manufacturing process? For this price, I would have expected someone to plug in for a quick op check before it left the manufacturer.
Now we get to see if the manufacturer will stand by the product and a replacement or full refund.

title: The machine is very slow
text: This machine works as described but it is very slow.  It only makes 9 cubes at a time and takes 7-9 minutes for those cubes to form.  The holding basket area is not refrigerated, you need to remove the cubes as soon as they fall into it or they will eventually melt back into the water reservoir.  If you are planning a big party and need a lot of ice, start making it a few weeks before and store in plastic bags in your freezer.  To fill 1 - one gallon plastic bag will take 3-4 hours to complete.  The cubes are small, about an inch in diameter, but if you use them in an insulated cup they will last for a fairly long time.  Use chilled water to make the ice, if you start with room temperature water it takes 3 or 4 rounds before the cubes will be at their largest size.  Once you start making ice you need to monitor it, you can't just start it up and walk away.  The machine itself is small enough to fit on your counter top and stores nicely under a cabinet.  The instructions are easy to follow.

title: Don't expect the claimed temperature accuracy.
text:
I'm guessing that most folks who purchased this weather station never checked the temperature readings against a known accurate thermometer like I did. All thermistor-based thermometers suffer from a non-linear response curve and this unit is no exception. It was impossible to adjust the readings so that they were consistent with the actual outside temperatures. The inaccuracy was about + or - 3 deg F, which exceeds what the manufacturer claims by a considerable margin. For example, in the afternoon the actual (using 2 different Hg thermometers of known accuracy) outdoors temperature would be 35-deg F while the unit would report 38-deg F. In the morning, with an actual temperature of 29-deg F, the unit would report 26-deg F. No amount of compensation adjustment could fix this.
The setup of the main unit was daunting to say the least. This was due to the poor documentation supplied as well as the convoluted non-intuitive setup routine, which involves multiple button presses and entries. Eventually, I figured it out but that doesn't save it from a failure to report the correct outside temperatures - which is the very reason I bought it in the first place.
There are a few 'pros' such as the multicolored back lighting, the substantial transmission distance and the ability to adjust the main unit for the remote unit's temperature readings , but at this price point I expect at least reasonable accuracy.

title: Overpriced and Less than Precise
text:
I made sure to purchase the correct liner for my new Samsung stove. However, the cutouts for the burners definitely do NOT line up with laser-like precision. Only one burner sits correctly, with the opening snug around the raised part of the stovetop. The others fit on top of the raised areas of the stovetop, rather than fitting snugly around them. This will probably cause any spills to flow right under the liner--pretty much canceling out the point of using it. The liner wipes clean, which I guess is a bonus since the ill-fitting cutouts guarantee I'll be doing about the same amount of cleaning.
Inaccurately cut holes may seem irrelevant to the seller, but when customers pay $50 for a product that markets itself as precisely matching each stove's model number, only to find it's not--well, it would seem that this product either needs to lower its price point or ramp up its accuracy. To charge top dollar for an item that's not as advertised is rather shady.
It's difficult to say whether or not this item will be durable, as I've owned it for just a few days. If I notice melting/fraying or any other issues, I will update my review accordingly.

title: Does what it promises.
text:
I got this for some extended travels over a few months where I will be driving from state to state, and will not always have access to a full size unit.

What I like is that it works as described, and cleans my clothes. It's light and easy to move. The spin works really well and really gets the clothes almost dry, to the point I was surprised.

For me, the downsides are; It requires a lot of user attention to get through a load or several loads. The spinner holds about half of what the washer holds, so after your first wash, you move half to the spinner and let it spin, then find a place to put those clothes while you load and spin the second half. then put them all back in the washer for the rinse, followed by a second series of the same thing...for each small load. That being said, I knew all that when ordering, and so it's more that I am disappointed after experiencing what it's actually like to wash with this, but they were clear about what I was getting. It would have been MUCH better to have the spinner of the same capacity as the washer. And even better if they were both the same thing, but they have those, and I didn't buy one because this was cheaper and more portable.

Other notes are that when you start the spin, you have to hold the unit steady while it spins up to full speed. Once it's at full speed it's fine, but getting there involves a lot of vibration and it moves all around. Mine also occasionally makes a grindy/clicky noise for a few seconds during the wash. I hope this is normal operation, and not an indication of something about to break. If it does break, I'll update this. I'm not sure what the supply hose is supposed to fit on. Not any faucet or hose valve I have in my house or have ever seen for sure. Maybe something that is standard in Asia?? But I just fill it with a garden hose and that works fine, and is probably faster too. Finally, it's not exactly a water saving type of washer.

BUT, like I mentioned at the start, I got exactly what was promised, and it should work fine for my needs. But it's not something I would buy for long term use.

title: LEAKS in my refrigerator ! ! !
text:
I would be truly upset had I not been able to easily resolve the problem! I own a year 2000 CROSLEY refrigerator that requires a Whirlpool compatible water filter. A year ago I purchased a Tier1 filter that worked just fine. Although the recommended replacement interim is 6 months, the filter also stipulates "or 300 gallons." As we also use Britta pitchers, it takes us a whole year to run 300 gallons of water through the fridge filter. This new Tier1 filter has the exact same product number (RWF1022) but the day after installation I noticed a trail of droplets running down the outside of the door from just under the dispenser port tray. This led me to investigate more closely and I quickly discovered a steady (every 3 seconds) drip, drip, drip coming out of the dispenser port in the fridge door.

I uninstalled the filter (the water dispenser works without it but the water will be unfiltered) and the dripping immediately stopped. This confirmed my suspicion that it was not mere coincidence but in fact a related issue. I put the new filter side by side with the old one. There were negligible design differences: a slightly different label, modest connector design differences that did not interfere with installation, etc. But as I thought it through, one thing caught my eye despite being difficult to detect at first glance. THE TWO LITTLE BLACK RUBBER O-RING GASKETS AT THE TOP OF THE FILTER ARE SLIGHTLY THINNER THAN THE O-RINGS ON THE OLDER FILTER!

So I removed the filters from both items and put them side-by-side for a close visual comparison. Turns out the rubber O-rings didn't just APPEAR to be thinner... they actually ARE thinner by about one-hundredth of an inch! So I took the old pair of slightly thicker O-rings and fitted them in place on the new filter. This solved the problem. This is an unfortunate choice if it so happens the manufacturer is "cutting corners" to pad profits. Even if it's an honest mistake, it's still going to create problems for some of the consumers who purchase it. In this case, ME! But if it's happening to you and you no longer have your old filter handy to swap O-rings, take one of them off an hie thee to the hardware store where they are plenty cheap. Just be sure you purchase rings that are a tad thicker — NOT BIGGER IN DIAMETER, JUST A WEE BIT THICKER RUBBER WITH THE SAME RING DIAMETER. And here's a hint... If it feels as though they resist installation, a thin smear of petroleum jelly on each O-ring should solve that problem.

title: Physical installation quite easy, wiring a minor chore
text:
We have winter temperature swings here in Chicago of between -15F and 40F. The 'automatic' adjustment of the humidity works exceptionally poorly. My unit is properly installed and passes the diagnostics. I still find myself walking down to the basement to adjust the unit myself. I will probably end up turning off that function and using it like my old 760. Docked 2 stars. Buy the 700M and save some money.

Purchased this to replace an old Aprilaire model 760. This is a drop in replacement - no sheet metal work is needed except to cover the opening of the 760 controller (this unit uses only a 3/4" hole for the humidistat.) You may need to reinforce the sheet metal if, like me, you have any rusting sheet around an old unit. No mounting screws are provided. I used #10 1-1/4" SS sheet metal screws - perfect size for the holes in the 700. Water line uses the same connector as the 760. Kit includes a connector and a new saddle valve - I used the old ones. No copper tubing is provided. If you have a finished basement, your biggest challenge may be running the line for the thermocouple to an outside location out of the sun and above the snow line. This unit has an external 24V power source that will need to be hard-wired to 120V. Be sure to read the pamphlet describing the controller - it clears up any questions you may have on wiring. You'll need to buy some 18-5 and 18-2 copper wire. Probably some 1/2" ID plastic drain tubing.

Units been up two days, is working. Will update if necessary.

title: Looks modern, boils quickly, easy to clean!
text:
[[VIDEOID:83e2bd3d6ecff592e963f16b918a748c]] Update (2023/03): After few months of usage, the largest burner P mode stopped working. Empava sent us a new unit but it only lasted few days until the same problem happened. We tried different induction cookwares bought from Costco. We are now looking to switch back to radiation cooktop.

----------------------------------------------------
We are happy with the cooktop so far! Boiling/cooking is quite fast. Easy to control. Easy to clean. The individual timers on each burner seem to be useful also, though we have tested but not really used often yet.

We also got prompt response from Empara Customer Support when having some issues/questions/concern.

Based on our testing the current in power boost mode on each burner is around 15A, 9A, 7A, 6.5A. They are close to the wattages in the product specs. This probably depends on the quality of the induction cookware as well. When all burners are off, the current is still about 1.8A, which is a reactive current not contributing to the real power/electric bill (according to Empava)

Few observations, though none is matter to us:

Power boost mode is off after few mins. When turning it back on, the burner may or may not output the same wattage for power boost mode. There is probably some sensor to ensure power boost mode is not on when the magnetice coil is overheat or so.

When cooking level is low, boiling is not continuous. It is on for few secs, then off for few secs. This isprobably the same for other induction cooktops out there.

The lock button is quite easy to be touched by accident, like by cleaning. We don't quite need to use this functionality.

When in power boost mode, the sound from the magnetic coil is significant. This is the same for other brand induction cooktops though. The 2 venting fans underneath produce little sound too. Though these are faded out by our hood fan' sound.

So there is still room for improvement but I would still give 5 stars for this price. This product is potentially beating other more popular brands out there by making these improvements.

Hopefully, this is going to last years in out kitchen. We will come back to update this review!

title: Excellent quality, great price, a bit tricky to install
text:
First, this hood looks fantastic. I upgraded all the appliances in a rental apartment to stainless steel, and this fits right in. It works great, is quiet, and the price was incredibly reasonable.

I took off one star because it is tricky to install. In theory, there are keyhole slots, so you should be able to put the mounting screws in pace in the cabinet, and then slide the hood on and tighten the screws down. In practice, my cabinets, like pretty much all cabinets I have ever seen, have a 1" deep lip around the edges on the underside. That means the provided screws are not long enough to reach the bottom of the cabinet itself, since the hood is pressed up against the lip. Also there is no template provided, so it would take some pretty exact measuring to preset the screws in all four corners. In the end, I just had someone hold the hood in place, and used some longer screws to just zip into the underside of the cabinet body. It's a little hard to reach up and over the stove to get the screw gun angled correctly, so it was a bit frustrating, but I was able to finish up in about 20 minutes. Highly recommended product, just know that the installation might take some finessing.

text: This dryer puts out about 120 degree medium flowing air starting from the bottom to vent holes in the top to let the humidity out. I tried drying 5 pairs of jeans and it took 6 hours. Wash cloths can be dried with the clip hangers. How much will this cost to run per month? The formula to figure this is, multiply the wattage the device uses by the amount of hours per day. Then divide by 1000. Then multiply by the kilowatt rate per hour you pay for electricity through your electric company. So for example this dryer runs at 900 watts, multiply by say 6 hours, using per week instead of day, That’s 5400, then divide by 1000. You get 5.4, then multiply the kilowatt per hour you pay through your electric company. I pay .098 cents per hour and I get .5292 cents. title: I'm not convinced this is genuine
text:
I thought that the fact this was sold by and ships from Amazon would mean this is a genuine GE part. I'm not positive that what I received is a counterfeit item, but it had a few red flags that prompted to me to order another one direct from GE and compare the two.

I'll share some observations:

1. The amazon supplied part comes in a blue-fronted box with a shelf hanger, the GE supplied part comes in a white box. Cardboard quality is noticeably different; the GE box is thicker and the inside cardboard is gray. Amazon box is thin and white on both sides

2. The amazon part feels lighter weight than the GE part.

3. Both were shrink wrapped (shrink wrap looked identical) and both had a blue circular sticker on the top. The amazon sticker was a slightly lighter shade of blue.

4. Both had a little carbon residue under the sticker (from the charcoal filter). However the amazon one also had visible grease, and the body of the filter was dirty. GE part looked clean aside from the carbon dust in the top.

5. The GE filter has all the info printed directly on the filter. The Amazon filter had a sticker. The corner of the sticker was folded over on itself which didn't seem right.

6. The Amazon filter has noticeable mold lines on the top ring. You can feel them with a fingertip. The old GE one I removed from my fridge, and the new GE one were both a lot smoother, the plastic also felt 'denser' to the touch. There ARE visible mold lines on the GE part but nowhere near as pronounced.

7. The bottom domed surface of the filter casing has been smoothed/ground a little on the GE parts. The amazon part has a blob of plastic from the injection molding process.

8. The amazon filter produced clear water immediately after installing it. I ran the required amount of water through it and from the first to the last bit, it came out clear. With the GE filter, the first couple of cups had a black/gray tint to them, presumably from the charcoal residue being washed out. GE filters I've bought in the past also had this. It runs clear after a few cups.

9. Both filters produced water that seemed to taste ok. No noticeable difference to each other, and no noticeable difference vs. the old GE filter I removed.

It's possible that the Amazon part is from a newer batch, that they've changed the manufacturing recently, or some other reason. I definitely feel more comfortable with the perceived quality of the GE part, especially considering they are about the same price.

title: Slowly produces ice and not well insulated
text:
Received the EFIC108 Frigidaire ice maker couple days ago. Regarding Likes and Dislikes.
Dislikes: it's not a Frigidaire product; I could not register the product on their site, nor find more info about the ice maker. Frigidaire customer service said it's not their product; they source it out to Curtis International product with Frigidaire's name.
Dislikes: The manual says first ice making cycle will last 8-13 minutes. I filled the reservoir a little more than half full and selected cubes. It took 2 hours to complete the cycle and produce less than a one gallon bag of ice.
Dislikes: Not well insulated. Cubes are hollow so the cubes in the basket start to melt before cycle ends.
Dislikes: The box reads "26 lbs in 24 hours". Could not figure out what that means. The reservoir is only so big and with a max fill up you will run out of water or the ice basket will fill up. Maybe if you monitor the ice maker 24 hours at a stretch and keep adding water and emptying the basket you can make 26 lbs before it poops out.
Not a good investment for me. I'll continue buying 10 lbs of ice at the corner liquor store for $1.79.

title: Not really made for smaller, crank out windows
text:
So I live in a house that's 130+ years old with many parts that are either original or at minimum 60+ years old, including these crank out casement windows. It's hard enough to find an AC that works with them, but then finding a way to cover the remainder of the window is even worse. When I saw this I decided to give it a shot, if it didnt work I was only out 10 bucks.

Long story short I managed to get it installed in about 20 minutes, but while its held up for a week at this point it's not really made for this kind of window.

#1. Its WAY TOO BIG for my 30 inch legnth of window, hence all the extra fabric hanging down that you cant cut off (because the zipper runs almost all the way throughout).

#2. Despite what they show in the photos it also isnt really made for a CRANK "OUT" style window. It took a decent amount of adjusting to line it up in such a way that the zipper was on the inside and the velcro properly fitted around the casement. If you have a window that comes into the house you should have an easier time.

#3 While I'm not complaining that this only cost about $10 USD I absolutely dont expect it to last very long, you can immediately tell that the material isnt made to hold up. Also if you have a wooden frame like I do expect to lose some of it when you have to peel off the velcro (especially when I had to adjust the layout), because that adhesive is STRONG!

Overall it does its function for now, but there are probably much better options - especially if you have similar circumstances to me.

title: Soak for 48 hours in water before installing for water flow

I noticed how much heavier the old filter was when I took it out and I remembered old filters I used to have said to saturate the filter with water by putting it in a glass for 24-48 hours. I tried that and then gave it a couple of good whacks with prongs up to knock out air (like another reviewer mentioned) and I reinstalled and it flows as fast as the old one did now. Hopefully this helps others and the water pressure stays consistent. Tastes like bottled water. Cancelled my return since water flows now. title: Video and instructions here
text:
This ice maker is commonly used to replace a no longer made unit found in Whirlpool, Maytag, Jenn Air, and some other brands. The original model is W1037751. Although many reviews state instructions were included, many others descibe my experience: no instructions at all. Removing the original unit is not intuitive as there are no visible screws, clips, or other fasteners. This YouTube video was extremely helpful: https://youtu.be/Y8sViu2zFnI
But that video does not address replacing a wire harness on the ice maker that is necessary if replacing a W1037751. That process is by far the most time consuming but is doable with these step by step instructions: https://s3.amazonaws.com/sm-backend-production-attachments/instructionsheet-w10885624-reva.pdf
If saving a couple of hundred dollars in repair service by doing it yourself is your thing, then this is the way to go. The sound of water filling the replacement ice maker as soon as I installed it, and the noise of dropping cubes a couple of hours later was gratifying music to my ears. The lack of instructions and tedium of wire replacement are the only negatives.

title: Needs Filters
text:
I assumed this would be a stainless steel meshed filter and would not need to be used with a paper filter. My screen cone filter I use now has eliminated the need to buy filters since it is a filter itself.
I am not sure the reasoning behind having a cone shaped stainless steel filter holder for filters since any cone shaped coffee carafe can hold a filter on its own. Being made out of glass as many carafes are would not need an additional filter holder, whether stainless steel or not.
Also since it is cone shaped it will only work with cone shaped coffee makers. If it had a base to fit on a cup or pot then using a filter with it might make sense.
This is also extremely thin and lightweight stainless steel and I question its ability to actually not leave any residue or have heat problems if it was used with certain holders, such as plastic.
Overall, disappointed since I do not want to go back to using filters yet this product seems to needlessly require them.

Third, water builds up on the top of mugs and glasses and never dries (even after two hours of the fan constantly running on and off) so I take a paper towel and soak up the water.

title: NOISY, FRAGILE but effective
text:
I really, really wanted to give this product a five star review because aesthetically it is simply gorgeous, and makes the kitchen look modern and clean but there are some drawbacks:
1) I use it “ventless”, which means it purifies abs circulates the air. Even with charcoal filters I see no purification so that filter may be a waste of your money. The fab does help eliminate steam that would condensate abs also smoke in general, but don’t think it will eliminate odors.
2) NOISY. Holy smokes. It’s so loud, even someone next to me I can barely hear or understand that person when it’s set on maximum, so keep that in mind, at this price point I expected a better fan/silent design. Is 2021 this is no excuse for cheap fans.
3) “Stainless Steel” casing around it is very thin, so thin that the vent grills came all bent on this unit. I only noticed AFTER I installed abs I was wiping them down how one side was bumped up, simply going with the cleaning rag on it depressed it up and down, but it’s still deformed. If you install your kitchen my advice is INSPECT THOROUGHLY before installing.
4) LIGHT: I love the fact it has nice bright LED lis, I just wish they weren’t all the way in the back, or if they are, at least angle them towards the front. Most people don’t use the back burners, if you do, it’s great, but anything in the front you get about 30% light on it.

Besides these cons, when you turn this helicopter in your kitchen it will suck the smoke nicely, I do like that it has two aluminum mesh filters that you can throw in the dishwasher too. The template made installation nice, just wish our unit wasn’t damaged.

title: Too Many Gounds in the Coffee Cup
text:
I primarily use Gevalia Traditional Roast coffee. Too many coffee grounds get through the filter. I can't drink the last 1/2 inch of coffee in my cup because of that. Many reviews comment on how easy it is to clean the MaxBrew. Not so much for the coffee I use.

To get rid of all the grounds:
1. I tap the side of the MaxBrew over a trash can, which gets some grounds out (but not that much),
2. I put a paper coffee filter (#4 but it doesn't matter as long as it fills the hole) in the sink drain,
3. I run water through the MaxBrew,
4. Once all the grounds are gone from the MaxBrew, I toss the paper filter in the trash after it drains.

Coffee grounds are a bad thing to put down your sink drain or garbage disposal.
Maybe with a coarser ground coffee this wouldn't be necessary. (I buy preground coffee.)

UPDATE: Since I wrote the above review, I've tried several different brands of coffee. Same problem, too many grounds. I've downgraded it one star, but I'm not returning it because that is it's only problem, and I might need it on a rare occasion when I'm without an actual k-cup but have some ground coffee available.

title: Works ok, customer support is very good
text:
After using this for about a year, it's overall just ok. Here are the quick points:

Pros:
- compact for the capacity
- customer service

Cons:
- first unit I got was defective
- provided hose that came with both units leaked
- cleans ok, not great
- doesn't seem like it will last long

I bought this unit because my specific space necessitate quite small dimensions... with these dimensions, you probably can't have a bigger capacity.
When I received the first unit, one of the rotating pieces on the bottom of the unit was clanging against another metal piece. After doing some troubleshooting with support (including me doing some manual work, by their direction), they concluded I couldn't fix it myself. So they sent a new unit to me at no charge. I was very impressed with their support.
Both hoses I got leaked... not just from the threading, but in the connection between the metal and hose... so the hoses are basically useless. Getting a high quality metal replacement from Home Depot is easy and cheap enough, but it's just extra cost and effort that shouldn't have been necessary.

The cleaning power is just ok. The spinning power is pretty good, but maybe the unit needs an agitator or something. I varied the amount of detergent to see if this was it... but either it's too much and makes the clothes dry super stiff and starchy, or it's too little and the clothes still smell coming out. I've had a magic chef that had better results, but the dimensions would not have worked for my current place (the magic chef is also bigger, so that could be why, but price was about the same).

Now after about a year, this unit is starting to make sounds that it did not make before... parts are probably knocking against each other due to plastic deformation or joints loosening over time. It's nothing nearly as bad as the unit I replaced, but it doesn't give me confidence. I wash about once per week. I wanted to get this so that I could do small loads I wouldn't want to pay for a full cycle on my building's laundry machines, and hopefully save money in the long run... however, due to the smaller capacity, and because I don't think this will last a very long time, I don't know that it'll last long enough to make up the cost (not to mention that it's worse cleaning).

Just received my washer today and I am thrilled. We're in the process of building a laundry room but because of money running low, it would be close to a year before we could get a washing machine. Then I heard about these mini washers that were only $100. After watching a ton of YouTube videos and reading alot of reviews, we ordered the Giantex mini. Granted this is our first day so I can't speak to longevity but for functionality I am very happy. We've run several loads and the clothing came out clean, smelling great and almost dry. The machine is very simple to use, fairly quiet and appears sturdy. I highly recommend and am thrilled to not be headed to the laundrymat tonight, 😂.
Update 09/05/18: My mini washer just died! Started a load then noticed I didn't hear it washing. Sure enough the washing tub was not rotating at all. I have always been careful not to stress the machine by overloading. In fact, this time there was 1 pair pants and a pair of shorts. That was it. I checked the fuse inside and that seems fine, so I have no clue. There's no bands loose or off and I know very little about these type of repairs. It was a great little machine but should have lasted more than 2 months.

title: Don't drain well
text:
Melitta coffee filters, After acquiring a percolater for brewing daily coffee, I quickly realized that I needed to have filters to keep the coffee grounds from getting into the coffee. These fit perfectly, and are convenient and are priced decently. So I purchased these with expectations that they would do the job. While they may help to keep some grounds out, vs not having any filter, they I still end up with grounds in the coffee, and a mess of grounds all over the filter. Thankfully the grounds do sink to the bottom of the coffee pot or cup.
I think these are made too thick, not letting the coffee run through very well. I've attempted making a smaller pot with less water, and added less coffee grounds. Still the problem remains, where the basket gets too full, and not draining well. I've had a hard time deciding on how to rate these. While they may be helpful, they still aren't doing their job well. I honestly have better luck tearing up and using simple paper towels.

title: Pump overwhelms my drains
text:
3363394 is the original pump part number I currently have in my Sears Kenmore, "Model 500" 110.28532700. top loader. It is a good washer, for the most part.

I have bought Whirlpool products for years because of their strong performance with me and a recommendations from appliance repair folks.

However, the problem with many new washers (including this one) is that they pump out at such a high rate, it causes my drains to overflow. Our house was built in 1963 and has older code smaller drain diameter. Newer homes have larger diameter drains. I thought this was my house's problem at first. I spent a lot of time and effort checking my drains, only to find out from my hardware store that this problem is very common with the new washers. It is all over the internet.

What were these designers thinking? This pump shoots water out so fast, it backs up my drain and gets water down my wall. I've snaked it and tried many things but after seeing all the complaints on the internet about this problem it is clear that the problem is very widespread and manufacturers are just putting pumps in that are too fast.

This is really not so much a knock on the pump as the washer design -- but both are by Whirlpool, so, touché.

title: Excellent range
text:
To give you a perspective of where I'm coming from, I previously had a 48", 8 burner, double oven Viking range. After moving, I only had room for a 30" range.

Pros:

-Looks good, This is a freestanding range, not a slide in, but it doesn't have a back piece that sticks up. I hate the way those look. You also have to reach over hot burners to get to the controls on most ranges that have the back piece. This is the only range with 2 ovens that is like this except for the Electrolux which is dual fuel and requires a 220 line. The top of the stove (under the burners) is stainless also. On most ranges it is black even if the front is stainless.

-Huge amount of oven space for 30". It has more than my 48" Viking had.

-Lower oven preheats to 350 in 8 minutes, which is pretty fast.

-2 powerful burners. They are higher BTUs than the Viking burners. The left front power burner can also can go down very low- almost like a candle for anything very delicate.

-Electronics. Most ranges have most of these, but the "professional" ranges like Viking do not. This includes timer, temperature probe cooking, delayed start, etc.

-Lower oven has an electric element on the ceiling to produce more even heat than just the gas burner on the floor. Not sure how this affects usage costs (electric costs more than gas almost everywhere in US for ovens). It is not 220, so maybe the draw isn't than much.

-Self cleaning. Yes, even cheap ranges are self cleaning now, but some professional are not. My Viking wasn't.

-Ball bearing rack. It moves very smoothly.

Cons:

-There is only 1 ball bearing rack in the lower oven. The other 2 (1 in upper, 1 in lower) are standard racks. For this price of stove, it would have been nice for them all to be ball bearing.

-The middle oval burner is not very powerful. It works fine with the included griddle for pancakes, etc., but you can't generate enough heat for many things. If I put my cast iron grill/griddle over it (after replacing the griddle with the grate included), it doesn't get hot enough to do a good sear. Griddle is non-stick and will wear out in time. I use the grate instead of the griddle. It looks better and gives you a place to move hot pots/pans.

-The lower oven is low to the ground. If you use the upper rack, it is fine. If you use the lower, it is awkwardly low. I try and use the upper oven and middle lower oven racks mainly, so not a big issue. If you are old, have back problems, etc., take into account that the bottom of the lower oven is almost at the floor.

-The upper oven can handle pizzas, casseroles, veggies, etc. You can't put anything more than probably 6 inches high. You can't roast a whole chicken. I think for most people, that is not a problem as you have the lower oven which is pretty big. Use the upper for sides, keeping food warm, etc. The broiler is in the upper oven also.

-I wouldn't have minded another power burner. The 2 back burners are pretty low output. I guess 2 powerful burners is pretty good.

Other notes:

-The noise from the fan is nothing. Those that complained have super hearing or a defective stove. It is more quiet than my Bosch dishwasher.

-If you like to bake bread, use the lower convection oven. Do your final rise of the dough in the upper oven which will be warm, but not hot from the preheating of the lower oven.

The Home Ranger pulley, particularly this model with the hook over the door, has helped me to quickly regain nearly full range of motion with less pain than expected. I do recommend the book vs the slightly cheaper option with just the strap - it becomes a pain to re-position the strap, whereas the hook just stays in place over the door.

Dislike:
The handle needs to be adjustable so you can have it higher on the rope. I would have to sit on the floor to use the pulleys based on the rope length. title: The water filter didn’t fit my LG fridge, but the air filter did
text:
We have a 6-month old LG French door refrigerator. I checked and double-checked to make sure that these filters would fit our refrigerator. According to the compatibility list, they would, as our fridge needs the LT1000P model filter.)

I removed the existing LG water filter and tried to install the Icepure filter. It would fit into the opening for the filter but it would not complete the 1/4-turn necessary to lock it into place. I read the instructions, and retried to no avail. My partner also tried, and it still wouldn’t lock in place. We then searched Google for any other comments about this product and found that many folks had problems with this filter not fitting their LG even though the compatibility list says it should fit.

We didn’t want to force the filter and end up breaking the connection for the filter given the very high cost of our new refrigerator. It wasn’t worth damaging our fridge to get this water filter to fit. As you can see in my attached picture, the edges of the filter that assist in locking the filter in place is clearly a different shape on this product than the original LG product. I would NOT recommend these water filters for an LG fridge.

title: Nice, but fancy features are just hype
text: The two ovens are both usable, for the wide coursing of the heating elements produced uniform heat in both, even when placing a baking sheet on the bottom rack position. But for this price, you darn well should get a few extra inches of heating rod. The fancy extra features have turned me off. 1) The control buttons. There is an array of 9 and an array of four buttons for the upper over, and a symmetrical array of 4 and 9 for the right. The arrays of 4 are identical; that's good. But in the larger 9-button arrays, only the warm button is in the same place on the two arrays. The buttons you will typically use (bake button, oven light button, broil, etc) are in different places on the two arrays, and so even once you are familiar with the oven, you will be hunting and pecking. 2) The manual. It reads like a computer software manual ("for the pizza feature, select the pizza button"). It does not explain why you would want to select a "pizza feature" instead of just using "bake". Is it hotter? - No, the max temp is still 550F. What's the difference between the separate settings for fresh pizza or frozen? The manual says that "1" is for fresh, "2" is for frozen. Well, that certainly explains it to full intellectual satisfaction. Moving on to the slow cook settings; neither the manual nor the oven display reveals the temperature, but you are asked to select among four types of food and two heat levels. I used a calibrated oven and a long temperature probe to measure the temperature of 4 quarts of water, heating in a 5.5 qt ceramic slow-cook covered pot. When set to "stew" and "Lo" and "7 hr cook time", the water reached 202F by 2 hrs, full simmer of 207F at 2.5 hr, 203 F at 3 hrs, and then dropped slowly, dropping below 200F by 3.5 hr. I don't know of a cook , hoping to retain nutrients and proper food texture by a low temp slow-cooking method, who would choose to nearly boil the stew for over an hour. Using 2 quarts caused hours of frank boiling. When I tried the "beef" and "Hi" setting on 4 quarts of water, it reached 209F by 2 hr and dropped to 200F only by 3.5 hr. Any beef would be cardboard texture by then.  Moving on to the "roast convection", this has nothing to do with roasting (which involves an oiled food in a uniform very hot oven). Instead, the top heating element comes on, which if not used very briefly, will char the topmost part of your otherwise evenly browned food. It is best used when one wants a broiled effect, but desires to keep the door closed. As long as GE won't engage the consumer by providing a mechanistic explanation of its dozens of settings, I would plan on using the ovens only in broil, bake, and convection modes.

title: if it's missing the authentication strip, return it for a full refund
text:
Authentic Samsung water filters come with an authentication strip and a magnet to verify authenticity. The authentication strip is stuck to the filter. You peel it off and place it on the magnet. If green stripes appear on the strip, then it is an authentic Samsung Filter.

If these components are not included with the filter, then you cannot verify that it is an authentic Samsung water filter. Under those circumstances, you should return it to Amazon, selecting "missing parts" as the reason for the return.

The reason Samsung developed this authentication technology to include along with their filters is to combat an industry that produces counterfeit Samsung water filters. The fakes look just like the real thing but do not include Samsung's authentication strip and magnet. Therefore, be warned.

2023 board fails again. Thought order the same board again, looked up Amazon history. Found out I bought both boards exactly 2 years apart…what a coincidence.

Decided to spend alittle more for an OEM board that is GE brand. Fridge works and also the temperature range is better than these boards. It regulates better my freezer is actually 10-15 degree colder than these 2 boards. I’ve done maintenance on temp sensor, heating units in past and with old none OEM boards the fridge did not regulate like the OEM GE boards.

I have an older GE profile fridge and I’m happy that it’s life is holding up. Some retailers would say time to upgrade and I would agree to a point. My fridge is going on 18 years, compressor is solid, wiring not brittle, internals holding up well.

Hope this helps someone deciding to replace their control board. Am I gonna wait another 2 years to see if this OEM board will hold up. Prob’ly not, buying two non GE boards 2 years apart is enough to conclude this product is a subscription to failure.
