title: Audit wiring before applying power
text:
Let me start by saying that the Grizzly H6154 has some good things going for it, but,
out of the box, it is not for the average person.

As stated by " Waydavis, 2/13/2016", the internal wiring should be reviewed, before powering the unit.
It is **NOT** UL marked, anywhere on the unit, or the box, and I suspect the design has never been
submitted for safety testing in the USA. To be fair to Grizzly, this is likely the case, for all similar style
impulse sealers, independent of brand. They all appear to be the same base design, though some vendors
may do a better job of putting them together, than others.

Mine arrived with an internal short, that would arc the wall outlet, when I attempted to plug it in.
After removing the bottom, I found that one of power wires had been pinched between the transformer
and the chassis, causing a short. Looking at the design, this is very likely to happen, on many units,
during shipment. The area above the transformer is used to route wires across the chassis. The transformer
is not properly locked down, with lock washers/thread lock, and the wires are not constrained or protected.
During shipping vibration, the transformer mounting screws loosen, allowing the high-voltage wires to slip
between the transformer and the chassis wall. The transformer is quite heavy, and that part of the chassis
wall has a sharp edge, so the wire insulation is pierced, resulting in a short.

Re-routing and protecting the wires, replacing the shorted connection, and locking down the transformer were
simple tasks. I also added a redundant Chassis to Earth Ground connection. Anyone with basic electrical
knowledge should have no problem making the changes. My unit now works great, and I have good confidence
in it's safety (though I still keep it unplugged, when not in use).

If you are someone who doesn't mind making a few "improvements" to a piece of equipment, the Grizzly H6154 is a
very handy device, with good features. The chassis is cast metal and strong. The lever arm is also well built, as are
the insulated mounts for the thermal wire. At just over $40, it is a good deal, for the handyman type. For anyone looking
to service their unit, please be aware that the control board schematic, in the manual, does not match the one in the
unit. More information on the subject, search for the following:

"Heat Sealer - How can the relay work and not the LED?"

A few tips, for using your sealer:

1. You will burn the Teflon fabric cover, if you run the sealer, for more than a couple seconds,
without bag material in the clamp. Be sure to test longer seal times with bag material in the clamp.

2. As mentioned by " Waydavis", you might want to adjust the lever arm activation switch, so it
engages just before the arm is fully seated.

3. Seal times seem to vary with bag material, thickness and width. I recommend practicing with on
the target material, before actually trying to seal a bag (start with a low setting).

4. Sealing will start as soon as the lever arm switch is activated. Try to be consistent with how fast you
close the arm, relative to your test runs.

5. If the seal time is too high, the bag material will melt, and stick to the Teflon fabric. Future seals will be
uneven, due to the clumps. It may be necessary to replace the fabric strip, if this occurs. Two spares come
with the unit, and replacement kits are available.

6. If the temperature is too low, the seal will lack definition, and will not match the grain of the Teflon fabric.
If it is too high, the seal will bleed into the neighboring bag material, due to heat conduction. I found I got the
best seal, when the seal closely matched the Teflon fabric grain, but caused minimal deformation of the
neighboring bag material.

text:
I've wanted a built-in ice maker for some time. There are 7 of us sharing the ice maker in a fridge and it just never cut it! I had two options in ice makers: nugget or cube. Nugget ice is much more fun, but it's not good for coolers. Cube ice works for both. So I got the cube maker. If I ever win the lottery, I'll get the other one too!

Anyway, the machine was a pain to install, but that's not its fault. First I hired someone because they had to move my fridge, tap a water line, and break through the wall to install the drain. They screwed all of that up and I ended up with a leak, a damaged fridge, and the drain line was leaking as well. They fixed two of the three a week later and now it works well (though the fridge is another story). The instructions were poor, that caused some of the problem (even the professional misread them). I mean, if you're selling a $500 product, can't you afford proper instructions with real pictures written by someone who speaks English?

All that aside, there is one thing I took off a star for: The unit doesn't stay frozen! It makes ice and dumps it in a fridge. It melts because that is a fridge not a freezer. And then it makes more ice. This causes a lot of wasted water and electricity, and it means that you absolutely must have that drain line installed!

I had another one of these some time back that cost a lot less and made about half as much ice a day. That one was insulated and stayed below 0, so the ice never melted! I didn't even connect the drain line and in 4 years of use, it never leaked. If I were to go back to the start of this project, I would have gotten that again. That's the reason I took off a star. The other style would have saved energy and cost $200 instead of $500... But overall, considering that I got the item at a discount here, I'm okay with this outcome.

text:
This machine cleans really well. Most of the time. Which is in comparison to our old machine, which made you wash the dishes before you had the machine wash them. That's the pro. Here are the cons:

CONS:
1) The terrible beeping at the end of the cycle. I was able to get it to go away after the end of a cycle (which kept waking us up at night) by watching some youtube videos. That should be addressed in the user manual.

2) How on earth are you supposed to get this thing to resume a cycle once you have opened the door mistakenly during a cycle?!!! All of the user manuals which address this refer to the panel on the front of the machine... which this machine does not have. Have not found a youtube for that yet. I HATE HAVING TO RUN A WHOLE NEW CYCLE after someone mistakenly opens the door during a cycle.

3) Related to points #1 and #2, you don't know when the cycle is over if you turn off the beeping. There is no indicator light that I have been able to find that displays once the cycle is complete. Which leads to opening the door early on occasion... which leads to a WHOLE NEW CYCLE being run. A huge waste of energy and water.

So in summary, this machine cleans well but is a pain to figure out how to run because the user interface is very poorly designed.

title: Avoid this one
text:
Decided to go with this model after researching the various ones on Amazon and the video review another woman posted. With the discount and an Amazon gift card applied it was worth the purchase I thought. Waited a week and it arrived. Opened and set up that day. The box it arrived in was horribly shredded. It was basically being held together by plastic ties and that was it. No idea if that’s from their handling or fedex handling. Added water using a bucket (as everyone states the included hose attachment is pointless and attaches to no faucet anywhere). Started up the wash cycle and tried to figure out an accurate soap amount. It was amazing to watch the wash cycle. Although no matter what clothes went in they end up twisting and tangling into a knot because the cycle is a little too vigorous but at least you know it does a good wash. Cycle ended and moved items to the spin side. And that’s where the excitement ended. Nothing but clicking. I rearranged the clothes and tried again. Nothing. Took some clothes out. Nothing. So on the phone with Amazon because apparently I have to pay to send this large defective machine back to the seller which means I’m losing money on a product that didn’t work. Amazon got a hold of the company and we got a response within 24 hours. They immediately apologized and offered a full refund or a replacement but also said I did t have to return the broken machine. I took the refund. So I now have a washer that works semi well but I have to physically wring out all my clothes and have to reconfigure how I rinse them. They take much longer to dry because hand wringing doesn’t take out much water.
So the two stars are for the good customer service I received from the company (not the third party seller, the company themselves handled it) and for the fact the washer side is decent.
Overall not worth the hassle and I’m stuck with a machine that only partially works.
The company obviously knows it’s selling a poor product to offer a quick refund/replacement and not want the machine back.

title: Almost great
text:
The hood itself looks nice, and definitely moves adequate air without being particularly loud. The push-buttons on the front feel a little cheap/loose, but at less than $90 it’s not enough to complain about.

My one significant gripe is in regard to the installation instructions and hardware provided. The only included hardware is 4 drywall screws, but (since this is an under cabinet hood) I’d assume most people plan to install it to a cabinet rather than drywall. Since the holes are pre-drilled, there’s no way to guarantee (or avoid) securing to a stud, and I don’t trust drywall anchors to hold a device that weighs several pounds.

There are instructions provided for hanging from a cabinet, but the instructions explicitly show running the bolts upwards from within the hood- which would leave you with a significant length of screw/bolt sticking up into you cabinet. You’ll also need to drill a separate hole for the plug- this is not mentioned. I used a 1” spade bit and that gave me just enough room as there’s no way to temporarily remove the plug to put the smaller end of the cord through later.

I ended up using the drywall anchors, but still drilled a separate bolt and washer (M5 fits) to help support, and to reduce the sag of the front side.

I’d go 4 stars, but the installation issues are frustrating.

We haven’t moved into the house yet, so I’ll update this in a few months after some use.

title: Better than hand wringing, but I don't entirely love it
text:
UPDATE: I'm downgrading this to 2 stars, and here's why. I've had the machine for about 18 months. First the latch on the lid broke, but it still works as long as I click it manually. Now, no matter how carefully I load it and how forcefully I squeeze out the air bubbles between layers, it shakes violently when it's running. The latest thing is it's stopping about 90 seconds into the spin cycle, so either the motor is wearing out or the timer is broken. I expect better at this price point for something that has carefully been used by one person a few times per week in the same spot for less than two years. I worry it's going to fail entirely one day soon, leaving me in the lurch. I won't be able to get it repaired for an affordable price, so it's more junk to send to the landfill. This is not acceptable.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: My clothes washer has been broken since THANKSGIVING, and thanks to the pandemic and my rural area, I cannot find anyone to repair it. Going to the laundromat isn't a viable solution for a number of reasons, so I've been hand washing nearly everything. The wringing was the worst part of it all, so I purchased this spinner.

First, it does centrifuge well. So far, I haven't had to run it more than about two minutes to get everything dry enough to finish on the line. Five stars there.

However, I have a couple of issues with the spigot. If you are washing a few loads separately and adding them as they are complete to the spinner, water will start to run out of the spigot. I'm glad I heard it dripping, so I didn't have a terrible slipping accident in the bathroom. Be sure to put your water collection container in place as soon as you start adding laundry to the machine.

Also, the spigot is positioned so low on the machine that it's hard to find a container low enough and yet sizable enough to catch the water. Even a dish tub/restaurant bus tub was too tall, and a bucket was out of the question. I had planned to put the spinner in my tub for draining, but the cord is far too short for that, and I hesitate to use an extension cord with this (I might later, if I find out it's safe). At this price, a great addition from the manufacturer would be an optional drain tube like you get with small portable washers.

Overall, it's better than hand wringing, but it's a bit of a pain to use. I'm going to have to buy a plant trolley so I can wheel it into my tiny bathroom when I need to use it. That's not the fault of the machine, but something to think about if you'll be storing it outside where you use it.

title: Defrost quit working after installing this board
text:
The defrost on the fridge worked fine before this board.

Jenn Air: JCD2389DEB

I needed a new board because the compressor and fans were not running on mine. After going through the wiring diagram I found that the neutral leg goes through the board to make all of these things work. I had tested every other part on my fridge before I bypassed the board and everything worked. I had replaced my board a few years ago for the defrost issue that is common on these fridges so I assumed it wouldn't be that again. Wrong. I installed this new board and my compressor and fans worked like they should but two weeks later my freezer is all frosted up so this board was defective out of the box. Luckily I am still within the 30 day refund period. I will try a different brand.

title: Good tasting water, doesnt last very long...
text:
This filter was reasonably priced(compared to other compatible filters) and if you decide to stock up and buy 2 or more at the same time, you will save a few bucks, which is a good idea because they don't seem to last as long as other brands.
The filter was easy to install - just pop the old one out and insert the new one, run the water until you get a steady stream of clear(at first it will spurt for awhile as the air gets out of the line; the water may be a bit cloudy as well, but be patient!)
I have a Kitchenaid with an indicator light which will turn to yellow when the filter is nearing its end, and then to red when it is done. With the first replacement filter, I seem to recall it lasting about 4 months before the light changed to yellow. We drink a fair amount of water, but dont really use the filtered water for much else. If this filter lasts less than 6 months I may try a different brand....it may be worth paying a little more for a longer life.

Will not work if need WB31T10010 and WB31T10011 GE/Kenmore.
They didn't even come close to replacing the WB31T10010 and WB31T10011needed for my Kenmore GE made stove. The small ones are close and I could use some tin snips to make them work. But the large ones are way off and the burner doesn't fit in them at all. They are also about 1/2" smaller in diameter.

Measurements of these 10124XN pans
Small: outside diameter- 7 7/16" inside range seat area: 6 5/16"
Large outside diameter- 9 5/16" inside range seat area: 8 1/4"

After an hour of research for the WB31T10010 and WB31T10011 you need the Range Kleen 11920-4x (119204X) These are the type B our ranges require

title: Does NOT work!
text:

You can hear it struggling, and you can see it too - you get less than half the 'normal' volume of coffee come thru. finally! Especially if you set your burr grinder on 'fine' (for espresso strength) my Keurig simply quit after being unable to push even a third of a cup of the brew! Also like some reviewers said, it is prone to "leak" during brewing if you leave some grinds on the sealing ring = weak coffee!
I saw it all in the pictures, got enticed by the silicone rubber seals on the lid, bought it against my own better judgement.. dumb, dumb!
Don't waste your money - buy something with a full side of mesh!

title: Inconsistent, but ok
text:
The problem with this device is that the results are inconsistent and mostly result in weak espresso. Specifically, about 1 time out of 10, the outcome is good, other times weak. It's not clear why, but I suspect that it is mainly because the capsules cannot hold sufficient coffee. Sometimes, somehow the results are good, but who really has time to perform endless structured tests to find out why. Not me...and probably not most people.

Now due the good news... They are well built and easy to clean...and every now and then the results are OK. Never as good as regular pods, but OK... So that is ok.

Not really sure what the brush is for, but it is not helpful to clean the pods after brew... The coffee is compressed in the pods.. The brush is soft. A better tool, which I purchased, would be a metal snuff spoon, so the compressed coffee can be picked out.

So yes, I would recommend these, but with the caveat that they are just OK. I will continue using them and maybe after a few thousand brews I will find the exact usage process to yield better results.

Good luck

title: DOES NOT FIT AS DESCRIBED
text: We recently purchased a new induction range to replace our ancient (40+ years) Hotpoint range. As expected, the oven element on the Hotpoint broke just before Thanksgiving and our new stove wasn't coming until January. Not wanting to spend a ton of money fixing a stove destined for recycling, I ordered this element because the description stated it would fit. WRONG. The contacts were too far apart and the screw holes were too small. I was not about to send it back so I made it work. I bored larger holes in the contacts and tapped new mounting holes in the back wall of the oven. Voila!  It worked! A special thank you goes out to the reviewer who suggested clamping/connecting vice grips to the short oven wires to keep them for falling back inside. I did just that and saved myself (and my family) from a lot of swearing!!! 4 stars because it works (minus 1 star for the hour + I spent making it fit).

title: One absolute beast of a dryer vent!
text:
This is one absolute beast of a dryer vent. After many years struggling with plastic or flimsy aluminum flapper vents, this is the vent to have. Extremely well built and HEAVY!. The only issue I had during installation was that the opening for the vent pipe was 1/8" smaller than 4". This required some adjustments to the vent pipe to make it fit. I used tin snips to cut 5/8" fingers in the end of the pipe, inserted it into the vent and then bent the fingers to hold the pipe into the vent. A bead of sealant and no leaks. Dryer seems to be happier and working better with less restrictive air flow.

Overall, one incredible vent that will probably last the lifetime of my house.

title: Not Sure if Leakage is Normal
text:
I'm still testing it and will update my review after more use. I just got it a week ago (REALLY FAST SHIPPING!). I ordered it Sunday though the ETA was the following week.

The packaging was discreet and doesn't say it's a washer for those worried that their landlord might see it. Unfortunately for me, I bought it with the dryer and the box that has the Pandra dryer shows in the label what it contains. I think the manager might have guessed what the other box contains but he didn't say anything. I had to use a dolly ($25 in Home Depot) to carry it from my manager's office to the third floor) but it did the job. It can be easily carried by a man without the need for a dolly.

So far, it's good EXCEPT for the leakage. I've run two loads (about 2-3 items each) in 2 consecutive days and on both occasions water leaked. I'll clean it up only to find the following morning that some water still leaked out and it's all over my toilet floor. It's not a lot but it was annoying enough that I had to remove my mats so it won't get soaked. I'm not sure if this is normal so I'm still observing it. I'll try again and this time will drain the residual water longer to see if that will solve the problem.

UPDATE: I'm on the third week (?) and have used this washer 2 more times since my last review. Both were huge batches.

The good: It cleans my clothes better than my laundromat. I just know.

The bad: The agitator is quite strong. Maybe that's why it cleans really well. But it's so strong it somehow unzips my mesh bags while washing, and some of the clothes in it comes out after 6 minutes of washing. These are good mesh bags and it seems impossible when you look at it that it'll be unzipped. As a lot of people here recommended, mesh bags are used not just for delicates but for long sleeves. otherwise, they'll all tangle down there.

The lint remover as someone said here is really useless and dislodges after a couple of uses. You can throw it away. I leave the lint removing job with my Panda dryer which is pretty good at that.

Speaking of lint, I concluded that the only place I can drain the water into without clogging is the toilet bowl. Others here have suggested using stockings, finch socks, lint catcher and whatnots but I don't want all that. There's already so many inconveniences to deal with with this washer. I don't want to add another one. If you're draining into the kitchen sink, bath tub or bathroom sink, you will need those but if you're washing in the bathroom, the toilet bowl is the best drainage. I tried the bath tub and I wouldn't do it again. With that strong agitator, the amount of lint when I washed 3 small face towels was ridiculous.

The drain pump is very weak. I needed to elevate the washer to fully drain the hose after use. When I left the residual water without helping it drain out completely, I found it all over my floor the following morning.

But the leakage DURING the washing/spinning/draining can't be helped. I don't know what's causing it. I've read all the reviews here on what is proper use and what is not but it's still leaking so it must be something inside I can't see. Some here said theirs don't leak and I've asked some guys in youtube who reviewed the item and they said their washers don't leak either. I hate returning items so I'll just live with it I guess. I'm putting a bath towel underneath. If it gets soaked, well I can always spin it. This is not a very ladylike washer!! Lots of lifting involved and wiping the floor for spillage and once, I freaked out when the hose got detached from the faucet and water spilled all over my bathroom floor!! =)

The hose is quite short. It's not ideal for where I positioned it in my bathroom. I needed a longer hose like at least 6 feet. I made a couple of trips to Home Depot to get a longer hose. I'm still on the lookout for better solutions coz the ideal source of water for me would be the shower spout, not the sink faucet which takes forever to fill up the washer tub. I might try next this "Danco Versa Spray Handheld Shower Head" or just buy a pail, make this whole process even more manual than it already is!

Everything as is, the time it took me to wash about 1 jeans, 2 dress pants, 5-6 lingerie, 2 long sleeves, 1 robe, 4 sleeveless shirts was 2.5 - 3 hrs. With the dryer, I would say total of 3.5 - 4 hrs. That's about 2 hrs more compared to going to my laundromat. It's still convenient to not have to travel to the laundromat carrying my one month's worth of laundry but it does take longer and it's very manual. Plus my sheets are always clean now, so are my small items (lingerie, towels, scarves, socks, active wear, etc). I don't have to plan my laundry day anymore. So yes it's still worth it.

title: Great Ice Maker / HIGHLY DISPOSABLE / Not worth the money!
text:
Let me first say, I love (d) my GE Opal ice maker. The ice maker produces great ice, it is very easy to operate.

However, it is a high maintenance machine. I knew that when spending as much money as I did on the machine I definitely wanted it to last me a long time. So I was certain to do the following:

1- use only purified water
2- place the water tank a good distance away, so that it would not over heat
3 - clean frequently, like once monthly with a professional ice machine cleaner

Even so, my first machine lasted me right at 12 months and the company sent a replacement machine…. After a painful process.

My second machine (the replacement) which I used the same precautions… lasted right at 18 months. This was passed the warranty period. Do not fear, maybe it was repairable. Just kidding, it is not. Turns out. This high dollar ice maker is highly disposable. DO NOT, I repeat DO NOT waste your money!

title: Suspect counterfeit filter
text:
There are notable differences between a genuine GSWF filter and the one I received. The biggest difference being that the installation handle is not parallel to the shelves after installation. All filters up to this point have had a horizontal handle and not a 45 degree angle such as this one.

The genuine filter that I removed was made in Taiwan and had a decal for a label. This filter is “made in USA” and is printed directly on the filter. There are several typos on the label.The genuine filter has a Uniform Plumbing Code shield while the suspect filter has an NSF circle.

The safety seal when removed left a film on the filter that could only be removed with a razor. Under the safety seal, the center is white and not blue like the genuine GE.

The installation adapter is only pressed fit to the body and not plastic welded like the genuine GE. There is a small gap between the adapter and body.

Installation went fine, the box looked legit. Buyer Beware!

This time I bought new, definitely original manufacturer parts, and glad I also got the pulley, because that was the screaming part. Four of the six drum rollers also needed replacing.

Silent night!

Big job for me. Your mileage may vary. But this had enough clips, simple enough install once I got the dryer apart. The belt was shorter than the one in my machine, but this is the correct kit according to the maytag site. So maybe my belt had stretched. Don't know. Didn't replace the belt as mine was good.

If you have my dryer, you may need two more rollers. The only thing I need now is a new blower wheel, but that will have to wait.

Don't wait up for the sequel. Just be glad like I am that this tale has a felicitous end.

title: Fortunately this model has both horizontal and vertical exhaust options
text: We had to do a lot of research to find out a suitable hood that would fit into our kitchen and would not require a major hose work. Most of the models have a vertical vent option. Fortunately this model has both horizontal and vertical exhaust options. We wanted the new hood to fit nicely under the cabinets (and sandwiched between cabinets on either side), which it did very nicely. This hood did not require any movement of the existing cabinets and the exhaust vent fitted very nicely with our existing outlet without disturbing the electrical outlets. The LED lights provide very bright light and illuminate the stove and the surrounding area. The exhaust fan is very powerful and can expel the strongest of the smokes and odors very quickly. It has a variable speed setting to adjust according to your needs. The sound is not too distracting if you operate the exhaust at the lowest level. The only downside (if you consider it) is that the switches are hidden from the view so you have to reach out inside (my wife is ok with that) The stainless steel finish is very nice and allows for easy cleaning.  Overall it is a very nice product at  a reasonable price and is strongly recommended.

The company does not claim the pods will do that either. Having said that, I was impressed with the pods once I got the technique right. Here are a few things you should pay attention to: a) the coffee grind has to be fine (not as fine as flour but finer than those medium roast you get at Starbucks). Yes, it will be watered down when compared to an original pod because it never reaches the 15 bars of pressure that one sealed pod does. However, the results are pretty good imo. text:

The Deflecto rods are more flexible which is a bad thing, it causes them to twist and wrap upon themselves. Also, the metal joints are raised on the Deflecto vs the flush joints on the LintEater. title: Buy a different Incubator
text:
Update: we just tried our second incubation. The digital panel is messed up and won’t reset the days counter and it won’t set to work the rollers unless I put it on “duck” eggs (which is not what I’m incubating). This time, zero eggs from the lower deck developed (yes all were fertile eggs- we’ve raised and hatched chickens for 10 years). Also the panned glitched one day and beeped incessantly for no reason while flickering like it was possessed for about 8 minutes. Buy something else if you plan to use it more than once.

We had an overall 70% hatch rate even using older eggs. It kept the environment very well. The thing that was difficult was the double deck made it hard to take apart at day 18 (before lockdown), candle all the eggs and keep temps. Also we had a higher hatch rate on the bottom so it was challenging to get the chicks out without losing temp or humidity. With so many hatching we had to get some out. We had hatching starting on day 21 and it went till day 24. By then it also smelled bad because of the humidity and the hatched eggs and the poop! Overall I’m very pleased.

title: LG is awful
text:
We purchased this refrigerator in February and it has had problems ever since. Almost immediately, the ice maker would stop working and needed to be cleaned out. That isn't the major issue, though.

The major issue is LG's refusal to fix their problems. We started noticing a petrochemical smell in the refrigerator. It would make the ice, eggs, cheese and anything with fats in it taste horrible. So I called LG. They sent a technician out and they had a face time call with their help desk. They said because there are ziplock bags in the freezer, it is making the odor. We removed the ziplock bags an cleaned the refrigerator. The smell persisted. I called again, they sent the same technician out and repeated the same process. This time they said that it is because there is food in the refrigerator that it is causing the smell. This is a distinct plastic smell that is overwhelming. It cannot be caused by food. LG is giving us the run around and refusing to take ownership of this faulty product. They are constantly blaming it on us.

I've done research and it turns out that LG has used a discount plastic liner that decomposes and causes this foul odor and causing the food to taste bad. It is unknown whether this is toxic or not. LG will not comment on any toxicity or even acknowledge that there is a problem. This could be toxic and putting my family and others at risk a d LG is refusing to address it. They are making one excuse after another and shifting the blame on us. I will never buy LG again.

title: Excellent service, Malfunctioning and flimsy product
text:
There are three parts to this review and I will try to keep this short and precise.

Quality of the product itself:
1) It is quite unbelievable how this product is worth $99. When I first opened the box, I thought I received a 5 lb toy. The plastic is thin and flimsy, not to mention that it is not even spinning, just like what the other reviewer had stated in his/her one star review. Having lived in Asia for many years, I can venture a guess how much this product REALLY is worth... sadly, I have to say, this thing is WAY overpriced. The margins are HIGH!!!
2) As shown in the pictures, there were cracks and "fractures" all over the machine, possibly due to damage during delivery. There are also leakages everywhere, which I honestly believe that it could be a safety hazard if the water goes into the motor and electric wires, and apparently was evident after we unscrewed the thing.
3) As an attempt to reconstruct this damaged product since it's already broken anyway, we took it apart and played with it. We ended up using the glue gun to repair the leakages and fix the motor belt so that it is aligned with the spinning wheel - right now we are giving it a test run as I am typing this. Will see if it works without flooding the bathroom.

Packaging:
1) There is no bubble wrap or any kind of protective layers of packaging other than a thin paper box which is what it comes in with. I am positive that this contributes to the several areas of damage to the machine, and that's truly a pity. I have initially posted several pictures demonstrating the cracks and damages, but was later contacted by the seller, asking me to remove them. Taking into the consideration that the majority of the buyers seemed to have a great experience with this machine, I honored her request and took the pictures off. Email me privately if you are interested in seeing those pictures.

Seller:
1) The seller is certainly worth complimenting. A representative, Christine emailed me back almost 5 minutes later when I first asked for a replacement. Prompt feedback, good customer service, and agreed to give me a full refund for the damaged product. At least the seller is willing to work with the customers and provide the help needed.

title: New Cooktop is great!
text:
Our new cooktop, the Frigidaire FFEC3024LB, fit all of our needs. The best part was the installation process. The instructions were very clear and concise. Not being very familiar in installing a cook top before I began by dismantling the old one in order to disconnect the electrical connections. Don't bother. The new Frigidaire comes with the connections already connected leaving you the only task of connecting the unit to the home's electrical source. Save some time and effort by just disconnecting the old from the wall source and connecting the new in its place. Total time for installation by a do-it-yourselfer was about 45 minutes to and hour. Also, the old cook top fit in the new cook top's packing. Easy for disposal at curbside on garbage pick up day.

In addition I had to trim the opening slightly for the new cook top to fit. It replaced a same size cook top but the dimensions needed were 1/16th of an inch more. A hand sander did the trick and the new stove top fit nicely.

The stove top has performed as expected. The larger controls are nice and are easily removable for cleaning. The controls each have very clear temperature selection stops and a delineated simmer selection that is very handy.

We had considered getting the white model but settled for the black model due to concerns with keeping it looking nice. So far cleaning is a snap and we only use hot water, soft cleaning rag and an occasional small application of dish soap followed by a water only based wipe. Very satisfied.

title: You are gambling if you purchase this product.
text:
If anything goes wrong, the seller will 100% ghost you. The manufacturer has no direct internet presence. They are only here on Amazon and one or two other big box company websites that they sell through. They have no manufacturer website, no contact information anywhere, and when you reach out to them through Amazon they will not respond if you have an issue with your purchase.

I really wanted to like this machine. In fact, I loved it ... for the 6 months that it worked. Despite having to buy an additional hose to reach my sink, and an adaptor to fit my sink (as others have mentioned), once I got this little guy up and running, it was wonderful. I was so happy! Laundry was no longer a giant pain in the you know what. It was perfect.

Until it wasn't. After 6 months of perfect use, this machine just stopped working. Water still flows in and out, but the spin/agitate function stopped all together. Zero movement.

I did my internet research — it wasn't the "lid open" indicator being tripped (#1 common reason spinning stops working), it wasn't a problem with the belt, the motor — none of the common issues when a machine stops agitating/spinning.

When one purchases such a large, pricey item, one expects it to work for more than 6 months. Or at the very least, it should come with a warranty. Nope! When I started this process the seller page originally stated to contact them for warranty information. (That phrasing has since been removed and replaced with, "contact Giantex to get information about any additional policies that may apply.")

So I reached out to the seller. Nothing. I contacted Amazon, they reached out to the seller. Nothing. Amazon sent some special message that's supposed to mean they MUST contact within two weeks — nothing. They reported the seller, "that usually gets them to respond." Noth-ing.

6 messages were sent to them between Amazon and myself over the course of 3 1/2 months. One long internet help chate, four lengthy phone calls, supervisors — the works. Amazon was very helpful, but this seller does not exist.

At least, they don't exist once they've got your money.

And, if you think that by some miracle you will get a response from Giantex if there's an issue, just take a look at their return policy before you purchase. 30 day policy — not very helpful for an appliance. (A shirt, or a book? Sure, a 30-day policy makes sense. But an appliance? 30-days doesn't cut it.)

And then take a look at the fees they will charge you for returning it.
Original shipping cost fee...
Return shipping cost fee...
15% restocking fee...

And if it's not in the original box they won't accept it ... yeah, ok. The cost of shipping this back, to receive a replacement or refund, IF the seller actually responds, IF you still have the original packaging (which is not even a full box, btw. It's 5 sides of cardboard with a styrofoam platform held together by what are essentially two industrial-strength zip ties... It's a hot mess.) — At any rate, returning or exchanging will cost nearly as much as your original purchase. They

Just do yourself a favor, and don't take the risk. Not unless you can be happy a gamble of maybe getting 6 months of use out of your purchase.

___

I will note that through this entire process of trying to contact Giantex, the reps on the phone at Amazon were all very nice and appeared to do everything they could to help. Once I got smart and started asking before I hung up the phone, what action I should take next IF they failed to respond to each message within the window, the process became a lot less frustrating. Still frustrating! But less so. I still spent hours on the phone, hours trying to find this manufacturer's contact information, information on how to fix it myself, calls to see about repair options ... but I appreciate Amazon's continued efforts and courteous customer service.

Amazingly, thankfully, after all of that effort, Amazon was kind enough to refund my purchase — even though they did not sell or distribute this product.

title: Rough start, but customer service helped me get it working
text:
Would be 5 stars except that I encountered the same problem as many other reviewers where the machine drained much too quickly to fill the tub at first. I called customer service, and they were very patient and helpful. Other than the need to work out this initial kink (seriously, enough people have had this problem that it should be in the manual), I have no complaints with the machine.

Here are my tips if you also encounter the drainage problem:
1. Lower the load size (if it is set too high, the controller will not allow the tub to fill to the recognized fill line and will drain too much in an attempt to avoid overflowing)
2. Unplug the machine, wait a few minutes, and plug it back in to cause a reset
3. Allow for some draining throughout the cycle (this is normal according to the company), but note that excessive water drainage should only occur during the spin cycle
4. Elevate the hooked segment of the drain hose to 90cm

title: If You Care about the environment, not your coffee
text:
I've used these coffee filters for a few days now, long enough to assess them.

Reports of them falling apart are true, they're very delicate. Folding along the seam is a necessity, not a simple recommendation. If I followed the proper steps, the filter never broke. But how easily the filter broke when I picked it up out of my Melita after brewing makes it clear missteps could lead to grounds in your morning Joe. Time was added to my routine in order to handle the filter with the care it needed. Ultimately, this should not be the fault or responsibility of the coffee-maker, the product simply ought to be sturdier than it is.

Perhaps more important is the taste. You will never fully escape the taste of the paper in filter brewing, but the "If You Care" filter's taste was particularly potent. It yielded strong flavors of cardboard and paper shopping bags, with little sweetness. It dulled more the delicate flavors that came through when I used different filters. I ran a test of doing several washings of the filter, tasting the rinses, and after three washes the taste remained more potent than I'd like. I don't have the time in my morning to give this filter multiple rinses, and then I'm risking weakening the delicate paper even further if I do.

In its defense, and why I don't give it one-star, it accomplishes what it says. For the toxin-conscious, this offers some level of reassurance. There is a bit of a thrill in feeling those moments of health-awareness. But those moments are fleeting, and you're ultimately left with a cup of coffee that would have been better with a different filter. And if you're anything like me, those beans traveled a long way to reach you - and making mediocre coffee with them is as much a waste as anything.

I doubt I'll be buying these again. For the person for whom compostability is highly important, then this is a decent product. It does work. But in doing so you are sacrificing convenience in handling, and sacrificing the flavor of your beans.

This happened to me twice before I gave up and bought a new dishwasher, of course a different brand. After I replaced my piece of crap LG dishwasher I took off the motor and discovered the problem. title: Drying sensors are a joke, and clothes don't "toss" properly
text:
Now that I've finished bashing the matching washer, it's time to turn my attention to the faults of this dryer.

First of all, the so-called "sensor" is a joke. Don't even bother using them; just experiment with whatever Timed Dry setting does the job for you. When I first got the dryer I set it to Casual, which on my former Duet came out to 36 minutes. Worked fine for a load consisting of one queen sheet set (top and bottom sheets + two pillowcases). Casual setting for the same load in this dryer was "supposedly" dry in 20 minutes (What the..???!!?). Naturally everything was still wet.

Speaking of Timed Dry, this machine does NOT let you choose the amount of minutes that you want! There are only pre-sets, and the only useful (ha) ones are 25 mins and 40 mins. Hello???? My old Duet let me set the exact number of minutes, which usually ended up being 37 for 95% of the laundry that I do. But this machine basically forces to you run it for 40, even if your laundry would be perfectly dry in 35 or 37 minutes.

Ours is stacked on top of the matching washer. Although the pair is absolutely level, the clothes "congregate" at the front door and continually wipe against it during the entire dry cycle. What's up with that??? When I complained to Electrolux they told me that my unit must be perfectly level. Well, my 18" spirit level says that it is. Then they said that this happens with "oversized loads". A pair of queen sheets plus 2 pillowcases is "oversized" for this machine? Seriously?????

Honestly I don't know which is worse, this dryer or its matching washer. They are both a huge disappointment and annoyance. My only hope is that I will have sold this house before either of them breaks or the second-year warranty expires.

title: Samsung Induction Range NE599 review
text:
Samsung Induction Range NE599 review

I have been using a portable induction cooktop for two years. It has a "cooking time control" fuction. I like those fuctions very much. I was thinking to switch my convectional range to an induction range if it has cooking time control function.
Recently, Sears reduced the price of Samsung NE599 induction range. I went to the Sears store twice to check the features of this range. The sales indicated the range has "Cooking time control" function because, on the middle of the NE599 control panel, there is a "Cooking Time" touch spot. The "Cooking Time" function is just what I want, plus there is a "Delay Start" function. It looks like a very good deal.

However, I was misled by the sales people and the control panel display. After receiving the NE599 I purchased, I started to test the function. I was shocked because there is no "Cooking Time" control for the induction cooking top! the "Cooking Time" control function is just for convectional baking oven only! What a joke! If the function is only for the baking oven, why the display is not "Baking Time"? I can't believe the $2199 priced range dose not have a function what a $79 priced portable one has!

Pro: Induction heating quickly, delay+cooking time function for baking oven.
Con: easy scratched cooking top glass, no cooking time control for Induction cooking zone, clock display too small

text:

The last couple orders (2nd half of 2018) have come only in a plastic bag, with what appears to be a photocopy of the front of the box as an identifier for the product. These filters have a less substantial feel to them, and no longer properly fit my humidifier. They are approx 1/2-3/4 inch too short on all sides, and most importantly, are not as thick as they were originally. Once they got wet, the fan pulled them forward enough that the water holes no longer lined up with the filter, and water sprayed out the back of the humidifier. I had to take a 2nd filter, and pull it in half thickness wise (which was much easier than expected), and add one of the halves to the filter I had already installed to make it fit properly (thickness wise, and offset so one covered top and right gaps, and other covered bottom and left gaps) and no longer leak.

title: Ice defrosts in the machine and it recycles and is refrozen. It makes the ice taste gross
text:
I loved how stylish it is. But, It is not what I thought an ice machine would be. I am really disappointed with it. I thought it would make ice and keep it frozen. But, that is not what this ice machine does.
After you clean it, turn it on and fill up the basin in the back. It starts immediately and quietly making ice. And the ice tastes fine until it defrosts and the water recycles back into the machine. I don't understand why the machine doesn't keep the ice frozen? We didn't open the lid either it just naturally starts defrosting and drains back into the basin and is recycled back into the ice making process. The recycled ice is so gross. And, you must throw the ice out. And, now you need to clean and dry the basin out before reusing it. And, this machine is big and heavy and you have to tip it over to get the water out of the basin. I don't know why their is not a separate basin for the defrosted ice to make that process easier. And, I dont understand why the machine will not maintain the temperature to keep the ice frozen? It took me a while to figure out why the ice started tasting gross in the same day. It was bc the ice melts and gets drained and recycled to make ice again. So everytime the icetray fills up we did our best to grab the new ice out of the machine and put it in a container in the freezer. It's a lot of work and it got old really fast.. We cleaned it everyday and dried it on the inside too before reusing. I wouldn't have bought this machine if I knew what a hassle it is to use. And, I used it for about a month and now i don't anymore. I would look else where if your considering a ice machine. Its expensive and too much work.

title: Not for Bakers
text:
I cannot talk about the double oven style, but I recently purchased the single wall oven. The first one installed did not work at all. None of the controls would operate properly. When I would set the control to broil, I would get proof. If I tried to bake, I got nothing. After GE insisting on trying to fix it by replacing 4 parts, they finally came to the same conclusion - the oven did not work. They did replace it within a short period of time.

The second oven I received, appeared to work properly. I was able to bake a cheesecake, rum cake, noodle kogel and banana bread pudding without a problem - note all small pan items. When I tried to bake cookies, I discovered a design flaw. My cookie sheets took over almost the complete rack. Should be no problem, right? Not right. The first batch I tried baking on the "bake" setting. My cooking time was 17 minutes. When I went to pull out my cookies, the ones in the upper left corner were browned (beyond where they should be), but the other cookies were not even slightly browned. I had to remove the pan or have burnt cookies in the back. I tried another batch using "convection bake multi rack". The results were even worse. The cookies in the back on both sides were now burning, there was a little color on the outside edges of those on both sides of the oven and a touch along the outside edge of the cookies in the front,but the middle remained very undercooked. The 1st GE tech replaced the broiler unit after noticing that the left side was brighter and on more than the rest of the unit and noting that the temperature was hotter in the back. I tried baking again after this change. The results were the same. The cookies in the back would burn while the ones in the middle were not done. Another tech and another confirmation that the back was hotter than the rest of the oven, this time it was determined that it was at least 25 degrees hotter. I figured out that the fan, which is located in the center of the back of the oven, was drawing the air in and then heated air was being pushed out two elongated vents on either side of it straight up the sides of the oven. This air is at least 25 degrees hotter than the set temperature. My other ovens do not shoot the air straight forward as this one does and I have no problem baking cookies or anything in a larger pan. I advised GE consumer relations about the problem and they say "the oven works as designed". They will not admit there is a problem or offer a solution other than to send out another repair company to come to the same conclusion. By the way, none of the techs or the consumer relations person cook very much and none baked.

My conclusion is - if you are a baker, do NOT buy this oven. If you never cook anything in a larger pan, then the oven may be very nice for you.

title: Bad taste from misinstalling
text:
I have ordered this filter several times, and until now it has always worked well. This time there was a persistently bad taste to the water. I almost threw it away and purchased another, but then discovered (from other amazon.com reviews) that the filter was misinstalled. The problem was that filter not fully inserted. In short, the filter is not correctly inserted until the arrow on the filter lines up with the mark at the middle of the Unlock/Lock line on the refrigerator mount. When you insert it, it goes up and seems to lock into place. However, it still needs to turn another 60 degrees (?) to line up and be fully inserted.

For this last filter, it took an enormous amount of force to get it fully inserted -- so much that I was afraid I would break the filter mount. It pretty much took my full strength to insert.

If the filter is correctly installed, is that it will start out spurting water as the air in the filter clears out, and their may be a small amount of black carbon debris. One way to check if the filter is installed correctly, is to remove it and see if there is water inside it.

Other than the difficult installation, the filter now seems to work well.

title: Not the Della Ice Maker you're looking for....
text:
Della makes a great ice maker, but this model isn't it. You should be looking at this one: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01GOYBWT8/ref=oh_aui_search_detailpage?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Why? This model makes smaller ice (both have a small\/large setting, and the large here is nearer to the small on the linked one), has an optic sensor to know when the bin is full, and that usually halts production with a barely full tray, given how it's engineered. The linked model uses a metal sensor that is a more reliable approach to know when the bin is full. This model is noisier, and slower.

If you never knew the difference and started with this model, you might be pleased enough. It's a surprise that the same maker would have such a swing in quality. I had the linked model and ran it nonstop for about a year when it finally gave up the ghost (I'm not kidding- this household uses a ton of ice). I bought this model thinking that any Della ice maker would be the same, and that's not proven to be true. I have since picked up another example of the linked model, and can confirm it's not a production error kind of deal. This model is going to the garage as a backup for parties and such. As a daily ice maker, it's not up to the task.

title: Double Ovens are  Double Misery!
text:
Frigidaire Gallery -Double Ovens are Double Misery
Have had this oven 8 months. Am amused by “reviews” written 3 hours after delivery. The oven initially would reach temp and then keep dropping. The thermostat was replaced very quickly by the Appliance Store I purchased it from- they immediately sent a very knowlegable professional. Unfortunately the oven is not holding temp again – can be as much as 50 degrees off. Am learning compensation methods. The 3rd time I went to use the lower oven I opened it and the left hinge failed – I almost had my right shoulder pulled out of it’s socket. Scary heavy door to catch!
The most egregious thing is that we roast a lot and the oven shoots smoke out from the area above the door/below controls. If you roast meats/fish you will be washing the walls and windows A LOT. I have a draw fan above the oven and it cannot divert it – it shoots straight out. You cannot roast potatoes under a chicken so they brown in the drippings unless you want to contend with LOTS of smoke. You must put a good ¾ inch of water in the pan to keep most of the smoke down. I am 75 years old and have been baking since I was 12 – we have owned 4 homes. I have had Kenmore, GE, Viking, and Thermador. Nothing has disappointed me as much as this which I had hoped would be my last double oven purchase. Stay away from this double oven, I wish I had. My whole 1st floor of my house is filled with smoke as I write this since I have a roast in the oven!

The new one looks just like the original and functions properly though the quality of construction and assembly is not very good 4 out of the eight screws I checked where loose and required tightening. The auger nut was loose and needed to be tightened. This is what I believe caused the original one to fail, being a loose it allowed the auger to move around in the plastic bush. As there are no alternatives I could only purchase another LG ice bucket.
This is not an indictment of the merchant that I bought the ice bucket from, but my description of the quality of the LG's product.

title: YMMV...It works but may not be worth the trouble or expen$e
text:
The vent works but was more difficult to install than anticipated and only gained a modest reduction in space between the back of the dryer and the wall. Unless you have a near perfect setup, you will definitely need a set of tin snips. Also, to complete the install, you will likely need to use aluminum foil tape to help seal the ends.

Now that I have it installed, I don't believe it was worth the effort or expense. As stated previously the improvement was minor, perhaps 1.5 inches gain. Also, there is one issue not mentioned that is major: Because the periscope vent is rigid, once installed, you have essentially locked in the position of the dryer and cannot move it significantly without having to remove the connection to the wall or dryer. There is no simple pulling the dryer out to retrieve an item or clean behind it. That alone makes me question the long term usability and value of this product.

Bottom line, I am using it but will likely revert back to the flexible aluminum hose vent eventually. It is a great idea but the actual installation and long term usability make it of limited value unless you have just the right situation.

title: If you like ice with NO off-taste or odor, THIS is the machine for you!
text: I've owned this ice maker for about two months and I've been very happy with it.  I bought it specifically because I like a lot of ice in my beverages but I can't stand the taste and/or smell that my refrigerator ice cubes impart on my beverage.  With this little machine, though, there is absolutely no off-odor or taste to the ice cubes.  Also, the ingenious design whereby the ice cubes will slowly melt and be "recycled" into new ice cubes means that there are no "stale" ice cubes sitting around for days.  I use bottled water to make my ice cubes to further ensure that there are no off-tastes or odors.  I usually fill a glass with ice cubes three times a day and there are always more than enough ice cubes waiting for me.  The only thing I would point out is that if you are buying this to make ice for a party, this isn't going to make enough ice for you.  If I had to guess, I'd say that it probably makes enough ice to fill two large glasses every 20 minutes, which wouldn't keep up with the demands for a party with 10+ guests.  The other thing worth noting is that these ice cubes, because of their size and design, tend to melt faster than a traditional rectangular cube.  As such, if you like to add ice to your drink and hope to see ice still in your glass 30-40 minutes later, this might not cut it for you.

title: Panda Ignored All Contact When My Washer Tanked Under Warranty
text:
Edit: While this unit started strong, the product support just has not been there. The lint screen broke and after multiple attempts to order a replacement through Panda went unanswered, we used a guitar pick to wedge it in place and kept going. When the unit started throwing error codes before the warranty expired, I tried emailing and calling every number I could find for Panda warranty and customer service assistance. No one even bothered to respond. Once the warranty actually expired, we went ahead and used it, error codes and all, and it rapidly declined. I would have gladly replaced parts myself to keep this thing running if the company would've returned contact and told me what to purchase. Now it's just another example of more plastic waste.😞
************
My husband paints for a living. My son cooks. I love to garden. Toss a typical teenager in the mix and you have a family of four who tends to produce a mountain of messy (even stinky 😬) laundry. I also keep a careful eye on our budget and we try to live as environmentally conscious as possible. I love this washer. Yes, LOVE. After humans and pets, I'd grab it from a house fire.
I can wash most bedding (we use duvet covers- but I have washed a full and queen comforter (separately, of course), sneakers, delicates, you name it. It cleans like a full-sized washer but takes up a fraction of the space and since I line dry, the optional extra air spin cycle is especially helpful on humid days.
I wash one to two loads a day to keep up with my crew and it has been churning like a quiet little sloshing champ for the last seven months or so.
The only con is (as many seem to note) the lint trap. Ours pops out frequently so we use a floating lint catcher, which works great.
If you have no room for a full-sized washer and are currently burning quarters at a laundromat, this could make a great investment and save you the weekly trip.

title: Nice counter top ice maker
text: The ice maker in our 4 year old Whirlpool fridge decided to die on us and the repair estimate was almost $500! We went several months without ice, but finally had enough and decided that we needed one to make smoothies and because our drinks were just better with ice cubes. We read the the reviews of the various models and finally decided on this Dreamircle. The ice maker is really easy to use. You plug it in, add water and push a button.  While it's making the ice it's quiet, but when the machine is moving the ice from the mold to the tray it makes a little noise. Nothing loud or obnoxious. Just the sound of it hitting the tray. If there's already ice in it, then that seems to absorb some of the sound so you hardly hear it. The size is not bad. It fits under our upper cabinets. In general I don't like a lot of clutter on my counter tops, but for the convenience of having ice, I will take it. The down side is it's not a freezer and won't store the ice. Once the ice is made, you have to use it or it will melt. When it melts, the water goes back into the water reservoir and is reused to make ice. Most of the countertop ice makers did it this way. Anywho, we make the ice, bag it and put the ice in our freezer.  SO other than that one inconvenience, it's been great so far.

title: Cheap parts! Use only in a pinch and replace with OEM parts as soon as you have the money and time!
text: I ordered this valve kit because one of the water valves on the cold water side of my washer started to fail. I bought this set to get my LG front load washer up and running again. The sellers listing was fraudulent because they show two versions of the part, one being OEM and the other a third party item.  They will only send you the third party non-OEM version and the quality is garbage.  The threads on both the cold water and hot water side were not formed properly so you really need make sure the water lines are tight with no movement when you put them on. Do a leak check! Also, the brackets that hold the valve assemblies fixed to the back plate of the washer are either too big or the valve assembly base where the bracket mount is smaller than the original design because both valve assemblies move when you try to tighten the water lines; there should be no movement. Use only in a pinch and replace with OEM parts as soon as you have the money and time!

title: Review of Dometic Icemaker
text: I ordered this ice maker to use in our RV and in our lanai when we have guests. It lives up to its promise to make ice quickly, but I've been disappointed in two things. First, the ice is very "wet" ice.  In fact it starts to melt as soon as it hits the storage container, so that when you scoop out the ice to use it, you get a lot of water with it. Secondly, the stainless steel outside of the ice maker has started to rust and we have only owned the ice maker a bit over a month. It actually started to rust almost immediately. My husband says that to be fair, I should mention that our lanai is outside and we live in Florida, so yes, it's hot outside. But I still think a portable ice maker should be able to handle warm outside temperatures. We used to have an ice maker on our boat and it was amazing in its ability to keep the ice freezing cold and hard in spite of temperatures exceeding 90 degrees in the cabin of the boat. This ice make doesn't do that. In all, I wouldn't buy this ice maker knowing what I know now.

Updated review (want to be sure you read this):
After only 6 months, this unit suddenly made an AWFUL, super LOUD, buzzing sound that scared the heck outta me. Not sure what it could have been but I didn't want to take any chances so I immediately unplugged the unit and it now sits in my garage collecting dust. Sadly, this was a waste of a lot of money. Very expensive paperweight lol

Initial review:
This thing only makes like 8 TINY cubes at a time. And I do mean ITTY BITTY cubes. lol Also, this unit is really noisy-- noisy enough that my mom's darn dogs would bark in the middle of the night at it, waking the whole household up. No bueno. Also, if u don't retrieve the cubes in a timely manner, they melt back into the water hopper, to become reincarnated as NEW tiny ice cubes lol! That concept, IMHO, is pretty neat tho... but the whole interior design of the machine is kinda lame. It gets yucky fairly quickly and cleaning it is a huge hassle. Not to mention, it's impossible to get the whole thing clean so u know if it's yucky where it's visible, then it's...euw where u CAN'T see. Gross.

So for a while I decided to give it a break bcuz I got tired of trying to keep up with this thing. Fast forward about six months later; plugged it in, gave it a quick wipe down and rinsed the inner workings best I could. Then about 10 minutes later, I realized it wasn't getting cold at all (I had made sure to not tip it any, thus causing the refrigerant to leave the cooling pipes). Another two minutes later, it began to make a horrific loud buzzing sound that was worse than the sound the garbage disposal makes when it tries to grind a utensil. So I unplugged it, hauled it out to the garage, where it sits to this day. We got a total of MAYBE two weeks use out of it, but more like 1.5 weeks... 😩 Save your money!

title: This item will work well for you... for about a month.
text:
I bought this item for the house about a month ago (we were still waiting on a new refrigerator we had ordered, so we really needed a way to make ice!). At first we were pleased with the product. It made ice pretty quickly (about every 6-8 minutes), and as long as we got to it quickly enough (either put it in a drink or stored it in the freezer) the ice was good. If you leave it too long the ice will melt, this is not an ice storage device-- merely an ice maker.

Fast forward to this evening. It's dreadfully hot where we live so we have put our (finally!) new refrigerator's ice maker to the test and consumed ice more quickly than the fridge can replace it. No problem, we'll just fire up the ice maker (we thought)... after they typical 6-8 minutes we could hear the first ice getting dropped out. But then, the machinery started making an odd whirring noise like something was stuck, and the little plastic shovel that scoops the newly made ice into the basket would not move forward. Finally after several moments of this whirring machinery noise, the ice maker turned off and red lights started flashing on it. Okay, I thought, I'll just try the ol' "hard reset" and unplug/replug in the machine. This initially seemed to fix the problem-- the scoop moved forward and the ice dropped into the basket. Success-- or so we thought. A few minutes later, same thing: ice drops in, machinery starts fighting for dear life, then quits and the red lights flash.

I finally gave up and turned the machine off.

Obviously I am very disappointed. This was not a super expensive item... but it was not cheap either. To compound matters, our return window closed on 10/2, so now I can't even return it for being suddenly defective. I feel like we're just out our hundred bucks and have a nifty looking doorstop on our kitchen counter.

title: Works well but with some additional guidelines
text:
What can I say. It's a washer & dryer. It does what it's designed to do and it does it pretty well.
There are some notable conditions to properly operating this washing machine that appears to be more trial and error based. Mainly the following:

Both the washer and dryer have a fixed weight and height limit. The former being more important. If there is too much weight, the washer won't operate properly and risks burning out the motor.

The dryer has two weight conditions. It can't be too little weight and it can't be too much weight or the spin cycle won't work properly. That's a matter of trial and error to figure out the exact range. If the spin cycle makes a lot of noise and jumps around a lot, turn it off immediately and check the weight load or you risk damaging the spin cycle motor.

I would recommend not filling the washer past the medium marker. It does have a "high" marker line on the washer but that appears to be too much weight for the washer to handle. As for water amounts, I fill it just slightly above the clothes and that seems to work fine.

Other than those oddball conditions, it works pretty great for an apartment. :-)

It won't hold my dinner plates, which I already knew were too big but I'll mention it anyway. It won't hold the serving pieces of my flatware or even my dinner knives. However, …

This unit does clean. You can hand wash dishes all day long and they won't “feel” as clean as coming out of this unit. It is quiet; more quiet than my regular dishwasher (which has died by the way). It will hold more flatware than it claims, but since my dishwasher has been out for months, I had lots of flatware to wash. I did this by using the basket for fruit washing. Just spread out the flatware. In the dish basket, I filled it with glassware – wine glasses, regular glasses, coffee mugs – and the water that comes out of the spray arm is not forceful. I have not heard anything banging around. Which is good!

I use the bucket method for filling the unit with water. Works well. So all in all, I've ended up giving this unit 4 stars.

title: do not buy for undersink disposal use
text:
This product works great for table lamps around the house, not for undersink use. There must be interference with stainless steel sink, because it does not work with a garbage disposal under the sink. It only works if you open the cabinet and hold the remote like 1 foot away from the receiver. I returned this product to Amazon for a refund. I found a cheaper one on ebay, but had the exact same results. The remote and receiver claim to work up to 15A loads, and most disposals are 1/4HP to 1HP motors, which is 186 to 746W, and on a 110V circuit, that's 1.7 to 6.8A. So this should handle one garbage disposal motor just fine. But under the sink, it doesn't.

What I did find to work with my disposal under the stainless steel sink is an outdoor lighting remote for Xmas lights. For some reason, it doesn't have the interference problems and works great. It just isn't white. And it's not advertised as a garbage disposer wireless switch.

text:
Product looks good but I couldn't use it because it doesn't go into my portafilter. Turns out, product has a dimple on the outside for which there isn't a corresponding groove in my portafilter; although the specs do not say it has a dimple, it's my mistake for not paying detailed attention to the pictures on which you can see the dimple. So, my mistake, my loss; I'll just look for the right one and buy it too. I contacted the vendor intending to buy a second one and asked this question:

My Question:
on September 28, 2022
Is this 51mm pressurized basket also available without the dimple on the side?

Their Answer:
hello dear customer
This product is suitable for your situation
I wish you a happy life
By KunJingDianZi Seller on September 29, 2022

My Reply:
on September 29, 2022
Thank you for your prompt reply.
However, It would be nice if you, at least, would have read the question being asked before giving such a moronic answer.
I bought the product, I tried it, it does not work because it has that external dimple. I need one without the dimple.
What is so hard to understand about that?
When a man of honor does not understand my question, he should ask me for more information, and I would provide it gladly; obviously, that is not you.
Assuming facts not in evidence is called speculation, and you, certainly, are very bad at it.
In the future, try to be an honorable man, because most customers prefer not to do business with people that give speculative non-answers.
Thank you

The Result:
Within a few minutes, I got a reply from Amazon saying my email was undeliverable because their mailbox was full. I find this very interesting because:
1 ) They received and replied to my previous contact whithin 24 hors
2 ) Their non-answer was promptly shown on Amazon as a real answer
3 ) My rebuttal never shows up on Amazon until I included it here just now
4 ) The item's manufacturer is listed as STRNEK, the vendor with the "full mailbox" is STRNEK 1, and STRNEK 1 is posting feedback answers as recent as only three days earlier.
5 ) If their mailbox is really full, How were they able to reply within 24 hours to the other contacts?

Product does look good and, probably, works well, so, two stars, maybe more if I could get it to fit and try it out. The company STRNEK 1, however, gets zero stars for its really poor attitude and bad performance towards current customers seeking to purchase additional goods. That averages one star, which is what they get from me at this time: not recommended.

When we took it apart to see why gas was not staying on at several burners we found an ill manufactured piece forced into place.  This pushed the gas line out of compliance. title: Not absorbing? Soak in HOT water + vinegar
text:
I've gone through several sets of these filters. All had the same issue: they wouldn't wick water beyond the portion of the wick that's submerged in the basin. It's truly maddening, since the original filters worked really well.

Soaked a new set in HOT water + vinegar (2 gallons water, several tablespoons white vinegar), and allowed to soak for 20 minutes. Installed as normal, taking care to ensure the filters were flush against the sides of the unit, so the air must pass through them (and not around them).

Seems to be working MUCH better! Water wicked further up, there's no "new filter" smell, and I'm going through the full 2-gallons of water every ~12-14 hours.

Not sure why this helps. Maybe the combination of HOT water + vinegar partially removes some of the coating? From the insert in the box, the microbial preservatives are: Cellulose (9004-34-6) & Pyrithione zinc (13463-41-7).

Cellulose: stuff in plant fiber
Pyrithione zinc: stuff in anti-dandruff shampoo, has fungistatic and bacteriostatic properties (also used by 3M in household sponges)

Neither of the above should really prevent the wicks from soaking up water, so I'm thinking the hot water/vinegar "softens up" the fibers or something. Whatever it does, it seems to make a huge difference. My humidifier is working again! :)

title: Quiet & powerful range hood – just make sure vent flaps close correctly
text:
[[VIDEOID:b4870dbe25b2486725976822298be21a]] TLDR: This 750 CFM/RH-801 unit looks great, runs very quietly while moving a ton of air, and the lights are very bright. It's a fantastic vented range hood – with one important installation modification.

We originally bought the 750 CFM/RH-01, but realized it was too high (7.5” tall) and the top surface stuck out a lot farther than we liked. The 750 CFM/RH-801 is only 6” tall, and I like the lines a lot more. (I do prefer the light/fan buttons more on the RH-01, but it’s not any kind of deal breaker – just personal preference)

INSTALLATION:
We did this ourselves. If you have DIY experience, it's not too bad, but you will need multiple people (I moved the oven out of the way & used a wood brace to help hold it in place during the install).

I had to make a couple of modifications during the installation:
1) I cut the plug off the power cord, pulled the cord off the top, and pushed it out the back end, so I could pull the wires inside the back wall & wire them into a junction box inside the cabinet above the hood. I appreciate that it comes with a plug - that way, you can check to make sure it's working correctly before installing it.

2) I used my own bolts and sets of large washers to attach the hood to the cabinet above (the supplied hardware was too small. No biggie).
3) Most importantly: I noticed that when the fans were on at the higher speeds, one of the vent flaps (damper) at the top of the unit went past vertical and could not close when the fan was turned off. Instead, it ended up lying on top of the other damper/flap. This would allow cold air to come in from outside.
To prevent this from happening, I added a piece of coat hanger wire inside the vent pipe (see photos: I drilled 2 holes & bent it down on each end & caulked the holes). The wire sits parallel to the hinge of the dampers, and is located about 2 inches above the hinge. This wire prevents the flaps from going past vertical, so they always come back to their original positions.

OPERATION:
1 button (leftmost) turns the lights on/off
You have to press 2 buttons to turn the fans on (only real knock on this design: The taller RH-01 unit is simpler): First, press the rightmost button, then press whatever speed you want: Q, or 3 faster speeds - marked with larger and larger capital I's (again, I think they could have picked better labels, but not a dealbreaker). If you hit the power button again, the fan will turn itself off after a few minutes (or you hit the fan speed button again (to stop the fan), and then the power button (to turn off the light on the power button)

I like the feel of the actual buttons. Our last range hood had labels on the actual buttons, which wore off over time. This should not be a problem with the BV hoods, since the labels are below each button.

The dual fans are really powerful and work smoothly. I did not have to balance (or rebalance) them. They worked well right out of the box.

SOUND LEVELS:
The dual fans are very quiet (see video). Compared to our old hood, even the highest speed allows us to talk without shouting.

LIGHTS:
The 2 lights only have one brightness setting. I was fine with this - our old range hood had 4 different brightness settings, and we only used the brightest setting, so it's nice to be able to hit a single button once to turn lights on, and once to turn them off.

I would prefer a slightly warmer color, but the lights are very bright & cooking on the stove top is very well lit, so no real problems.

PROS:
Powerful fans remove steam/odors efficiently
Very quiet fans
Bright lights
Sleek dishwasher-safe stainless steel filters.

CONS:
You have to press 2 buttons to turn the fans on
Vent flaps may get stuck in the open position

The pros far outweigh the cons, and my vent pipe modification took care of the main drawback.
I highly recommend this range hood.
