title: Recommended for weather watchers
text:
Very handy device! I've taken this out while camping, while riding my horse, and while operating HF. In my non-scientific tests, it's proven reasonably accurate. The anemometer needs to be held in the general direction of the wind to be close to accurate; this can be problematic if the wind direction is changing constantly. I don't consider this a negative, as this is expected of a handheld device like this. The thermometer seems to be unaffected when briefly exposed to direct sunlight.

The anemometer function provides a Beaufort scale, as well as wind speed in mph, kph, knots, feet per second, and meters per second. The display can be set to show max, average, and minimum speeds. Temperature can be displayed in Fahrenheit or Celsius. I like that the meter displays relative humidity, as well. A backlight is available at the push of a button.

Batteries are included, as well as a lanyard and a soft carrying case. The carry case will keep the meter from being scratched up but will not protect it from being damaged by other, heavier objects. This device is not water proof, nor is it marketed as water resistant.

I'm looking forward to using this during the spring storms we see in Kentucky - not in the rains, though! :) I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is interested in weather watching.

title: Despite negative reviews, this product is legit!
text:
I was VERY skeptical of this product after reading several reviews alleging this was somehow a counterfeit product. Long story short, this product is just as advertised and works perfectly.

A few reviews I read mentioned that OEM filters are made in Korea, compared to this "counterfeit" which is made in Mexico. When I opened the box, the first thing I did was check to see where it was made. This product is indeed made in Mexico, so I was highly disappointed at first and fully expected to have to send this back. But I took out my OEM filter to replace with this one, and to my surprise, the original product in my refrigerator was also made in Mexico. After seeing this, I decided to give it a try. I listened very closely for any "strange noises" coming from the fridge that other reviewers said occurred when using this filter. Nothing. There were no strange sounds, no lack of water pressure, absolutely nothing happened, and there was no change to my fridge after installing with this Amazon product.

My only guess is that people are not choosing the correct part number for their refrigerator. Samsung doesn't make it super easy to find the exact model numbers of their units, so maybe this is the cause of the bad reviews. If you match your model number with this filter, you will have no problems with this product. Highly recommended, especially for the low price compared to local retail stores.

title: The amazing flying water filter!
text:
We've owned our Frigidaire for 10 years now and have pretty consistently replaced our Puresource2 water filter about every 12 to 18 months. This last time, didn't work as expected.

As before I slid the new filter in place and proceeded to flush it as directed. Aaaand I almost took a filter to the face as it launched from it's compartment. So I tried it again, this time holding down the filter to see if the pressure would equalize at some point. No such luck. The moment I moved my hand, leaping filters again.

Now, I noticed the filter looked slightly different, but the holes all appeared to be in the same spots and heck, it's a PureSource2, not a 2.1, or 3. But when I called Electrolux they confirmed the design had changed which may result in flying filters.

I have to give Electrolux some credit. There's a workman in my kitchen right now installing a new filter base courtesy of Frigidaire. I just don't understand why. Why change a format just enough that it fits but then can't work? It doesn't make any sense, especially when it now puts Frigidaire on the hook for free replacement parts. It's not like an iPhone where every year it gets thinner, thus rendering all past accessories obsolete. It's a fridge. Once you design the filter you don't need to make it smaller, even if new models are somehow more efficient.

Anyway, if you have a similar issue, call the number on the box. Electrolux is aware of the problem and will make it right.

title: Fine tunes the Aeropress into the espresso maker it's designed to be! BUT SEE WARNING BELOW!
text:
This should actually be part of the standard Aeropress package. If you read the instructions - and I know many don't - the Aeropress is designed to make espresso. IF you want a "regular" 8 oz cup of coffee (An "Americano" - although I don't know anyone who drinks a puny 8 oz cup!) you are supposed to fill it with hot water only to line #1. Most people should fill to line 2 - then stir the grounds with the paddle-shaped Aeropress "stirrer" (note - if you decide to stick with your stock paper filter Aeropress setup USE the paddle! If you stir with anything smaller you'll often move the paper filter and end up with grinds in your cup!).

Then with the Aeropress you push away for about 20 seconds; with this unit you wait one minute, THEN press. And because of the design and the grounds swelling a bit, it takes more pressure. And I'll add - if you stick with the stock
Aeropress filter setup - STILL wait a minute before pressing - your coffee will taste MUCH better!

But with the Trobing unit what comes out of the single hole - like an electric or mechanical espresso maker - is a cup of espresso, with the squirting action and additional pressure creating the "crema" on top - same as any other espresso machine (it increases the "BAR" pressure to that approaching an expensive manual "pressure" - not stovetop - espresso maker);

Then you can drink it straight; or add hot water to make an "Americano" or steamed/frothed milk to make a latte. It's that simple.

The mistake almost everyone I know has made is filling the tube with water (whether using a stock Aeropress or one with this gadget). All that does is make a pretty bad cup of espresso - NOT a cup of coffee! Again - read the Aeropress instructions!

FWIW I use a fairly fine grind made with my "Rocky" grinder and I get virtually no "fines" in my cup. If you do, you probably need toi upgrade your grinder, which is a critical part of the process (NEVER buy ground coffee!!!!!). Cheap griners set on "coarse" generally make a mixture of sand-like grains - and confectioner's sugar! A GOOD grinder makes a consistent grind - but you'll pay for it. Maybe not as much as I did for the Rocky (over $400) - but close.

When it comes to coffee, the grind is an example of "you get what you pay for"! But the Aeropress with the Trobing filter/ejection nipple attachment is an example of an incredible bargain!

It makes better espresso and better cups of Americano coffee than my expensive Breville espresso maker - which is now used only for steaming and frothing milk for lattes, cappucinos, caramel macchiatos etc. - but the espresso part is always made with the Trobing-equipped Aeropress.

And a couple of notes - if you have trouble attaching the unit, you have the filter placed upside-down. Trobing does need to improve the instructions and point out the filter unit only attaches ONE way - however, I get a laugh from those who complain "it doesn't fit!". Just TURN THE THING OVER!

And to empty it - 1) take the cap off with the filtr inside (which may have some grounds on it) and set it aside; 2) still over the trash can, pull back slightly on the Aeropress plunger and then quickly press it down - the "puck" will eject into the trash with a bit of grounds on the rubber tip.

*WARNING*! WHEN YOU EJECT THE PUCK CHECK TO BE SURE YOU DO NOT ALSO EJECT THE METAL SCREEN - I DID, FAILED TO NOTICE AND DUMPED THE TRASH WITH THE SCREEN IN IT. AND WHILE THEY DO SUPPLY AN EXTRA NIPPLE, THEY DO *NOT* SUPPLY A SPARE SCREEN. AND IF YOU LOSE THE SCREEN THE THING'S USELESS.

I am going to have to buy some brand of replacement screen and hope it fits, as I can't find a source for Trobing screens. So I've lowered my rating to 4 stars.

BUT - if you do it right you simply rinse the parts off in the sink. There's no mess and it takes about 30 seconds or less.

IMO every Aeropress owner should have the Trobing attachment. AND a spare screen!

AND again, to those that get "fines" in their coffee, or the coffee tastes bad, or have other issues - READ the Aeropress AND Trobing instructions;

....buy a GOOD coffee grinder (if you REALLY want good coffee plan on spending $200+ for a grinder); grind your coffee immediately before making it; store your beans in sealed (preferably vacuum) containers at room temperature (EVER refrigerate or freeze coffee - cold temperatures destroy it)...

AND NEVER BUY GROUND COFFEE - EVER. Except as a present for someone you don't like. ;-)

title: Ekobrew versus Keurig reusable filter
text: I purchased the Ekobrew refillable cup, after I already had the [[ASIN:B000DLB2FI Keurig My K-Cup Reusable Coffee Filter]]. First off I will say I hated the Keurig reusable filter because it leaked and made a very VERY weak coffee. I love K-cups but they are pricey. So I was looking for another option that would let me use my own bagged coffee. The Ekobrew had the best ratings for the reusable filters. Also the Ekobrew had the best ratings for people who had the Keurig Reusable filter, and more people said they preferred the Ekobrew. The Ekobrew is also cheaper then the Keurig's version. First thing is that it's a better design then the Keurig Reusable filter. You don't have to take apart your system to use this, like you do with the Keurig version. It does not cause the machine to leak as much as the Keurig Reusable Filter does. Like I said there is still some leaking, but most seems to get into the cup. Now as far as the strength of the coffee, I noticed that on the instructions it said that the grind of your coffee will really depend on how strong or weak the coffee is. It says that if it's too fine or too thick of a grind you will have a weak coffee. I do not own a coffee grinder so fine tuning my bagged coffee to a perfect grind, was not an option. On hand I had some [[ASIN:B002C56OBU Community Coffee Ground Coffee, Hazelnut, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 3)]], I found this to be too thick of a grind, and the coffee was very weak. I tried putting it in my food processor in hopes of breaking it down a bit, and it helped ever so slightly. Currently I have [[ASIN:B001EQ4EEW Millstone Hazelnut Cream Ground Coffee, 12-Ounce Packages (Pack of 2)]] which seems to be a finer grind then the Community coffee was, and it is making a bit of a stronger cup of coffee. So if you had a coffee grinder you could probably fine tune your grinds to a perfect cup. All together I think this is the best I've found of the reusable filters. I don't think it's better then a K-cup itself, but it seems to be decent. I do think they need to fine tune these filters a little bit. I will keep using the Ekobrew with the Millstone coffee. I already enjoyed Millstone and it seems to brew a good cup of coffee per my tastes. My recommendations? If you were to buy this, you will probably need to play around to get the cup of coffee that you like best. I would definitely recommend this over the Keurig version. My rating is a three and a half star, but they don't have that option so I gave it a 4.

title: Excellent Quality
text:
An insurance guy recommended that I replace my existing washer hoses with burst-proof hoses. These stainless steel braided hoses satisfied the need.
I decided to get 8 foot instead of 6 foot to have some slack. In hindsight, the 6 foot would have provided enough slack, since the hoses connect at the top of the washer, not the bottom.
I chose this brand instead of other brands because they seemed to have fewer unresolved complaints than the other brands. I inspected the hoses upon arrival and they looked good.
The wrench that came with the hoses was handy for attaching the new hoses. It didn't quite work as well on the old hoses, but I was able to get them loose enough to remove them.
Incidentally, the old hoses were marked with "replace every 5 years." They were installed 13 years ago. The rubber washers and inside of the hoses were showing some signs of deterioration, so it was probably a good thing that I replaced them now.
Incidentally, when I moved the washer to get access to disconnect the old hoses, I noticed a few long-lost socks and a pillowcase behind the washer, along with a lot of dust. I used a Dyson vacuum cleaner and a mop to clean it up before sliding the washer back into place.

title: Laundry POD = Letdown
text: I thought the Laundry POD would prove to be a helpful and convenient product to help my mother stay on top of laundry. She lives in a tiny apartment, and the laundry room is down the road. I thought a Laundry POD would help her save money, time, and hassle... but the Laundry POD ended up being just as much of a hassle. My mom told me she wasn't too happy with the Laundry POD, and I thought that maybe I'd be happy with it... I wasn't happy with the Laundry POD either, in the end. I found the Laundry POD to be time consuming, cheaply made for its price, ineffective, inconvenient, and pretty much just a big letdown. The price is outrageous for this product, and unfortunately, I did not realize this until after I bought one and used it multiple times. Using the Laundry POD is an intense workout, rinsing the clothes (which the Laundry POD doesn't do well - hardly at all, actually) is an intense workout (because nobody likes hunching over the tub to rinse some clothes out - especially not with my crappy bathtub faucet that has no pressure whatsoever), and then, as if you weren't already sore and exhausted, ringing the clothes out (because, like all other steps of the process, the POD doesn't really do effectively - the Laundry POD gets clothes nowhere even close to damp, let alone dry) is yet another intense workout. This product leaves you sore, exhausted, cranky, and this product doesn't do much in terms of cleaning clothes. It's a laundry letdown. I could've done quite a bit of laundry with the money I spent on this stupid thing, which is not the greatest thing to think about in terms of how I feel about the product. I feel stupid for buying one of these, really. I hope interested shoppers take my advice: do NOT buy a Laundry POD. I could go on and on about how much of a letdown the Laundry POD is, but I have to go to the laundromat, which is exactly what I suggest doing instead of wasting money on one of these stupid things. Trust me, it's not worth the price or the hassle!

title: Plunger VS. Eco Wash. What I found after trying both.
text:
I have been washing laundry by hand for several months now with a Rubbermaid tote and plunger from Lehman’s. For my husband, who works in construction, myself, a stay-at-home mom living largely outdoors, cooking over a fire, etc. my two year old son, and baby girl, who is cloth diapered.

Washing laundry is time consuming and laborious, taking a couple hours per load.

We bought the Econwash after reading reviews for the quick wash time hoping to do a ten minute load each evening, washing the day’s diapers and underwear. Then just doing a large load with the plunger once a week.

What we learned after doing a couple of loads in the Eco wash is this:
1. I had been plunging for way too long previously, the eco wash taught me that the water and soap only needs to go through the clothes a couple of times to get them clean. It’s more about the number of cycles.
2. Wringing out is the most time consuming part of a load, and is still the most time consuming with the eco wash. And a lot more frustrating with the quite small opening. I would squeeze the clothes before pulling them out, then wring over a bucket, trying not to drip all over the place in between.
3. The Eco wash does take less water because it uses pressure rather then plunging to get the water through.
4. The Eco wash does leak a bit, plus with the constant transfer of clothes and water in and out, dripping is unavoidable.
5. The Eco wash is not very sturdy. Had the wash time made it worth it to keep, my husband probably would have fabricated a stand. It creaked back and forth with the weight of the clothes and water while turning. The plastic just seemed to flex and all over.
6. After doing an Eco wash load following the directions exactly, doing two minute cycles; two rinses (to get the pee out of the diapers), a wash, and two more rinses to get the wash water out. From start to finish the load took me about one hour.
Then doing a plunger load the same, taking 2-3 minute rinses and a 5 minute wash cycle, which took about an hour and ten minutes, start to finish, BUT for three times the size of load. We sent the Eco wash back and are back to using the plunger.

All in all, I think it is a great idea, I desperately wanted it to work, and I think it really could with some improvements to the size and design.
I found that it really isn’t that much better for time once you add in all the rinses, heating and transferring water, ringing out and hanging to dry. Plus the inconvenience of water dripping everywhere, and having to transfer to wring out. PLUS the fact that for every one 1hr. 10min. plunger load I do, I have to do THREE 1hr. Eco wash loads.

That’s my two bits, I hope it’s helpful to someone weighing their options!

text:
I made the switch from my trusty Hario V60 to the Wave and haven't looked back.

I meticulously brewed 2-4 cups of coffee with the V60 every day for 4 years. Even controlling for amount of coffee, water, and water temp with careful measurements, I found it difficult to get consistent A+ cups of coffee with the V60. Especially when trying out new beans. There was always a few adjustments to make with the grind size and my recipe.

The Wave, on the other hand, is WAY easier to get consistent, quality cups. By just my second cup, my coffee was already tasting better.

Both the V60 and the Wave are top-tier pour over methods but, if you're not a pro, I'd suggest opting for the Wave. It's less temeperamental and, with less effort, your coffee will be generally better.

title: Not OEM!  No way, no how. This is a rebuilt part. Just hope it lasts.
text:
It may have been OEM before the rebuild but the part I received is not original equipment. The photo they show has the correct impeller on it. It's not what I received. The impeller that came on the part they shipped is very flimsy and not nearly as dense/thick plastic as the original part it replaced. If you look at all the failed one-star reviews, that's the impeller on the part that they will ship to you not the one in the photo. I'm giving it two-stars because it fit and I hope it works for longer than some of the failed reviews here. Having said that. My LG is working again and all it cost me was $26 and an hour of my time.
For those about to attempt to replace your pump, there are two ways. Through the bottom or remove the front panel. I removed the front panel only because there was no room to tip the machine on its side. There are half a dozen YouTube videos showing how. BUT what they don't show you is how difficult it is to put the door boot gasket back on. There's a steel wire that's spring loaded to hold the boot in place. It requires a special spreader tool to expand it far enough to slip on. Since I didn't have one I improvised and asked for help. It took three hands and three flat head screwdrivers to pry it back on. Just put the ring on as far as you can by hand and then slowly wedge the ring down. Easy peasy. In all it's less than an hours work.

title: Buyer (and installer) beware!
text:
I know this element is a cheap, aftermarket knockoff, but I honestly didn't expect too much out of it going in. After watching a couple of handy YouTube videos I thought I would try to replace my busted element with this one. It arrived very quickly (on my doorstep by 7AM on a Saturday, no less) so I swapped it out.

After I replaced the old element, reassembled the dryer and plugged it back in, it tripped the 220v breaker. Twice. Dumbfounded I took apart the dryer again and double-checked all of my wiring (I took photos and video of the original setup). It was then I noticed that a small part of the element wire was accidentally welded onto the metal frame of the element itself, causing an electrical fault. After grabbing some pliers I was able to break the wire free from its frame and it seemed to work fine after that.

Just be careful when putting this in to avoid any serious damage. I was thankful for my breaker but it could have been much worse.

title: These are not Graco Filters
text: The Graco Humidifier filters as advertised by the Buy-It-Now-Store indicated they were for the Graco 4 gallon Humidifier.  The humidifier filters that I received were packaged as Hamilton Beach for a Hamilton Beach (HB) Humidifier.  As I later learned, the picture that the Seller shows herein is even a picture of a Hamilton Beach Blue Filter which is supposed to be a higher grade filter than the "Standard" HB Filter and is a few cents more than the Graco Filter - but this it is not a Graco Filter.  When I contacted the Seller for a Return Authorization, they responded with an authorization for the filters and a "NON-Pre-Paid" shipping label with the instructions that I had to pay the postage for the return.  Since when do I have to pay postage for an error on their part??  After some back and forth correspondence, they agreed that they would reimburse me for the postage I would have to pay, but they would only refund me a $12.00 partial refund on my total purchase of $46.38.  After a couple of hours searching around the internet, I learned that the 4 gallon Graco model humidifier that I have is no longer produced and it seems that Graco is also no longer producing the filters either.  In addition, I did also find on the internet that the Graco filter and HB Filters are interchangeable in addition to another brand but I don't know if this Store even knows that. title: Does not work with NG
text:
I was excited about the unit when received. It looked reasonably well made and would fit near my NG gas grill.
The first item noted is that while equipped with standing feet, the design of the gas connection fitting does not allow the unit to stand evenly. The unit must be used as a drop-in to some kind of table or countertop opening. To be fair, the burner is advertised as a drop-in style, but the attached feet suggests that the unit was planned as a self-standing but designed improperly. The Amazon picture of the gas connector is quite different from the unit I received. I had planned to use the burner as a drop in on an outdoor kitchen counter, so this is more of an FYI.
Before cutting into a stainless steel counter to mount the burner I tested the unit with a working NG connection, used for an outdoor pizza oven. It was immediately evident that the burner barely operated using NG, yielding a very small flame. This behavior is usually related with burners that are designed and engineered for LP gas which operates at higher pressures.
I suspect the orifice(s) within the burners are for LP use Smaller diameter), and this product did not come with NG orifices. I did not test with LP but it may work fine. I also found that this product is fundamentally not returnable, but Amazon has been great to help to rectify the issue.

title: Fixed the fridge that wouldn't hold temperature
text: My 10+ year old fridge wouldn't hold temperature allowing it to go over 47F. It seemed to be running fine, just wouldn't run often enough to keep the cold. I decided that thermostat was to blame and purchased this replacement. The install was easy, there are youtube videos with detailed step-by-step instructions. There were only a couple of extra steps I needed to do - one was that I reused the plastic sheath from the old thermostat on this one. This one's is kinda loose and I was worried it wouldn't properly clip in place around the cold air vent between freezer and the fridge. The second thing (which was kinda annoying) was that the metal tabs that hold the plastic dial on this thermostat were too wide and dial wouldn't not fit properly. Unfortunately, I discovered that almost at the end of the assembly and had to backpedal, take the thermostat back out and file the tabs on the side a bit to make the knob fit. Recommendation for those using this part is to try fitting the knob first (you can just take it out of the fridge panel without any disassembly and try fitting it on the new thermostat). Given that I have a GE panel mount dishwasher, it is important for the dishwasher to stay in a precise position so that its panel lines up with the adjacent cabinets. My counter was not installed with a wood block underneath the stone so the only way to mount the dishwasher was on the side.

While the dishwasher had hardware for side mounting, it was poorly designed and allowed the unit to slip out of its position over time. This was an extremely annoying feature of the GE dishwasher such that I cannot necessarily fault the counter installer for not thinking enough to provide a wood block underneath the counter.

The Dishwasher Undercounter Mounting Kit worked exactly as described. I am also uploading photos of the product label, instructions, and dimensions since these are helpful to anyone else deciding whether this kit will solve his/her dishwasher mounting challenges.

To sum it up: this mounting kit is a life saver when you have a dishwasher that does not come with the mounting hardware that it should have in the first place.

text:

Door on the problem unit is hot to the touch, no reply to original review from the seller. Appears the “high quality seal” wasn't even touching the body of the unit in some places. A third of the interior ultimately became one solid ice block as we were unable to do the manual defrost sooner. Threw away an entire trash bag full of food. Cannot find a manual to identify how to get a replacement seal or otherwise troubleshoot.

2-3 months after purchase:

I was searching for upright freezers to fit specific dimensions with a plain black front, preferably no LED display on the front (to fit and visually disappear into my antique cabinet) and settled on 2 of these! I was very excited as they fit and look perfect for what I needed. I used to have a chest freezer, but having an upright so that you can easily see what is stored within IS so much better than a deep freezer where things get lost at the bottom. And I loved them at first but…

-they are so noisy, which makes my search (and extra money paid) for a nice quiet refrigerator, which is to the left of the cabinet, pointless.
-not to mention these freezers are only about 2-3 months old and look at these ice dams!! They are closed/sealed tightly every time, so this is unacceptable to me! My old igloo deep freezer was $100 secondhand and still never did this after 4 years of use. VERY DISAPPOINTED at this.
-i don’t like the sloppy edges where you can see the insulation and whatnot, but i didn’t mind it when i unwrapped the freezers, bc they were otherwise (visually) perfect. Sharing since i know it’ll be a real issue for some.
-i THINK i can reverse the door swing on the left freezer and may do that later since I’ll have to remove it from the cabinet to manually defrost anyway.

***keep in mind that i intentionally placed this in my home where the freezers never receive direct sunlight, because i was concerned about energy consumption and longevity. So there’s no good reason for them to be so noisy and building up ice dams like this.

I’m just a few months into having these, and I’m just very let down.

title: Bogus Chinese marketing
text:
[[VIDEOID:9d8b370eb32985227ffb41b3f0ca213d]] Like the 99.9% of Chinese no name brand products sold on Alibazon, this one is no different- nothing but exaggerated claims (read- lies).

The 8.26" advertised cooking coil/element diameter- the main reason I bought this unit- is not even 5" (see photos). Ironically, even the printed circle is far smaller than 8" in diameter, not that the circle itself is of any consequence...
Otherwise, the induction cooktop works, but be ready to be stirring a lot if you cook in but the smallest pots and pans- the temperature distribution is very uneven outside of center.
Also, get ready to have all your nice cooking pots and pans ruined- eventually, the center area will pop up and instead of a flat surface they'll take on a convex shape and the oil/liquid will be pooling on the outside perimeter of a pan.

I do like the simple knob control which seems pretty unique in the China Sea of all these copycat induction cooktops- just so much easier to use and quickly adjust temperature or power output. So one extra start for this simple design solution.

I also purchased a Nuwave Gold model after I'd ordered this Cooktron cooktop. Nuwave also advertised a 8" coil element and cost some 60% more, but turned out to have the same exact size coil, around 5" (all these "brands" most likely source and use all the same parts inside) Seeing how Cooktron top was $40 vs $70 for nuwave and it has better control, the Nuwave is going right back. Cooktron is also supposedly 1800W vs 1500W for Nuwave, but I suspect those numbers aren't to be trusted either.

And now I am out an oven again until technicians arrive.  If this trend continues next year (after my protection plan expires) I will be paying to have a three year old oven repaired.  This oven gets regular to light usage, because we eat at my in-laws house most days, and we keep it very clean. text: I was excited at the possibility of fixing my ten year old washer with a sub $10 part instead of replacing the whole machine for hundreds of dollars. I ordered from 'partshouse' because I wanted expedited shipping and paid $12.17. The part did indeed arrive very quickly, but unfortunately, it was broken. I noticed immediately that it did not "click" when I moved the switch, and my suspicions were confirmed when I installed the part and it didn't work. I filed a claim for return that day and was immediately informed that the information had been forwarded to customer service. The next day I received a message that a new item had already been sent out and that I did not need to return the old one. So, as frustrating as a broken part can be, I think the situation was handled quickly and satisfactorily. The new part worked, and I was able to install it pretty easily, even though I had no expertise in this area (there are some good walkthroughs on the web). I waited two weeks to write this review to make sure that this new part wouldn't break, and it hasn't. I would therefor recommend this product.

title: Performance issues with my GE Opal 2.0.
text:
It worked great until 2 days before my return window expired on 8/11/22. I experienced performance issues with my GE Opal 2.0. The water added to the reservoir is filtered by a 5 stage RO filter system. This filter was intended to add a layer of protection for the recirculating water in the system. After about three weeks, the Opal 2.0 add water light kept coming on. I used the manual and app to troubleshoot. When removed, the ice machine worked fine. I changed to a new filter thinking it was the end of life for it and went to bed. I decided to return because filters are advertised to last 3 months not 3 weeks. I believed the other filters will eventually lead to the same issue.

Update...On 8/16/22, WaterdropDirect reached out to me. They arranged a new overnight shipment of 3 ice maker filters +1 pitcher+ 3 replacement filters for the pitcher to compensate. I agreed to accept the offer. They contacted me again on 8/19 to ask if I had received the items and how I felt about them. On 8/22, I let them know that I had received the pitcher w/filter. Great for my bedroom, I can fill it with water and have filtered water upstairs anytime I like for me and my dog. I had not put their Opal filter into the ice maker, currently there is a GE Profile branded filter in there that I bought the next day. It is rated as a 3 month filter as well, so I will have to wait until that one needs replacing. So far the GE branded filter has made it past the 3 week mark. I will put a Waterdrop filter in and see how long that lasts after the GE Profile filter is depleted. I promised I would update them when I do. I increased the stars to 3 based on them reaching out to me and trying to make things right with me as a customer. Since my water that I add to the reservoir is filtered by a 5 stage RO filter system I probably will not be buying anymore filters. I did look at the reviews that came in between my review 8/11/22 and today (9/7/22), you make your own judgement from there.

I got this for the crack between the stove and the counter. In our kitchen there is no counter on the other side of the stove, so there was some flexibility in terms of how big the crack was. Also, because of where the gas line to the stove was, the stove, and the Kleen Seam, was pushed forward from the wall (compared to the counter) and didn't provide a great fit.

Ultimately, I moved the stove over so that there is now a 4-5 inch gap between the side of the cabinets and the stove, and the stove can sit back against the wall since the gas line is now to the side. When drips and food fall down there, it is much easier to clean, and the Kleen Seam now lives in the laundry room behind the hampers.

This would probably work best in a situation where the stove was flush against the back wall and surrounded by cabinets, in a home with older kids or adults. Second, our refrigerator is about 3 years old but the ice maker unit burned out because these are made with plastic parts which can come apart. My old unit’s plastic frame partially popped open and the unit’s stripper got bent and caught up which caused the motor to burn out.

With that said this replacement unit appears to be working and was an easy project to install. I am giving the icemaker 3 stars, mostly because we are just happy to have ice again.

The ground coffee that I'm using, Cafe Du Monde's coffee and chicory blend, tastes amazing using a traditional coffee pot, but for some reason it tastes like overcooked vegetables in the Keurig. Perhaps this drip method isn't precisely the same as a more traditional machine? I don't know. I can live with a certain coffee type not lending itself to a certain brewing type; that's common.

My major gripe with this filter is IT GETS GROUNDS EVERYWHERE. Filled only halfway (well below the recommended fill line), brewing causes grounds to cake onto the water mechanism and overflow the filter altogether, leaving tons of floaters on your next use unless you perform a pretty thorough cleaning of the unit. As the whole idea of the Keurig is to make it easy to make a single cup of coffee, this is a major flaw, and why I can't recommend "My K-Cup" in the least.

title: Great machine, but you have to be willing to change your laundry routine.
text:
This is a fabulous washing machine, and it can replace a washer/dryer combination. However, you have to be willing to change your laundry routine, because it can't dry clothes like a conventional dryer. The clothes will be damp. Depending on the fabric, some are dry enough to fold and put away. Others need to be set out, or hung up, to dry. I don't mind the change in the routine, because the ability to toss clothes into the machine in the morning, and return from work 12 hours later and fold/hang up the laundry is terrific. However, I can't put it away until the next day, because it needs to be left out to dry.

If you are willing to change your laundry routine for clothes that aren't quite dry enough to put away, then this is a great machine. However, if you are expecting it to produce bone dry clothes like a conventional dryer, then you will be disappointed.

For me, it's 5 stars. I don't mind the change. For others, it may be a huge disappointment.

title: Gets the clothes really clean and hooked right up in minutes!
text:
Update: Found out the hard way that this thing puts a lot of lint down the drain. You won't see it, but you'll know 5-6 months later when your drain won't work anymore. Use some sink strainers.

The hardest part was getting some old faucet adapter that a previous tenant put on the tap out, but once it was off, this hooked right up to my kitchen sink. For those complaining of slight leakage, you should buy some quality channel lock pliers, get a good grip, and give the faucet adapter and the water hose hookup to the washer a final turn with that, otherwise there will be leakage.

I had a large laundry hamper full of dirty clothes, which usually takes $7.75 to do at the laundromat between the 6 load washer and two dryers running for an hour when I hooked this up. The bad news is it took about 3.5 hours to send this all through, but the good news is I skipped the laundromat and just sat here and swapped out loads until they were done. The spin cycle does a good job at getting the water out, and all you really need to do is use an extra large laundry rack, which cost about $15-20 at your local big box.

To easily store this washing machine in the closet, I recommend the "SPACECARE Mobile Roller with 4 Locking Wheels - Adjustable Furniture Dolly" which is sold separately on Amazon for about thirty bucks.

I'm so happy that I can save time, money, and not risk getting someone else's laundry funk all over my clothes at the laundromat (strange smells, greasy spots, people spill bleach and don't clean it.....). If this machine lasts 5 years, it will have paid for itself 7 times over. You don't find investments like that.

title: Louder than I was expecting for a 4 speed fan.
text:
I replaced a 17 year old hood that was pretty quiet with this one, as i am updating appliances to stainless steel. Even though the outside box was in good shape, when I unboxed the unit, I found the plastic box covering the electronic board had a broken mounting ear, causing it to flop around. I contacted Ancona, and they are sending me a new plastic cover. Good points for their service department.

Instructions are in English and French. The English part describes the 3 speed fan without the time delay shutoff (only has 5 buttons instead of 6). Had to figure out how the time delay shutoff works, found a guy at work that understood French, and he helped translate. Found out that the 3 minute time delay (yes it's 3 minutes, not the 10 advertised in the description) only works for the upper 3 fan speeds, not for the lowest "quiet" setting. Invoking the time delay on the quiet speed causes the indicator lights to flash for 3 minutes, and then nothing changes. On the upper 3 speeds after the three minutes of flashing indicators, the fan shuts off as expected. I questioned Ancona about this, and they confirmed the delay doesn't work on the quiet speed. This limitations wasn't described in the French translation either. They need to update the documentation before everyone returns the unit for this "defect".

As to the noise, yes this unit is noisier then my previous 17 year old Venmar unit. The Venmar had a squirrel cage fan, the quietest fan type you can have. Since this was a 4 speed fan, I really expected the "quiet" speed to be comparable to the low speed on my old one. You can carry on a conversation next to it on "quiet" but it isn't pleasant. I ended up buying a Japan to USA power converter (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004S2COIC?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00), which changes the incoming 120 volts to 105 volts. I fed this 105 volts to the hood, and everything works ok. The "quiet" speed is now better (of course the air flow is reduced also, but there are 3 more speeds to select from if you need to move some more air). Still louder then my old Venmar, but acceptable. The maximum speed didn't seem to be reduced with the step down transformer installed.

I replaced the lights with LED units (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B015673OFO?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00) that work from 10 to 20 volts, and they don't seem to mind the reduced 105 volts I am feeding the hood with now.

There is a loud "beep" for every button push, louder than your typical microwave button beep. I find this a bit obnoxious also, you really don't need that loud of feedback on pressing buttons. My dog would look over each time a button was pushed! Since the plastic box cover for the circuit board was broken (and removed for the moment), I took a small stick-on felt circle (the kind you put on the back of pictures/mirrors so they don't scrape the wall they are hanging on) and stuck it over the small black beeper on the circuit board (around 1/2 inch diameter black cylinder with a hole on the top). This reduced its sound by half, and made the beep noise acceptable.

The unit looks good, and for the price it is OK, just wished it was quieter (both fan and beep noise).

text:
First of all, I like the idea of a counter top dishwasher. It's convenient; no bending down to load.

What I don't like is the cheap plastic covered micro switches. You may as well go ahead and order a replacement control PCB from Sunpentown dishwasher parts; you'll need it. Cost is $23,10 at the time of this review and with shipping it's around $30.00. It doesn't matter if you buy this one or another brand, they all use these cheap switches. I hate to say it, but some auto companies use these cheap plastic covered switches. When you see them, you'll know they cut corners.

Another thing you need to know is if you have problems finding an adapter for the faucet, go to a family owned hardware and have them check the thread size with a thread gauge. Take the faucet filter with you.

Other than the cheap switches, I like this dishwasher.

On this model the bake/heating element is under the oven floor. Manufacturer's recommendation is that "grease all oven rack side edges with a light coating of vegetable oil after cleaning them by hand or in the oven to maintain the ease of sliding in out the oven.

Also, note you should be sure you have the right pans for the cooktop and oven for radiant glass cooktop. Stainless steel, aluminum and copper bottom is recommended (porcelain enamel on cast iron only recommend if bottom of pan is coated). Not recommended - porcelain enal on steel, glass-ceramic, stoneware and cast-iron ubless specifically for glass cooktops. Flat-bottom woks, okay.

title: Not as good as advertised
text:
This machine is rather awkward to use and potentially dangerous.

There are a few things about this washer that the store & instruction manual does not state that you definitely should know, consider yourself lucky to be reading this review.

1. The manual never states how to actually use the drainage hose, so I figured that you must dispose of dirty water from the washer machine manually. Turns out it AUTOMATICALLY dumps the water, and it also doesn't make any chime or noise when it's done with your clothes (not until you open the hatch to get your clothes... what? Why?) I had attached the drainage hose to my sink but it broke free and fell to the floor, I had no idea it was flooding my kitchen as I worked in my room.

2. This washer machine may be small, but it uses a LOT of water. Think you're saving money buying this thing? Think again- you'll be spending much more on your water bill using this washing machine as compared to an eco-friendly one. How do I know? Look at fact #1 above; it dumped water all over my kitchen, and it flooded my 7 x 5 ft. kitchen with around 1/2 inch deep water, and some water even got into my dining area. It did all of this when I had it set to a medium load. THAT'S A LOT OF WATER FOR A SINGLE MEDIUM LOAD.

3. You'll need to buy a rolling pallete if you plan on using this washing machine, because it is rather heavy and unless you plan on leaving it in front of a kitchen sink or a bathroom sink, you'll be moving it around a lot. Oh yeah, and it usually keeps around 1/2 gallon of water inside of it- better not let it tip or fall. You'll also need to buy an extension for the drainage hose, because it isn't long enough AT ALL to reach a standard-height kitchen sink. I mean it'll reach, but in my case I had to take an iron skillet and use it as a weight to hold the drainage hose in place over the sink (which by the way, didn't work- the drainage hose was too short and it yanked itself free from underneath the skillet, and flooded my entire kitchen).

Overall, would I recommend this product? Hmm...

If you have no washer/dryer connections, (like in some apartments or really crappy homes) then sure- get this portable washer so that you don't have to make trips to the washateria. Just don't expect to be saving money (see note #2).

In all other cases, if you have washer/dryer connections, get an ordinary washer instead of a portable one. This washer does work well- when it's not flooding your home- but it is also a bit awkward to use, and if you don't follow the directions from the manual TO THE LETTER, then... I hope you have flood insurance.

And no, you can't wash something like a comforter in this thing. Maybe a few toweis or a small blanket, but no pillows & comforters.

title: Meh
text:
It's a non-ducted hood, so it's only going to be so good since it can't vent outside.

Size: I checked a bunch of range hoods out at a local store before settling on this one. I was disappointed that even the higher-end models at three times the price didn't fully cover the entire oven like my old one did - it's the same case with this Broan model. This one's lip is very short and only covers a bit more than half of the range, instead of the entire range (on a standard 30" oven/range), which makes it pretty useless for capturing smoke & steam from the front burners.

Noise: Yes, it's noisier than my old one (and somewhat flimsier, but it's not like I ever touch anything other than the fan & light switch on it, so whatever). I can't tell if the fan really works because smokey stuff (on the back burner, which actually goes up into the capture area) still stinks up my kitchen. The fan noise is fairly obnoxious too, it sounds like it's been installed for ages & is old instead of brand new, if you've ever heard a well-used fan before.

Filter: After reading through the reviews, I did buy the five-dollar charcoal filter. The stock one is a blue one and the one that Amazon suggests has what appears to be a black carbon filter on it. I can't tell if it makes a difference between it still smokes out my kitchen because the lip only covers half the stove, and even the stuff that is filtered still blows smokey air into the room, so what good is it? What a dumb design, to not fully cover a standard-size stove - I would have gotten the more expensive one with the dual filters & better lights, but that one covered the same area, was three times more expensive, and there aren't really any other good non-ducted options on the market that I could find easily in-store or on Amazon.

My lightbulb shorted out when I turned it on the third day in, so I don't know if that's a defective or just a random coincidence. It was fairly easy to install, although the holes were different than my old one & I had to get a drill to punch holes where the wood lip was on my upper cabinets. That was kind of lame.

Overall, disappointed, but I more or less knew what I was getting into. For the price, it is what it is. It doesn't look horrible, at least, and it's slightly better than having nothing to funnel the air in at all, I guess. It was super easy to install, aside from the some of the holes (in particular the front right) not lining up with my (standard-sized) cabinets. I was hoping it was going to be better than it was based on the the high numbers of stars & reviews. Oh well.

text:
This unit is better than we expected based on the descriptions provided by Broan. It is quiet and powerful. Installation and hookup were relatively easy (though it IS heavy), after we studied the electrical scheme of the hood. Broan does not make it easy to find out what parts are actually necessary.

We obtained a Broan 336 Blower to replace the incredibly noisy internal fans of our Broan Elite E6448TSS. (Those internal fans made a HUGE hum, vibrating our entire house, at every speed. Broan Technical Support even stated to us: "It's a VERY noisy unit!" So they KNOW!) The controller in the E6448T is the same one used in the Broan E64E48.

Bottom line:
-If you need a high-performance (over 1000 cfm) range hood, and you think noise might be a problem, seriously consider an external blower hood.
-Don't buy Broan internal-fan hoods.
-Broan external blowers are much better equipment than their internal fans.

title: Don't buy this product, unless you have money to waste.
text:
If I had a chance to give Bosch NO star for their low quality products and horrible customer service, I would gladly do it.

After much debate between choosing Bosch or Thermador, I reluctantly purchased this product to be the showcase of my newly-updated kitchen. My wife and I were very excited to finally use a "semi high-end" brand name cooktop. The installation of our cooktop took too long due to issues finding an gas plumber. We purchased the product in June and it sat in a box until September.
After the second use, I attempted to clean the product by following the manufacturer's exact recommended care guidelines. I used a plastic sponge for washing dishes and dish washing liquid. The surface of the unit immediately discolored and got ruined.
I contacted Bosch's support to complain about the quality of this appliance. They told me that there was nothing they could do for me because the "cosmetic period" had ended. Bosch has a 30-day cosmetic warranty period. Also they told me that they would not honor the warranty because I did clean the cooktop surface in the direction of the "finished grain" of the metallic surface!!!!! They made up with all sorts of nonsense reasons why they couldn't accommodate my request to exchange the product.
The best they could offer me was to have the top replaced and I would have to pay for the labor cost. Replacing the top would require a town permit, hiring a gas plumber at $250-$500 an hour and a final inspection.
I am so disappointed in Bosch and its products. I will never buy another product from them. Total rip-off......

title: Good but requires experiment to get acceptable drying
text:
I purchased the Panda PAN60SF portable clothes dryer about a month ago through Ebay, which is why my review is not listed as a verified purchase.

I am happy with the Panda dryer. I have the larger 3.75 cu. ft. model, which is plenty roomy enough for my needs, and has the capability of getting my clothes bone dry in a reasonable amount of time.

It should be noted that the product description states, “Since it's 110V, it may take longer to dry than a regular dryer which is 220v.” This is true so potential customers should be mindful of this. Nevertheless, contrary to other reviews, it does dry my clothes just fine; however, the controls are wacky, and I had to experiment to obtain satisfactory results.

I set my first dry to about 60 minutes, but the Panda did not get warm enough to do much drying. In fact, the air coming out did not feel much warmer than room temperature.

The problem is with the controls in that it combines drying time with heat level on the same knob. To heat on high you have to set it between 120 and 200 minutes, even if you do not need that much time. Warm air is generated between 20 and 120 minutes, and unheated air when set to less than 20 minutes. It also has a separate low/high heat button which makes matters even more confusing.

For the second dry I set it to a longer time, over 120 minutes which provided much hotter air. The clothes dried completely, but I did not need nearly the amount of dry time. Now I always set it for the hot section on the dial (120 and 200 minutes), and just check it when I think it is done. Normally I do not need more than 45 minutes.

Why, for heaven’s sake, do they not have separate controls for heat and dry time? It would be much more convenient and a four- or five-star product with just that one improvement!

Finally, I will discuss the lint filter. While it is not the easiest thing to keep clean (which definitely should be done between each use), it is nevertheless excellent. I have a separate filter outside the unit for the extracted air, but it catches very little lint because the filter inside the Panda does such a good job.

It is a good clothes dryer and a good value, but users will need to experiment to get acceptable drying.

title: Switch was an exact match that was unfortunately wired backwards
text: All of the numbers on this switch were an exact match for the switch taken out of the dryer. I installed it and turned on the dryer, nothing happened. Opened the door and turned on the dryer and it worked fine. I removed the new switch and compared it to the old one. Two of the wires were reversed. I took a small screwdriver and gently bent in the tabs that held the pin into the connector on both wires. The pins easily pulled out of the connector. The tabs were bent back out so they would engage when inserted back into the connector. I rewired the switch to match the old one and the dryer is now repaired and working. It was an easy 15-minute repair that wound up being done twice. I saved a lot of money repairing the dryer myself.

title: Good for emergency repairs, but don't expect long term operation
text:
After 12 years of being a happy GE fridge owner, the original defrost heater module broke.
So I bought the Antoble defrost heater regardless of the negative comments about the smell. It turned out that the initial smell was negligible and after the replacement, the fridge worked great for months. Then today, I noticed the temperature in the fridge was creeping up again. So I removed the cover from the evap coils only to find that the coils were covered in thick ice again (this is an obvious sign of a failure of the defrost heater, thermistor or defrost control board). Since the diagnostic checks confirmed correct thermistor and control board operation, I ended up manually defrosting the coils then testing the heater element. As suspected, the Antoble heater was broke. What I didn't expect is the extreme damage of the gasket between the glass tube and the receptacle. On the GE defrost heater, the gasket was in great shape even after 12 years, on the Antoble, it melted away in 2 months. I give it 2 stars because the heater wire held up for 2 months, but I won't buy from this vendor until they fix the design flaws (gasket and heater wire issues).

title: Filter is not compatible with units requiring the DA29-00020A
text:
This review is for advertising only. Samsung recently made hardware changes with how the water filter interfaces with the refrigerator. Older refrigerators used part Number DA29-00020A with only one o-ring on the outside for a total of 2 o-rings used. The newer refrigerators use part number DA29-00020B which are stated as being backwards compatible to the older “A” version. They are not. The new filters use an additional o-ring on the outside for a total of 3 o-rings. This new configuration does not allow the water to pass through filter and through the dispenser on the door.

This is documented on the Samsung owner forums and the only fix for it is to replace the fixture within the refrigerator.

text: Review is for Metronic 16inch heat sealer, sold by Jiaro International:  Ordered one of these to seal vacuum sealer type bags. We are a small non-profit, with very, very low volume, so we only seal a few bags at a time. First sealer came and didn't work at all, right out of the box. Checked everything I could, and no power, no heat and now indicator light. It was immediately returned.  Got a replacement after several days. It actually worked... but ONLY FOR TEN BAGS. It's not like we process 100s of bags at a time. I tested it with 2 bags, when we got it, and it worked that day. Then I used to do a "second seal" on 2 bags, and it worked that day. Today I was making bags from a roll, where you cut the length you want and seal the bottom, prior to filling. Five seals went okay, then the sixth bag, literally NOTHING happened. No power, no "tick" sound when the heat had been applied, no indicator light. Keep in mind, these bags were being sealed MINUTES apart, so it wasn't like I was overheating it by sealing bags one right after another. This piece of junk is going BACK to Amazon and the search is on for a RELIABLE manufacturer and SELLER.

title: Great idea, but should be nade angled
text:
This is a great idea! Since I switched to a front load washer, I’ve been leaving the door ajar to prevent the rank smell. I was excited to find this product and see that I’m not the only one with this problem.

The Treerit magnetic washing machine door prop is simple, well made, and easy to install. Comes with 3 metal discs with adhesive backing in case your machine has a plastic door. Just peel and stick one on the door, then put the prop in place.

I have two complaints:
1. The prop does not sit square against both the washer and the door causing an insecure fit. It should be made at a slight angle rather than straight to accommodate the angle of the open door.
2. The magnets could be stronger.

Overall, a fairly good product and does the job okay, but could be great if made at an angle and stronger magnets. A little overpriced, in my opinion.

- A more level surface to double for food prep or setting items to cool.
CONS

text:

We had a GE Opal ice maker before, and I would say this one makes ice faster than the Opal but the ice consistency isn't quite as nice. It's also a lot cheaper than the Opal. We had quite a bit of trouble with the Opal, including getting two warranty replacements, so the bigger question is how well this one will hold up over time. Only time will tell on that; I'm writing this after having the ADT for about a month.

One concern is that the User Manual says there is a one-year warranty, but there is no information on how to contact them. Not a phone number or an email address. There isn't very much information about operation or maintenance in the User Manual, either. Customer service was actually a strength of GE, and we don't yet know how it's going to be for this company. Do they even have customer service?

The following ADDED LATER

The last paragraph above has turned out to be very important. After just four months of use, this ice maker has totally stopped working so I am adding this and reducing the rating to one star. According to the product description and its very short User Manual, there is a one-year warranty, but there is absolutely no information on how to actually contact them! When I contacted Amazon about this problem, they gave me a number to call “ADT” for warranty, but that was the number for the ADT security company. The woman I talked to didn't know anything about ice machines. This is NOT an acceptable state of affairs.

title: Good, but would be better with auto-reset
text:
This is a fine thermometer. I really like that it shows precisely what I want... the current temperature, the high temperature and the low temperature. Three things I would like to see improved, from least important to most important.
1. I could do without the smiley face. It adds no value to me, and distracts from the temperature data I want to see.
2. The display alternates between showing the temperature and the humidity. I live in Southern California, and humidity readings are not important here, since we rarely have humidity of any consequence. It would be nice to outfit this with an option to not alternate displays.
3. The most concerning problem is that there is no auto-reset of the high and low temperatures. So as it is, you'll see the high and low temperatures not just for today, but for the period of time since you last manually reset the unit. That could be a day, a week, a month, or longer. The programming of this unit needs to be changed so that the highs and lows automatically reset each day, or perhaps once the temperature bottoms-out and starts to rise each day.

Most everything else is appropriate use good judgement.  It can handle a Queen sheet set okay, I usually untangle them before starting the rinse cycle.  Remember to clean the lint trap regularly. I use my timer on my watch to remember to start the rinse cycle and spinner/dryer.  The spinner really does do much better to wring the extra water out than my old washing machine. title: Not up to the Bosch name and service is terrible
text:
Bought this at a big box store. Installed it myself. Was immediately impressed by the quietness and disappointed in the length of cycle. I have 6 kids and we need to run 3-4 loads a day. A 2-hour cycle makes that difficult.

Within a year the washer would start and within 3 minutes display clean - despite having done nothing. I called Bosch expecting help like I have always received with my Bosch hot water heaters. (With the water heaters the techs will troubleshoot over the phone and even send warranty parts directly. With one of my units they sent me a replacement heater without charge because of the problems being experienced.) The second the appliance phone tech found out I was a homeowner and not a service tech he hung up on me. (I am a licensed PE with extensive electrical experience and ended up explaining electrical theory to the tech that finally came out.) A month and three trips later their tech finally had the problem fixed. They just changed parts until something made it better. $300+ bill (for a $500 dishwasher). Fortunately it was all under warranty.

Now, 18-months later the symptoms have returned again. The quality of the wash has also been degrading - leaving lots of debris in glasses, etc. I will not fix it this time. The part (that fixed it last time) is $200+.

text:
I bought this non-pressurized basket for my Breville Cafe Roma machine. The basket fits in the portafilter with no issue, but the problem is with the volume indicator lip inside the basket. If using a tamper that's appropriate for the size of the basket, then it gets caught on the lip of the volume indicator and ruins the tamp. You have to pry the tamper out and at that point the puck is ruined. On top of the physical issues, I wouldn't recommend this basket with a machine like the Cafe Roma. The machine just can't generate enough pressure to get a good shot with this non-pressurized basket and you're basically just brewing drip coffee if using it.

All-in-all, if you're thinking of purchasing this thinking you're going to get better shots out of your lower-end machine with a cheap upgrade like I did, it probably won't get you any closer to a better product. Better to save your money and put it towards just getting a better machine instead of putting lipstick on a pig.

title: Junk
text:
I bought this gasket (NOT from this seller) to replace the gasket on my ~2005 Jenn-Air stainless steel dishwasher. While the old gasket wasn't leaking, it's worn out down at the ends and I thought I'd replace it proactively.

The replacement part Whirlpool now is a different design that's thinner and lighter than the original gasket. The part that holds the gasket into the groove in the dishwasher is way flimsier than the original gasket. I spent at least 45 minutes monkeying around with this gasket to get it to stay in the groove and eventually kinda sorta got it situated. Ran a rinse cycle, the darn thing leaks.

Put the original gasket back in...took 30 seconds, seats properly and securely in the groove, doesn't leak. FML.

title: Not OEM. You may have to alter this part to make it work.
text:
Bummer, when you have to repair a repair part before you can use it, but that’s what sometimes happens when you don’t buy OEM.
In my case, even when the switch actuator was fully depressed by the existing rod on the washing machine lid, the switch was not closing. Rather than return the switch I opened it up by gently prying off the white cover. In order for the lid switch to work, the spring (yellow line, in second picture) needed to be deflected by the actuator (yellow arrow) so that the angle of the spring (dotted yellow line) was below the angle of the contactor bar (green line). That was not happening. I had a choice of either shaving off some of the outside of the switch case to allow the washing machine lid to close the switch actuator further, or move the fulcrum (green dot) of the contactor bar. Using a needle nose pliers, I bent the bottom brass detail upward (red dot). I then bent the top prong of the detail (blue dot) back into alignment, so it would line up with the receptacle when finished. Working fine now.

title: Terrible cooling.  It's been a royal pain.
text:
I have had nothing but trouble with this kegerator. First off, there is massive ice buildup in the back where the cooling coils are. If you adjust the temperature knob to the recommended "Mid to Low if you live in a cooler area" then the ice block in the back is smaller, but the temperature in the kegerator stays a balmy 55-60 degrees. If you adjust it to between Mid and Max, then it lowers it down to around 45-50, but you get a LARGE chunk of ice in the back. I have YET to ever get the kegerator to drop the temp below 45 degrees, even on Max and whether it has a keg in there or not. Balancing the kegerator at these temps is wildly difficult as well, which just adds to the constant frustration. The first keg I put in was a corny of homebrew, and ended up with nearly 1/3 of the batch down the drain in the form of foam. The second, a 1/2 bbl commercial D-keg, is still giving me fits. No matter the pressure settings, it started with 100% foam on the paltry 4' of beer line they give you, and went to just about 50% after painfully changing out the beer line to around 13'. I'm still fighting with this every other day trying to balance this system out. Also not helping anything is the adjustment knob on the pressure regulator. It's ridiculously scrawny. Make sure you keep a pair of pliers IN the fridge so they'll be handy.

So far, I'm pretty unhappy with the cooling, pressurizing and dispensing operations of this kegerator, which makes up the bulk of what it's supposed to do well. Don't bother trying to contact the customer service dept for this either...it's non-existent. The thing keeping this from being a 1-star is that after 2 months of tinkering around with it, it still looks very nice. Do yourself a favor and just break down and get a real refrigerator and a conversion kit, or just spend the extra $300 you'll add to this in parts and aggravation on a decent kegerator.

Please don't make the same mistake I made.

title: Good for small items or delicate items…
text:
Firstly, I purchased this foldable machine to wash cloth face masks and delicate underwear items that I normally handwash. This machine cleaned my daughter’s face mask really well (surprisingly very clean) and I also washed 3 child sized tank tops and a child white cardigan in one load. All of which came out really clean but extremely damp.

It is very quiet and has a bell to alert you when the wash and spin cycles are completed. The wash cycle has 2 options 5 and 10 minutes in duration. The last option is 6 minutes for a spin dry function, which is why it comes with the small expandable basket spinner.

This is why I gave the machine 4 stars because it does not extract water well from clothes during the spin cycle. Also, there are no English instructions in the box. You will need to figure things out on your own; however, it is fairly easy to set up and to start washing. This portable foldable washer would be perfect for travel in a suitcase (fits in my carry on) but please don’t think you will be able to wash a full load of clothes at one time. This is for small items that are not very heavy ie. underwear, socks, t-shirts, light shorts, bras, slips, gown, baby clothes). I am size 4 in women’s so a pair of my jeans may work in this washer but if bigger it will be too heavy for the bottom agitation levels to move, which may break your washer.

title: Not tall enough for Bunn coffee makers
text:
Although Amazon suggests buying this along with a Bunn coffee maker, the Bunn coffee makers require a taller filter. The re-usable filter they sell bundled with this coffee maker on Amazon is the standard (shorter) size so you can't really use it with this coffee maker (unless you like wiping grounds out from the inside every day that splash up on the inside). So what I do is put one of the tall Bunn paper filters inside the re-usable filter (which initially was an attempt to slow down the water and brew stronger coffee). The tall paper one keeps the grounds from splashing around and I just lift it out and throw it away. The re-usable filter keeps the hi-tech water-slowing-down-device (i.e. a piece of tin foil) in place. I later send Bunn an email asking if they sold a permanent filter and here was their response:

"Unfortunately, we do not sell a permanent filter for our home machines and as far as we know, there is not a permanent filter on the market that is tall enough to accommodate the amount of water at one time that is distributed from our machines when brewing. Most of these permanent filters are too short."

title: Works great when used right.
text: After seeing so many negative reviews we decided to purchase this mini kegerator. It really does help to have some knowledge about draft systems and how they work. The mistake that most people make is giving it too much Co2 and then complaining of too much foam. You got to realize that YOU are the regulator with these kind of systems. In other words the Co2 dial is basically like a garden hose in that it doesn't automatically stop at a certain pressure no matter how much or how little you turn it on. It will eventually just empty out all the co2 into the mini keg and then all you will get is foam. It needs to be either "on" or "off". What we do is after we install tap into mini keg and place into mini kegerator, we hook it up to the 2 hose attachments then fill up glass until it starts to pour very little beer. We then turn co2 on for about 5 seconds and then turn off. This provides enough pressure to provide a well poured beer with a proper head. Also it's good to pre-chill the mini keg in a regular household refrigerator before hooking it up and pouring beers. We use a Gatorade bottle filled with cold water and it provides the perfect amount of water to fill basin and will steadily keep beer at 36f. Another thing is there are about 3 different type bungs that come on these commercially sold 5 liter mini kegs. 2 of them have a rubber rim and work fine without having to completely remove and replace the bung that comes with the the mini keg. But one type such as the one that comes with Fruh kolsch 5 liter mini kegs must be completely removed because it is all plastic with no rubber rim to seal. The unit does comes with a reusable rubber bung that you place into the mini keg and use We made our own tools consisting of panel pulling pliers and tools that work easily and hassle free to remove these type of bungs that must be removed. We do have a full size kegerator and keep full size kegs for draft at home but we do like to serve 5 liter mini kegs of various German beers as "special guests" and we are very happy with this mini kegerator. But for those new to this, it really helps to watch YouTube videos so to get at least a general understanding of how these systems work before giving up and writing a trash review.

title: Did help with vibration, a bit
text: During a recent renovation, we stacked our front loading washer and dryer.  After the stacking, we ended up with a tremendous amount of vibration when the washer enters the final high speed spin cycle, to the point the floors shook. We looked at the various pads and feet on the market that claimed to help minimize vibrations.  I choose these because the material appeared sturdy and they looked easier to install than a pad under the whole machine, and a pad might block the overflow drain.  They arrived quickly, and were exactly as advertised.  The material feels solid enough that they should hold up.  We had a bit if a challenge installing them, since it requires lifting each corner, and it is hard to slide the machine once they are underneath, but I read a trick on line to spray some window cleaner on the floor where we wanted them to slide and we were able to get them all in place and slide the machine back in.  the result?  Much less vibration. There is still some, but they did improve the situation at a reasonable cost.

title: Product is very fragile, does not ship well. A lemon arrived at my house.
text:
On the plus side, this induction cooktop would have 5 stars if it got here in good functional condition. It worked very well after the first visit by Sloan Appliance Repair, an excellent shop. I look forward to using the completely repaired or replaced configuration, whenever that happens.
Don't order this online. Pay whatever extra it is to a good appliance store which will deliver, install, test.
I don't know if it was bad quality control at mfr Electrolux, shipping damage, or both. If we had not procrastinated 5 weeks as I am an old 155-LB weakling, we could have done an Amazon return/exchange.
It turned out that I could remove our radiant cooktop and install this one. Then when I closed the breaker the indicators went through an almost-normal startup sequence, then it was very hard to get any response from the controls. The most I could get was an error code indicating missing or defective temperature sensor.
Because Sloan is in high demand, the soonest appointment they could give me was 2 weeks out. The technician checked it, opened it, and discovered connections that had fallen apart. Also, the touch-sensing control card was not against the underside of the glass, because the tabs of its plastic frame had broken off. He ordered a new card, and advised me it would take a couple of weeks to come in. We placed a washcloth folded twice under the broken card to hold it in place. After assembly, the unit worked perfectly except that the touch points and indicators were a little out of place.
What I mean by worked perfectly: Functionally this is a very good design, and it's _induction._ I could go on about how well all the features work, but that would be very long.
This includes the basic induction cooking difference: The traditional radiant glass top is sluggish. It heats the glass first to some insane temperature, so the glass can heat your pan. If you get something to a boil, when you turn the heat down, it takes a long time for the glass to cool enough to stop the boil. You have to get in there and move the pan off the hot spot. And then, I'm not so skillful that I can prevent spills. I often spill food or stir it out of the pot. The extremely hot glass bakes spills to a crisp quickly. As I am not a neat freak, my crispy spills turned to sticky char with repeated ops.
An induction top, like a gas stove, lets the pot cool down as soon as you reduce the heat. If some directions say "remove from heat," you can turn the heat off and there you go. The glass is no hotter than the pot, and cools just as quickly. The glass is too hot to touch, and H appears to so indicate.
Today I boiled some water for an instant food. I could see the water start to swirl in seconds. When it came to a big frothy boil, I reduced from Power Boil to 6 and the froth settled right down.
The tech brought the new control card a few days ago. It seemed to work fine at first. The next day, I was buffing the glass with a paper towel and the unit started beeping as it does. I think the control had become sensitive to static charge. I could not turn it on. It worked after I held a moist towel to the glass for a while. This morning when I tried the first few times to turn the unit on, it would only come up in Locked mode. I had to get patient and work out how long to hold my finger on Lock, to unlock. Then I could fry my eggs. Sometimes when I have the one burner going, I can't start another one. I have called on Sloan to come back out.
To summarize--
* When this model works, it works very well. If your local store's installer puts one in and it's good, I think it will work well for a long time.
* This design does not ship well, at least in single boxes instead of stacked on pallets. The first one we ordered was sold through Amazon by a distant appliance store and when the truck arrived, the driver came to my door and explained that he discovered our item was a box of broken glass. The second one, same store, we got a call that the item would not arrive. I got the impression that it broke en route. Amazon disqualified that store and got this possible lemon directly from Electrolux (mfr of Frigidaire). There was a puncture, so I opened the box and saw perfect glass. I should have, as we always hear, reported the damage to the carrier and Amazon.
I am going to ask Sloan if they can just get me a replacement unit.
On the feature ratings below, 5 stars on each of those specifics.

text:
Yes, if you want coffee within 1/2 hour, you must break that vacuum seal in order for the coffee to drip through. The problem with this Melitta knockoff is that the Chinese (I suppose) didn't care enough about the ease-of-use of this product to create a good one. On the original that I had with a Melitta 10 cup thermos from the '70s, the ridges on the inside of the plastic cone extended almost to the top rim. That design prevented the paper from sticking to the sides and promoted am efficient drip. As has been written before, with this product the paper does stick; and you must lift the paper at the top edges repeatedly to get the drip flowing smoothly. That's a real pain, not to mention messy if you fill the cone to the top - and it could easily have been resolved with a proper understanding of the concept by the manufacturer, or a desire to make a quality product - neither of which took place I suppose.
