title: Thoughtless design results in frustrating use - Do not recommend.
text:
This is honestly the most frustrating range I have ever worked with. While nominally okay, the range has three design flaws that leave me continually frustrated:

(1) No low temperatures: The oven does not go below 300F. If you need to slow cook something (e.g. brisket or pulled pork), you cannot use this. Similarly, all of the burners on the range have flames between High and Medium, there is no true low flame level. The only way to reduce temperature further is to move to a different burner (there is one Large, two Medium, and one Small). Because there is only one small burner, you can only simmer one thing at a time.

(2) The Small burner is in the front: The small burner is nominally where you'll put something to simmer for a long time. Why is it in the front? Instead, I have to reach over the simmering dish to get to the Medium burners in the back.

(3) Tiny interior oven dimensions: I know it's a 20" oven, but I've had several. I could always fit my 16"x14" cookie sheets. However, in this oven the interior is 17"x13.75". This is due to the thick oven walls and the fact that the rack supports are recessed into the wall instead of protruding out of them. In ovens this small, every .25" matters.

Other annoyances:
- Oven is bad at high temperatures (400F and above). Takes a long time to come up to temperature, and then varies wildly according to my oven thermometer.
- When you drop the oven temperature (e.g. heat to 450F then drop to 375F), the oven will shut off. The pilot light is still burning, but the main burner never comes on again. Eventually you notice that your bread is sitting in a 200F oven, and is ruined. Good times.
- Oven needs manual ignition (same as burners). Even my cheap old Premier range lit the oven automatically.

It's very pretty, but this range seriously under-performs ranges that can be bought for half the price (e.g. Premier that I had previously). To be clear: Those ranges aren't great, but this one is worse. I really wish there were a solution for someone who lives in a small space and is serious about cooking. I would pay $2k or more for a good oven. Sadly, this isn't it.

title: Disappointing Performance and Durability Issues.
text:
I recently purchased the Portable Dryer 1600W-67 Inch Clothes Dryer with Foldable 3-Tier Electric Drying Rack, hoping to find an energy-saving and space-efficient solution for my small apartment. At first glance, the compact design and ease of assembly seemed promising. The 3-tier design provided ample space for my laundry needs, and the digital automatic timer was a convenient feature.

The Anion technology, which claims to eliminate bacteria and odors from clothes during the drying process, initially made the product feel like a great investment. However, my satisfaction with the dryer was short-lived.

After just a few weeks of use, I encountered a significant issue with the dryer. It stopped producing hot air, making it utterly ineffective for drying my clothes. This was a major disappointment, especially given the initial promise of energy savings and efficiency.

Considering the dryer's malfunction and lack of durability, I cannot recommend this product. The unreliability of the dryer not producing hot air is a significant drawback that must be taken into account before purchasing. It is disheartening to invest in a product that fails to deliver on its core function.

In conclusion, the Portable Dryer 1600W-67 Inch Clothes Dryer may be an attractive option for those looking for an innovative and convenient solution for small spaces, but its performance issues and lack of durability make it a poor choice. I would advise potential buyers to look for alternative solutions that offer better reliability and longevity.

After some really tough twisting and finger hurting, I got the thing on the Aeropress, just barely and made a cup of coffee. The second and not nearly as important problem is that it made the Aero Press more difficult to clean. When u remove the filter holder the coffee spills all over instead of staying in the press so you can just place it over the drain and push on the plunger
They send a brief instruction page with the filter and suggest that if all else fails you can call them and they'll give you some further tips on securing the filter to the Aero Press. I don't have time to fool around with them. If they have something to add why not just incule it with the instructions. Paper is cheap, time isn't

title: I've not been able to find another 7" damper anywhere of better quality). The damper rattles and makes much more ...
text:
The hood seems generally well designed and manufactured with care. I'd give it a 5 based on the hood operation EXCEPT it doesn't include a built-in damper. For installation, I purchased a flimsy damper from Home Depot (so far, I've not been able to find another 7" damper anywhere of better quality). The damper rattles and makes much more noise than the fan itself. I was unable to get a useful suggestion from the manufacturer's support email contact.

In my installation, the external exhaust it through the wall about 12" above the hood so there was no possibility of locating the damper remotely. The top of our kitchen cabinets are about 2' below the 10' ceilings so extending the exhaust through the roof is not possible.

Do NOT buy this unit unless you can solve the damper problem. The Broan unit we replaced (for double the air flow at about the same noise level) had a built-in damper which made not identifiable noise. I frankly don't understand why Proline wouldn't include a damper in the unit.

Their installation instructions are a bit confusing as there are details like the electrical connection which have change. Also, they provide one manual for multiple models and the only distinction is to compare the picture of the control panel. The mounting holes are not uniformly spaced from the edges and no drill template is provided so we had to hold the relatively heavy unit in position to mark the location of pilot holes. Off page references in the manual are wrong or the referenced material is actually missing. None of this was a show stopper but it must made installation more difficult than needed.

Oh, and our unit includes a clock ... a 24Hour only clock ... which displays when the fan or light or on.

2018/1/21: I was able to eliminate 95% of the damper noise by using heat duct tape to secure the damper in the collar which fits between the hood and the duct. Also, I added a small piece of foam weather stripping to the base of each damper 'blade'. About 1" from the bottom. This keeps the two 'blades' from bumping against each other.

title: Worst installation experience ever!
text:
I bought the product before Thanksgiving. This review has 2 parts: Installation and product performance. Installation gets 1 star. Performance so far gets 4 stars.
The product was clearly designed with no thought or consideration about ease of installation. Here's why:
1- The product is supposed to be hanging from 4 screws from under the cabinet. The screws need to be drilled with perfect precision, otherwise when you are lifting the hood to install it in place it won't go it. Remember you have no visibility at that point. What does Zephyr do to help you with this? Just a diagram of distance measurements.
What could they do to improve this experience? Supply a template sheet with drill holes marked so you can tape it under the cabinet, drill the holes, and be done. By the way that would also help ensure you have enough space under the cabinet without any lips or sides intruding.
Cost for that improvement? $0.05?
2- Once the hood is hanging from the screws, you need to tighten them (as the manual suggests). You need to do this laying on your back on the stove. But even then the front screws are impossible to reach though. Why? The only way you can reach them is at a 45 degree angle from front. Now imagine tightening a screw at 45 degrees. You will damage the screw head, and then you are stuck half way. The best way to avoid this is to take the hood down. Redrill the front holes at 45 degrees, and reinstall it that way. Does the manual specify that? No!
What could they to improve this? Clearly state the need to drill the front holes at 45 degrees.
Cost for that improvement? $0.00.
3- The power cable that comes with the unit has no plug, and is just about 4" long. What is the rationale for not having a plug and such a short length of cord? I don't know, but I can say that by the time you take the cord through the cabinet, you have little room for error when you are attaching a plug. I could bet that 90%+ of customers have an outlet within 3' of the unit. If you offer a 3' cord with a plug, and some minority of customers needs to change the cord, well they can cut it, and change it. Now everyone has to go through that.
Cost for that improvement? $1.00 max?
4- Finally is there a way this experience could've been world-class at low cost? Yes. They could change the installation process using simple system similar where four 1" mini-rails that you install under the cabinet, and then simply slide the hood into place. That way the unit is firmly attached vertically. To prevent horizontal play the unit can be attached to the rails with 4 short fat screws.
Cost for this improvement? The 4 mini rails, the corresponding rail-catcher on the top of the unit, and any delta in sheet-metal stamping. All would be less than $5.00

I am sending the washer machine back on Friday waiting for pickup currently to get my refund but in the meantime I am still not happy with my most recent purchase.

The used price $253 was a good some of us can't buy new always but still a good hit financially speaking for someone trying on a tight budget dishing out the money all at once but we stopped and thought it save money long term because I'm spending $30-50 a week at my local laundromat for myself & my boyfriend's laundry.

I wanted to set it and forget it! Not sit there wait to change it from cycle to cycle.

The first question from Amazon agent was did you get a manual with it? No I didn't! The Amazon agent sent me one through email.. it was thoughtful of them but wasn't in the box as a paper manual book from black and decker. title: I love this Portable Ice Maker
text: I love this Portable Ice Maker.  I cleaned it out and started using it the next morning.  As stated, it was quick, about 6-7 minutes for the first large ice cubes to be finished.  Because they are a little "wet", I let the machine drop a few times before scooping ice into a plastic bag and laying it somewhat flat in the freezer.  By the time the next batch was ready, I took the bag from the freezer, dropped it on the counter to break any pieces that may have frozen together, and put the ice in the freezers bucket.  I filled the freezer bucket in a few hours.  It was a bit of a nuisance to have to put the ice in a bag first but it wasn't that big of a deal.  It's fast, reasonably quiet and makes the perfect size ice for adding to water bottles, which sometimes have smaller openings and won't fit larger cubes.  Definitely worth the money.

It seems to be working fine so far, but only time will tell. Your results may be better than mine. Maybe mine was built on a Friday? Who knows. Either way, quality control needs to be more attentive. So if ordering this heating element, make sure to thoroughly check the individual coils and connections. I probably shoulda just sent it back for a replacement, but I needed this dryer up and running.

This item came in pretty dirty on the inside, which I thought was weird but soap and water fixed that. I live in apartments and it’s pretty loud, so I try not to use it too early or too late in the day. This is my second time using it - I had a regular size hamper full of clothes along with three full bed sized sheets I needed to wash. I started around 8am and ended around 2ish pm. (I was washing dishes, cleaning my apartment and working on hw in between). Very portable, and not heavy. I was able to lift it onto my kitchen counter (for the elevation) and I just stand on my kitchen chair while I’m using it. To get the water in, I just used buckets for now. The hose it came with is too small for my sink. I’m waiting for my detachable shower head to come in so I can just input the water from there and drain the water in my tub.

Washing:
For my clothes, if it’s heavy like work pants or jackets, I put only about 3-5 items and it worked well. For regular items like socks and underwear or light shorts and shirts, I was able to fit it about 8-10 items. Really depends on your clothes. But just know the spinner side will only fit half of what you washed. Example: I put 4 work pants to wash, but when I put them in the spin side, one two fit.
For my bed sheets, two were super thin and I was able to wash both together but had to spin them separately. I washed a bedsheet that was thicker and had to wash and spin it on its own.

Spinner: it’s true what they say. It won’t dry your clothes completely but it depends on the material. Some of my clothing came out dry and some didn’t. Whatever didn’t, I just hung up and opened the windows and by the end of the night - everything was dry.

Overall, I love how this machine washed everything. On the first drain, the water was gross but after the second drain, the water came out nice and clean. The spinner does it’s job and spins most of the water out of your soaking wet clothes to 85% dry.

Steps I used:
I wash my clothes on “normal” with detergent first (left side) for about 12 min, drain the water, then throw my clothes in the spinner (right side) for about 2 min, then throw clothes back to (left side), put the cycle to “normal” to wash with fabric softener for about 12 min, drain water, then back to the spin side for about 5 minutes to finish off.

Tips:
1. Use only a little bit of detergent and fabric softener.
2. Don’t over do it. It’s a small machine so it’s obvious that only a certain amount of items will fit.
3. Clean out your filter after you are done using the washer side (left side)
4. Wipe the inside of your machine down (on the spinner side there will be hair, lint from clothing and whatnot), and keep the lids up and open so it can dry out.

One thing I didn’t like at all - there’s a weird smell that comes from the machine while you use it, it made me a bit dizzy and nauseous. I’ll update this review after I’ve done a couple more washes to see if the problem continues.

I hope this review is helpful!

title: Equator Washer/Dryer Combo Black
text:
I've been using the machine for about a month now and have a few comments on it's operation and quality.
Pros: The machine cleans the clothes well and it dries the clothes completely even though I have seen other reviews indicating the clothes are still damp. I have found that when you first open the door and take the clothes out, they do feel damp. However, once the clothes are removed from the machine, the damp feeling goes away immediately. This may be a result of condensing drying where moisture does not fully evaporate inside the drum.
Cons: 1-The price point of this machine is relatively high for it to be so cheaply made. The first issue I noticed immediately was the cheap plastic door handle. That handle is going to break merely from normal use. The warranty information clearly states the handle is not covered. Clearly this has been a problem in the past and instead of using a metal handle the manufacturer chooses to claim no liability for the part. 2-The window covering the display gets covered in condensation during use. Since electronics and moisture do not mix, it's just a matter of time until the display fails. 3-Noise; the water pump is in use for about 75% of the wash/rinse/spin cycles and 100% of the dry cycle. This pump is very loud and annoying. I'm not sure why the manufacturer felt it was necessary to attempt to continue pumping when there isn't any water left in the drum. This will be the second part to fail since it is used so much. 4-Preset cycles can't be modified; the options can't be modified like water temperature and number of rinses. I prefer using the "Heavy" cycle but find it totally unnecessary to have 3 rinses. That is a waste of water and energy. The "Quick" cycle has 1 rinse but the wash cycle is only like 3 minutes which is not long enough to clean heavily soiled clothes. Even compact machines with a low price point allow for modifying the cycle settings.
If the above issues could be corrected it would be a perfect compact machine.

You can see a big difference between the little ridges near the top of the filter that latch onto the filter housing. I found I had to remove the top try near the filter to insert and turn it for a proper seal.

It is such a tight fit that I originally did not think that it was a correct replacement. Just be careful when installing it and it will eventually go in.

Note this is also smaller than the original as others have pointed out. The original one is larger and lasts longer so not a perfect replacement in my view. Unfortunately this seems to be the only replacement model from Samsung. There are a couple of other brands but you never know about those.

Mike

title: Design flaw holds this element back
text: I have had 3 of these elements in my Electrolux dryer in the last 6 years (including the one it came with).  The main reason I have had to replace the element is 2-fold:  (1) I was using flexible dryer duct that traveled around 20 feet before exiting the house.  As you may know, flexible duct is horrible at collecting lint in the folds and won't fully clean out even if you use a leaf-blower.  This likely sped up the process of the element overheating.  However, the other reason is (2) The design of the element allows the inner partition of the element to warp and eventually touch the outer sides of the canister, causing a ground condition and basically killing your element.  Had they designed this thing a little better, the element wouldn't warp and wouldn't cause a ground-out even if the dryer was getting a bit too hot.  Considering how much these things cost, that's a big deal.  So, to summarize, install solid ductwork (cheap and easy, so no excuses!).  Second, realize that over time, your element will warp and eventually fail unless they change the design (not likely). B-minus....

title: Lower bearing and Spindle not sized correctly
text:
This is not an overly challenging repair but it does have the potential for complications. For me the wash basin was seized to spindle and required extra effort to remove. The bearings and bearing press in this kit worked well and went together as they should. My next problem was the spindle installation. The spindle would not drop fully into position and required a little coaxing with the hammer. Every time I did this the bottom bearing work knock out of place and I would have to re-seat it. This involves starting over with the bearing press. By the third time I did this I decided to check the spindle against the lower bearing and it was immediately clear no amount of hammering was going to get the spindle into the lower bearing. They are sized incorrectly and are incompatible. I then checked the new lower bearing against the old used spindle and they went together perfectly. My wife is a nurse and we need our washer (especially now during covid), so even though it was worn, I put the washer back together using the old spindle. Everything from that point on went smoothly.
Two stars for the parts that worked, the press and the video they recommend you watch on installation. I didn't return because I was in a pinch and could make it work with the old parts. Please be sure to check you spindle against the bearing before you start the project. It could save you some time and heartache. I would have returned mine before taking everything apart if I'd done that.

title: Quality-built fan, but is not effective in cooling my attic
text: I live in southern Arizona. Our 2100 sq ft single-story ranch home is stucco with a tile roof. Summers are very very hot. In fact, by mid-April we’ve already seen temperatures up to 93F. Our attic reached 114F on that day. So I was hoping the gable-mounted attic fan would cool things down a bit. Mind you, our attic has a vented gable at each end, and is unobstructed. I strategically suspended a Govee battery-powered Bluetooth temperature / humidity sensor in the middle of the attic and monitored data before and after the attic fan installation. Unfortunately, the single, gable-mounted fan is not at all effective in reducing attic temperature - even on the highest fan setting (10). It does blow hot air out. I can feel it as I stand below it in the driveway. But it just doesn’t move enough air. It is clear that I’m going to have to mount another fan at the opposite end of house to suck air in and assist airflow. One minor gripe I have about the AC Infinity AIRLIFT fan is that the sensor cable is much shorter than the control cable. Why? I ended up having to purchase a separate extension cable from Amazon - which works great btw.

title: Works for what I needed - 4 1/4 stars if I could do that.
text:
Downside first: These things are overpriced in my opinion. Literally just three in a package which equates to ~$5 dollars apiece. OMG.!!

Plus side: They work perfectly for what I need!!

Why did I buy them? I have 8 not so cheap double walled cappuccino glasses (I make a daily cappuccino and don't want to wash the same two every other day, I am in hurry most morning to get to the office). So, I have one glass for each day of the week +1.

I use the dishwasher about once a week to wash most of my dishes. Normally that would be end of story, but what happens is that 1 or 2 (usually 2) of the glasses would tip over in the dishwasher and fill with dish water...Yuck!! (I don't have the latest and greatest up to date model).

This is where my friend Amazon steps in. Searching for something that would hold these glasses down, I find these pieces of urethane plastic. After looking all over google to see if I could find them cheaper (I couldn't at the time), I added to cart and completed my purchase.

A few days later they arrived. I used them the next time I washed dishes. I applied them as indicated to the little arm in my dishwasher to hold down the glasses, ran the load, checked when it was done, and no glasses have tipped over. I have used them over a dozen times now and no issues. My only concern is being in the hot water while in a slightly flex position seems to cause them to hold that shape afterwards.

Yes, there are other people just using rubber bands to accomplish the same result, but I liked the idea of these dish flip holder thingies.

TL;DR They work. They keep my glasses from tipping over in the dishwasher, and to me that is worth the price.

title: make sure you need this product before ordering
text:
Hi
After watching the Blower Wheel replacement video (part#WE16M17) from repairclinic dot com on youtube, went ahead and check my product on GE dot com for the correct replacement piece, then ordered WE16M15. There is tension clip that needs to be adjusted to fasten the wheel to the motor shaft. This task can be accomplished without removing the motor. You may not need to replace the blower wheel you have, rather tighten the tension to secure the wheel. If you do not clean the lint from this wheel every 5 to 10 years depending on use, the lint will jam the wheel and cause the devise to loosen from the motor shaft. Regretfully I order the part before disassembling the motor from the base. ( I am not the first to order this wheel from Amazon when they did not need it, since the product arrived in an open box). Wanted to post this review to prevent Amazon customers from ordering this product when they don't need it. Hope this is helpful!
Thanks

title: Great for bulk coffee, but not loose tea leaves
text:
My wife loves Downton Abbey. I actually got her hooked and now, she loves everything British and British history. She always loved tea, but after watching the series, she prefers loose tea leaves in a diffuser pot.

I got her a Keurig Duo coffee maker and these stainless steel pods thinking she could just put her loose chamomile tea leaves in it and have a nice cup of tea.

Boy, was I wrong! Tea needs to steep, i.e., sit in water. The longer it sits or steeps, the stronger and more robust the flavor of the tea. Using this reusable K-pod doesn't allow the tea to soak in the water so there is no flavor and no tea in the cup.

I'm sure if I experimented and densely packed the tea so the water would take longer to filter through it that I might be able to get more flavor. But the cost of packing so much tea is just not worth it (not to mention what it might do the coffee maker).

I read where some users put bags of tea in the carafe and used the hot water to fill it, but that's just like using a diffuser pot. So, my wife ended up using her original tea kit and not these pods.

My mother-in-law tried the pods with bulk Hawai'ian coffee and said it tasted great. So for coffee, these pods are a good alternative to pre-filled K-pods. For anything else, it's useless.

title: Works OK, But Leaks
text:
This product is well-made and it does work -- you can brew your own coffee in a Keurig. However, it LEAKS. I have experimented with differing methods and there is no way around it. Apparently it overflows during the brewing process splashing coffee everywhere. I would say 1-2 tablespoons of leakage. After brewing I first wipe down the brewer spout (usually it is covered with coffee), then hold a paper towel under the brewer opening and pop it open. This catches the drips that otherwise end up on my counter top. Finally I wipe out the interior of the brewer.

How big of a deal this will be for you I can't say. For me it takes the convenience out of using the Keurig. The prepackaged K Cups work perfectly every time, and there's no cleanup of the machine or the cup. So I'll be using standard K Cups for coffee.

I would like to point out that it seems to work better for tea. I put a single bag in the Fill N Save and may get a drop or two inside the brewer, but nothing like brewing coffee.

title: Filters well but doesn't last as long as it should, watch for failures!
text:
This unit does have the specs to filter pretty much everything out of the water when it is new it however doesn't last as long as it should. We notice the water flavor start to change at around 85 gallons. The filter is supposed to last 125 gallons. SO $50 per filter with only 85 gallons = $0.59/per gallon. A RO system will run you about $0.02 per gallon and isn't hard to install yourself, consider that route early and save a lot of money over the long run.

Beware of mid life filter failure! Note your flow rate when the filter is new. if the flow significantly increases during the life of the filter (eg sprays out of fridge at much strong pressure) then the filter may have failed internally and is just bypassing your tap water. This happened on one of the 5 we have purchased so far.

title: Do Not!! Use packaged manual
text:
[[VIDEOID:12b2a6c5fe599d937e7a23f99376db1e]] There are two different models, the JL is the newest. They use different carbon filters if converting to non-exhaust (in room circulation). So you can't order filters through mfg website until you have product s/n in hand so they can sell correct carbon filter. The actual hood width is 29.5", which matches the template. There should be a slight gap on either side. Mine will be tighter than the 2/5" recommended, more like .25 ". Picture of carbon filter installed prior to install. It will be a pain after as with a 25" gap between stove top & hood and filters being recessed, the stove will need to be removed every time filters need changed unless you think it possible to lay on the stove upside down and manuever within a 25" gap.🤔

Download and print the latest online version of the manual before doing anything else! The packaged one is likely obsolete based on package date.

Pictures in product description do not show location of power cord (right side). Ordered a plug to fill previous power hole on left side (once again Amazon). Templates go on with print side against the wood. If not you get outlet hole on wrong side. I cut a 1.5" hole centered for new power cord (measure 2x cut once). The part about bending over excess on template is for top template. Remember there is an extra gap on template edging beyond the printed line take into consideration.

The directions only indicate the weight as "heavy" (it is actually 59 lbs and change per TS). Better make sure your cabinet supports are screwed into studs and not just drywall anchors, so your significant other does not end up wearing it, if not I hope your job is good enough to cover alimony & child support 😉. There is no way to use the wall keyholes as designed for a under cabinet install, but you can use the top ones (a must & first point of connection). The packaged manual directed screwing into drywall before top. The new version does a 180.

You have to remove stove/oven to install (obviously)& space is a premium so getting holes properly aligned is critical to success. Use the template as a rough only, then measure the crud out of it every which way but loose twice over. Take into account trim and cabinet offsets for reference measurements if not you will pay for it.

One support person said some people vent into cabinet (when using carbon filter kit and not exhausting through a wall) and the drawing only shows hole in cabinet bottom, not top. At 500 cfm and nowhere to go expect back pressure, overheated motor, and doors flopping like your cabinet is haunted, not to mention a mini sauna from vented clean steam into cabinet, unless the carbon filter blocks "all" moisture and fills drip pan. Black mold in a cabinet would not be fun. If there is a gap between ceiling and cabinet top, best to cut a hole directly above the first.

A 8" hole will not likely be enough for bottom hole if using the keyhole slide method in top ideally 8.5 or slightly more"). They need to relocate exhaust vent in design slightly to compensate for the offsets in my humble opinion. Why you ask? Well with an 8" hole you have exactly .25" clearance between duct and hole (when it is not collapsed) add width of compressed duct plus the 1/2" offset (1/4 all around) to slide top from keyhole to slot (final resting place) and you have a preinstalled duct ramming into a cabinet instead of through a hole with 8"! Bending the duct to try forcing it in is asking for damage to it. Duct must be installed before hood goes up depending on whether your entire cabinet bottom is flush or if you have standoff supports with gap in middle see picture. If there is a gap, there will be no room to attach ring to duct after installing hood. The alternative to a larger hole might be to set up some temporary support to rest the hood on and have someone hold in place while someone else sinks screws into all the predrilled/anchored holes. Picture attached of one concept I may use if run into a duct clearance issue. This is where keeping all that scrape lumber around pays off and you can tell your wife, I told you so. New lumber is not cheap. Also due to weight and only 4 wood screws on top, you are going to want to use the beveled washers on top to disperse the weight to a larger area than screw head. Well because the beveled washers provided are the same size as keyhole or a smidge bigger, when raising the hood over preinserted screws it is unlikely they will drop through keyhole in order to allow sliding but hey maybe not. Just saying pre-fit the beveled washers before getting to far in as it would be irritating to raise it up and not have the washers drop through. You may need to buy your own or plan to insert screws and beveled washers while someone holds up 59lbs who keeps saying hurry up I can't hold much longer then drops it with 2 screws in, ripping out the bottom of your cabinet ouch. The wood screws are designed for the washers so even though no direction in manual provided how to use them, they better be on bottom side of hood when your done.

(Think"everything" through before you grab the first tool or pencil or end up measuring everything 4x). Instead of buying an 8" flange to come down from top hole, I bought a 8" louvered & screened vent to point exhaust in direction of my choosing. It is the tightest fit imaginable to get the provided ducting over it, but it can be done and avoids the cost of a flange & is so tight I won't need a band. See pictures ( Amazon is your friend here - struck out at Lowes).

Getting top hole aligned with bottom hole is tricky. Take into account the inside cabinet wall side thickness when measuring bottom edge to align top hole as bottom hole won't have the extra material. My top hole kisses (lip locks) the cabinet support at the top. Drill a small test hole from bottom to check saw alignment from top down to make sure you don't cut through a support ledge. You may need to offset slightly to avoid that screw-up.

This hood may sit a lot lower than what it replaces. Measure from cab bottom to stove, subtract 10, should be 24-36, if not reconsider your purchase. Still waiting on my hole saw..first one defective arbor pins would not align with saw sent back. Second one discounted "like new" was missing arbor and bit all together. So now after research the correct arbor on order via Amazon from same German mfg. so it should fit. I trust German QC more than some others and leave it at that.

Hope you found humor in this review but the installation will be anything but funny if you do not spend the time to triple check centered spacing side to side, hole spacing to back wall and spacing between holes. Wear gloves and use care to prevent dings and scratches, ie don't throw any tools at it while cussing. 😉

title: Worst Oven Ever - And Dangerous!
text:
This range was in our kitchen when we purchased our home last year. The kitchen had been remodeled and the oven was brand new. I cook A LOT and it gets dangerously hot on the top of the range when using the oven - if you have young children like I do, I strongly caution you not to purchase this range. For example, if you're baking something and also using the top burners, and you've left a metal spoon on the top of the range, when you go to grab the spoon to stir what's cooking, watch out, if you forget to use a pot holder, YOU WILL BE BURNED and if you're like me you'll throw the spoon in the air after forgetting (again). On the plus side, if you need to defrost something quickly (currently defrosting frozen fruit while baking cookies), this is excellent. But, if you proof bread, don't leave it top of the range if the oven is on, IT WILL GET TOO HOT and kill your yeast!!

I called Electrolux/Frigidaire for months and had the range tested several times - it's just a low end model with poor insulation and no engineering fix to correct the excessive heat. So dangerous! And, the broiler is horrible - it's in the bottom of the range (where you typically store pots/pans), but you can't store anything in the drawer and good luck lifting hot meats from the bottom of the range (without burning the kids!!) without spilling everywhere - HORRIBLE design! Convinced yet? I just cannot say enough bad things....would NEVER purchase this model and brand again. Customer service also very disappointing - they do not take safety issues seriously or handle well at all (at their own admittance by the end of my ordeal!!).

title: UPDATED - you get what you pay for
text:
UPDATE: I wrote a very unflattering review earlier and I’m back to add context now that I’ve bought the original filters to compare. The product isn’t bad, but it is not a like comparison to the original Honeywell filters. These filters have smaller mineral traps (the blue layer), the wicking layers are fewer (I count 10 on these and somewhere between 20-25 on the Honeywell’s), the wicking layer’s weave is much less dense on these compared to the Honeywell, the dimensions are not quite big enough to fill the filter holder while the Honeywell is almost too big so it needs fills it completely, and these just don’t last anywhere near as long before getting crusty/smelly/delaminating/all of the above.

At the end of the day these end up not wicking anywhere near the same amount of water up to the humidifier’s fan so the output is vastly reduced compared to a Honeywell filter, and of my 4 pack one was so bad it didn’t wick water up at all. For me no amount of a cheaper cost justifies how poor these perform. I have completely moved back to using official Honeywell replacements. For cost official Honeywell filters were $20 for 2, and these were $20 for 4.

I will be raising from 1/5 stars (given out of anger) to 3/5 stars as this product is what it says it is. I just do not think it’s a good product.

Pictures added for comparison.

ORIGINAL: Bought this pack after I went through the wicks/filters that came with my HEV620. The manufacturer’s wicks/filters would wick water about 2/3 of the way up the wick/filter. These don’t even pull water up an inch past where it sits in the water. I’ve tried multiple wicks/filters from the pack, and all behave this exact same way.

This product is a complete waste.

title: Not For K-Supreme Plus Smart Brewer
text:
I do not recommend this reusable pod for the K-Supreme Plus Smart Brewer because the Pod ID feature does not recognize it as a pod and so it only offers the "hot water" option when using it. I didn't forsee this problem because the brewer recognizes store brand K-Cups and the "My K-Cup" reusable pod. It doesn't know what coffee is in them so it can't recommend a brew setting, it simply says "Classic Brew" and requires you to pick a saved favorite or enter a new setting.

With this pod the message indicates that there is no pod in the holder, that you need to insert a pod or press "K" for hot water. Selecting hot water would still get you coffee, sort of. The stream for hot water is faster than what it is for brewing so your coffee would be weaker, and you wouldn't be able to change the temperature.

I managed to brew a cup by putting the lid of a My K-Cup against the reader before closing the brewer to trick it into thinking that's what was in the holder. I don't know if that trick would work with anything else but it would be a pain to have to do on a regular basis. I only use reusable pods occasionally so it's something I can live with, though I wish I didn't have to.

I gave three stars instead of one because it's understandable that an accessory made by one company may not work 100% correctly on a product made by another company, and I imagine that it works fine with the other Supreme models that don't have the Pod ID feature. Now, if this pod had been made by Keurig for use with their own brewers this issue would not be acceptable, at all.

title: Good to go
text: So far so good have had this dryer now for a month, use it a few times a week. Drying time is good a full dry load depending on wetness of clothes is 60mins on average. Clothes that are very wet will take double that time. The lint filter is compact and easy to maintain, the manufacturer recommends cleaning the filter once a week but given the size of the dryer and depending on how often you use I would recommend cleaning it as often as possible, for me I clean the lint filter after two uses to keep maximum drying efficiency between loads. The unit is fairly quiet, it does make noise but it's not loud to where In my opinion it would distract you from carrying on with other household tasks or enjoying some form of entertainment. The panda dryer is also safe to use with dryer sheets. title: Questionable accuracy and precision
text:
I run a guitar repair shop and it is very important to monitor and maintain a consistent humidity between 45% and 50%. That being said, I need to keep hygrometers that will maintain consistent readings. Please refer to my photos for what I found:

The Indoor Digital Hygrometer Thermometer being reviewed here is the black horizontal one. The black/silver one an AcuRite I purchased at the same time (reviewed elsewhere). The white digital hygrometer is an AcuRite I purchased over a year ago from Home Depot, which has been fairly consistent and reliable. Each of these can sit out in my shop, in a guitar case, or in my storage room.

I let all 3 hygrometers sit together in a corner of my shop about 5 feet away from my dehumidifier for about a week. As you can see, the Indoor Digital Hygrometer Thermometer regularly tracked higher than the 2 AcuRites, often by as much as 5 percentage points, but not consistently. It did not change as readily if moved into a dry part of the building or outside. It appears that 50% is a "sweet spot" and that it tends to lose accuracy as it is exposed to humidity levels higher or lower from there.

I give this 2/5 stars because I intend to keep this and use it (most likely) in a storage room where I do not expect many changes in humidity and where I will keep less wood that will be susceptible to humidity. I will have to keep in mind that it will (on average) measure about 5 percentage points high. I can't say I'd recommend this product since it appears to be unreliable both in accuracy and precision. This appears to be a case of "you get what you pay for."

title: Biggest mistake ordering this!
text:
My husband bought this vent hood for its great suction ability. That is true. That is the good news.
It took my very handy husband and an equally handy and strong neighbor a couple of hours to install this unit. It would have been nice to have had a drilling template, for one thing.

The first time we used the auto clean feature, we removed the oil retainer some time after and got soapy water all over the back of the stove. Perhaps the manual should have said to wait about an hour for the hose to drain before emptying the oil retainer.

Within about three months of buying the vent hood, it stopped working so we were sent another one with another agonizing installation process.

The first time we did the cleaning and maintenance, the gaskets on the filters were misshapen and would not go back on so we had to order more which took one month to arrive. Since we couldn't wait that long, my husband had to buy a product to make his own gaskets…a very messy process.

Three months later we discovered that the auto clean feature wasn't working.

We did another cleaning and maintenance yesterday and I can't believe that we, up in our 70’s will be forced to do this forever.

We have one more year on our two year warranty, but we don't have the energy, heart, or inclination to take it down yet again and get another Hauslane vent hood in which we have stopped having any faith.

I am amazed that it has gotten so many good reviews. They are what caused us to buy it in the first place.

title: Leaking Oil
text:
Based on the dates of the other 1-star reviews, it seems like Costway has a bad batch of product--or I just have bad luck. I bought this as a gift for my husband after he raved about one that his parents have. I was super excited to give it--he was super excited to receive it. We waited more than the recommended three hours before plugging in and were sad to see that it would only produce two ice cubes at a time--and maybe 6 ice cubes per hour--one large cube and one small. Over the last two weeks since its arrival, it may have made one half basket while on for hours. We have tried to contact company per their packaging insert to try to troubleshoot fix ourselves, but the phone rings off the hook. Today it is leaking oil.

UPDATE--I reached out to the company who asked me to send a picture of the leaking oil. They then refunded me my money. I am appreciative of that so I've increased my rating to 3 stars even though I'm still unhappy with the fact that I REALLY wanted a working ice maker and still don't have one.

title: REMOVE THE 4 TRANSPORT BOLTS IN THE BACK OF MACHINE!!!!
text:
I set up the washer/dryer and was super excited until I started the first load! The thing shook my basement so violently like it was possessed and walked around… it also ripped the drainage hose out of the wall and water was everywhere. Needless to say I was over it… the washer wasn’t full of clothes, the washer/dryer was level. I couldn’t figure it out. I contacted Amazon customer service and started a return. The day before it was scheduled to be picked up… and then I saw a video about “transport bolts” AND how you have to remove all 4 bolts. I cancelled the return!! Then 5 days later it started doing its walking thing asking so it’s not the bolts. This combo Absolutely SUCKS! It takes FOREVER to dry… No exaggeration 4hrs at least. I started to hang drying the clothes it dried faster and cheaper than running the dryer, I end up returning it. The great thing about amazon is the return, they send a company to the house and picks it up as-is no box. You just need to put it by a entry door first!

BUYER BEWARE UPDATE: 30 days+ no refund…. It is a complete nightmare dealing with amazons refunds department it’s been over a month still no refund and the crazy part is a customer can track it on the same system to see where the package is… it’s been sitting in a Amazon warehouse since October! I called Amazon and was told to call back on 11/1 to get a manual refund…then the date changed to 11/4 and then the date changed to 11/14. Each time I call regarding this I get transferred to at least 5 different representatives. This is the first and last large appliance I purchase from Amazon….the refund process is the absolute worse. The end result is Amazon is tying up my money and I’m still without washer/dryer.

title: Cloth diapering user
text:
I'm a cloth diapering parent and moved in to an apartment with a shared laundry facility. I knew the laundromat was not going to work so we needed a portable washer. Ive never used one before so i didnt want to invest a lot of money to have the thing break on me after a short period of time. I figured this washer was a good starter washer. I hope it lasts a minimum of one year. Two would be better! Though I suspect the hoses will crack at some point before that since they are cheap. Fingers crossed that they don't.

Initial set up, i didnt realize the drainage hose would constantly drain if it wasn't hooked in an upright position. My mistake. It took me a bit to figure out what I was doing wrong. Second issue, the hose to fill up the tub is useless. I'm going to have to take another reviewer's advice about getting a short garden hose. Right now I'm using a one gallon pitcher to fill it up. Kind of annoying but it's temporary. Third issue is the drainage hose is short so I can only fill the tub up so high before the water is spilling out during a wash. This limits me to 6 prefolds per wash. With twins, I can see this is going to leave me doing multiple loads of laundry each day. Fourth issue, the first day I used the washer it smelled like burning plastic. I had to open every window in my apartment to air it out. Second day he smell is minimal.

I'm just beginning the stripping of my prefolds and so far so good. They're getting clean. I can see the manufacturing chemicals and residues in the water when I empty the tub. My babies are due any day now so I will have to come back and edit this review after I've seen how the babes' bottoms react. I am only using prefolds so I don't have any comments on how wel microfiber, wool, fleece, wash in the product.

title: Nope. Just Nope!
text: I've been refilling my Nespresso Vertuo pods using Recaps aluminum refill caps for months now without a hitch. I took apart several Gran Lungo capsules, weighed the contents and carefully viewed the grind size, then duplicated that with my own custom roast. I even load my capsules with a little less coffee than the Nespresso brand contain. 9.5 grams to be precise. Never a problem. Ever. However, using these lids the machine immediately goes into error mode. Upon close inspection, I realized that I need to use less coffee in the pod AND the grind size needs to be much bigger, so it doesn't plug the tiny holes on the outside rim of the silicone lid. Guess what that means? Weak coffee. I had high hopes for these, and the only reason I'm giving 2 stars instead of one, is because if you like weak coffee and you want to use drip grind size coffee in your pod, they will kinda work. Seriously, you can't even open a store bought pod and use the coffee inside with this lid, it won't work. Disappointing.

text: After researching many lines and types of vent hoods I purchased the 109.36, after speaking to the folks at Proline. The shipment was on time and damage free. Installed relatively easily, In a kitchen remodel so had to adapt the hood to both cabinets and 2x4 locations. Once installed two things where quickly noted. First was how quiet  the hood was in all speeds. I did install a new 8" straight run no 45s or 90s in the exhaust. We went from a broan 230 CFM to this new unit and the proline is only 53db on low and 63db on high. The broan was 60 db at only 230 CFM. The second item noted was the LED lights.  They are more of a night light than cooking lights, not very bright. Proline please address this and the hood would be a 5 star for sure. the light is either on or off,Very dim. The saving grace to this is the warming light sockets, placed some LED lights in there and have sufficient light to cook with. Use the front lights for night light and the rear warming light with led bulbs placed in them for cooking. We are pleased with the unit after installation and first use.

title: Looks nice, but flawed design
text:
I got this to replaces our previous pod refill device which has been misplaced. I wanted to like this, but it is flawed.
First the pros
1 The finish on the wood is excellent, it is a really nice-looking piece to have on your countertop.
2 The base unit has a slot cut in it to store the foil lids, so you don't have to stash them in a drawer where the get crushed.

3. The foil lids were sized perfectly, the last kit I purchased the foil lids were a bit larger in diameter and had too much overhang.

CONS.

1 The first thing I noticed was the tiny scoop and brush. The scoop is so small it takes multiple scoops to fill the pods. I grabbed a tablespoon from our drawer. The brush is too small to be effective. I grabbed a clean paint brush from my wife's craft table.

2 There are no directions. I had done this before so the lack of directions didn't hurt me too much, but if you hadn't refilled these pods in the past a few words and pictures for guidance would be nice. Also there a was strip of double stick tape in there with no explanation of what it was for.

3 The holes cut in the base to hold the pods stable while filling and attaching lids were not cut deep enough to properly support the coffee pods. An espresso pod would work, but we normally drink the coffee in the 7.77 pods and the pod is taller than the depth of the hole. This will be remedied in the drill press before I fill another set of pods since the base is thick enough to cut the hole a little deeper.

Overall, I believe there are better choices on Amazon for refilling these pods, but in my opinion, if the manufacturer took a couple of simple steps, this would be a 5 star item

title: Fire hazard
text: Changed the element in my 20-yr old Kenmore with this part. I noticed it seemed to get crazy red hot when I installed it in 2020 but researched and read that most dryers get red-hot like stove elements. In Jan. 2023 my wife went down stairs to see if clothes were dry. She screamed "the dryer is on fire" ! I ran down & the flames were traveling the dryer vent already and coming out of the element area. Thank God she caught it when she did. I was able with her help to get the fire out before it started the subfloor above on fire but suffered some pretty good blisters in doing so. Before you ask, YES we cleaned our dryer vent before each load. Like most houses , we had the cheap run of the aluminum foil type vent, DO NOT USE THAT CRAP it should be illegal,  it will burn !  I have taken all that down and am going to replace w/ the rigid galvanized vent pipe. I have also added a Co2 fire extinguisher next to the washer dryer area. NEVER EVER leave home with a dryer running ! AND DON"T BUY THIS REPLACEMENT ELEMENT ! Buy a OEM approved replacement and all thermostat/thermocouple fuses that go with that part ! $30 bucks savings is not worth you , your children, pets and home !

title: Ridiculously expensive
text:
These filters are ridiculously expensive. I think the appliance manufacturers see the filter market as a major revenue stream.

We live in a developed country, with some of the best water standards in the world. If we assume our municipal water supplies are meeting the mandated standards, these filters shouldn’t be necessary. In cases where the utilities are not - looking at you Flint, MI - these filters often don’t help with those contaminants. We buy these because we’ve been conditioned to think we need them. title: This set may fit but gave me trouble
text: This is a set of aftermarket belts that is proof that good price isn't always a good deal. I love my old Maytag washer and for the first time since it was new (20 years) I had a bad agitator/spin drive belt. Bought this set of belts that included the pump-out belt. This Maytag washer is made so when the wash cycle is done and it goes to the spin cycle the motor reverses to spin dry and the O.E.M belt rubber is hard enough to allow the belt to slip until drum is at full spin speed, This way the motor never is pulled slower that it's full RPM. This aftermarket drive belt was not to O.E.M spec. and didn't allow the belt to slip, this pulled the motor down and over heated the drive motor. Because I was already in a middle of a load of wash the only thing I could think of was to grind the outer edges of the V of the belt down one layer of the multi layer belt. This worked for now. MY ADVISE IS TO ORDER O.E.M MAYTAG/WHIRLPOOL BELTS.

title: Excellent Range Hood at a Great Price!
text:
I'm very pleased with this purchase and would recommend it to others. It has a much higher air flow capacity than many of the other range hoods costing much more. The electronic display is much easier to clean than push buttons. I like the timer feature that will automatically turn off the fan after a predetermined amount of time. The stainless steel filters are sturdy and easy to clean. The plug on the power cord makes for easy installation, if you have an outlet appropriately placed. My previous range hood was hard-wired, so I had to install an outlet to plug in the new range hood. I wish the clock could be set to the 12 hour format, instead of the 24 hour format, but this isn't a major problem since most range hoods don't even have a clock. The biggest problem I had was that the chimney was about 8 inches too short, requiring me to reuse the chimney from my last range hood, and since the dimensions were different, I had to place wood trim behind the chimney, as a spacer. Overall, installation would be very simple, if your ceiling isn't as high as mine and you could use the provided chimney. The instruction manual was good, but it didn't describe how to install the chimney brackets and the two round spacers that were included. This is a good quality range hood. It was packed very well and arrived within two work days. As I said, in the beginning, I'm very pleased with the quality and ease of installation and would recommend this range hood to others.

Update: After three years of little use and regular cleaning of the filters, the fan started making squeaking sounds and froze up, shortly afterward. I'm very disappointed. As little as this fan was used and as often as the filters were cleaned, I expected this fan to function for at least 10 years.

title: Poor Fit for B60
text:
This part appears to be a minimum specification item designed to separate you from a few bucks once and it took 10 days to arrive. The manufacturer does not appear to care about quality and probably has never tried it in a Keurig machine.

The part does not appear to be an OEM replacement part. The plastic is softer than the original and it does not clip into the machine as does the original. The needle also has a larger bore and this will likely mean that the water runs through the pod faster and may produce a weaker brew. It works -- but just barely. When the pod holder lifts out with the pod, I'll need to get another version to preclude damage to the machine if it is closed on a poorly seated pod holder.

Next time, I'll be ordering the one that is Amazon Prime and that I can get in in a day or two. I suggest you try ordering one of the others. It'll cost more but you will get it faster and it may be a higher quality part. Who knows, it may even work well. Good luck!

title: ***Edited*** Too much plastic taste
text:
***EDITED REVIEW***

After a successful year of using these two filters I bought another replacement. Remembering the issues I had before (see original review below) I grabbed an old gallon jug and measured TWO gallons of water to absolutely ensure I had cleared out any gunk remaining in the filter from the manufacturing process. After a day or two I filled my water cup and started drinking (first thing in the morning). The water tasted a lot like plastic again. This time it was bad enough that my wife noticed it as well when I had her check it. Refund requested. We'll try a more expensive option and see if we have the same problem.

Seller "Certified Battery" requires me to pay for return shipping and will only refund 80% because the item is damaged. Do not buy from them!

***Original Review Below***
I checked the model number on my refrigerator and searched Amazon for a water filter that would replace it. The description on this filter said it would fit my fridge and the price was way better than the official product replacement. Good shipping, came quick, great price, five stars. One thing to add... I didn't read the directions before installing the filter. It is VERY straight forward, pop the old one out and pop the new one in. There's a little turn involved but that is clearly marked on the bottle. One thing I forgot: you have to clear out or purge the new filter prior to using it. I noticed soon after installation there was a moderately strong plastic-like taste to the water. It didn't get any better the second or third day. Suddenly, I remembered when the guys from the store installed my fridge they ran a bunch of water into a bucket before telling me the water was ready to use. As soon as I remembered that I grabbed a bucket and ran at least 1 gallon out of the system. Plastic taste: gone. Oops. I doubt there were any health repercussions, but I would have preferred not to be drinking weird tasting water for a couple days. By the way, my family did not report noticing the taste, that's how mild it was. So today the water tastes great and I've got a second filter on standby when this one expires in a few months.

title: LG microwave
text:
I recently mounted this microwave over my stove between some cabinets. It does fine microwaving food, but the vent fan is SOOO loud, even on the "Low" setting. I think this is the loudest microwave I've ever seen.
Also, there is no Timer function, which baffles me. Pretty much every microwave ever has had a timer function for cooking. We ended up buying a magnetic timer for the fridge for a few bucks. This microwave looks nice.

FOR THOSE WHO WANT TO MOUNT THIS MICROWAVE UNDER A CABINET: I've seen several people saying their microwave caught on fire while cooking. I remember reading the instructions and them saying you have to adjust the microwave's case depending on how it will be used. If the microwave is sitting on a counter, it will vent differently than if it is mounted under a cabinet. If people are mounting their microwaves with the vent covered instead of changing the provided hardware to make it vent correctly, I bet that would cause a fire. I think the default setting is for it sitting on a counter.

This is the same microwave as the LG LMV1683SW (white) and the LMV1683ST (stainless).

title: Wonderful machine that fits the need but is very rough on clothes.
text:
The eco-egg fills a need I have that I couldn't find any other solution for: small home without the plumbing for a washer/dryer. It's incredibly easy to use, lightweight, and feels durable. Mine is kept under the sink and I can simply pull it out and set the drain hose into the sink. Although it comes with a quick-disconnect hose for water hookup, I was able to buy an adapter and y-hose at the hardware store to hook it into the supply for my sink, giving me a more permanent mount without getting in the way of the faucet. The load size is unsurprisingly small, but more than sufficient for its purpose. Laundry isn't a chore to do every two or three days since it only takes a few minutes of actual time to manage.

Despite how great this product is, I couldn't give it too many stars because it's really hard on my clothes. Almost every load brings a new rip, tear, or snagged thread. I believe that this is related to the design of the top of the shell, where some sharp edges poke out around where the water comes in. If it weren't for this fact I'd give it five stars without hesitation. In the meantime, a few ruined clothes are still cheaper to replace than it would have been to install a proper washer in my home and the hassle saved from going to the laundromat is more than worth it.

text:

I disassembled the old one. In my case the failure was caused by arcing across the mechanical 240V/25A over the years which eventually destroyed the copper contact pads. I cleaned them, but replacing the whole timer unit was the long term solution.

The photos show the contact pads on the original timer for the heating element switch and the carbon residue from the arcing.

title: It got worse and worse until it was so loud that I ...
text:
It's hard to imagine a single refrigerator causing so many problems.

I was bed-bound with a broken ankle when the machine starting making a racket. It got worse and worse until it was so loud that I couldn't sleep. Keep in mind that I couldn't walk and was stuck in a place without phone service.

I did a lot of on-line research and learned about a problem with Samsung refrigerators freezing up a solid block of ice behind the refrigerator section. This makes the circulating fan continually ding on the ice, until it is ultimately unable to move. The problem is caused by a drain at the bottom of the refrigerator section; it freezes over and then liquid from the defrost cycle can't drain.

The solution was to take everything out of the refrigerator, remove the shelves and drawers, and then unscrew the back panel to get at the ice. I did all of this standing on one leg and in great pain. The ice was so bad that the back panel wouldn't come off. It took about 24 hours for the ice to melt enough to remove the panel and for the remaining ice to melt.

There's a little metal clip-thingy that you can install over the drain hole to keep the drain from blocking with ice. I didn't have it on hand, of course, so had to reassemble the refrigerator without it. I ordered the part - it's cheap - in case the problem would reoccur.

Three months later: there is water all over my floor from the drain pan. It appears that the drain hole is plugged again. I will have to take all day, and possibly part of tomorrow, to go through the whole process of unplugging, disassembling, and waiting for the ice to thaw. Then I will add in the little clip to keep it from happening again - hopefully, anyway.

It's three days before Christmas. I have a lot of food in my refrigerator. Some of it will have to be thrown away.

Samsung - and any other manufacturer who reads this - we are tired of appliances with lots of features but low reliability. I need appliances that don't cause me a lot of stress, and don't require replacement after three or four years. Yes, I'm willing to pay more for a reliable refrigerator. I'd pay DOUBLE if it didn't mean having to buy refrigerators twice as often as is reasonable.

title: A Simple Fix to no Ice. Genuine Samsung 9-Cube Ice Marker Part (Made in Korea)
text:
My 9 year old Samsung French Door fridge decided it wouldn’t make Ice anymore. Well it started making less and less until it stopped all together.

Like all the other reviews say, this is a simple fix and likely your issue to no ice. I was nervous about finding the right replacement part as I was getting mixed parts from different sites including Samsungs own replacement part site. If you don’t know if this is the correct ice maker replacement, just take a photo of your old one from underneath. As you can see from my photos, the original was DA97-07365A. The updated version for my fridge is this DA97-07365G.

For install, you need to find a #2 Philips screwdriver and the breaker in your fuse panel. I was luckily that my fridge had its own breaker, but if it didn’t I would just have killed the entire kitchen breaker and dealt with resting clocks on my oven and microwave. Don’t be silly and try to move your fridge to unplug it and ruin your floor.

After install (and turning back on power), press and hold the Test button for 8-10 sec. If you don’t hear a “ding-dong” sound from holding the Test button, come back again after a few hours and try again. It took me a few tries and about 3-4 hours before I got the “ding-dong” sound. Minutes later Ice started dropping. Magic!

title: Design Could be Better
text: Bought this ice maker to avoid an expensive repair after the one in my side by side fridge broke down for the second time. We have the original Opal ice maker at work and is still going strong. Be sure to clean the until regularly and used filtered water to avoid mineral deposit build up. The biggest disappointment is the extra side water reservoir. I thought this would be great and reduce the amount of times I needed to fill the bottom of the ice maker. I was very disappointed to discover that water is transferred from the side water reservoir to the ice maker by flowing up a tube in the back of the unit and draining down on the existing ice to reach the bottom of the ice maker. This only manages to melt a good portion of your ice that is made already every time it pulls from that unit. Rather that transferring the water directly to the bottom where it is needed to make ice, it just dissolves a good amount  of your existing ice. After seeing a full ice tray reduced time after time by flowing water when it was already more than full, we disconnected the side water reservoir completely. Problem solved but what a waste of what should be a nice feature.

title: A mixed bag...
text:
l purchased this product over 3 years ago, and it has been the primary cooktop for our kitchen. We do cook regularly and the cooktop does undergo a good amount of use daily. Having used it for 3 years, I think the product has been a mixed bag of wows and oh-nos. We have had some issues with the cooktop (details below) and being quite handy, I had opened up the cooktop and replaced parts myself (although I would not recommend this unless you are sure of what you are doing). I have had a good look at the insides and some of my feedback is based on that.

Pros:
- It is beautiful. When we bought the cooktop, we did extensive research and visited all of the home appliance stores to pick the cooktop we wanted in our home. This one was simply the best looking and most well designed one to catch our eye.
- Its well designed. Although a bit cramped, the burner layout allows for simultaneous use of most burners. The grill design provides good support for both flat bottomed and curved bottomed (woks!).
- The central burner is awesome. The guy who came to fit our gas connections compared the central burner at full to a rocket taking off!!! and he was not very far off... :) The central burner (at 20000 BTUs) is really a big burner, and is the primary burner used in our kitchen. This will be a big attraction to chefs used to Asian cuisines (perfect for stir frys, pressure cookers, etc.)
- The knobs and controls feel solid. The controls and knobs do not feel plasticky and flimsy. They have "gravitas". (Although the knobs are also a weak point - see the cons).
- Its fairly easy to clean. The supporting grills and the burners are easily removed, and allow for quick and easy clean up (again another plus for those cooking Asian and Latin cuisines).
- The blue knob backlight is beautiful and it serves to easily and quickly identify which burner is on. Serves to remind you, if you are slow cooking something, and have to step away from the cooktop.
- The safety alarm is quite useful. Its loud too! Keep it on and any child trying to play with the knobs will be well reminded to refrain. It also turns off the gas flowing to the burners (so ignoring the audible alarm will still not result in gas/burner being turned on).

Cons:
- The central burner is not designed for the heat it generates. After only 3 years of use, the central burner started deforming (warping) and recently it warped enough to start affecting its performance and create concerns for safety. I finally replaced the burner (again GE replacement part from non-GE internet store - try Sears Parts Direct or Appliance Parts Pros), and had to really work to get the deformed central burner out from the cooktop. The only reason I can think for the warping is that the burner was not designed to handle the heat generated (or was intended for very short uses). We do favor the central burner for our cooking and we do love cooking (3 meals a day x 7 days a week), and maybe GE had intended the cooktop and central burner for a different (maybe lesser) use.
- The gas control arm (which is manipulated by the control knob) can get stuck/jammed. One of the control arms on our cooktop got stuck. There was nothing that led up to it; one day it was working, and the next it was jammed. I tried everything I could think of (lubrication, force, etc.) to get it loosened up by and nothing worked. Finally, I had to order a replacement (get it cheaper through internet, not GE) and change it out. I am thankful that for us it only got stuck in the OFF position and all we had was a loss of service in that one burner.
- The knobs are a weak point, and expensive. While the knob itself is solid, its connection to the underlying control arm is not very strong. Its made of plastic and it can easily break if you apply too much force (especially if the underlying control arm gets stuck, like mine had). I have had to replace only that one knob.
- The electronics (knob backlight, the safety alarm, the switches for igniters) is fairly flimsy, expensive and one-for-all. Each of the knobs has a switch box behind it that controls the back-light, feeds into the alarm unit, and feeds into the igniter circuit. All of the switch boxes from all of the knobs are interconnected and can only be replaced as a single unit. This means that if a single backlight is blown or stops working, you have to replace the entire knob-circuit-web. This is expensive. The switches inside the switch boxes have fairly thin and flimsy switches, which can easily break, especially if you mess around inside. The good part is that the GE designers created 3 separate circuits for the backlight, the alarm and the igniter - which allows one circuit to misbehave without affecting the other two. For example, in our cooktop the central burner backlight switch broke and the light remains on all the time; however the alarm and igniter circuits work perfectly fine. I had the choice of replacing the entire circuit-web, but since this always-on light was only a convenience issue, we chose to just live with it.
- The side burners are all weaklings. For those used to the majesty of hot burning stoves/cooktops, the side burners will be a major let down. In our kitchen the central burner sees the majority of action and the side burners are delegated to those cooking activities that are trivial. Even then, the smaller two are rarely, if ever, used.
- The support grill is very high. This makes it look like the heat from the flames is not efficiently getting transferred to the pot on the grill and that some heat is being lost by virtue of the flame not reaching/touching the pot. I am told that the hottest point of the flame is just outside the tip of the visible flame and hence the height of the grill; if so, this may not be a drawback. I am not sure of the scientific truth, but psychologically it aggravates the lack of "strength" of the side grills!

Some more background to our experience so far. The breakdowns we have had (control arm jamming up, knob breaking, electronic switch breaking) all happened in the later part of the second year of our use. The breakdown of the central grill occurred towards the end of the third year of use. Although the long durations between breakdowns make it look like normal wear-and-tear; we have never had any breakdowns with our extensive experience with gas cooktops we have owned. We have owned and used gas cooktops extensively in India, and the normal lifespan for a gas cooktop usually exceeds 5 years, before it is replaced; mostly due to cosmetic issues, not engineering ones. This makes this cooktop stand out (in a negative manner), although this is our first experience with an non-Indian brand so dont know if this is considered normal.

Having experienced through all of the issues, I still think this was the best cooktop we could have got then, and it still continues to be used in our kitchen. We have had no reason to consider replacing the cooktop, although if I had to get professional support to fix the cooktop issues we had, this feeling might have been different (from a purely financial point of view).

UPDATE============
Its been just over 6 months since I first wrote the above review. Now the cooktop is getting close to about 4 years of use.

Since I wrote the issue, I have had 3 knobs break/come loose. In two of the cases, I simply hacked the knob by using a twist tie to keep the plastic stem from completely breaking off. The 3rd one did completely break off. From other reviews too, the knob's plastic stem seems to be a really sore point.

Recently we had an extended power outage in our area, which brought up an interesting observation. The igniters on the cooktop are powered from the mains power. This means turning on the cooktop requires external ignition source (matches, lighters, etc.) if you loose power. This is not necessarily a drawback, but just something to be aware of.

text: The seller lists this as a direct replacement for the center section of the rotor on an LG WM2501HVA. I put it on with out comparing it to the old one. Got a clanking sound on the spin cycle. Turns out the hub is not deep enough to hold the assembly against the center shaft. The shaft bolt bottoms out and leaves about a 3/8 inch gap between the hub and shaft. title: It makes nice clear ice fast! But it does NOT maintain a long term "storage" environment - unless you don't mind smashing clumps
text: I purchased one of these clear ice units and was quite pleased with the initial performance.  It made clear ice which was great to have in our drinks and it made the ice quickly and efficiently.  My issue with it was the ice came out very wet and that translated to big clumps of ice if that ice was transferred to a freezer for longer term storage.  Though the description uses the term storage, this unit does not "store" ice as consumers would expect. The holding area where the ice is dumped receives no more cooling than the ice that is present provides.  The ice will melt just as it would if it was sitting in a lightly insulated cooler.  It's a matter of semantics but I don't call that "storage".  A freezer "stores" ice.  This device does not. This devices traps ice.  It makes wonderful 1x1" dimpled cubes that are great if you use them right away but the wet cubes will clump big time if they are transferred to a freezer. Store bought ice does the same thing.  I ended up returning the unit for a refund within 30 days and spent half the amount on an icemaker kit to install into our extra refrigerator in the basement.  I don't get clear ice, but at least the ice sticks around a lot longer without the serious clumping.  If  I needed a steady supply of fresh clear ice this Luma machine would be the machine I get. It isn't obnoxiously loud during operation and it makes ice much faster than a standard freezer mounted ice maker; 10-15 minutes for each batch.  Helpful hints I learned: draining the unit is easy: place it next to the sink and open the drain plug.  The unit should be off and *plugged in* to get a complete drain of both reservoirs. Hold the power button in for at least 10 seconds when powering on for slightly thicker ice.  Note to Amazon: I always check your site first but you were sold out. I went with another online retailer. It happens.  :-)
