*Updated Review* I ended up being able to return the original unit in exchange for another one. The second unit works much better. While the coffee is still not what I would call ‘piping hot’, it is much hotter than the first coffee maker. The original must have been defective. I have been able to figure a way to make a larger, hot cup of coffee with this unit. See my comments under this review.
Original Review- I purchased this coffee maker for a vacation home with a small kitchen. While it looks great, it simply does not heat the water enough to brew a decent cup of coffee. The water which goes through the pod is lukewarm at best, and the coffee tastes like you made it with warm tap water... and this is coming from someone who doesn't like their coffee really hot! Literally the WORST cup of coffee I have ever had. Since it was for a vacation home, it didn't get used immediately after buying it, so I did not know how bad it would be. Now it's too late to return it. A complete waste of money.

title: Works With My 2.0 K400 Series
text: At first I was very hesitant on purchasing this product. From what the reviews said, it was a 50/50 shot of whether it was going to work or not. I got it anyways since it was under $10 and I wasn't going to be butthurt about $10 if it didn't work. I opened the box to find the two reusable pods and thought "How the heck is this huge thing going to fit in my Keurig!" Come to find out, the part where you insert the pods is able to expand! Haha! Didn't know about that! I inserted the pod and didn't get an error screen! Which was such a relief! I was able to brew a carafe without any problem. I did fill up the reusable pods to about the top of the metal mess and my coffee seemed a little watery. However, I haven't brewed a Colombian roast in a while so it could just be how the coffee tastes. In all, I think this is a great product SO FAR. The reason I am giving it a 4 star instead of 5 is because it would be nice to have a MAX fill line for the coffee grounds. I was a little unsure on how much I could put in because I like my coffee on the stronger side. My suggestion for others would be to just buy the product and see if it works. You won't really know till you try it in your own Keurig.

title: Diluted
text: The large mesh filter works fine, but the single-serve pod filters are unusable if you want a decent cup of coffee. The bottom & sides of the pod filter are all wire mesh, and the water flows through and out so quickly that you get an extremely weak, diluted cup of coffee. I’ve even tried cutting out a circular piece of paper coffee filter and covering the bottom of the pod filter with it to slow down the flow, but the flow out the sides is apparently so fast that it still results in a tasteless cup of coffee. A pre-loaded k-pod of coffee has only a small hole in the top and a small hole in the bottom when installed in the coffee maker. The water is forced to flow out slowly, so it is in contact with the coffee grounds for a long enough period of time to pick up the appropriate amount of flavor from the coffee grounds. This single serve filter pod is a very poorly designed product.

text:
After our cheap-o washing machine and dryer broke down, we decided to make a Black Friday purchase and get both the dryer and washing machines from Best Buy. My husband and I researched the heck out of what was available on the market. We compared features, cleaning options, and prices. I came across one site that had over 1700 reviews for this machine alone - the average review was a 5 out of 5.

I could not be happier with the products. While it is true the washing cycle takes longer than a top load washer, the end result is amazingly different. The matching dryer seems to work more efficiently than our old one and makes up for the time difference between loads. My toddlers socks came out white and the dirt stains gone. Even some of the old stains were removed. There are a lot of fancy dials and sounds on the machine however once you get accustomed to the settings, it is very easy to use. The pre-wash and steam features are a nice bonus. I especially like the top area to load the soap and fabric softner. The load capability seems quite large to me. Several pairs of jeans, pants and tops can go in at once. While running, the machine is fairly quiet. This is a beneficial feature since our laundry room is located in the center of our home. Is it wrong to fall in love with an appliance? If so, guilty as charged. Now if only they could automate the folding process I would be in heaven!!

title: Owned for almost 2 years
text:
We’ve owned this ice maker for nearly two years now, and feel enough time has passed for a fair review. Over that period of time, it has been running every day 24/7.

Overall, it does what it’s supposed to do; however, if you plan to use it as much as we have, be prepared for some maintenance and possible repairs.

A short time after purchasing it, we noticed some water on the countertop near the back of the unit.
This was caused by a lack of sealing on the inner left side near the upper tank. When the unit runs, water shoots out of an upper hose to fill the upper tank as it should, but while doing so, it also splashes onto the left inner wall and leaks through inside the unit and down onto the inner framework and eventually onto the countertop.
This was repaired by making a shield out of aluminum foil and placing it along the inside wall near the pivot point of the upper tank. A simple fix that worked.
Just last week another issue with the ice maker happened. It stopped pumping water, although the movement of the upper tank would still cycle. A search on the internet found that an inner micro switch was a possible fault. Testing with an ohmmeter confirmed the switch was shorted and needed to be replaced. This was another simple fix that cost less that 10 dollars to repair.

I’m only giving 3 stars since although it does make ice, and has run continuously for the past 2 years. The water leak issue is a design fault that could easily have be resolved by the manufacturer by molding a shield into the design.
Regarding the switch, this may have failed due to the water leak, however wear and tear was probably the reason since the water leak problem was repaired nearly two years ago.
Cleaning is essential, and not just with vinegar/water through the “cleaning” function. The top tank area under the black plastic cover must be cleaned by hand on a regular basis, and the stainless surround cover must be removed at least bi-annually to inspect and clean dust build up on the evaporator.

text:
As other reviewers have noted, this filter does not have sufficient capacity for many 10-12 cup percolators. It would be nice if they offered more than one size.

Also, I find that I have had to increase the amount of coffee I use in my percolator (an old Corningware 10-cup model)to get the right strength--I think it's because the filter is so small in diameter that some of the water misses the basket entirely during the perking process (Pouring a half a cup of the just-perked coffee back through the grounds creates a stronger brew, but who wants to do that every time?). People with other makes of percolators may not experience this problem. If I could control the length of the perking cycle this problem might be resolved, but I can't. With coffee so expensive, it's aggravating to have to use more!

I used to have a wonderful old percolator (I think it was a Presto)that had both a fine in-spout strainer and an adjustable strength setting. It kept the grounds out of my coffee and I could control the length of the perking cycle. I wish they still made it, because it made perfect coffee with any grind.

title: We really like the stove - works wonders
text:
We really like the stove - works wonders, above our expectations. The high burners bring things to a boil much faster than our old stove and the simmer burner allowed me to reduce spaghetti sauce without burning the bottom of the pan (unheard of here).

The top oven is the only one we've had need of so far. With the baking dish we used was just a tad tall and it had to be slid over to the side due to the position of the broiler. Not a big deal, just a geometry issue.

The one thing that keeps it from being a 5 star is that the recess in the back of the range is different from all other ranges we have had previously. Our gas pipe stuck out of the wall 4-5 inches on the right side, while the recess was only 2 inches deep on the left. So we had to have someone remodel our gas pipe in order to push it back toward the wall. It still sticks out an inch from the wall due to the flexible hose trying to fit in the recess too.

I'm glad we bought the range, but I would have liked the usual recess in the back.

title: Solid product but could have improvements
text:
This product is a quality product overall. It is quiet, cold, and essentially provides all the benefits of a mini-fridge that you would expect. I got the 4.0 cubic size in order to make sure I can hold everything I needed. However, the general set up of the interior of the fridge is not setup well.

The fridge has a soda can rack on the door which is basically just a waste of space if you do not keep soda or beer cans in your fridge. It takes a good amount of space on the door that could be used for other items.

Also, the bottom of the main part of the fridge allows for barely any room to fit a larger item like a gallon of milk.

Lastly, the bottom shelve on the door has a bar that is held in by two holes on either side of the door, however, the bar provided barely spans the width of the fridge and falls out frequently. I had to duct tape the bar to the sides of the door just to ensure it would stop falling off.

All in all, this fridge is average-quality. It would be greatly improved by a redesign of the interior spaces in order for users to fit items that they want, not what the company thinks you may have. The can rack is simply a novelty add on that is unnecessary and wasteful of space.

title: DO NOT BUY!!!
text: Please do yourself a favor and do not buy this range. I wish someone had told me all of the reasons you will hate this range. First of all it is seriously over priced. I owned this stove for approx 4mths when the real troubles started. I did not buy my stove from this company. There is only one big element. It looks like there is two but in reality there is only one. You pretty much have to cook everything on 8-9 or high, anything lower was just a simmer. The piece of metal that runs across the top above the knobs scars at nothing. My husband sat a pizza pan on the top and it was part way resting on the metal, he used the pizza cutter while holding the pan with the other hand and just the slight movement looked like he took sand paper to it. The knobs look great being on the front but in reality this is a real pain as grease and food drop on them while cooking, there is no way to avoid this and also no way to clean behind the large ring that the knob fits in. The knobs themselves can be removed for cleaning but the base cannot. There is a gap between this ring and the stove which food gets in. We had  a accident involving pancake batter being dropped on one of the knobs and I could not get it out. I tried a tooth pick, I tried laying a wet cloth on it to soak it and it simply could not be removed. The touch screen on the front looks nice and works great but is super sensitive. It works like the touch screen on a iPhone, iPad etc. It is not one you push you just barely touch it. It is made of glass. On one occasion the oven was cut on just by rubbing against it and on another occasion I went to  get dinner out as the timer was going off only to discover the oven had been cut off and the food was still raw. Everything else was done but the main course was raw chicken....not good. You would really hate this setup if you have small kids. The oven drawer is a joke it takes forever to heat up and only has one element resulting in burned food, also as we all know oven drawers seem to attract dust bunnies even if it is barely ever opened. The final straw was the piece of metal above the knobs developed a bulge in it for unexplained reasons. Because of this bulge the rubber gasket that fits between the glass top and the metal started to work its way out of the slot. I pushed it back in only to have it back out inside of a week. GE sent out a repair man who ordered a new part, when the part came someone had attached the gasket on the wrong side of metal piece making it unusable. I got a second part shipped UPS when I opened the box it had a used parts  in it with food on it and no rubber gasket. The gasket problems resulted in electrical problems where moisture was able to get between the glass top and the metal piece.This is where all of the electrical parts are located for the knobs. This resulted in the oven thinking the door was not closed and the oven will not come on until the door is closed. It would just keep saying please close oven door. I would open and close the door until finally it would recognize that the door was actually closed. After nearly 3 months of dealing with this mess the place I bought the stove from brought me a new stove. I lost approx $300.00 by doing this but I was just happy to have this nighmare out of my house. The only thing this stove has going for it is that it is pretty. Stay away.

title: Makes a nice cup of coffee
text: I bought this French Press because I got tired of having a cold second cup from my old one.  I bought this thinking that it would do a better job keeping the remainder of the pot hot while I nurse that first cup.  It doesn't do that so well, the exterior of this French Press gets pretty hot, which kind of surprised me.  Over the past week, I've played around a bit with making coffee in it, and tried two different things.  If you fill it up with hot tap water, and let it sit while the kettle is on, it warms the pot up alright, and your second cup from it is still pretty hot (~20 minutes later), but beyond that you'll be microwaving the next cup.  Or if you fill it will boiling water while you grind your beans, and let that sit while the kettle comes to a boil, you can enjoy hot coffee over the course of about an hour.  So keep that in mind if you're thinking of purchasing this French Press.  The fit and finish are very nice on this, and since it is Stainless Steel it cleans up nicely.  One of the nicer features is that it has dual screens, so it does an excellent job of filtering out the small bits and grit from the coffee. title: $217 repair bill after only 2 years
text: A severe design flaw should deter you from purchasing this refrigerator.  This refrigerator/freezer worked well enough for 2 years, and then like clockwork, water slowly started to leak from the inside bottom of the refrigerator unit.  This water originated from the defrost cycle.  Normally, the defrosted water flows out through a drain located below the heater/defrost coils.  Because the system could no longer handle the water, ice began to form and plugged the drain.  The accumulated ice caused water to back up and rusted the drain plate.  I called Samsung to see if they would honor their warranty, but they would not pay for the repairman to fix the problem.  I had to pay $217 to fix this problem temporarily, plus the cost of replacing the food that spoiled.  Of course they did not cover that.  You see, the refrigerator door was open the whole time while the repairman ran back and forth to his truck while a lot of my food sat out at room temperature to clear space.  Who knows if this problem will happen again?

title: Lasted 5 months. The manufacturer is a scam, no way to claim the warranty.
text:
The pump lasted 5 months before the shaft broke and the impeller fell off.
During those 5 months, it made a loud electrical buzzing sound while pumping (as one other reviewer noted).

Since I'm only the second reviewer to note buzzing, I assumed I had a dud. I attempted to claim the "lifetime warranty". However, when I followed the email provided, I received this immediate response: "You are receiving this email because you have inquired about an Amazon order. Please note that this email is for a brick-and-mortar building supply company located in the state of Maryland, and NOT for the unaffiliated online appliance company you purchased from. They have fraudulently used our contact information for customer service. Please refer back to Amazon for customer service regarding your order. Thank you."

I concluded:
- The email is true. This is legitimately a fraud and not sold or manufactured by BlueStars.
or
- The email is lying and they don't want folks redeeming their warranty.
But what's for certain is, THERE'S NO WAY TO CLAIM THE LIFETIME WARRANTY.

Amazon support chat refunded me. But, only after asking that I send in my pump... in two pieces 🤣.

I bought this machine to hold us over for a couple of years as I intend to remodel my kitchen eventually and put a regular one in, but I don’t want to tear out cabinets just yet. There are six people in my house, and most of what we go through is cups. There were cups stacked to the ceiling it seemed, and I just could not keep up. I’ve had this for a week so far, and I’m very happy with it. I like that it doesn’t have to attach to the faucet. It’s not any louder than the regular dishwasher I had at my last house, so I’m not sure what that’s about. Based on other reviews, I’m careful to only put a small amount of liquid detergent in it, and common sense tells me to make sure the hose is coming down from the back of the machine so that it can drain properly.

My only complaint is that for such a big machine, the rack inside is really tiny. It’s about the size of a small dish drying rack. The machine itself doesn’t fit on my counter, so I have it on a table near the cabinets with a bucket under it. It works for us though. I also hated the utensil tray, so I use the utensil holder from my dish drying rack, and that works fine.

If anything changes in the future, I’ll edit this review, but so far it’s good.

title: So Easy to Refill!
text:
I loved my old water cooler. Cold water when I wanted it; hot water for my tea whenever I wanted it. I was heartbroken when it croaked (and a little annoyed that it only lasted 3 1/2 years.) So I did a lot of research into water coolers before I bought a new one. And although I was suffering without my cooler it took me quite a while to make my decision. And I admit that 99% of my problem was that I hate paying shipping charges — that’s why I’m an Amazon Prime member! But sometimes there is no avoiding the unpleasant things in life. And I would like to add that I received my water cooler long before the date promised when purchased. (The other 1% was because the price of water coolers seemed to have skyrocketed in the past 3 1/2 years — but maybe that was why mine had such a short life — I did not do a lot of research for the first one — it dispensed hot & cold water and I was happy. But one of my family motto’s has always been “You get what you pay for”.)

This is the number one selling water cooler on Amazon. That helped in my decision process. I also became really attached to the idea of a bottom-loading dispenser. I cannot lift a five-gallon jug of water and have always been dependent upon someone else in the house to change the water for me. Then I became attached to the idea of self-cleaning — because cleaning a water is really a pain in the butt — and it wastes a lot of water, in my opinion. And admittedly, both of these features added to the cost of the machine.

I read every single Amazon review before I finally gave in and ordered the cooler. I was able to mentally counter almost every major complaint any one had. The LED light can’t be turned off? I love it — it adds a night light to my kitchen. My brother, who won’t even use the cooler, commented on how much he liked the new one because of the “night light” feature. And I defy my middle brother to complain that the water isn’t cold enough out of the cooler (he used to whine about that every Thanksgiving about the old cooler!)

The space where the water dispenses isn’t tall enough? I always just tipped the 23.7 FL OZ sport bottle that I keep refilling — not a problem. Well, actually, it turns out that is the one complaint I have about the cooler — and the reason for giving it four stars instead of five. On my old cooler I tipped the sport bottle under the cold water spout, filled it and replaced the lid I drank from. This cooler does not have spouts! The panel where the water is dispensed just has holes from which the water is dispensed. There are arrows that indicate where the water will be dispensed, which is great for a glass of cold water or a mug of hot water for tea. But if you’re trying to line up a tipped bottle — or even a 16.9 FL OZ bottle which fits in the space — you’re almost guaranteed water in places you did not intend. I now keep a small funnel on top of the dispenser to refill my bottles. It’s a simple solution but every time I use it I think how much easier things would be if this machine simply had a dispenser spout.

I am extremely pleased with both the temperatures of the hot and the cold water. And while I have not had the occasion to make multiple cups of hot tea yet, I have refilled five bottles at once and each one has been as cold as the last.

One last “odd” note — the installation instructions mandate a four-inch margin behind and on the sides of the machine — the same as my last cooler. This one, because of the slightly rounded bottom door, seemed to stick out further into the not expansive walking space in my kitchen. I had to turn it sideways, with the back to the adjacent cabinet and the side to the wall. It looks a little odd but actually makes the “night Light” much more effective.

title: Perfect fit for broken original--requires fair mechanical skills to replace
text:
Our aging LG 79640311900 washer suddenly started banging and smoking during a spin cycle. Some research online suggested that we had burned out a bearing. Once I pulled the machine apart to explore, the cause of the bearing failure was likely that the spider had failed first (into three pieces, no less--see photo). The scraps were still bolted in place, but the tub was seriously off balance. This replacement spider cost less than an OEM LG part and fit perfectly.

Anyone interested is doing this job on their own can save several hundred dollars compared with a service visit, but realize that replacing the spider (and bearings, if necessary, and the rubber "door boot" seal in our case as well, since the off-kilter tub had melted part of it) isn't for the faint of heart. You'll find some excellent videos on YouTube that detail the process, but plan on spending several hours and most of your patience getting everything apart and then back together again without breaking things further.

title: Looks good but lacks top quality construction
text:
[[VIDEOID:3c293d655b1f86d86fdb91ac067da5ea]] Observations noted in regards to other reviews:

The clock display is in 12h time not 24h time.

The blue protective plastic is there for a reason. Just take your time taking it off. Unfortunately, the instructions didn't say to disassemble the light section to remove the blue protective layer there. If you don't, removing the blue layer will be a nightmare and make the unit look cheap with small fragments everywhere. What's really sad is that some areas that need protection don't have any protection. One area that needed protection is the display. You'd think that would be the one area that would have it to prevent scratches.

The LED light is on the whiter side, maybe closer to 5000K in color. The light could be a little brighter, but it's enough to see the entire cooktop.

The fan always starts at fan speed 3. You'd think that it would start in fan speed 1 so as not to scare you, but nothing doing, there seems to be a lack of common sense here. Also, when using the touch controls, you must press and hold the power button for about 2 seconds to wake up the system, then pick what you want to happen. Be it the fan or light. When you press the power button to turn off the fan, its starts counting down for 1 minute, which is great. Press it on more time to turn it off immediately. It would make really good sense if you could just press fan or light to get to those functions directly, but you can't. You have to press the power button for 2 seconds again then press the function button you want. Slightly irritating logic there.

INITIAL IMPRESSIONS:

After receiving the vent, I opened it and took a quick look at it and tried it out. This is the video that was shot recording the different fan speeds and sound levels. The phone is very close so it is much louder than it really is installed. But take notice of the motor "hum". Looking at the vent I noticed that a motor mounting screw was installed incorrectly. So I reinstalled all of the screws and made sure everything was mounted correctly, but the humming didn't get any better. While pressing on parts of the housing, I noticed that the humming would be slightly diminished depending where I pressed. 1st red flag. The metal it was made out of also seemed thin and flexed quite a bit but was well protected. So I decided to go ahead with the install anyway.

On install day, I took the vent out of all of the packing and what I found was interesting. A dimple on the front of the vent and a dented side panel towards the back of the vent. All of these sections were hidden under the Styrofoam packing which wasn't damaged one bit. The packing box was in excellent condition so I can only assume that the vent was damaged at the factory. So much for quality control. The metal was so thin that I could just push the panel from the inside and correct the dent. No special tools, just my fingers. The dimple was on the crease so there was no correcting it, but it didn't look that noticeable so I let it go. Red flag number 2.

The installation was straight forward and by the included instructions, which by the, is not very detailed. After completing the installation, the hum was very noticeable and kind of irritating. I pressed on different sections and found a spot that made it slightly quieter and inserted a piece of foam between the cabinet and top of the vent. The hum is very noticeable on fan speed 1, so I'm thinking that the motor is of a lower quality. I also noticed this type of thing on cheap window AC's when running on low versus higher speeds. The vent housing essentially becomes a resonating chamber amplifying the sound even louder. A little sound dampening material would have gone a long way. The blower assembly itself creates some vibration as the fan is not well balanced, but this vibration doesn't seem to get transmitted to the surrounding areas. Other than the hum, the air flow and sound created is pretty quiet on low. On the second speed, the grease filters create a very slight whistling sound. The vent sounds great without the grease filters. My guess on this is that the way the air has to go through the vent is the cause.

FINAL THOUGHTS:

After using it for a while, is it worth the $200+ price, maybe. If the metal was a little thicker and the manufacturer paid closer attention to proper testing of operational noise, definitely! The touch panel programming could be improved. It's a nice looking unit and removes a great deal of air, so functionality is very good. Hopefully I was able to provide some useful information toward your purchase and maybe to the manufacturers.

title: Great if you don't want to walk to the laundromat
text: I got this for my apartment that has a laundromat further away in the complex and didn't want to walk all the way over there to wash laundry (especially in the middle of winter!) Also hoped to save a little change too so we bought it. It is quite loud when it runs, and it's not the most "efficient" product, but it gets the job done. The washer portion is pretty good overall, the spinning portion can be a little sketchy at times and thump around if you don't have the clothes in there properly. I also have issues with draining, so I often have a small bucket with me to drain the water manually. Also since the filling tube is too small, I manually fill the tub with water, but I don't mind. Overall, it's good to know it's not a washer you are probably used to. You do need to be careful to desperate lights and darks, (I recommend if you have fuzzy clothes to wash them separate too) and just be aware of certain materials being together. So with all that to say, I wouldn't tell someone not to buy it, but don't buy it believing it will completely replace a washer unit and you're going to need to hang dry your clothes after. Once you get a groove on how you wash your clothes, it gets easier though, and it beats bringing your clothes to the laundromat!

title: Not a pour-over cone, but a drip cone
text: I admit I had no idea what a drip cone was until I bought this. I'm used to making gravity-brewed pour-over and wanted a larger cone that I could put directly into a flask and make coffee for more people. In good pour-over cones, there should be no water resistance. You pour in the water and it should escape immediately. That way, there is no saturation of the beans, no immersion brewing, and the resistance of the water flow is controlled by bean grind. In this cone, however, the water does not flow immediately out. Like another reviewer, I added more holes (8 x 2mm holes) to attempt to increase water flow and it did help a little, but it would be impossible, without cutting a large hole (which is what I may do) to increase the flow to the correct rate. This is more like one of the god-awful machines that brews large pots of over-extracted coffee. I admit that this was my mistake. It isn't advertised as a pour-over cone, and I mistook it as such. Nevertheless, it is worth differentiating that this is a 'drip' cone for people who like that kind of thing, not a pour-over cone for coffee lovers.

title: Let's be honest...
text:
If you're looking to buy this compact to dishwasher to take over all your dishwashing needs, you will be sorely disappointed. A lot of the reviews will have you believing this compact dishwasher will exceed all your expectations and be big enough to fit all your dishes in it. It simply is not. In fact, any plates with a diameter greater than 8 inches won't even fit in this dishwasher. Pots and pans are a definite no-go as virtually none of them will fit in this dishwasher. Make sure the rims to your bowls flare out, as even straight rimmed bowls will have difficulty fitting in this dishwasher. I was quickly mistaken for thinking this dishwasher was going to take over most of my dishwashing.

With that being said, this dishwasher works decent as an aid. It will fit all your silverware in it, but most of the cooking utensils, like spatulas, will have to still be handwashed. It's a good supplement especially if you live in an apartment. Measure the clearance between your countertop and any cabinets that may be hanging over the countertops because if you don't have at least an 18 in clearance, you'll just end up sending it back.

I debated on whether I wanted to give this 2 stars or 3. I ultimately decided on 3 because I do use it often enough. However, I probably wouldn't have bought this if I would have known how little space it actually provided. All in all, I'm not too impressed by this product and I'd only recommend it for people who are single and live in an apartment.

I put the Sharpie in my pics for reference, and the second pic is next to the Melitta that holds a #4 filter. The glass is really thin, so I understand the reviews that mention it breaking when it was dropped.

On the plus side, it does look really nice and the ring on the bottom pops right off for easy cleaning.

If you only drink a 6 oz cup of coffee, then you may be happy with this. I can't image how tiny the 155 must be. I need to make a 16 oz travel mug each morning and it takes refilling it nearly 4 times completely full to make that much coffee.

I made coffee 3 times with it and am returning it at a loss. The filters are not eligible for return, but I'm sending them back too. Not much I can do with them.

We got this item fast and in perfect condition. We used it approximately 3 weeks and then the 4 points where the "cone" part is press welded to the base part came loose. That meant a couple things: first being that coffee grounds now were able to pass through into your cup. Then secondly, the whole funnel area became unstable and would not stay upright when pouring liquid into it. That's dangerous when you are pouring hot water! What I did like what that it was a stellar filter - until it broke, I never had one iota of a ground in my cup. I got a really great cup of coffee every time if I followed the ratio guidelines. I prefer a totally fresh cup of coffee every time, and it eliminated making too much and not feeling like drinking it that day. The addition of a rubber grip all the way around the top of the funnel as well as around the base made it super easy to handle when it was hot from use. Hope that explains my 3 star well - it's not a total bomb... until it is.

I have not yet replaced this and went back to my good ole coffee press, but now that I have used the pour over, I really miss it. The taste is different - which surprised me!

I actually processed this for a return then when I went to get it and package it up, my husband had thrown it away so I was unable to send it back for a refund. However, it appeared I would have had no issues returning it and getting my money back had I had it to return.

As the top portion of the original filter is separated and worn out, I tried the lower basket portion with the lid from the new filter. At this time the message disappeard and I was able to finish brewing. I am not sure what will happen the next time I'm brewing coffee.

Update after about a week of use:
I was contacted by the seller and after following their advise it looks now that both filter are OK. I did really nothing, other than seating the filters firmly in the filter housing. According to the seller, there is no microchip embedded in the filter, so it seems that perhaps a very small dimensional difference between these and the original Keurig product had triggered the error message.
Second update on 9/5:
Lately, after making the first cup of coffee, after refilling the same filter, the error message ALWAYS cames back. What I am doing now is this: I use the second filter to make another cup of coffee. For some reason using a dry and cool filter the coffee maker would not display an error message.

title: A bargain fix for slow drip from door gasket
text:
While I was searching for a the part to replace the shock absorbers for my front loading washer, I saw that this was a popular part to fix the very slow drip for the door. I didn't even know this was broken...just thought water pooled in the gasket. Nope, in an old (17 year old) front loader, this part starts to leak very slowly so that there is always a very slow drip into the door gasket and then out the door, creating rust spots on the bottom of the machine. This fixed it!

This part matches the old part exactly, however the screw holes that matched my machine are quite a bit smaller than the matching screws. In that case, you would need to drill them out a bit or get slightly smaller screws. The metal is too strong for the sheet metal screw to cut a new thread. Note that some of the holes in the part are threaded for a larger size, but those don't line up with my washer.

You can replace this part just by opening the top lid, you don't need to remove back or even slide out the washer if you have access to the top.

title: Not a surge protector?
text:
My opinion of this product is mixed. First, the bad. It’s marketed as a “surge protector” but offers neither a “connected equipment warranty” nor a rating in joules of its ability to absorb a surge. (Some Amazon users claim it is rated at 303 joules but offer no evidence. My unit is not marked.) Buying this as a surge protector would be like buying a “container for liquid” that might hold 5-gallons or 1/2 ounce, except that when you get that you’d know right away. With this, you’ll never know how much it can take. Also, when your equipment is destroyed by a surge you’ll be paying for the repair yourself. Other products from larger brands offer equipment warranties of $5,000 - $100,000. If the actual rating is 303 joules, this may actually be the least-capable surge protector on the market. For this review I’ll assume it has a capacity of zero joules.

Next the good. While I can’t call this a “surge protector,” it is interesting for two other reasons. First it has a delayed-start timer. While not an engineer, my research suggests that keeping equipment turned off for a few minutes after an outage can spare it from damage resulting from further fluctuations and also from restarting at the wrong point in its operating cycle. Second, it monitors the voltage level and shuts off outside of a 90 to 140-volt range. This might save the equipment from brownout damage. Personally, I’d feel better if the range was narrower because I understand a 10% drop in voltage may be harmful. I’ll let the electrical engineers among us report whether this range is adequate.

Here’s my recommendation. If your equipment is susceptible to damage from a surge, use this only in combination with a surge protector. Be careful about the connection sequence. Some surge protector warranties are not valid if the appliance is not plugged into them directly. In that case, plug the appliance into the other surge protector and plug the surge protector into this GSM-NP. Be sure to choose a surge protector with a cord as the cordless direct-plug variety may not work due to the odd convex and angled design of this device.

title: Cuisinart strikes again!
text: I had high hopes for this Cuisinart product, however as most Cuisinart products we have purchased lately, it has failed to live up to its name. We purchased this product to replace its predecessor, the SS-700, we had for 4 years. The SS-700 brewed a single cup of coffee very quickly, but after 4 years the heating element did itself in. Cuisinart, undoubtedly, realized the problem with the SS-700, thus the SS-10 was born. While the concept seemed to work great at first, it seems that these units are made with cheaper, more faulty components, as well. We purchased the SS-10 in the beginning of October 2016. By the beginning of May 2017, it had started showing signs of faulty workmanship in the components. Now, I have followed the regular maintenance of the descaling cycle using white distilled vinegar, but that apparently wasn't enough to keep this product alive. By  early May, it started showing signs of decline as it would take a very long time to brew a cup of coffee. It seemed that the length of time kept growing over the next month, even after running seven descale processes through it in a four week period. Finally, I had to breakdown and call Cuisinart when I got the dreaded "EEO" code. Their initial response was "to unplug the unit for at least an hour and a half to reset the unit," which we did. Immediately, the unit displayed "EEO" again on the next attempted brew. So, again with the phone call to customer service. This time they issued me a service number, a call tag for the faulty unit and said a new unit would be shipped to me. Hurray, I thought. Only, after two and a half weeks  went by with no new coffee maker on my front porch, I began to wonder what was happening. I called again, only to find out that the units were on back-order. They could not tell me when they would ship again, and that it could take another 3-4 weeks. Oh well, I thought. Then to my surprise, a week and a half later the new unit was sitting on my doorstep! It was a Friday gift! What a way to go into the weekend! The next morning, I got up and set up the unit, following the set up instructions provided in the box. Only this time, when getting to step 6 (the part about brewing 8 oz of water to flush the system) nothing happened. No pump running sound. Not a drop of water moving. Then the error code "EEO." I thought, maybe the reservoir isn't seated correctly. So, I lifted it, and set it down and watched to make sure the gasket actually lifted from the pass thru channel, and tried again. Still nothing, just "EEO." I turned it off, back on, tried again. Still nothing. I unplugged it, waited for a couple of hours, tried again and nothing. "EEO." So, I called customer service again. They said that I would have to try to brew a cup several times before it might start working. I informed them that I had tried at least 7 or 8 times, and still nothing except the error code. So, they said they would ship me a new unit. However, they were on back-order again! So, I politely asked if I could just get a refund. The lady, as helpful as she could be, said that Cuisinart's policy is that they do not issue refunds. I asked, what would happen if the next unit was also faulty? How many times do we have to do this with a clearly, defective appliance? She informed me that after 3 or more attempts to replace the unit, we could issue a LETTER requesting a CREDIT from Cuisinart, which we can use to buy another Cuisinart product. As a consumer, I find this to be not helpful. If I do not want their product anymore, I must resign myself to the fact that they got my money, and I got a piece of junk in return. They win, I lose. I know this, after this experience and my last experience with a Cuisinart blender (don't get me started on that), I will NEVER buy a Cuisinart product again. I urge anyone reading this to second guess themselves before purchasing a Cuisinart product, as well. They used to be one of the greats. Now, they are just out to sell an inferior product over and over to claim as much of the market share they can get their hands on. What ever happened to quality products? What ever happened to quality workmanship? Sorry, Cuisinart, but you've joined the ranks of the marginally mediocre. Good work! I hope you're proud of your achievements. You've made it to the bottom with the rest of the world of product producers.

This machine's agitator will stretch out shirts and other blended fabric clothes if they are not washed in a mesh laundry bag. Also, lint created from washing is very visible on dark clothes. Floating lint filters help but they don't completely solve the problem. Like many people, I wish the spin dryer was a bit bigger. But despite the issues I mentioned, it seems like a well-made product and is much more convenient and less expensive than going to a laundromat every week.

Update: 1 year later and it's still working really well for me. Now that I have been using it for a while, prefer not to let my clothes agitate for very long, only enough time to thoroughly wet my clothes and to mix the detergent, then soak for at least 20 mins both for wash and rinse. The long soaks get my clothes really clean without stretching them out.

title: Really Odd Design
text:
This has been rated on various web sites as the best of 2021 an 2022. That's why I bought it. I needed an unvented range hood.

They claim one person can install this. Forget about that. You need two people if you are installing the 36" hood. It's way too heavy and cumbersome for one person to manage getting it in the necessary slots. Maybe the 30" is easier.

Turns out the design is odd AND it looks like Broan might be going out of business. Here's why: if you use this unvented, the slot for the air to exit points directly up toward the ceiling, What that means is, if you have white cabinets like me, they are going to go yellow pretty quickly because the exhaust is basically blowing over the doors everytime you use it!

I had to jerry-rig a way to divert the air more forward using a sheet of plexiglass and opening my cabinet doors each time I use it.

Further, you need to purchse carbon filters to get the grease smoke. These are expensive -- if you can find them. Broan's web site says they are discontinued! I found a couple places that had a few left and bought them all.

And speaking about discontinued, if you go to the Broan website, nearly all their products are discontinued -- including this range hood! They were bought by another company a year or so ago and I wonder if they are going out of business.

Kind of sorry I bought this brand, but now it's too late.

title: Fast, Compact Machine that makes Hot Coffee.
text:
This is our 5th K-cup machine. First two where Keurig's, which had constant problems with clogging and short cupping. Both died within weeks of the warranty expiring. The next was the Cuisinart 700, which was fantastic for the first couple years. Then it started to short cup, and required rebooting (un-plug) every couple days. We followed that with an ICoffee Mozart, which was the most trouble free machine we've owned, until it started leaking internally a few days ago. Since ICoffee is currently in limbo (new stock is months away), we looked into another Keurig, but gave up on that idea once we read reviews claiming that the machines clogged regularly, had control panel failures, and temperature problems. By chance we came across the SS-10 on Amazon, and ordered one. First thing we noticed, is that the SS-10 is much more compact then our old 700, which is a plus. Another plus is that the machine heats up almost instantly. No waiting a minute or more like we had to do with the Icoffee. The menu and control panel are virtually identical to our old 700.

We've brewed a dozen cups so far, from name brands and a small local roaster, and have not had the mess that some reviewers report. We did take the advice from some of the other reviewers, and "seat" the K-cup, piercing it with the bottom needle, before closing the lid. After looking at the design, I think this step is a requirement. Coffee is hot. 178 degrees in the finished cup on Xtra Hot, and 169 degrees on Hot.

Now for a couple small inconveniences . Due to the compact design, the clearance is only 6" with the drip tray installed, and 7-3/8" with the drip tray removed. My wife's thermal mug, which she used everyday with the Icoffee, will not fit under this machine, even with the drip tray removed. Our old 700 had 5 temperature settings where this machine only has 2. Again, minor inconveniences. The big question is, will this machine last longer then our previous 700? Time will tell.

UPDATE: Only 1 week old, and started having problems with it bursting K-cups. Traced the problem, not to the top punch that some blame, but a clogged bottom needle. If the bottom needle clogs, pressure in the K-cup causes the top to burst open, leading one to believe the problem is in the top punch. So, if this happens to you, clean the bottom needle. Just run a straightened paper clip through the bottom needle, and it should start working fine again. Had to drop my rating down to 4 stars due to the clogging. I hope this will not be an ongoing issue. In the year and a half I had the ICoffee, it never clogged once.

If you're one of those who has a hankerin' for ceremony with whatever it is you're doing, or making, or drinking, then these are right up your alley. People who think the 'tea ceremony' is the bee's pajamas and inexplicably enjoy coffee too, should flock to these little beauties like a Karcrashian to an iPhone cam. Did I say these buggers were, as the Brits are wont to say, 'fiddly'? I must have ... at any rate; these things are fiddly.
They DO, however, work as claimed, insofar as keeping sediment from your preferred cuppa. But keeping grounds out of your little basket thingy? Not so much. You'll still have to clear the basket of grounds, just not as many.
As stated in many other reviews, they're a bit large-ish, and need to be stuffed into the basket either by advanced origami techniques, strategic slices with a pair of scissors, or just mashing the dang thing in there, stuffing in some grounds and going about your bid'ness.
I keep them around for when I have a need for more finely ground, darker roasted, cat-pee smelling grounds that produce a cup of electricity.

text:
I was skeptical that this would be able to dry clothes effectively. It does, for the most part-- just leaves them a little bit wrinkled in some cases. It gets a full load done in a couple of hours, but you throw it in and let it do its thang, no having to remember to change from one thing to another as in a separate-unit washer/dryer. Seems to get clothes very clean, too, so the washer part works well. The space saving was the major selling point, but the size of the interior is small at 2.0 cubic feet. Since I would rather do laundry more frequently than, say, save up several cubic feet to do, this wasn't a big deal at all, but it probably would be for folks who are washing a lot more clothes.

The major disadvantage is that the display broke after only 6 months, and the company wanted $88 to replace it. An extended warranty (through the manufacturer, third party, or through a credit card) is highly recommended.

text:
So I bought this because Kenmore thinks we should be paying $80 for a standard water filter for some reason. Me, being a completely sane and frugal person decided to get this. It *almost* perfectly fits in my Kenmore Elite fridge, but the neck on this filter is just a few millimeters shorter so it doesn't "lock" into the slot. Still, I was able to push it up as far as it would go and close the cover, and I'm getting fantastic water flow with no leaks, so I guess the lock is non issue for me but it's definitely something to consider, as other fridge models may run into leaks or the filter not fitting at all despite being technically compatible.

Make sure you prime the filter! Run a gallon or two of water after installing the filter so you can have nice clean water. After priming mine, the water is perfectly clear and tastes just like it did with the original filter.

title: Great unit, but don't expect too much
text: In reading these reviews while trying to decide whether to buy this humidifier, I was frustrated that everyone seemed to be focused on the installation process - how easy, problems, etc - and nobody would tell me if the thing actually works. So, I bought one anyway and had it professionally installed. For those of you who may wonder how well it works, here's the deal: Yes, it works pretty well. Based upon general observations after owning my 3200 sq ft house for 15 years, I estimate it raises the humidity level by about 8%. We are maintaining a steady 29% humidity regardless of how cold or dry it is outside. Today it's 22 degrees F outside (-6 C). Its clear and very dry, and it's maintaining 29%. Obviously the more the furnace kicks in, the more this humidifier kicks in too, so I am not seeing less humidity on colder/dryer days. I wish it could hold 30%+, but I'm actually quite happy with an 8% increase and a constant 29%. I'm in Toronto, and it's cold here! I had a Honeywell True Steam before this, and the one season that it did actually work, before falling apart, it increased humidity levels by about 10%. But it was so complicated, and fraught with design flaws. I went with this humidifier over the steam unit (Aprilaire 800), because although I hear it is much better than the Honeywell, my contractor told me it is a 'higher maintenance' unit that the 700. But I like that it's a simple unit, and functions independent of the furnace motor, like other steam units which switch on the furnace motor to circulate humidity independent of the burn cycle. The Truesteam ran that furnace motor all day! And ran up my electric bills too. So the Aprilaire 700 has been running for two months now. No problems. We're happy.

title: You get what you pay for - junk
text:
I always thought the brand-name LG filters were over-priced ripoffs. Man, was I wrong. There's something about the design or build of the Water Sentinel brand that seems like it's restricting the water pressure. Or something like that.

My LG refrigerator is a French door model, with an ice maker in the door. With this filter installed, it would plunk out two, maybe three, sets of ice per day. That's not enough, even for a household of just two people. The water dispenser stream - which isn't exactly Niagara Falls under normal conditions - was slower and weaker as well. I don't know if that's what was causing the ice maker troubles or not, but it's another bad sign.

I put in a proper LG filter and whattaya know - full ice maker all the time and happy water drinkers.

In other words, pay up. Get a discount on a two- or three-pack of real LG filters. They last roughly six months each, so make the investment. You'll be much happier in the end.

title: In short, I love this little washer
text:
I've had this little washer for 4.5 years as a way to (eventually) save money ($1.25 per wash in my building's laundry room), not to mention time and hassle (that laundry room is four floors down). Between this washer and my two drying racks, I've spent only about $10 on laundry (not counting detergent) in those 4.5 years. It's quiet, it's efficient, it's easy to hook/unhook from my sink, and it definitely gets the job done.

I have had to replace the drive belt (in fact, that's why I'm on Amazon today), but I got mine as a refurb, so that may be a factor in how long the belt lasted. The only real problem I've had was with the casters — their stems, which screw into the corners of the base, aren't long enough. With the casters screwed in, they rub against the casing and won't rotate properly (the wheels turn, but the casters mostly stay facing one direction because they're up against the casing). I've looked closely at the instructions, and I'm not doing anything wrong — but since that doesn't seem to be a complaint for anyone else here, I'm going to assume I'm missing something, either literally (a part) or figuratively (I'm just dumb). I jury-rigged a fix (so I guess I'm not *that* dumb), so the problem is solved for me.

In short, I love this little washer.

title: Newly installed door seal leaks worse than failed seal it replaced.
text:
Reasonably priced seal with quick delivery are the main credits for this product. Original dishwaher seal was caked with dishwasher soap residue and had discolored, also it allowed a few drips to exit the dishwasher door at the lower right corner, onto the floor. New seal was easily pushed into door frame channel and cut to same length as original door seal. First dish wash cycle literally poured water from both lower corners of door. Wiped up floor and reset seal with less insertion pressure into the door frame channel…same flooding occurred. Pulled out seal and without any stretching or forcing. Installed for a 3rd time using a flat edge for uniform insertion height into channel.
Leaked a little less, but it now takes a ridiculous amount of force to close and seal thr front washer door.
Carefully removed entire seal one more time, and placed into a large metal bowl of hot (not boiling) water for 5 minutes to soften seal material. Installed final time using flat face of ruler for uniform insertion and depth into door channel. Final test run resulted in minor leaks at left corner lower corner of door onto floor, and high effort to both close and later unlatch the door. Seal shore hardness is excessive, it’s ability to both compress and memory for spring back is poor. Not a viable replacement seal for Maytag/ Whirlpool dishwashers. If available, I will try the OER part purchased directly from Whirlpool Parts, in Factory wrapper. This aftermarket part was not acceptable, as it resulted in both poor fit and poor function.. Weatherbug

title: Did not Quite fit my Whirlpool Lower Rack
text:
Pros: Appear to be well-made and heavy duty with stainless steel axles rather than plastic.
Cons: Product Description is not clear enough with one obscure reference to order the correct height when no other height choice is actually offered.

The new wheels installed easily on the front of my whirlpool rack. They held the rack approximately a half inch higher than my old wheels. The installation on the rear of the rack had a minor problem: the top extension interfered with the operation of the adjustable last row of tines, but I was able to make an adjustment to get that to work. However, the problem was not just a minor change in height, the wheels also made the rack too wide to roll smoothly into the dishwasher. The real problem happened when the rack was about 2/3 of the way in. My Whirlpool has two small strips above the rail at the rear of the case, and the old wheels were made of plastic thin enough to go past the rail while the wheels rolled under them. I tried the new wheels and the wheels went under the rail but the plastic of the supporting frame of the new wheels was too thick to slide past, so that the rack bound up and could not be inserted far enough to close the dishwasher door. My model number was not listed in the "for example" list but it is a Whirlpool, and the height of the wheels was not the real problem (nor would I know where to look to order the correct height). If the "correct height" wheels were made of the same thickness, my problem would still exist. Because I can't test these more to determine whether they hold up and function well and because the width of the plastic was a problem, I deduct two stars and give a three star rating.

title: It works, but WILL fail after about one year
text:
This pump is ok if you're in a bind. Replacing it really sucks, ours made it about 1.5 years and the quality was noticably less than that of OEM. Expect it to fail much sooner than the official manufacturer model.

Do yourself a favor and spend the extra (slightly less than 2X) and go with OEM, and don't be fooled by the Amazon store masquerading as OEM/Genuine, it is a falsified name intended to trick users into thinking they're receiving genuine, OEM products.

Once this cheaper pump failed, we opted to replace with OEM the next time around since the replacement process really is such a chore... comparing the 2 pumps side by side (this product vs. OEM) there were noticable quality differences on all fronts, OEM wins hands-down! They will last closer to 5-10 year range per my research, so the extra $25 to go OEM was worth its weight in gold not having to replace the failing pump every 12-18 months.

title: Shockingly bad cleaning job
text:
I wish I had done more careful research before buying my Samsung dishwasher. Not exactly this model, but it has identical problems.

The chief issue is that even when you scrub all the loose material off your dishes, it still finds a way to eventually clog up the upper arm- which has to be as bad a piece of industrial design as I've ever seen. A clog in a single hole makes the arm stop rotating, so whatever position it stops in irrigates the dishes directly above that spot.

Also, the ads make a big deal about something called "storm wash" which directs extra jets of water. Good idea, except that those jets are confined to the back corner and work only for about an 8 inch by 8 inch square.

It's an almost useless piece of junk and I'll replace it as soon as I can save enough money.

title: I would have given it 4 stars for its performance but I found the output in the description some-what mis-leading.
text:
GENERAL COMMENTS:
Let me begin by saying that if you don't use more than 4-6 standard size trays of ice /day then this machine is probably not worth it for you. No ice-machine I've seen is even a close 2nd to the ice-makers that are available in most refrigerators these days in as far as production, ease of use, convenience and quality of ice so if you have the option of purchasing or using a refrigerator with an ice-maker by all means take that option. This ice machine definitely has a learning curve and is not as turn-key as I thought, however, there are a few simple tricks you can do that will enhance it's performance and output. I would have given it 4 stars for its performance but I found the output in the description some-what deceiving. Another consideration that you will have to make is the counter space that the machine takes up.

OPERATION:
The machine produces the 1st batch of 9 bullet shaped cubes (which are 1/2+ the volume of traditional cubes) in about 6 minutes as described but succeeding batches take considerably longer. It takes from 3 to 3.5 hours to fill the hopper which is 9.5"x 5"x 4.5". The description states that the machines produces 26 lbs./day but that's if you operate it for 24 hours. When the ice comes out it is wet and it will stick together after it is put into the freezer the same as the bags of ice you buy from Walmart, C-stores, etc. The difference is that ice from these locations is made from tap water and could possibly have sanitary issues depending on how it was bagged. This machine gives you the control of sanitary handling and the option of using spring or purified water.

A few operating tips to enhance performance:
1.) When the hopper fills up, the full ice indicator light comes on and halts machine operation even after the hopper is emptied until the sensor warms up. If you desire the machine to keep operating, cover the sensor (a metal rod on the right side of the hopper) with the ice scoop, handle pointing up. If you forget, hold the sensor between your fingers until it warms up and the red indicator light goes off.
2.) Put some left over ice into the reservoir to speed up the process.
3.) Store the ice in a small bucket/container lined with a bag, that way you can pull the bag out and bang it on the counter if the cubes freeze together and then easily put them back in the bucket.

I hope this review will help you to make an informed decision about whether or not this machine is right for you.

text: Let me first say I DID not buy this item through Amazon.  I don't want to give Amazon a bad name.  In total honesty I purchased this item at a local thrift store for only $10.00.  I had been wanting a counter top ice maker for a couple of years but didn't want to pay the higher prices without knowing exactly what I was going to get.  You know, is it too large?  Does it take up more counter space then imagined?  Does it make enough ice?  Those type of questions.  So imagine my delight when I found it for only $10.00.  Well, know I can say I know the reason why the previous owner got rid of it.  Well I can say it got me through the summer months and then one night I was awaken by the loud screeching and scraping noise coming from the machine.  Before I laid down it was working great but all of a sudden it just went crazy.  After investigating I noticed the basket that catches the water was cracked.  It would catch the water but not make the ice.  Even though the coils would frost up but it just would never actually complete the job of making the ice.  Then it would 'go through the motions' of filling the basket with water and all the loud screeching and scraping it just not make the ice.  I guess for the money I paid for it I could have rated it higher but like I said I see why the previous owner donated it to the thrift store!

title: I hate this ice maker.
text:
The good, the bad, the ugly!

We are replacing yet another ice maker. This OEM is leaking in two spots in the tray, causing two months of &350+ water bills! This is our third ice maker in 11yrs. When the OEM gives it a one year warranty, that kinda tells you they aren’t made to last the life of the fridge.

First the good.
It came with a wiring harness, which I was not expecting. The bottom of covered so there aren’t any accidental shocks to the back of the hand when reaching in for ice, it happened to me once. The two top mounts have large slots that allow the screws to be pre-screwed and the unit is simply “hung” on the screws. The OEM Whirlpool has holes that were always a pain to hold the unit, nut driver, and screw while trying to line it up. It has two sets of fingers to sweep the ice. Finally, it arrived next day!

The bad:
The wiring harness plug is not the correct plug for my Maytag fridge. Not a problem, it’s very easy to swap the OEM plug. The cubes are HALF the size of OEM! The tray that the fill tube pours water into is a little too low and water is splashing out as it fills. Which means the last two trays aren’t filling completely.

The ugly:
We have had it for 3 days and it still hasn’t filled the OEM bin halfway. The motor is so weak, it can’t get out of its own way! The fingers often get stuck and need to be manually moved to dislodge it from being stuck. Sometimes lifting the bale to off/on a few times has triggered it. There have been SEVERAL times that “jumping” it. Even then, it has been so weak that it screams in agony. I have been wrestling with the water fill level dial on the side because the factory setting was creating a big block of 8 pieces of ice.

Final thoughts:
Maybe so have a lemon? Perhaps the seller will see this review and reach out to me and die whatever it takes to help our lives get back to normal. If not, this ice maker is going back. I knew there was a slight risk buying aftermarket parts. I have never had any problems buying parts for our Whirlpool washer & dryer. This ice maker cost me $65. Maytag has the OEM unit for $140 shipped. My local Whirlpool parts distributor has the same OEM that is now being replaced for the third time in 11yrs for $220.

I guess the thing that REALLY PISSES ME OFF is that the ice cubes are HALF the size (length) of OEM and it takes an hour to make a batch of ice. The OEM makes ice in 20 minutes, like clockwork.

title: Great little washer
text:
Got this washer for my apartment so I could do laundry whenever and save some money not going to the coin laundry machines. The cite said that the hose could attach to normal sinks which is not the case. It will attach to outdoor plumbing like a garden hose faucet, not your sink or shower. That was an easy enough fix since I had to go to the hardware store to get a longer hose attachment to reach my showerhead anyway. When you get this you will probably need another hose and an extension cord as both of those are very short on the machine.
At first, I was just unscrewing the showerhead and then attaching the hose to the shower, but that was leaking and I used a lot of plumbing tape so I got a little valve thing so I could just leave both things attached and just flip the switch. That made doing laundry super convenient.
The washer itself is great. It takes about 45 minutes to do a load on normal. Clothes come out very clean. Clothes come out about as damp/wet as a normal full-size washer, so don't expect the spin dryer to actually dry the clothes. I was hoping that it would dry them a bit more. I tried just running the spin cycle to increase drying but it didn't make them any dryer because they are all just pressed up against the sides at the end. Some reviews said it only fit about 1 pair of pants and maybe some socks. This is not the case for me. I can fit about a week or 2 worth of my laundry in one load. I can also wash a full set of sheets (full-sized bed) and a towel in one load. I think the 7.7lb load means that it is the weight of dry clothes you can put in the washer when you start it, it will get heavier as the water is added.

title: Beware Defective Board received from Amazon
text:
As we all know by now, these GE motherboards are the worst. My repairmen want to swap them out at every repair. I personally have had mine changed 5 times in the last 5 years.

So I thought it would be easy enough to do on my own, when I last had an issue with the freezer not defrosting. So I ordered one from Amazon (a GE OEM part). It turned out that I did not need to replace the motherboard at that time. So, I stored my Amazon GE Board away for the next time.

Well that time came a year later, when it again stopped defrosting. I replaced the defrosting heater and thermodisc, but it still was not defrosting properly. So, the repairman wanted to replace the motherboard. I told him I had one, and he began to install it. He looked at it closely, and pointed out the dust on the motherboard and slight dirt on the connecting prongs - indicating that the motherboard had been used before. It failed to work correctly, and I ended up having to buy one from the repairman anyway.

Since I purchased the motherboard over a year ago, according to Amazon's policies, I am no longer eligible for a refund. So, buyer beware! There are a lot issues with this motherboard to begin with, and we do not need unscrupulous stores selling defective or previously used parts too. Shame on you Amazon.

title: OK flow sensor  while it works.
text:
My DW7933LRASR dishwasher was blinking 3 lights Normal, Heavy, and Smart Auto shortly after pushing start of the cycle. Machine drained water and terminated wash cycle. After observing machine behavior and researching on Internet I came to the conclusion that Flow sensor is the culprit. After replacing this sensor the problem is gone. Replacement of the part isn't very difficult, but awkward due to obstructed access to connectors and clamp. I found using long nose pliers worked best for me.

Update. After 3 month of working OK with this new sensor Samsung dw failed again with the same symptoms. I moved dw from under the counter and started washing outside so I could observe this sensor. Water was filling dishwasher, but sensor float was stuck at the bottom of the assembly and refused to float. See attached pic. As a result dw canceled wash cycle, drained water and started blinking error state. After fifth try the floating piece popped up and dw proceeded with wash cycle as intended. Sensor housing is clean and clear, so float seems to get stuck with no apparent reason. It's probably not manufactured well enough to work long time.

title: There may be other problems with your washer if you are looking for this part.
text:
Alright this WAS the part I was looking for. It was correct for my washer, and it was a suggested replacement for the error I was receiving. HOWEVER. This part did not fix my problem and may not fix yours either. if you blow through the small hose and the washer clicks (while the washer is running the diagnostic cycle) then this part is not faulty. I had a hunch that it wasn't bad but it took me wasting $100 to realize it.

My problem was two capacitors on the main board at the top of the washer that were slightly bulged and needed to be replaced. This mainboard is cryptic to remove from the washer, but it is not difficult. waste of $100 for me as they strictly do not allow returns. Replacing the capacitors was a $20 fix if you have the tools and know what you're doing.

title: Bought porcelain, received coated metal

Unfortunately, by the time the coating started wearing through and showing rust, it was too late to return them. I already had to return them once because they sent me three large and one small bowl! Back when I ordered them, the only options were metal and porcelain; the "coated" option did not exist (maybe they got in trouble with their fibbing and changed it?). Porcelain enamel coating is nothing like real porcelain. So buyer beware...if you're looking for genuine porcelain bowls I'd go somewhere else.

title: It’s a little under built but so is OEM
text: Identical to OEM which also failed after four years and I am replacing. Some people on here are claiming this is built poorly. I can’t attest to the metallurgy of the coils but I can say as far as the diameter of the coils and all the components this is identical to the OEM part and a hundred dollars less. Only way I would buy the OEM seeing how I’m replacing an OEM part as if I could get a 5-6 year warranty on the coil otherwise just buy the aftermarket. I bought this product two years ago and one coil has failed. Unfortunately these particular dryers and this particular  coil design are very prone to failure. It is absolutely crucial that you clean your lint filter every single time and if you’re putting in a bunch of say wool blankets you might want to clean it in the middle of the load. Make sure that you have an unobstructed 4 inch short run for your dryer. If there is any back pressure that slows down the flow of air then it doesn’t matter if it’s aftermarket or OEM these coils will get too hot, sag and burn out. I’m guilty at running my loads on sanitize a lot and that wears these coils out faster. My suggestion for anyone that is having these coils or ones like it burn out, don’t use the sanitize setting too often it’s too hot. Make sure your lint filter is unobstructed make sure your dryer run is short and also unobstructed. Every month pull out the lint filter get a small attachment for your vacuum and suck out the bottom of the area in which the lint filter goes because a lot of lint gets in there and then that lint prevents a good seal and then lint gets into the the fan and it starts to clog it up and it pushes less air. These dryers are finicky.

text: I suppose if you know exactly what you're doing and exactly what you're looking for, then by all means order exactly the parts you need to do your exact job. If you're not sure then order this part if you are doing any kind of under the sink plumbing with or without a garbage disposal. If it turns out you don't need it just put it in the junk drawer until the day you chop it up and scavenge its parts for some other use. I had installed and reinstalled new plumbing under my new sink several times and kept getting it wrong so when I ordered some brand new snappy drain parts to go at the task a different way, I wasn't sure if I would need this or not. THANKFULLY  I ordered it just in case. On a previous attempt to install my new dishwasher with my new plumbing for my newly remodeled kitchen, I had cut down the end of the drain hose on the dishwasher to fit the plumbing from earlier attempts. This little piece of cheap but intelligently designed rubber with a few hose clamps SAVED the day. I was able to resize my dishwasher drain hose to fit the new plumbing fixtures instead of having to take all that stuff out "AGAIN" just to replace something else I screwed up. This is one of those items you should order regardless. It's a wonderful "JUST IN CASE" type part you should have in the pile with all the other extra parts that are left over after attempting to do it yourself. I'm going to order another one "just in case" to stick in that bag full of extra pvc pipes and various parts  I'm not using anymore. Something will happen I'm sure and I'll have an extra one around to MacGyver with.

title: Washes, but don't count on other things working too well...
text:
Great idea, needs improvement...a lot of improvement

The 2nd use, our tube that connects from the faucet to the machine split, causing water to leak everywhere. A roll of plumbers tape fixed the issue, but the tube shouldn't have broken to start with.

The lint catcher is totally useless. On our first wash, it popped off. It continues to pop off. By the end of the first week, I got so frustrated with it, that I threw it away, because the plastic just doesn't hold up to staying connected to the machine. Now I have a lint problem. There are 3rd party lint catchers, according to other reviews I've read, that you can get online - but the point is that I shouldn't HAVE to buy something else to take care of it.

The machine leaks. I have a video of it leaking around the top of the unit down the sides. I would have assumed this was because it wasn't draining, but I'm watching steady streams of water come out the exit tube into our toilet, which is level with the machine.

The timer on the spinner doesn't always engage spin when the two doors are closed. I've had to unplug/replug the machine back in to get it to "reset" to get it to work.

The spin bucket top (the ring around the bucket) comes loose often and causes it to rub on the machine, which has caused the plastic to shred around the top. This causes an unbalanced bucket, and a heck of a lot of noise sounding like the machine is going to take off like an airplane.

The machine overall does a good job with washing though once you get the hang of it. Most items tend to ball up in the center, so you have to keep an eye on it. I just wish it didn't have these other issues. I have used it less than a month - I shouldn't have to pay to send it back to Panda to have it repaired. I haven't even contacted them because I'm sure that is what they will tell me to do. I am searching for a replacement that will work in place of our Panda. I should get a working machine, without issues - from the start.

title: Only one lid, so plan to stack these
text:
I was thinking this came with two lids, allowing for a side-by-side setup, but it only has one. Actually, given the way I'm likely to use these, one lid is really all I need, even if used side by side.

I have one Easter Egger hen, Pippin, who really puts out the eggs. Not enough eggs that I don't often buy an 18-count carton at the grocery store, but enough that I have to be concerned about keeping track of which eggs are the oldest so they can be used first. A "first in/first out" setup like you find with can rollers is ideal, and until now I didn't have that option for eggs. My countertop spiral egg skelter has too steep of a roll and, sometimes, one of Pippin's eggs will be too big to fit in it.

These egg holders, first and foremost, fit in the fridge very well. They roll the eggs gently. The incline is slight, so the eggs definitely roll down when you take one out, but not so fast that the eggs break. To do a first in/first out storage, however, requires always having to take the lid off to put the new egg(s) toward the back, so I won't use the lid. This is okay with me. I'll use the bottom egg holder for my 18-count white large eggs that I get from the grocery store and the top egg holder (sans lid) to put each day's new egg toward the back of a stack. (Or maybe I'll use the lid with the grocery store eggs and put Pippin's egg holder beside it with no lid. I don't want to have to take the lid off each day I add an egg. This will leave room to put something else on top of the lidded egg tray.)

I haven't quite worked out my rotational system yet, but I'll probably plan to pull my eggs from left to right and also put in new eggs from left to right at the top (back) of the stacks. Right now, I've got 10 blue eggs, so I put three stacks of three and then the extra egg at the top of the left stack. As I take out the eggs, the stacks will roll down and the fresher eggs will be in the back. I won't have to remember which ones are which, and this will work great. For the lower holder, I will fill the whole thing with 18 eggs, pull them from the tray until they are gone, and then order a new carton.

The piece that fits the lower egg holder for stacking another tray on top is very sturdy and neatly designed. I really like this set of egg holders, and it's definitely going to make my life easier.
