title: Exact Replacement...Almost
text: [[VIDEOID:daf4a5c5a0d91e8cef746ef0a615c173]] So this is probably no fault of the seller, but I am disappointed with this product. Whomever designed these products did a disservice to customers. Obviously I need to replace the auger motor in my refrigerator. This auger and my older auger are identical, so I thought. The shape, specs and connections are one in the same. I even hooked up the new one and it turned with no problem (I’ve attached a video of the new auger working). The problem is when I transferred the shaft from the old to the new it was too big. The shaft is 7/16 but the bore on this auger appears to be 3/8. 1/16 of an inch on the shaft is the only difference between the two. After doing more research, it appears that the “exact” replacement for my unit is at least $50.00 more than this unit. $50.00 for the only difference being that the shaft bore is 1/16 of an inch smaller? That’s ridiculous!  There is no mention anywhere, that I’ve found, on Amazon or Whirlpool or any other part sites where the shaft dimensions are either discussed or provided. Nowhere is the shaft size outlined as being a potential difference Why would Whirlpool or it’s parents company develop two parts that look basically exactly identical but are made to take SLIGHTLY different size shafts and not provide customers a heads up?  At this point, I will attempt to find an adapter or a work around in order to get the shaft to fit. If not, I will just return the part and get ice the old fashion way.

title: Fixed problem with LG WM2688HWM not draining
text:

I also replaced the circulation pump while I was at it, just in case, but that pump looked like it was in much better shape.

Replacement was time consuming but not too difficult thanks to videos on the Internet. I went slowly since I am not use to washer repair. Oh... take photos with your phone before you take stuff apart or disconnect wires! I almost wired it back incorrectly but I looked at the photos I took and fixed the connections. UPDATE: Some people seem to say it doesn't matter because it's AC.

Also, to make sure you get a genuine part, I'm told "Look for PLASET molded onto the white plastic, not printed on label."

Minus one star because this pump failed in the first place.... a 5 star pump wouldn't have failed. Hopefully they have made some improvements so this pump is more reliable now.

You couldn't really double-stick tape them up on the back or you wouldn't be able to change the batteries. I guess you could double stick tape the front if you need to read it through enclosure glass but it would be a drag trying to take it off to clean or move it. title: Good.  not great, but good.
text:
Ordered this as my stove's old thermostat reads much higher than true, and I would often get overheat warnings at modest temperatures (300+). No instructions are included, understandable as it is intended for many models, but I think that at least something should be included. Perhaps at least an explanation of how to disconnect the old thermostat's clip without breaking it. I managed, but it would have been nice. For my stove, replacement took about 15 minutes, some of that time spent trying to find the fastest way to complete the task, basically not removing anything more than required. Installation required two differently sized sockets. Once complete, what better way to test than to bake a cake? I set the thermostat to 350 degrees, and once preheated my thermostat read 345. A vast improvement, as my old stove thermostat would need to be set to 450 to read 350. Making pizzas a few days later, to achieve 500F, I had to set to 510.

I'm very satisfied with the amount of improvement, as it saved me from buying a new stove, but I would have preferred if the new thermostat read completely true instead of 5-10 degrees shy.

title: Pretty good.  Some cautions, tho
text:
For the price, this is a nice hood. I bought it mostly for the high suction, and for that reason I like it. There are some things to be cautious about.

Some pros and cons:

Pro: LOTS of suction, fairly quiet at all speeds, removable & washable baffles

Con: Difficult installation, light brightness not adjustable, horrible instructions

The pictures show the installation as I'm in process of building the cabinets. You can see that the baffles are covered in plastic film. There's a lot of it, and taking it off is a pain. You can also see that the flexible duct the unit came with is plenty long, and seems to be of pretty good quality. The controls are simple, but on the plus side there is an on/off button for display panel, so it can be turned off (no light) or left on depending. The on/off doesn't have to be pressed before turning the lights or fan on - it's just for the display.

As mentioned, it has a lot of suction, but only 4 levels / settings. I think for most cooking, 'low' or 'medium low' would be fine, leaving 'medium high' and 'high' pretty much unused for most typical household cooking. While these speeds would be great above a char-broiler or when blackening catfish, I don't think I'll use them much in regular cooking. This means there isn't as much flexibility: a unit with the same number of speeds but a lower maximum CFM would give more options in the typically used range. I will be home brewing in this area, so I wanted the high CFM, and the hood provides that without too much noise.

The unit comes with really bad instructions. There is a template, but even after trimming and folding as per instructions, it didn't fit. Also, it has a cut out circles for where to cut the holes for the electric plug and vent. Much better would be to not have cut out the circles on the template and instead mark the centers so those points could be transferred. Om the plus side, there is plenty of room to insert / tighten / adjust mounting screws once it's fairly in position. As plenty of people have noted - it's heavy. A helper would have been very useful for installation.

All in all a good product for the price if you need this much power. If you don't, I suggest looking at one of the similar models.

For writing this review and including pictures, Cosmo will send me a bonus gift they value at ~$25.

title: No more laundromats!!!
text:
I purchased this item through a different vendor (J&R electronics) specifically because they do an excellent job packing items for shipment. They added extra air cushioning and a few layers of cardboard. Since the machine was getting shipped from NY to CA, secure packing was very high priority for me.

The machine itself is very heavy. I am a small woman who lives alone and I swear, I spent more time trying to muscle this thing out of the box than actually setting it up!

Attaching the bottom plate is not nearly as difficult as I was expecting. The "front" of the machine is the edge that has the control buttons directly above it. To easily attach the plate, hold the plate over the bottom and insert all the screws, inserting the screw furthest away from the last screw you inserted (e.g. insert the screw at 12 o'clock then the screw at 6 o'clock, then the screw at 1 o'clock, the 7o'clock, etc). Tighten all the screws 1/2 or 1 twist by hand. Then, going through the same "furthest away" pattern you did before, tighten all the screws halfway. Finally, tighten all the way being very careful not to strip.

If you simple go "clockwise" around the machine inserting screws, I imagine the plate will not go on/some holes will be blocked. If you sink the screws all the way in on the first pass, you probably will not be able to insert all the screws. As you tighten the plate and it becomes flush with the machine, you will notice some of the tough-to-tighten screws become easier to tighten, as the metal plate shifts.

I put all the screws in myself using a phillips head screw driver. This was probably a bit more labor-intensive than using an electric or drill.

Then, remove the aerator from your sink of choice. Screw on the silver piece, the "sink adaptor". Be mindful that your sink may be reverse threaded (normally things are lefty-loosey righty-tighty, but some older or fancy designer sinks are reverse threaded) Grab the intake hose, screw the white end into the machine. Take the brass fitting and screw this into the gray end. Press the little white ring/widget on the brass fitting towards the grey hose bit to quick release/attach to the sink adapter. Make sure everything is TIGHT. I did not adequately tighten the white machine connection, and got a soaking in return. If you're concerned, throw a dishtowel over the connections to prevent some of the spray.

Take your drain hose and hook it over the sink faucet, or nestle it in the sink. I flop mine over the intake hose and position it so that the opening to the drain hose hook is pointing a teensy bit up and at one of the sides of the sink, so that a "blast" of drained water will just push the hook around the sink. Be careful if you are using a bathroom sink, this puppy drains quick!

Follow directions for loading/operating the machine. Note that this thing does rebalance quite frequently and does the spinup-drain-spinup-drain-spinup-pause thing a LOT. No, it is not broken, it did not quit mid-cycle, it's just a quirky machine.

You do want to make sure you are using HE detergent with this machine, as otherwise it gets SUPER bubbly (we use All Free&Clear detergent plus oxy). After the spin cycle, it takes maybe 12 to 14 hours for clothes to dry.

All in all, setup was not terrible. If you're not handy, it will probably be challending but if you've ever asssembled ikea furniture, you can assemble your washing machine. I promise. Including time to remove the outer box(es) and a single "quick wash" cycle, it took 90mins to get set up.

It gets my clothes clean. because of the hose/other potential water-leak issues, I would not run this machine without being close by (meaning, 1 room away) and periodically checking on it unlesss the hose is totally secured/stationary to something solid. I don't have a good place in my kitchen to do this, otherwise I would be a lot calmer whilst running it. I took away a star because many of the materials used to make this machine (e.g. the hoses) are cheaply made and will need to be replaces probably within the next 12 months depending on use.

All in all, we are extremely happy with this purchase. My upstairs neighbor actually stopped in (he has been thinking about purchasing this model) and my description of the install process basically sold him. No trips to the hardware store. No power tools. Really, if I can install this properly, most people can. If you have difficulty, bring the part in question to your local hardware store (NOT home depot/lowes) and ask for help. Some of the parts/fittings/methods might be confusing to someone who is not mechanically inclined.

I plan to update this as my owenership goes on, but so far so great!

Edited to add:
As of 9/19/16, the washing machine is STILL going at it! The basket has become a little more prone to unbalancing over the years, and one of the pegs that hinges the lid cracked so you have to be careful when opening/closing the lid to ensure the peg is properly seated or the lid flaps a little (like flaps up and down <1CM near the handle). I attribute this partially to aging plastic and partially to us leaving the lid open with the hoses leaning against it at times. The peg broke about 2mos ago so roughly after 4 years of use. Next year we will probably replace the hoses per manufacturer suggested maintenance - I didn't think we would need to as I didn't expect this gadget to be in use for 5 years!

It has paid for itself many many MANY times over - not only in saving trips and $$$ to the laundromat, but in rent. We would probably have moved to a place with in-unit laundry, which would have run at least $100 more per month. Over the last 4+ years we have done an average of 1-2 loads of laundry a day (averaged over a week - 3 loads sheets/duvets, 2 loads pants, 2 loads athletic gear/sports suds, 2 loads work shirts, 4 loads socks/underwear/tees/pajamas, 1 load sweaters/misc, 2 loads towels & household linens. we are a household of two.). I have noticed a bit of buildup of cat hair (we have 2 short haired shedding machines) on some of our clothes, likely due to the fact that we air dry with a fan + dehumidifier rather than a 'regular' dryer. No issues with buildup in the machine itself.

The only items we found this machine has difficulty washing/must go to the laundromat are an ikea loveseat cover (Klippan model, 1 piece for whole couch), a heavy terry cloth hooded bathrobe, a queen size down comforter, and a 6ft by 4ft flatwoven cotton rug.

Edited to add:I bought this washing machine in 2012. It's still going strong (albeit with slightly more frequent unbalancing issues) almost 5 years later. Some of the LEDs go on the fritz and one of the plastic lid hinges cracked (you have to *carefully* lower the lid or pop the hinge back in line, could fix this with epoxy but I'm lazy). Our two adults + two cats household has done 99% of our laundry including queen size sheets & duvet covers in this machine. Worth every penny!

title: Not a substitute for refrigerator ice maker, and not Alexa smart plug or timer compatible
text:
This makes ice, just as the listing says it does. Put water in, ice comes out. But...

My refrigerator's built-in ice maker died, and I needed a replacement for morning iced coffee. That's my main use - not soft drinks or ice water. Does this make ice? Yes, it makes thumb-sized hollow ice bullets. BUT. There's no freezer/storage ability in the unit. I knew this going in, so that's not a surprise. But, it's important. This makes ice very quickly, and will keep making ice. As it makes new ice, it tips the cubes into a basket. New cubes come in, and the "old" ice in the basket melts. The melting starts immediately - the water drips through the basket into the water bin and gets pumped back through to make more ice. There's nothing keeping the ice cold, except the machine tipping new ice into the basket. The warmer the ambient temperature of the room, the faster it melts. Still, that's not news.

Here's the thing. If you think you're going to wake up in the morning to a basket of hard frozen ice, sufficient for your 30 oz travel tumbler of ice coffee, that's not really going to happen. There will be a bin of ice, maybe 5 inches deep. The bullets on top are brand new and solid. The ones on the bottom are on their way back to water. And they're hollow bullets - that means there's less actual ice than the room they take up in your glass. They have a lot of surface area and are not super hard, so they melt QUICKLY if you pour hot water over them. You may need to rethink your recipe - let the coffee cool before you pour it over ice, or go with a cold brew.

My method with ice from the refrigerator's ice maker is to brew highly concentrated hot coffee (Aeropress) and pour it over a full travel tumbler of ice. Like magic some of the ice melts to make the coffee the perfect strength. The rest of the ice stays unmelted for hours in the tumbler to keep the coffee cold for a while. NOT happening with this ice maker. Nope. Not even close.

The bullets are not as hard as the ice from the refrigerator ice maker. It melts faster. Even filling up the travel tumbler with ice, the ice is nearly gone (and the coffee not chilled) within seconds of my pouring the hot coffee over it. AND, there's no more ice in the basket because I used it all in the 30 oz tumbler.

My initial thought was to use an Alexa-compatible smart plug to go on at 4 in the morning, make a full bin of ice, and then shut off when I left for work. Then the machine wouldn't be making ice all day while I was gone. Nope. Not workable. In order for the machine to turn on after the power is off (or the smart plug turns on), one must push the ON button. Unless I was going to get up at 4 to hit the button and go back to bed, my hopes for an Alexa-controlled ice maker were dashed.

Next idea? This one actually worked, but it's not really simplifying my life. After work I start the ice maker. As it pops ice into the bin, I tip the bin into a container and put it in the freezer. Over the next couple of hours, I keep tipping more ice into the container. Then I just turn off the ice maker (or let Alexa do it). The next morning, I have a full bin of ice in the freezer (more than a single bin from the countertop machine), fully frozen (not as soft as what came directly out of the machine). Since the bullets in the machine are in a perpetual cycle of freeze/thaw, the bullets in the container may need to be broken apart some. The bullets are wet when I put them in the container, so they stick together when fully frozen.

Make my 30 oz travel tumbler of iced coffee, enjoy it in the car on the way to work. Come home, and repeat the "make ice before bedtime" routine so there's enough for the next morning's coffee.

Not a perfect solution, and not one that I'm willing to continue indefinitely. I have already scoped out the available room in the freezer to just use stacking ice cube trays until I can replace the broken part on the refrigerator ice maker.

As for noise, yes, I can hear it in the living room (about 25 feet from the machine). Is it loud? Not particularly, but I can hear the clatter of ice dropping into the basket. If I had this on all night and my bedroom were near the kitchen, I would probably hear it. A light sleeper could awaken from the clatter. The compressor runs constantly when the machine is on, blowing hot air out the side. If that were going all day, it would be fighting the a/c in the kitchen, for sure. The compressor makes a sound like a small fan, which may or may not bother some people.

title: Great Product Just (Unfortunately) Not With Gevalia Coffee
text:
I bought this filter with some trepidation because there was a warning about the fine grind espresso coffees clogging the mesh filter. I have several pounds of Gevalia Papua New Guinea and Colombian coffee I wanted to use in my new Keurig Vue 7000. Problem is, the grind is fine and does cause some clogging, leaving an ounce or more of water in the filter cup after brewing, and requiring almost two full scoops of coffee to make one decent 10 oz cup. I suspect that's about 50% the fault of this filter cup and 50% the fault of the Vue 7000 though, because all of the Vue cups have more coffee than their K-Cup relatives, so they require more coffee to begin with. I suspect Keurig will say that's because they give you the option of larger cup sizes with the Vue. Anyway, I find that a bit wasteful, but I can live with it to get a single cup in a minute...time is money too, right?

There is a considerable amount of residue in the bottom of the coffee cup with the Gevalia coffee, but I seldom drink the full cup anyway, so that is not an issue for me. I agree to a point that the residue actually adds to the body and is similar to the coffee you get from a French press. Additionally, you can see oils from the coffee beans around the rim of your freshly brewed cup of coffee that you do not get with conventional paper filters, which also adds to the flavor and body of the coffee.

All in all, I think this is an excellent product that extends the usefulness and economy of the Keurig Vue. I recommend the product.

title: Horrible waste of money
text:
I bought a Frigidaire FPHC2399KF in November 2009. It has never worked properly. Nor has the replacement unit Frigidaire supplied. That's right, 3 service calls, one entirely new replacement unit, and a new temp sensor later and I still don't have a fridge that works properly. My first unit had a large wave in the side that was noticeable, and even more troublesome both fridges have had awful temperature control. The freezer can not properly control temperature, and drops as low as -14 F several times a day (with a setpoint of 0 F). We were careful not to make any changes to the default settings on the second unit before observing this problem for a while because we were afraid that somehow we had messed it up. Only after watching the unit overcool for several days did we attempt adjusting the setpoint to +3 deg to see if maybe that would work better (it didn't). Not only does this excessive cooling make such things as digging through the bags of painfully cold veggies, or eating ice cream inconvenient (so rock hard that neither my husband or I have a prayer of scooping it straight from the freezer), but it causes some of our fresh food drawers to freeze because some air exchange occurs between the two compartments. Delicate items, like lettuces, have to be carefully positioned in the fridge to prevent damage. Even carrots & celery can't be kept in certain compartments because they got frozen all the way through and totally lost their crispness. To top it all off, the humidity adjuster on one of the drawers totally broke off.

Frigidaire's customer service is equally dissatisfying. I've spent hours on the line with them to be provided with no useful information. Originally they just told me to adjust the humidity control sliderson the drawers, but now they are just telling me to have my local service provider continue replacing the parts he is guessing are bad. They provide NO actual technical assistance from anyone who has any kind of in-depth technical knowledge of how this unit works. No one who might know what part really is defective so that I could talk to the repairman about replacing that part. Just the same routine over and over - they tell you to call your local servicer and continue with the repairs because the unit is fixable. But then my unit never actually gets fixed. I just waste time having parts replaced with no affect on my fridge performance. I've even had them tell me that my first unit didn't have this problem - apparently their rep didn't note that in my file. Fortunately, the service company did document that issue so I can prove that it is a recurring problem. The only helpful person I've spoken to was a corporate lady who was calling to follow up on a survey I filled out giving them horrible customer service marks. She at least sent me a contribution toward my food losses. But even she hasn't fulfilled her promise of having a product technical specialist call me.

Evaluation by an electrical engineer showed that the heating element burned into an open state, apparently due to penetration of water onto the coil surface.  There were multiple failures which caused the coil to burn out:  1) a broken seal; 2) a crack in the protective glass (likely caused by water dripping directly onto the glass tube); and 3) inadequate shielding at the ends of the tube which allowed melting frost to access the glass tube. Relations in Germany had this Italian frother, and we bought one because the wonderful coffee we had with them every morning could not be better than when using this. It is easy to use and clean, and the double mesh filters make the froth super fine and quick. Perfect for serving guests something special. This is a great way to make stiff volume of frothed milk. Only drawback is that it understandably doesn't work as well for a single serving; the pitcher is too large to be as effective.

Later we discovered a hitherto unknown use for this frother:
-Heat a couple cups of water.
-Mix in some powdered cocoa mix.
-Froth and serve the most unusual hot cocoa your guests will have ever had.

The device has held up for us for years. Makes a great gift for coffee lovers. Highly recommended.

title: Three Damaged Units, Horrible Exterior Design, AVOID
text:
Final conclusion: I would avoid this unit. Problems with all 3 I ordered - Two severely damaged. I had to heavily modify the base of my cabinets to accommodate the VERY POOR design.

Firstly, the top wire outlet is so close to the back right screw support that you either have a visible wire in your cabinet, or you have to build your vent box an extra 12” to the side, losing valuable cabinet space. Also, without a provided template, you have to measure near perfect to drill the hole for the wire to avoid compromising rear right screw integrity. This wire outlet should have been within a few inches of the vent outlet. If there was any space inside the back of the unit, I would have drilled a hole through the metal and ran the wire inside.

Secondly, the plastic vent outlet screws into the top with 3 protruding tabs. Your cabinet needs to be cut out an additional 1.5”-2” just so the unit will fit flush underneath the cabinet. Again, losing even more precious cabinet space.

Thirdly, the dimensions provided are not accurate. They fail to account for the screwheads and metal overlap on the back and top of unit. I had to cut out existing tile to accommodate this. I was replacing a unit that failed, and the measurements provided for this unit fit my space. Yes 1/8” can be a huge problem when fitting to an existing space!

Project was held up due to other projects being delayed. Did not inspect item upon receiving, because box was fine. Opened 2 months later to install. Huge dent on most visible part of the unit and scuffs on the front. Damaged area was covered in styrofoam. This product was sent to me already damaged. Return window expired - unsure if I can get a replacement.

Update: Ordered replacement. Severe damage again. Third time is a charm? Check your item immediately would be my advice.

Update 2: Third unit visible exterior had no damage. However, top (unseen once installed) dented in. Plastic vent outlet broken.

title: Perfect except for one major flaw - at least in mine
text: Let me preface this by saying I feel the unit I received was defective. There is no other explanation because of the many excellent reviews of this coffee maker. I loved everything about this coffee maker except the one big problem. It made coffee quickly and relatively quietly compared to the Keurig top of the line model  that was only about a year old that it was replacing. I loved the ease of using the water tank (lid simply lifts on and off where my keurig had to be fitted just right), how hot the coffee was, and how nice the unit looks sitting on the kitchen counter. The fatal flaw was grounds in the coffee cup from the first cup brewed. Sometimes just a few grounds , sometimes quite a bit and then sometimes a crazy amount. I have a feeling one of the needles was defective from the factory. This kind of issue should only occur in an unit that has been used a lot with the needles not cleaned out (using an unbent paper clip) and maybe an older unit never decaled. Should never happen in a new unit. When I returned it to Amazon I almost just had it replaced but decided to bite the bullet and bay $40+ more for the current top of the line Keurig (Elite). In true Amazon fashion I processed the return request this morning and they delivered the Keurig unit I ordered same day. I dropped the return Cuisnart at UPS this afternoon and noticed tonight Amazon has already refunded the money. I have ordred hundreds if not thousands of things from Amazon and this is only the second or third item I have had to return. Knowing they stand behind a product if there is an issue makes shopping with Amazon a no fear no pain experience.

title: A-OK
text:
I bought this after watching few reviews here and the manufacturer video. I think the contraption works fine if you follow the instructions. If you see water leaking, it's likely because the filter disk is upside down or not put in properly. If you put the filter disk correctly, it works as advertised.

However my bigger problem with this is the depth of the cap. The cap sits about 1.2 inch inside the cup, so if your cup is small and you usually fill coffee all the way to the top of the cup (which you can do with the original cap that comes with the aeropress), you cannot do that since the coffee will start touching the cap half way making it difficult to plunge further without creating a mess. If you usually fill your cup half way (or about 1.5 inches lower from the rim of the cup, this may be ok for you. Basically you need a much larger cup to pour the same amount of coffee that you were with the original cap. If you see the manufacturer video agree reading this review, you'll see that they cleverly put the aeropress fully on top of the mug instead of resting the rim on top of the mug. This is a bit deceptive and hides a major flaw of this design.

It has all the usually-recommended features, like dryness sensor, end of cycle buzzer and a 'wrinkle guard' feature (it tumbles the clothes every so often after they are dry while the dryer is waiting for you to come and retrieve your clothes).  All these are options you can adjust yourself. There are other 'built in' features that I appreciate as well.  I like its large capacity for clothes. It has easily accommodated every load i have put into it.  I also like the size and placement of the lint filter. It is rather large and long and is accessible from the top of the unit. Unlike other dryers I have had, I never have any trouble cleaning all the lint out of the filter and I have not (up til now) ever seen the filter overloaded with lint.  I also appreciate that the door opens 'down'. This allows me to have additional surface area I can use when I am both putting in or taking out clothes. Of course these features are matters of personal taste but I have found them quite useful.  The entire experience has been very satisfactory!

title: This is Genuine Induction, Not Radiant as Described. Needs Magnetic Cookware.
text: Just got this cook top, checked elsewhere to make certain it was a true induction cook top. I'm doing a preliminary review just to clear that up. I suppose the name of the product is what's so confusing. It's not a "radiant", it's an induction. Now that that's cleared up, here are my preliminary review. Wiring was a snap, it has a nice long conduit and appropriately heavy wires. You need 30a minimum circuit, I have 50a. The cook top looks are stunning. It gleams like polished obsidian. I had a radiant cook top with the same ceramic, and it did scratch on the burners, but that may have been from overheating. The ceramic on this one hardly gets hot, so it may not scratch and dull as badly. The shiny surface it a real fingerprint magnet. Wish it were textured like "fingerprint proof" refrigerator doors. Good news is, it's super-easy to clean. It heats large pots quickly. The biggest burner looks huge but is  10". No problem heating a 12" skillet or stock pot. We like the controls, and are already used to them. The fans are very quiet, but there is "induction noise" on the highest settings. The burners are so powerful you seldom need to run them at setting 9 or "boost" setting.  A slow boil can be maintained on setting 4, or even 3 with a lid on. 1/2 point off both the fingerprints and the induction noise, both annoying but neither are deal killers. I suspect it's impossible to find an induction cook top without these traits. Will be happy to answer questions.

title: Coffee Capsule - Excellent Quality works with Vertuo
text:
High quality design. This item is built to last. I read some reviews that said to experiment to learn how to use it. So I did.

I had some store bought pre-ground coffee. I did two cups. First cup was 3 scoops. Second cup was 4 scoops. Not much different, both weak. I think it was too coarsely ground. I don’t recommend ore-ground coffee from a store unless you can get it finely ground. I don’t blame this device, I blame the grind setting.

So I moved on to whole bean. Alto Grande.

I ground it myself - fine. Loaded 3.5 scoops. Tamped it. WOW! Success. That was a solid cup of coffee. I had some “crema” but less than the store bought pods. I’m pretty sure that with a couple more attempts I will have this down. I would recommend this.

Pros - quality built. This thing is Stainless Steel. I fully expect it will outlast my Nespresso unit. Once you get your grind level, scoop quantity, and tamping down - you’ll appreciate having this. Less hassle than reusable systems that require replacement foil.

Cons - none really.

Bottom line. I had a Keurig for 10 years. It never made good coffee. It broke and I went for a Nespresso. Nespresso is a better cup but more expensive per serving. This reusable pod is good for the environment and your wallet. And better than a Keurig any day. BTW buy some decent coffee. The Vertuo pods are newer so there is not a ton of selection yet. This device is a game changer for selection. So ya, get you some good coffee and enjoy. 👍

title: I think it will be good.
text: Our kitchen cabinets were set up to accommodate a small European oven that is no longer available in the US (Creda).  The small sizing gives you very limited replacement options. We replaced it once with a Fagor since it was 1/3 the price of any other option.  It performed adequately for a few years but some of the functions stopped working and the gaskets were falling off and the top burner element kept falling down so we decided to replace it.  The Verona instructions have you do a high heat several hour procedure in order to burn off/clean out the oven (having worked in manufacturing we perfectly understood the need to clean off all the protective oils that are on new machinery).  It did surprise us when the first real cooking (a couple of roasted chickens) produced enough smoke to necessitate opening the doors, skylights and ventilations fans.  However, since then (about a month and we use the oven a lot), everything has worked very well.  At the moment I suspect that either we had some excess oil from manufacturing or had some sort of grease spill from the chickens on that first event.  The controls are simple and intuitive.  Oh, I did have to push firmly against the oven door in order to get it to lock for a self cleaning (after the initial smoky event).  So, despite some early issues, I think it will be good.

title: Not so eco friendly or family friendly
text:
Setup was easy. Machine does feel terribly cheap. It also arrived dirty and I am sure I bought a NEW one, not a return. We are a military family and I bought this thinking it would be good to use for the next month while we are without our household goods. After running several loads through it though, I have to say I'll be better off taking my laundry to the laundromat and spending several hours and $20 there to get it done.

Capacity: First load I did was a test load of hand towels, probably 10 of them. They did well, wash and rinse. Then I tried to wash my children's pajamas. Once the clothes were wet and began agitating, they began to tangle, which led to unbalanced load. The agitator plate was moving, but the wash was so tangled it could not move. I tried a load of 5 toddler shirts and the same thing has happened. They tangle and then they just sit on top, floating, while the agitator spins below them. At this rate, I'd be better off using a washing board and doing them by hand.

Water usage: The water waste on this machine versus a standard machine or even an HE washer is awful. You have to manually fill the machine for wash and rinse cycles. Now I suppose you COULD reuse the wash water by draining it into a 5 gallon bucket and adding it with the next load. But you still have to manually fill this and I'd estimate it uses probably 4 or 5 gallons on a "large load," which can't be more than one pair of pants or a bath towel, so 10 gallons approximately for a large item, is just not worth it.

Does it clean? Now, if the load stays balanced and if you have that magic ratio of clothes to water to detergent, yes, I would say the agitation would be sufficient.

Details: wash cycles range from 3-15 minutes. Spon cycle goes from 1-5 minutes. It requires a LOT of manual labor though, with filling it and draining, filling and draining....switching to the spin basket.

This would maybe be ideal if you are a single person living in a tiny space or an apartment. But the ratio of water wasted to clothes being washed adequately needs some work. I will be returning.

I found instructions that work on the description of a like-model:

Set Starting Humidity: Press the up button once to display the starting humidity, press and hold the up button for 3 seconds, the starting humidity number flashes, set the desired humidity value through the up and down buttons
Set Stop Humidity: Press the down button once to display the stop humidity, press and hold the button for 3 seconds, the stop humidity number flashes, set the desired humidity value through the up and down keys
How to Restore the Factory Settings: When the power is on, press the up and down keys at the same time, the digital tube will display 888 and then automatically jump to detect the humidity, that is, restore the factory settings.

I hope this helps someone.

title: Nice looking, Powerburner works great.
text:
We moved from a 16 year old GE Profile 4 burner gas cooktop to this GE Cafe 5 burner cooktop.

Installed it this weekend and cooked: soup in a large 8 qt pot, boiled water, used the griddle for bacon and French toast, sautéed some vegetables.

Pros:
- Powerboil feature works great and boils faster than even the most powerful burner on the previous stove.
- The middle burner has a two stage burner -- you can have a very low flame. Great for low simmer or keeping something warm.

Cons:
- The knobs do not come off for cleaning.
- The griddle has a very shallow liquid well. If you're cooking bacon, there's not much room for grease. 4 slices of bacon was enough to fill it. There's no way to drain it, so had to resort to sopping up the grease with a paper towel. I will not cook bacon on it again.

Things to Consider:
- There are 3 grates -- one each over the two side burners, one over the middle burner. These are heavy and you must move them to clean under them. Our old stove had individual grates, so you only moved one to clean underneath.
- The cast iron grates scratch the stainless if you're not careful when you move it.
- the overall height from the counter to the top of burner is higher than our old stove. We have an over stove microwave and we lost some clearance.

I read some reviews that said the height between the flame and the pan was too great. We measured our old stove and measured this. They were both the same, and we measured a number of other cook tops at Home Depot. There wasn't much difference. The issue that some folks my have had may be related to BTU rating of the burners of the old stove, vs the new stove.

All in all, happy with the stove.

title: Works, with some care and effort
text:
The filter is NOT a replacement for Kenmore 9915. When installing the filter, the filter does not turn as far as the original Kenmore 9915 filter, and will not turn the last ~ 20 degrees. I might forgive the poor fit, except without the filter completely engaged, sometimes the filter pops out and water sprays onto the floor! Fortunately while I was able to turn off the water before anything was damaged.

I sent a query to the supplier, and was sent instructions for installing the filter. (but there was nothing that I didn't already know) I also asked the supplier if they offer a filter that replaces Kenmore 9915, and I have not received a response.

If anyone has found a good replacement for Kenmore 9915, please let me know!

----

Update to the review:
To diagnose the problem I purchased a genuine Kenmore 9915 from another source, and I examined the differences. With some work I am able to use the generic filter.

My findings:
1) The genuine 9915 has a slightly different design (see attached picture), and perhaps the design affects how far the filter can turn? (I'm not really sure) I used a dremel tool with a router bit to adjust the plastic 'stop' on the generic filter to make it closely match the Kenmore.
2) Inside the filter receptacle there is a tab that must fit into the u-channel slot of the filter (see picture). The tab in the receptacle is used turn water on/off during filter replacement. When the tab is turned clockwise the water is on. When the tab is turned CCW the water is off. In my case the tab in the receptacle was ahead of the slot in the filter, and this prevented the filter from fully turning. To fix the problem I had to move the tab CCW and then reinstall the filter making sure the tab was fitting into the slot.

With these changes the generic filter is working!

Doug

title: Review from a french press gal...
text:
update 2022, just passed the 2 year mark in owning the SS-10. The lid no longer closes tight enough to trigger the start of coffee making. I would need to press down the lid to start it however it would stop mid stream. Contacted cuisinart and was sent a replacement, the SS-10P1. both the SS10 and SS10P1 looks identical. The SS10P1 lid is hard to open not smooth. feels like an old person with creeky stiff joints. I don't know if this stiffness means more durable and hopefully i wont' have previous issue with loose lid. Fingers cross this one will last longer than 2 years. These machines are not cheap and if it continues to fail in short amount of time, I will have no choice but to revert back to french press.

For the last 20 years or so, i've been a french press gal. I grind my own beans daily and use a french press so i can get the deepest boldest coffee flavor. I have alwasy been a skpetic with these coffee machines fearing weak coffee.

pros
a. Sleek looking machine without taking up a huge footprint
b. nice size water reservoir, 72 ozs
c. can use own grind with the home barista resusable filter. this was a must for me as i had no intentions of purchasing pods.
d. can brew tea as well. I put loose leaf tea in the filter and all day long i am brewing hot tea!
e. XHot setting is pretty hot!
f. dispenses hot water at a press of button (almost..see below).
g. brews a 12 oz cup very fast. did not time it but seems less than a minute.

the cons...

a. the boldness of the coffee is indeed a tad weaker when compared to french press at 4 minute brew... I usually load 2.5 tbsp (maximum) of coffee grind for a 12 oz cup. I will have to play around with smaller cups, 10 or 8 ozs to see if i can get a bolder brew.
b. you have to open and close the top in order to activate functions. For example, i can't just presh "hot water" to dispense hot water. I must open/close top then press hot water. Wish the hot water button can active on its own.

in all, I'm very happy with the purchase. it is awesome to be able to simply the moring coffee routine (i do still grind my own beans but doing so on weekly instead of daily basis) and declutter my countertop of french press, water kettle, and bean grinder. it is also great to have access to hot water for tea throughout the day.

title: Like most others
text:
Like most others, I was running multiple cycles on my dryer and clothes were still damp. I contacted several companies about cleaning my exhaust vent, and all wanted $129 or higher. I watched a couple of You Time videos about what they do and found this product. There was absolutely no reason why I couldn't do the exact same thing these companies were doing for a lot less money! So I found this product and spen't $17 on Prime to get it in two days.

Holy moly, did this thing work!!! Within the first few feet, I was getting a ton of lint falling out the vent.

Using the product is very simple, you just screw the additional lengths on to the others while they are up inside the vent. It tells you right on the package to only go in the clockwise direction, and then you move your power drill in and out to thoroughly clean the vent. The sections go on very securely, and there is absolutely NO REASON to tape the sections together unless you are an idiot that can't read the instructions. Do NOT use the drill in the counter-clockwise direction, or the sections will unscrew themselves. It's not rocket science.

I have a roof vent and the 12 feet of extensions were more than enough to reach from my laundry room all the way up. After I finished running the brush the full length of the duct twice, I took my electric leaf blower and blew out any remnants. I know it worked because before using it, I noticed a small pile of lint on the roof by the vent, and it subsequently blew away.

And just that quickly... The dryer is drying the clothes on one cycle only!

Save yourself a lot of money, and use this tool once or twice a year!

title: Review for EcoSpin
text: I have been researching off grid washing techniques and I really wanted something that would wring out the clothes for me because that is my LEAST favorite part of hand washing. I have been using the EcoSpin as a washer and "spin dryer" for all of our socks, underwear, dish towels, or a few tshirts at a time for the past 2 weeks. It works great as a spin dryer no dripping wet clothes on the drying rack! My number one complaint is that IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO REMOVE THE LID AFTER WASHING GET THE CLOTHES OUT! Takes me forever to try to grip the little groves and get it off.. even my body-building husband has given up with frustration. Next I am worried about the lifetime of this because the plastic it is made from is very flimsy and the turning handle often seems it will just break off!  It also drops off some plastic dust from inside the handle as you turn (i oiled it to keep this from happening). Made cheaply for the price of the product. I planed to use it to wash cloth diapers(prefolds), but I don't think it will work efficiently to wash them without lots and lots of effort. However it will save my hands from wringing! Takes a little while to figure out the best method for detergent to get the clothes drying soft, but I got the hang of it now! I will have to save up to try the other Avalon Washer but for now I'm back to the bucket plunger method which goes much smoother now I can spin dry! (Photo number one showing plastic dust from the inside of the handle- and number two showing some dirty sock water after a 4 min lady powered wash cycle!)

title: Compact and convenient!
text:
Okay here are my honest thoughts. It a "tad" bit smaller than I would imagine. I am 6'2" and it comes to about my mid to lower thigh when standing next to it. My condo does not have a washer and dryer hookup and they nearly charge $4 in total for a wash and dry (almost $2 for each) so I bought this as a viable option.

What I liked:
- It's compact and "quiet", I have it back on my patio and it is kinda hidden as my HOA doesn't really like personal washers (it's a liability issue).
- When it it's empty, it's actually lightweight (feels like 30-35lbs?). But if you cannot lift heavy things/will be moving it around, then I would recommend getting one of those 4 wheel box dollies for $25
- It definitely gets the job done. Just remember it's only a 7lb drum so it doesn't hold a lot do you'll have to do more/ frequent "loads"
- There are a bunch of settings/ options to choose from. Only one option has an actual "soak" option, and six have a wash/ rinse and "spin" option.
- Most cycles can be done in about 30 min or less and the times are for all load sizes.
-It is super sensitive to detergent. The 1-2tbsp that is actually recommended for washing and some scent beads/boosters will do the job.
-If you are manually filling water, then the wash will start immediately once the desired load size has been selected and the water level has been met (there's some sort of sensor I believe). If not, the drum will not start-- since it's waiting for more water for from the intake pump.
- It's great in a pinch if you only have a few things to wash/ don't want to put on a full load of laundry on at the laundromat

Things I didn't like:
- the sink hookup isn't universal is it's really hard to find one that fit the sinks I had and I ended up manually filling up the drum with water. I have used the 3L settings, which uses an equivalent of 30L or about 7.5 gal of water per load, so not really water efficient. (Unless you recycle the grey water after each wash).
- If you over fill on detergent, then you run the risk of having major soap bubbles on your clothes after the rinse spin cycle.
- The drain pump is strong so be careful on where you have it draining. If it's not hooked into a bucket (I used a standard 5 gal for draining and filling) or taped down to a kitchen counter, it will spill all over potentially flooding your area. (which happened to me on my first load)

Some additional helpful information:

If you are manually filling:
1L= 16L= approx 4.25 Gal
2L= 23L= approx 6.10 gal- after draining/ spin you may have less than 5 gal of water to dump out
3L= 30L= approx. 8.00 gal- after draining/ spin you may have about 6-7 gal of water to dump out so I would keep an eye on the bucket or whatever your draining into, if it's not a sink.

Since I have used the 3L the most here is what I was able to fit in each "load"
- approx 5-6 shirts (with one being a hoodie) and a pair of jeans
- approx 4-5 shorts/pants
- approx 3 shirts/short combos and 2-3 pairs of underwear
- approx 3-4 towels (if you have XL size/ beach towels it may only be 2-3)-- honestly. I put 4 towels in (which filled the drum) but only filled/set the water to 2L, they came out fine.

Also, the installation instructions for the replacement temperature should include as the final step of the installation, to calibrate the oven in accordance with the GE procedure for Profile ovens. title: Side Braces On Small Burners Don’t Reach Drip Pan Edges
text:
Product: MP22YA Electric range burner element replacement set includes 2 X MP15YA-6 inch, 2 X MP21YA-8 inch Green

I’ve had to replace a burner here and there over the last couple of years, so I decided to start fresh with a whole new set. With this set, it was more cost effective than replacing a single burner occasionally.

The plug fits my stove perfectly. They plugged in without any problems. The problem is how they sit in the drip pans. Three out of four of the burners don’t sit correctly in the drip pans, so there is some wobbling. It’s not a lot, but it’s there. In fairness, I’ve had a problem with drip pans. I’ve replaced several and have had problems finding ones that would fit with the old burners properly. I kind of wish I had gotten a set of burners that came with the drip pans to have a better chance of the correct fit.

All of the burners heat up, but two of them have spots that don’t get “red” like the rest of the coil (see pictures with stove on high). It’s not bad enough to cause any real noticeable problem when cooking, but it makes me wonder about how long these coils will hold up. A couple of the red rubber (?) pieces on the end of the plugs were not perfect out of the box. I’m not an electrician and not sure how important they are. I noticed several were gone on my old coils when I took them out, and they have been working. One of the plugs was a little bent in. I was able to gently push it out so it was straight without any problem before I inserted it into the store. I did get a bit of a smell the first time I turned the burner on, but it was the smell I’ve gotten with other new cooking appliances, like a toaster oven. It went away after a couple of minutes. All of those things added up to me feeling like these weren’t the best quality burners.

I haven’t decided yet what I will do with the wobbling: new burners with drip trays, new drip trays or just go with the slight wobble unless it causes a major problem.

title: Ideal refrigerator but with a big problem...
text:
We loved this refrigerator for its size and reliability... until after 9 months. A loud motor noise began ruining our lives. When you open the door, the motor turns off - the noise comes back after you close the door. The noise was coming from behind the bottom freezer. Not sure if it's the fan or compressor. We tried defrosting and taking the plug out and back in to reboot... but no luck... the noise returns. It sounded like a gas-powered lawn mower inside the house and not the usual refrigerator muffled buzz. It's so loud you need to raise your voice and talk over it. The refrigerator still works but it's the loud noise that is driving us crazy.

We called Danby customer service and they were responsive. Unfortunately, all their "service depots" that were nearby us were in Canada. None of them would cross the border even if one was located 15 miles away. Danby contacted some refrigeration repair places and none of them would service this refrigerator either due to our location or they only repaired specific brands.

Danby customer service said they would see about some other options and will call me back. I will update this review.

title: Doesn't clean clothes
text:
I put two dresses, a pair of spandex shorts, and a tank top in with detergent and hot water. Spun for one minute to agitate and let soak for 20 minutes (instructions don't say to do this, but it felt like it would be more sanitary). I then spun for two more minutes, alternating spinning directions. I also unhooked the cover and rearranged the clothes to make sure nothing was in the same position. I then let drain, filled with clean cold water, spun for two minutes, drained again and repeated the clean water cycle. Then I spun really hard for about five minutes until no more water was coming out.

When I took my clothes out, they were still as dry as they would be if I had wrung them out by hand. Not dripping, but by no means remarkably dry. That's fine, but both of my dresses still had TONS deodorant residue on them (that i was able to wash away in five seconds with the sink faucet, so it's not like it was a stubborn stain) and my spandex bike shorts still had a bit of a stain from a washable magic marker (that i was able to get rid of in about 20 seconds with some detergent, my nail, and the sink faucet).

This does not clean clothes. Do not recommend.

Drinking coffee really is a new experience with these filters.

The other ones are bleached filters (they look perfectly white, while these look slightly brown), and they don't seem to do as well. Not sure why, but every time I use these, I love my coffee (and vice versa, when I use the white ones, I question everything I know about Chemex...). Yes, they are more expensive than a Walmart variety, but it is worth it.

Bottom line, get a Chemex, and get these filters. The two together are a perfect match, and you will not be disappointed.

title: Laundromat no more!
text:
I work full-time, go to school full-time, and am the mom of a toddler. This machine has saved me so much time, it's unbelievable. I used to spend about 3 hours a week at the laundromat, away from my family, unable to do anything else while I was there (and the cost!). Now I can just hook up this bad boy at home and not worry about dragging all of my family-of-three's clothes back and forth. (Let's not even talk about going to the laundromat in bad weather!)

I was skeptical, like you probably are, about how this washer would work. Not all the reviews are great. Some people have leaking, grinding noises, etc. So far, so good, for me. Yes, there are little styrofoam bits that are stuck under the motor when it first comes in. It's a pain to clean them all out, but once it's done, it's done. Snapping the bottom piece on was a strangely weird challenge. My husband finally figured it out after trying one way, and then the other, for a long while. But, it made us feel so victorious when he finally got it, that we immediately forgot how irritating it was. (B&D, please explain that better in the instructions, or redesign that bad boy).

Attaching the quick release spigot on the sink was a comedy of errors for us, but that was due to our particular sink. There is very minor leaking from around the hose on the sink side (so it's draining into the sink, not on the floor) when our cold water is turned on and the machine is running.

But how well does it wash the clothes? Excellent. Yes, the loads are small, but it's quick. 41 minutes on normal cycle, which is the one I use the most. Normal cycle has an excellent spin so if I hang up the clothes to air dry overnight, they're usually dry by morning, or mostly. Jeans/pants take longer. Towels take forever, but that's to be expected. Yes! I can wash my towels in this washer and they are "bath sheets". I usually put one in with some hand towels or washcloths and it's full and ready to go. I can do our queen sized sheets as well. I just washed a king sized fleece blanket and that was a tight fit, but it worked.

All in all I love this machine. It's light enough for me to just pick up and carry to the kitchen when I wash clothes (I think it's around 35 lbs), or there are the wheels to roll it. It's small enough to store in between uses. I personally haven't had any problems, but from the reviewers who did and tried to get the problems fixed, it seems like the company is very helpful to their consumers. Give it a try, it's really worth a shot. I waited a long time to buy, read a million reviews of various other portable machine washing systems, and finally got this. I wish I ordered it sooner!

title: Diluted coffee - design issue?
text:
I have the Ninja CFP307 DualBrew Pro and was looking forward to using these reusable coffee filter pods because I have a few favorite brands of coffee that don’t come in K-cups and because I don’t like all the plastic associated with regular K-cups.

The pods themselves appear to be well made and sturdy. The scoop funnel is also very nice and really helps measure the amount of coffee and enables you to just “drop” the coffee into the pod which helps avoid spilling it. The Directions say that you should not fill the pods more than 75%, I am assuming this is so that the “teeth” of the machine have enough room to enter the pod.

The pods fit pretty well into the Ninja basket though you must remember to keep the “Front” pointing to the front. Unfortunately, as others have indicated, it is a bit of a struggle to close the lid of the coffee maker and sink the "teeth" into these pods - and I’m always a little fearful that I’m going to break something in the attempt.

My biggest issue with these pods is that the first 3-4 seconds of the brew that flows from the Ninja coffee maker into my coffee cup is just hot WATER. After a few seconds it then begins to dispense the actual coffee, though in a still slightly diluted form. As a result, the coffee is very weak - to the point that I am not able to drink it. I’ve tried to pack the coffee into the pod more compactly; I’ve tried using more/less coffee in the pods; I’ve tried the “Classic” brew method; I’ve tried all three of the included pods - and I still end up with the hot water at the beginning of the brew cycle.

In trying to figure out why these pods only produce hot water at the beginning of the brew cycle, the only thing I can figure is that the regular K-cups have only ONE small exit point at the bottom of their plastic pods whereas the bottoms (AND sides) of these pods have a mesh across the entire bottom of the pods thus allowing MORE water to exit the pods in a faster time. It’s like a gate - if you have a really wide gate it will allow more traffic to enter than if you have a really narrow gate - the wider the “gate” the more water you’re going to have flowing through the filter. I am posting a photo to illustrate how diluted the coffee is with these pods - you will notice that the coffee using the regular K-cups is darker and richer than the cup using these pods (I really hope the small photo will be able to show the color difference between the two brews).

I have not read any other Reviewers describing this issue so maybe I'm an outlier. If I find out that this problem is solvable, I will certainly revise my Review. I really want to like these pods & I hope I discover a solution since I really do have a health concern with all the plastic used in regular K-cups.

title: Hoping for a better seal over time
text:
I have a GE JBS260F2ABR electric range/stove with only about 12 inches (300 mm) of seal length left across the top of the oven/door interface. I think this model was made ~ 1990. The nameplate is corroded, so it is difficult to read.

Pros:
- It does at least install correctly... or so I think, since there's no instructions.

Cons:
- Too short to make a full seam around the oven. This probably varies from unit to unit, but since I checked my model # and it fit, I'm a little disappointed there's wasn't excess to trim off and have a full seal.
- Surprisingly expensive

Notes:
- I did a test run afterwards to see if there was improvement. It does not seem to have improved the heat seal. However, it may need a "burn-in" period before it seals better.

I have read instructions that you can slip this seal around the existing lip with soapy water and a screwdriver. Forget that. Some coarse instructions for those with similar ovens:
1) Unplug the unit and pull it from your wall
2) Remove the door - there are lots of videos on how to do this
3) Locate the fasteners that pull the inner oven chamber tight against the housing and loosen them ~ 0.25 inch (6 - 8 mm). Some ovens have screws inside the oven to loosen and slide the interior forward, to relieve the grip on the door seal. Mine had two nuts on the rear face to loosen. Don't over-loosen them!
4) Pull the inner oven towards the front of the unit - this seal should no longer be gripped tightly between the inner oven and housing
5) Remove old seal - pay attention to the lip orientation
6) Install new seal same way as old seal

Bottom line: if you're overhauling an older machine - like mine - this seal is ~15+ % of the cost of a new range/oven unit and it will take a bit of time to replace. If you're doing a lot of repairs, consider this a sizable chunk of the investment towards a newer, better designed machine. It may be worth it to upgrade. Time will tell if the seal quality becomes satisfactory. If you have a newer machine, it probably doesn't use this kind of seal anyway!

title: Do Not Force These On!
text:
It worked (why it got any stars), but with a BIG WARNING:
The metal reinforcing ring on the inside of these knobs make it extremely difficult to easily push them onto the timing control's stem, which is plastic. Forcefully doing so made the timing control come off its mounts inside the panel and the only way to fix this was to take the entire panel apart to re-mount the timer control and get enough leverage to force these knobs over the stem without breaking things (there is so much cheap plastic on these Chinese-made dryers).
Be Careful: If you force these knobs onto the timer's stem you run the risk of breaking the cheap plastic mounts holding the timer control to the panel (inside) and then the entire panel will need to be replaced at around $120!
DO NOT FORCE THEM ON!

That said, I was able to get the knob on, but should it need to be replaced in the future I'm uncertain that I'll be able to remove it without breaking the cheap plastic stem on the timer control. A new timer costs around $50.

If I were to do this again I would buy a knob that didn't have the metal-reinforced bracket inside. This is a good product in concept, it just falls short of working properly because the internal measurement tolerances are off by a millimeter, or two. I ended up spending an entire evening making this knob work for me, when it should have only taken minutes with a plain, non-reinforced replacement knob.

title: Looks nice, works OK
text:
I bought it not at amazon but at local retail store.
Looks nice, works fine, but I can say nothing about reliability because I installed it just a few days ago.

My old range-hood was extremely noisy comparing to this one, but if you think this range-hood is so silent that it could barely be heard than you are wrong. It does produce quite a bit of noise – but it sounds more like noise of the rushing air than like electric motor.

Our old range hood had regular 60 watt bulb and we had a very bright light over our kitchen range. This range hood comes with two sort-of LED pot-lights that produce less light and illuminate only front part of the range. These LED lights look sexy but they are very insufficient for us.

About eliminating bad smell from your house:

My old range hood was probably around 100 cfm and it was practically useless in removing bad smell from the kitchen; this range hood is rated as 720 cfm and if you think it completely eliminates any smell spreading from you kitchen to the rest of your house - than you are wrong. This range hood certainly does better job by removing more smelly air to the outside but when my wife bakes in the oven (for eggplant salad) chunks of onions, chunks of eggplants and garlic the smell of this still spreads around the house. Two things are worthy to mention here. First, if your AC or furnace is ON than the blower fan will cause an air circulation in your house causing smelly air from your kitchen to spread all over your house. So, you are better to turn OFF your AC or furnace when you are cooking really smelly stuff. Second, if you have doors in your kitchen than close them when cooking smelly stuff and running the range hood – it will help a lot. If your kitchen doesn’t have doors and you hope than $1000 investment into this range hood will completely eliminate any smell in your house originated from the kitchen than you will waste $1000.

About installation:

First, it has so-called knockouts for screws/bolts (and knockout for wires on electrical box). These are not real knockouts and you cannot knock them out using screwdriver and hummer, don’t even try or you will damage the unit. These “knockouts” are only to indicate where to drill the holes for the screws/bolts; yes to drill in stainless steel (and installation instructions clearly state it). So, you have to have (or buy) drill bits capable of drilling through stainless steel.

Second, it is much heavier than less expensive range-hoods. Alone you cannot hold it and screw it to your kitchen cabinet - you must have someone else helping you.

Third, it arrives prewired so that wires come out from the top of the range-hood. I used these wires to wire the range hood and I didn’t drill hole in electrical box (to connect wires inside it). Rewiring of this unit looks really challenging. Wires coming out from the top originate from the electrical box (inside the unit) and they are attached with clamps to the back wall deep inside of the range hood. I did not try, but I think it would require removing both motors and fans to rewire this unit. Also, instructions assert that first thing after opening a packaging box (and before doing anything with the unit like drilling holes – or you cannot return the unit) the unit has to be powered and tested (both fans and lights) and these prewired wires come very handy (I used them to test the unit).

title: Great Product AFTER They Are Modified
text: First let me say that these knobs are much better than the original manufacturer's.  These are metal knobs with a plastic insert vice all plastic from GE.  So I'm hoping these won't melt like my originals did.  But I had to take a star away from my rating since they are actually NOT equivalent to the GE's WB03K10303 part.  When I first installed these, I found that they were sticking out too far from the stove.  See first picture.  So I decided to figure out why starting with removing the plastic insert.  I noticed that the shaft tube was sealed in the back preventing the stove's knob shaft from going far enough in.  Pic 2.  My original GE knobs have openings and their tubes are not "sealed."  To remedy this, I took a drill and made a hole just big enough for the shaft to go through.  Pic 3.  Now when I pushed the knob on the shaft went through the hole and the knob now seated perfectly the correct distance away from the stove.  See Pic 4.  Now the knobs look just right.  In order for these knobs to be form / fit / function equivalent to GE's WB03K10303, they need to make the hole in their inserts like I had to do.  Just be careful and drill slowly with just the right size bit.  It is an easy fix and much simpler than cutting the stove shafts like some people have indicated that they have done.

title: Cancels out benefit of Senseo
text:
After trying various pre packaged pods for my Senseo and not really being happy with any of them (not strong enough), I was happy to find what I thought to be a great solution to my problem, i.e. make my own pods!

But after pulling out my coffee, grinding the beans to the right granularity (you have to pay attention here!), carefully putting the grounds into the eco pod (it still always spills, making a mess), snapping pod together, putting coffee back, I had to stop and ask myself what the point of the Senseo was in the first place: EASY, quick, mess free, but mediocre coffee. I don't think it pretends to be anything more than that, and it does that quite well.

Introducing this customized pod business into the equation completely negates the whole reason for the Senseo in the first place!

In addition to that, I still could not pack enough coffee into the Ecopod to make a strong enough cup for my tastes, so it was no better than my Timothy espresso pods (which are pretty darn good if you haven't tried them, mostly because they simply have more volume of coffee in their pod), but ALSO was a huge pain to make/clean up after, etc.

So there really is no point to these imo. If you are going to go to all the trouble, you might as well just stick with a real espresso machine or a real coffee machine.

Also, not sure what is so environmentally friendly about a pod made from petrochemicals, in plastic wrapping? I think the traditional pods with the paper filters are a lot more enviro friendly if you ask me, since I put them in my compost pile and they break down very quickly.

The product itself works as advertised, and costs less than $10, so it gets a couple of stars for that, but stick with the pods if you ask me.

One more note: if you like strong coffee like me, this is definitely a no go. I always use TWO of the normal pods (either the dark roast or the Sumatra) and hit SINGLE SERVING. Comes out about right for me. Then I tap the single serving again briefly and hit the power button, so the water comes out for about 1.5 servings. Perfect! This method isn't possible with the ecopod of course, so another negative...sorry!

title: Rusty ice maker
text: The ice maker makes rusty ice. The metal that should be stainless steel or rust resistant, is rusty and leaves you with rusty ice cubes or rusty crushed ice. If you put your ice in dark drink (tea, coke, beer, etc) you would never know. But plop some ice in milk or empty glass wrapped in a paper towel, and you'll notice small orangish brown spots on the ice. Inspect the ice maker to find rusty parts. I called Frigidair and they said they have a "specific clause in their warranty that say's they do not cover rusty parts". To put such a clause makes it seem evident that it was a planned problem in production from the beginning. It will take about 8-12months for you to start to see rust. Most people never notice or check. Even though none of their employees would like to be served a glass of rusty ice. The replacement part is $40-$80 depending on your model and it is NOT covered by the Frigidair warranty or if you buy from Lowes, it is NOT covered under the extended protection warranty. The replacement part only carries a 90day warranty.

title: It will probably work, if you're careful and buy loctite.
text:
DO NOT USE THE CHEAP FOAM-TAPE IT COMES WITH!!!

I'll make this review quick. Here's what you need to know:
-You have a granite / quartz countertop, and you don't have anything to sink those screws into.
-These are cheap, and they'll probably work, so you buy them.
-You know the tape on the back is garbage, so you buy https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000DZD0HC/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1 this 2part Loctite Epoxy from Amazon.
-Peel that crap off the back (it really isn't hard), and clean it w/ Acetone / fingernail polish remover.
-Dry fit everything, totally flush, exactly perfect.
-Mark where these granite grabbers go.
-Pull the dw out, TAPE THE BACKSIDE OF THE HOLE on the granite grabbers (u can't put a screw in if it's full of epoxy).
-Don't overkill the epoxy, this stuff is really strong. Then clamp these in place for 20-30 min.
-Install the dw -- DO NOT CROSSTHREAD THOSE CHEAP, CRAPPY SCREWS -- I did it with one, and it almost made this impossible.

title: Nice functions cannot overpower the exceedingly awful repair rate
text:
I've bought Kenmore in the past (and you can still buy this machine at Sears, it's just not here on Amazon at present), and I read the Consumer's reviews of this dishwasher and other reviews at the time. Mine is now 18 months old.

We had one repair call during the 1-year full warranty, for a complete pump assembly failure in the first 6 months. Now, the flanges that hold the wheels on the top rack in place have fatigued and snapped off, leaving the top rack tending to fall off. Kenmore Elite promises a two-year parts warranty, but it turns out that this is a deceptive warranty. In order to get the parts replaced, one must FIRST pay one of their technicians $75 to go to your house and declare the part defective. THEN, one must pay the technician to do the repair--though you won't know what that will cost until the tech is standing there saying "yep, you're right, that part needs replaced". You run the risk of the tech declaring it isn't a manufacturing defect but something that is somehow your own fault. And it doesn't matter if it's a repair or replacement you can easily do yourself (like snapping in a new roller wheel). Where to get parts for a reasonable price? Well, here on Amazon, of course. But I shouldn't need to be replacing this kind of part after only 18 months of operation.

The machine also has a persistent, erratic leak around the door seals. Wonderful complement to a kitchen with wood floors.

We agree with other reviewers that this machine's tendency to failure is abysmal, especially for a product line which used to have a wonderful reputation for reliability. We're especially disappointed because, when functioning the dishwasher is reasonably quiet and does a decent job of cleaning.

Other disses:

Don't get too excited by the "powerwash" feature. It doesn't add significantly to the cleaning power of the machine and does add to the energy consumption when activated. It certainly doesn't work as advertised.

There is no option for a quick rinse.

The time-remaining display is stupidly graphical--a series of bars which supposedly each indicate about 20 minutes of remaining runtime. Why not simply display the time remaining? Even my washing machine can do that.

Short version: don't buy this.

title: Very good first attempt... some suggestions...
text:
First, this is the very best app-enabled smart egg tray on the market, bar none. So if you've been thinking of taking the plunge (who hasn't?), don't even hesitate. This is the creme of the crop, although I'm anxious to see for how long. I use the app more than any other app on my phone. But over the last few weeks, I've come up with some improvements that would make this product perfect.

- I want the App to integrate with Facebook, so that my friends can all benefit from the regular updates on the age of my eggs. (I'm really social). Ditto for twitter. A tweet when an each egg reaches a pre-defined threshold would be amaaaaaazing.

- I want custom ringtone alerts for each egg. I need to know WHICH SPECIFIC EGG. The ability to name each egg would be very useful. (And not just UUIDs. I want to personalize with names like "Alexandar Graham Bell", "Alexander the Great", "Alex Trebeck". You get the idea. And maybe even more than Alex-based names, although that's probably overkill.

- The 14 egg capacity, as others have mentioned, is really bad. It should be 15. This alone would make it worth a full $100.00.

- It should have bluetooth built-in, not some overpriced add-on that I have to buy. It really gripes me when companies do this, and everyone just assumes blue-tooth would be built-in, because it's so obvious. And then you go to pair your blue-tooth device, and it's NOT INCLUDED.

- The app has very limited control capabilities back to the tray in this initial version. I want to be able to do things like rotate a specific egg (by name, preferably. See above.) Or rename an egg.

Anywho, I love, love, love this product. I'd love to meet the inventor of this product so I could shake their hand. *fist-bump*. <- That's for you, inventor!!!

title: Makes good coffee, but different than chemex
text:
It’s nice to not need paper filters, but this product changes a lot about the way you have to use a chemex. Water drains *much* faster than with paper, so your brew ends up less like the pseudo-immersion brew you usually get from chemex and more like a standard pourover. You can use a finer grind to alleviate this a little, but that makes the filter harder to clean, and it isn’t easy to begin with.

Anyway, it makes perfectly fine coffee, but don’t expect to not have to tweak your chemex procedure quite a bit and expect to have to make a few compromises along the way.

title: AVOID - ARRIVED DEAD, NEEDS MODIFICATION TO FIT - READ COMMENTS FIRST - BUY TOMOON PART INSTEAD
text: There are a lot of hall sensors to choose from.  This is one you will want to avoid.  My part arrived dead (resistance tests open between pin 1 and pin 5, and open between pin 2 and pin 5).  On top of being completely non-functioning, it requires physical modifications to fit the stator.  Almost gave up and called repair service until I read some of the comments of other customers stating they received DOA parts.  I ended up ordering another one by TOMOON (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08NB5VNC6/), got it a day early, resistance tested correctly, snapped into place perfectly (exactly like the original LG part) and washer is working perfectly now.
